BURHAN:v4p58/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p58/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p58/r3.claim: Good is attributed to God in the language of blessing and what is in His hand, while evil is omitted from such attribution as a matter of reverence; this is the sense of evil not being toward Him.
BURHAN:v4p58/r3.anchor: لكن الخير يضاف إلى الله تعالى إرادة محبة ورضا والشر يضاف إليه

BURHAN:v4p292/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p292/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p292/r2.claim: In الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم, غضب is the single opposite of blessing: the first group is believers and the second disbelievers.
BURHAN:v4p292/r2.anchor: فإن الغضب ضد النعمة والأول هم المؤمنون والثاني هم الكفار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.claim: Al-Harali maps al-Fatiha's verses to the seven letters: praise, lawful and forbidden, command and prohibition, clear and ambiguous, then the corresponding petitions; its opening gathers all seven.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28#s002/r1.anchor: فالآية الأولى تشتمل على حرف الحمد السابع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.claim: The transition from al-Fatiha's plea for the straight path to al-Baqara identifies that guidance with this Book, then describes the guided and rejected groups to teach the path to follow and the path to avoid.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31#s002/r2.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو

BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r1.claim: A further reading of guidance is to turn from everything besides God and wholly obey Him, even under Abraham's, Ishmael's, Jonah's, Moses', or John and Zechariah's severe commands.
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r1.anchor: طلب الإعراض عما سوى الله وإن كان نفسه والإقبال بالكلية عليه حتى لو أمر بذبح ولده

BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r2.claim: Calling the path that of people God favored, rather than people killed or punished, softens the demand and invites believers toward prophetic and saintly states.
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r2.anchor: دون أن يقول صراط الذين ضربوا وقتلوا تيسيرا ما وترغيبا إلى مقام الأنبياء والأولياء

BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r3.claim: The Prophet said that Surah Hud and its sisters made him gray because he was commanded to remain steadfast.
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r3.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "شيبتني هود وأخواتها" حيث ورد فيها

BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r4.claim: Steadfastness means moderation between excess and neglect across natural and spiritual traits; the law sets this balance in action, speech, money, and character.
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r4.anchor: فإن الإنسان من حيث نشأته وقواه الظاهرة والباطنة مشتمل على صفات

BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r5.claim: The Prophet advised a would-be ascetic to fast and break fast, pray and sleep, because his self, wife, and visitors each had rights.
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r5.anchor: إن لنفسك عليك حقا ولزوجك عليك حقا ولزورك عليك حقا فصم وأفطر وقم ونم

BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r6.claim: When Umar recited loudly to wake sleepers and repel Satan, the Prophet told him to lower his voice slightly; he told Abu Bakr, who prayed softly, to raise his slightly.
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r6.anchor: ولما رأى صلى الله عليه وسلم عمر رضي الله عنه يقرأ رافعا صوته

BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r7.claim: The author grades spiritual integrity by combinations of heart, action, and speech: complete inward and outward integrity is highest, while integrity in only one or two can harm its holder.
BURSEVI:v1p11#2/r7.anchor: والمستقيم على أقسام منها : مستقيم بقوله وفعله وقلبه ومستقيم

BURSEVI:v1p13/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p13/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p13/r1.claim: Those You favored is a complete substitution for the first straight path; favor here means the religion's beneficial gift.
BURSEVI:v1p13/r1.anchor: {صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} بدل من الأول بدل الكل والإنعام إيصال النعمة

BURSEVI:v1p13/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p13/r2.speaker: أبو العباس بن عطاء
BURSEVI:v1p13/r2.claim: Ibn Ata assigns knowledge to knowers, truthfulness, contentment, certainty and purity to saints, patience and compassion to the righteous, obedience's sweetness to seekers, and steadfastness to believers.
BURSEVI:v1p13/r2.anchor: قال أبو العباس بن عطاء : هؤلاء المنعم عليهم هم طبقات

BURSEVI:v1p13/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p13/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p13/r3.claim: Another identification, matching 4:69, is prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and the righteous.
BURSEVI:v1p13/r3.anchor: كما قال تعالى : {فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهدآء والصالحين}

BURSEVI:v1p13/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p13/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p13/r4.claim: The path belongs to God by law and choice, and to servants as something they follow and obey; both attributions express its relationship to each side.
BURSEVI:v1p13/r4.anchor: وسره من وجوه : الأول : بيان أن ذلك كله له شرعا ولنا نفعا

BURSEVI:v1p13/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p13/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p13/r5.claim: Attributing the path to God cuts off the servant's vanity; attributing it to the servant comforts and honors him, and removes Satan's hope of stripping believers of dignity.
BURSEVI:v1p13/r5.anchor: أنه أضافه إلى نفسه قطعا لعجب العبد وإلى العبد تسلية لقلبه

BURSEVI:v1p13/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p13/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p13/r6.claim: Repeating path indicates two journeys: the frightening way from servant to Lord, where caravans and mounts are lost, and the way from Lord to servant.
BURSEVI:v1p13/r6.anchor: وتكرار الصراط إشارة إلى أن الصراط الحقيقي صراطان : من العبد إلى الرب

BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r1.claim: Not those angered or astray substitutes for those favored, describing the favored as free of anger and misguidance; ghayr can mean different from, not, or except.
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r1.anchor: وكلمة غير على ثلاثة أوجه : الأول : بمعنى المغايرة وفارسيته "جز"

BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r2.claim: Divine anger cannot mean its human beginning, so it denotes its end or effect, such as punishment, retribution, or painful seizure.
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r2.anchor: أن القاعدة التفسيرية أن الأفعال التي لها أوائل بدايات وأواخر غايات

BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r3.claim: Misguidance means deliberately or accidentally leaving the sound path; sinners fail in action, while the ignorant fail in knowledge.
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r3.anchor: والضلال : العدول عن الطريق السوي عمدا أو خطأ ، والمراد بالمغضوب عليهم العصاة

BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r4.claim: A common reading identifies those angered as Jews and those astray as Christians, but neither group's label is exclusive because Scripture attributes both traits to both.
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r4.anchor: أو المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود لقوله تعالى في حقهم : {من لعنه الله وغضب عليه}

BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r5.claim: Anger fits the Jews especially because of their rebellious unbelief, aggression, killing prophets, and saying God is poor while they are rich.
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r5.anchor: بل المراد أنهما إذا تقابلا فالتعبير بالغضب الذي هو إرادة الانتقام لا محالة باليهود أليق

BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r6.claim: Mentioning both groups after the favored expresses full fear alongside the hope of favor; the Prophet says a believer's fear and hope balance.
BURSEVI:v1p14#2/r6.anchor: فائدته وصف إيمانهم بكمال الخوف من حال الطائفتين بعد وصفه بكمال الرجاء

BURSEVI:v1p15/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p15/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p15/r1.claim: Divine anger perfects the function of the left hand: mercy and severity have distinct effects, and severity completes what cannot be repaired by mercy.
BURSEVI:v1p15/r1.anchor: واعلم أن حكم الغضب الإلهي تكميل مرتبة قبضة الشمال

BURSEVI:v1p15/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p15/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p15/r2.claim: Anger also purifies, like a doctor cutting a diseased limb or fire separating gold from lead and copper.
BURSEVI:v1p15/r2.anchor: والسر الثالث التطهير كالذهب الممزوج بالرصاص والنحاس إذا قصد تمييزه

BURSEVI:v1p15/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p15/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p15/r3.claim: Bewilderment has blameworthy and praiseworthy forms; a beginner resolves confusion by identifying the goal, sound path, guide, helpful practices, and obstacles.
BURSEVI:v1p15/r3.anchor: والضلال هو الحيرة فمنها ما هي مذمومة ومنها ما هي محمودة

BURSEVI:v1p15/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p15/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p15/r4.claim: The bewilderment of advanced knowers is not a defect but appears after perfected knowledge, witnessing, and insight into the secret of existence.
BURSEVI:v1p15/r4.anchor: وحيرة الأكابر محمودة لا تظنن أن هذه الحيرة سببها قصور في الإدراك

BURSEVI:v1p15/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p15/r5.speaker: النجمي
BURSEVI:v1p15/r5.claim: The Najmiyya reading describes the two groups as people who missed divine light and wandered in the self's desires, nature's darkness, and imitation.
BURSEVI:v1p15/r5.anchor: وفي تفسير النجم {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضآلين} هم الذين أخطأهم ذلك النور

QASHANI:1:6-7/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:6-7/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:6-7/r2.claim: Those under wrath are like Jews who stop at outward forms and bodily pleasures, veiling themselves from spiritual truths and intellectual delight; wrath entails expulsion, distance, and darkness of appearances.

QASHANI:1:6-7/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:6-7/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:6-7/r3.claim: The astray are like Christians who stop at inner lights and special mercy, overlooking God’s outward manifestation and losing vision of the beloved’s beauty throughout creation.
QASHANI:1:6-7/r3.anchor: الذين وقفوا مع البواطن التي هي الحجب النورانية

QASHANI:1:6-7/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:6-7/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:6-7/r4.claim: Muhammadan unifiers answer the calls to seek pardon and paradise, fear God and believe His messenger, and worship God without partners, thereby combining love of the essence’s beauty with the attributes’ goodness.

QASHANI:1:6-7/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:6-7/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:6-7/r5.claim: The unified path joins hope and fear, prayer for complete light, steadfastness, gardens, reward and light, seeing God’s face wherever one turns, and the best reward with increase.

QASHANI:1:6-7#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:1:6-7#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:1:6-7#2/r1.claim: Those who do good receive the best and an increase, completing the cited evidence that the unified servants are rewarded with both mercy and divine vision.

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r1.claim: God keeps the seekers from settling among likenesses through the gentle gift of union and disclosure of majesty and beauty.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r1.anchor: حل بيننا وبين مساكنة الأمثال والأشكال ، بما تلاطفنا به من وجود الوصال ، وتكاشفنا به من شهود

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r2.claim: Guidance to truth prevents reliance on the means of spiritual practice and keeps conjecture from clouding the oneness of God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r2.anchor: أرشدنا إلى الحق لئلا نتكل على وسائط المعاملات ، ويقع على وجه التوحيد غبار الظنون وحسبان الإعلال

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r3.claim: “Guide us” asks God to remove the darkness of one's states and the shadow of one's striving so that His holiness and generosity become lights by which one finds Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r3.anchor: أزل عنا ظلمات أحوالنا لنستضيء بأنوار قدسك عن التفيؤ بظلال طلبنا ، وارفع عنا ظل جهدنا لنستبصر بنجوم

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r4.claim: The straight path keeps Satan's impulses, the soul's notions, inherited imitation, routine instruction, habit, fatigue, weak resolve, and greed from delaying arrival or insight.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r4.anchor: حتى لا يصحبنا قرين من نزغات الشيطان ووساوسه ، ورفيق من خطرات النفوس وهواجسها ، أو يصدنا عن

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r5.claim: The straight path is proved by Scripture and Sunna; innovation has no authority or route upon it.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r5.anchor: الصراط المستقيم ما عليه من الكتاب والسنة دليل ، وليس للبدعة عليه سلطان ولا إليه سبيل

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r6.claim: It is also the path validated by signs of monotheism, witnesses of realization, the early Muslim community, and lessons drawn from evidence.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r6.anchor: الصراط المستقيم ما شهدت بصحته دلائل التوحيد ، ونبهت عليه شواهد التحقيق ، الصراط المستقيم ما درج عليه

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r7.claim: The path separates its travelers from self-interest and its seekers from claims to personal entitlement.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r7.anchor: الصراط المستقيم ما باين الحظوظ سالكه ، وفارق الحقوق قاصده

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r8.claim: The path leads to monotheism and lets its traveler witness divine care and generosity, so effort is not mistaken for a claim that reward is owed.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r8.anchor: الصراط المستقيم ما يفضي بسالكه إلى ساحة التوحيد ، ويشهد صاحبه أثر العناية والجود ، لئلا يظنه موجب

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r9.claim: Those favored with this path are saints and the elect, whom God has annihilated from themselves and established through Himself, without hidden divine stratagems stopping them.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r9.anchor: يعني طريق من أنعمت عليهم بالهداية إلى الصراط المستقيم ، وهم الأولياء والأصفياء . ويقال طريق من (

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r10.claim: Another description of the favored is that they fulfill God's rights without turning aside to secure their own interests.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r10.anchor: ويقال صراط من أنعمت عليهم بالقيام بحقوقك دون التعريج على استجلاب حظوظهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r11.claim: They are also described as purified of their own traces so that they reach God through God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r11.anchor: ويقال صراط من ( طهرتهم ) عن آثارهم حتى وصلوا إليك بك

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r12.claim: They have been freed from Satan's snares, the soul's errors, and imagined arrival before human traces have faded.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r12.anchor: ويقال صراط من أنعمت عليهم حتى تحرروا من مكائد الشيطان ، ومغاليط النفوس ومخاييل الظنون ، وحسبانات الوصول

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r13.claim: They rely on God, disown their own power, and witness their prior happiness in God's choice and His unity in what He decrees as pleasant or painful.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r13.anchor: ويقال صراط من أنعمت عليهم بالنظر والاستعانة بك ، والتبري من الحول والقوة ، وشهود ما سبق لهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r14.claim: The favored preserve proper etiquette in service and remain aware of reverent awe.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r14.anchor: ويقال صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بحفظ الأدب في أوقات الخدمة ، واستشعار نعت الهيبة

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r15.claim: They preserve the rules of sacred law even during overpowering disclosures of spiritual realities, never exceeding knowledge or neglecting a ruling.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r15.anchor: ويقال صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بأن حفظت عليهم آداب الشريعة وأحكامها عند غلبات ( بواده ) الحقائق حتى

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r16.claim: The suns of their knowledge do not extinguish the lights of their scrupulousness, and they never neglect a rule of the Law.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r16.anchor: ويقال صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم حتى لم تطفئ شموس معارفهم أنوار ورعهم ولم يضيعوا شيئا من أحكام الشرع

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r17.claim: The favored remain servants even when the power of spiritual reality appears.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r17.anchor: ويقال صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بالعبودية عند ظهور سلطان الحقيقة

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r18.claim: Those under wrath are struck by abandonment, deprivation, rejection, separation, and expulsion.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r18.anchor: المغضوب عليهم الذين صدمتهم هواجم الخذلان ، وأدركتهم مصائب الحرمان ، وركبتهم سطوة الرد ، وغلبتهم بواده الصد

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r19.claim: They are also described as humiliated and ruined, occupied with pursuing gratification while imagining they possess something; their misery has a divine secret.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r19.anchor: ويقال هم الذين لحقهم ذل الهوان ، وأصابهم سوء الخسران ، فشغلوا في الحال باجتلاب الحظوظ - وهو

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r20.claim: Another group tasted nearness for a time, then was turned to distance and failed to reach the intimacy it desired; its effort and hope came to nothing.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r20.anchor: ويقال هم الذين أنسوا بنفحات التقريب زمانا ثم أظهر الحق سبحانه في بابهم شانا ؛ بدلوا بالوصول بعادا

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r21.claim: Those under wrath forgot divine enabling and closed their eyes to the sight of divine support.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r21.anchor: ويقال غير المغضوب عليهم بنسيان التوفيق ، والتعامي عن رؤية التأييد

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r22.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r22.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r22.claim: Those who go astray fail to witness God's prior choice and the unfolding of His decrees.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r22.anchor: ولا الضالين عن شهود سابق الاختيار ، وجريان التصاريف والأقدار

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r23.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r23.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r23.claim: Those under wrath also neglect the etiquette of service and fall short in fulfilling the conditions of obedience.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r23.anchor: ويقال غير المغضوب عليهم بتضييعهم آداب الخدمة ، وتقصيرهم في أداء شروط الطاعة

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r24.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r24.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r24.claim: They can also be people cut off in the deserts of absence, scattered by worries through valleys of conjecture.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r24.anchor: ويقال غير المغضوب عليهم هم الذين تقطعوا في مفاوز الغيبة ، وتفرقت بهم الهموم في أودية وجوه الحسبان

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r25.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r25.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r25.claim: Saying amin after the Fatiha is Sunnah and means “Lord, do and answer”; it seeks enabling for deeds and fulfillment of hopes through humble petition.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r25.anchor: ويقول العبد عند قراءة هذه السورة آمين ، والتأمين سنة ، ومعناه يا رب افعل واستجب ، وكأنه

QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r26.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r26.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r26.claim: The strongest means for the needy is continual seeking of God's aid, expressed through sincere supplication and disavowal of one's own power and ability.
QUSHAYRI:v1p13/r26.anchor: وإن أقوى وسيلة للفقير تعلقه بدوام الاستعانة لتحققه بصدق الاستغاثة

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r1.claim: The blessed are knowers granted knowledge, saints granted sincerity, contentment, and certainty, the righteous granted patience and compassion, seekers granted obedience's sweetness, and believers granted steadfastness.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r1.anchor: أنعمت عليهم بالمعرفة وهم العارفون ، وأنعم على الأولياء بالصدق والرضا واليقين

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r2.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r2.claim: God's favor includes teaching them the path's dangers, Satan's tricks, and the ego's treachery.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r2.anchor: وحكي عن أبي عثمان أنه قال : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بأن عرفتهم مهالك الصراط

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r3.claim: The blessed path is acceptance of the obligations God imposed.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r3.anchor: وحكي عن محمد بن الفضل أنه قال : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم لقبول ما افترضت عليهم

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن الوراق
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r4.claim: Divine care keeps the blessed steadfast on the path of intimate conversation with God.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن الوراق : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بالعناية على الاستقامة

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r5.claim: The blessed were assigned happiness in pre-eternity.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم في سابق الأزل بالسعادة

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r6.speaker: بعض البغداديين
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r6.claim: God's favor annihilates attention to blessings through the lasting joy of nearness and intimacy.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r6.anchor: وحكي عن بعض البغداديين أنه قال : من أفنيته عن النظر إلى النعمة

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r7.claim: The blessed see what was decreed for them eternally without that disclosure distracting them from God.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بالنظر إلى جريان ما جرى عليهم في الأزل

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r8.speaker: مالك بن أنس
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r8.claim: The blessed path means following the Prophet.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r8.anchor: وحكي عن مالك بن أنس أنه سئل عن قوله ' صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ' فقال : متابعة النبي

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r9.claim: The favor consists of faith, guidance, enabling, care, watchfulness, and protection.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بالإيمان والهداية والتوفيق والرعاية

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r10.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r10.claim: The blessed are granted knowledge of God and understanding from Him.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r10.anchor: وقال جعفر بن محمد : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بالعلم بك والفهم عنك

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r11.speaker: بعض البغداديين
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r11.claim: The blessed relinquish personal interests and stand with God in good etiquette.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r11.anchor: وقال بعض البغداديين : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بفناء حظوظهم

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r12.claim: The blessed witness the Benefactor rather than the gift itself.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r12.anchor: وقيل : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بمشاهدة المنعم بغير النعمة

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r13.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r13.claim: The blessed have outward Islam and inward faith, echoing God's gifts both outwardly and inwardly (31:20).
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بالإسلام ظاهرا والإيمان باطنا

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r14.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r14.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r14.claim: They have cosmic darkness removed from their secrets and spirits purified by holy light, so their aspiration witnesses God alone.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r14.anchor: وقيل : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بإزالة ظلمات الأكوان عن سرائرهم

SULAMI:v1p41#2/r15.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r15.speaker: محمد بن علي
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r15.claim: God's favor restrains their limbs through awe while they serve Him.
SULAMI:v1p41#2/r15.anchor: وقال محمد بن علي : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم قال الذين زممت جوارحهم

SULAMI:v1p43/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p43/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p43/r1.claim: The blessed path comes from God's hidden realm through the lights of His guidance.
SULAMI:v1p43/r1.anchor: وقيل : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم من غيبك المستتر بأنوار هدايتك

SULAMI:v1p43/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p43/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p43/r2.claim: The path is worshipping God as though one sees Him, as in the Prophetic definition of excellence.
SULAMI:v1p43/r2.anchor: وقيل : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بعبادتك على المشاهدة

SULAMI:v1p43/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p43/r3.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
SULAMI:v1p43/r3.claim: The blessed path means following the Sunnah.
SULAMI:v1p43/r3.anchor: وسئل سهل بن عبد الله عن قوله صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم قال : متابعة السنة

SULAMI:v1p43/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p43/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p43/r4.claim: God's favor includes granting permission to converse with and petition Him.
SULAMI:v1p43/r4.anchor: وقيل أيضا : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بأن أذنت لهم في مناجاتك وسؤالك

SULAMI:v1p43/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p43/r5.speaker: الحسن
SULAMI:v1p43/r5.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the recipients of favor as Abu Bakr and Umar.
SULAMI:v1p43/r5.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم قال : أبو بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهم

SULAMI:v1p44/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p44/r1.claim: Those under anger are abandoned, expelled, and humiliated; the astray have left God's guidance, knowledge, and guardianship.
SULAMI:v1p44/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : غير المخذولين ولا المطرودين ولا المهانين ولا الضالين

SULAMI:v1p44/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p44/r2.claim: The condemned follow the path of the doomed, while the astray follow desire away from guidance.
SULAMI:v1p44/r2.anchor: وقيل : غير المغضوب عليهم في طريق الهلكى ، ولا الضالين عن طريق الهدى باتباع الهوى

SULAMI:v1p44/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p44/r3.claim: Those under anger are consumed in Satan's wastelands; the astray are expelled from obedience to the Merciful.
SULAMI:v1p44/r3.anchor: وقيل : غير المغضوب عليهم المستهلكين في مفاوز الشيطان ، ولا الضالين المطرودين

SULAMI:v1p44/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p44/r4.claim: Anger is associated with seeing one's own acts or seeking compensation for deeds; error is failing to see favors or thank God for enabled service.
SULAMI:v1p44/r4.anchor: وقيل : غير المغضوب عليهم برؤية الأفعال ولا الضالين عن رؤية المنن

SULAMI:v1p44/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p44/r5.claim: Anger follows bad etiquette in service; the contrasting phrase refers to turning back in repentance, though its wording is broken in this segment.
SULAMI:v1p44/r5.anchor: غير المغضوب عليهم بترك حسن الأدب في أوقات القيام بخدمتك

SULAMI:v1p44/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p44/r6.claim: Anger is linked with ostentation, and error with abandoning Sunnah in the pillars of worship.
SULAMI:v1p44/r6.anchor: وقيل : غير المغضوب عليهم بالرياء ولا الضالين بترك السنن في أركان العبادات

SULAMI:v1p44/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r7.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p44/r7.claim: He associates being under anger with leaving this chapter's recitation in prayer and being astray with not reciting it; the wording is awkward in the source.
SULAMI:v1p44/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان : غير المغضوب عليهم بترك قراءة هذه السورة في صلواتهم

SULAMI:v1p44/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p44/r8.claim: Anger means being left to oneself, while error means losing God's protection and attachment.
SULAMI:v1p44/r8.anchor: وقيل : غير المغضوب عليهم بأن وكلتهم إلى أنفسهم ولا الضالين بقطعك الاعتصام عنهم

SULAMI:v1p44/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p44/r9.claim: Anger follows innovations, while error is abandoning guidance and Sunnah, including the Sunnah of saying Amin aloud after the chapter in prayer.
SULAMI:v1p44/r9.anchor: وقيل : غير المغضوب عليهم باتباع البدع ولا الضالين عن سنن الهدى والسنة

SULAMI:v1p44/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r10.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p44/r10.claim: The supplicant asks God to act accordingly and not leave him to himself for even an instant.
SULAMI:v1p44/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : أي كذلك فافعل ولا تكلني إلى نفسي طرفة عين

SULAMI:v1p44/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r11.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p44/r11.claim: Amin means heading toward God, who is too generous to refuse one who heads to Him.
SULAMI:v1p44/r11.anchor: وقال جعفر : آمين أي : قاصدين نحوك وأنت أكرم من أن تجيب قاصدك

SULAMI:v1p44/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r12.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p44/r12.claim: Amin admits incapacity to praise God through one's own attributes except by following Muhammad al-Amin.
SULAMI:v1p44/r12.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمه الله : معنى آمين أي : عاجزين عن بلوغ الثناء عليك

SULAMI:v1p44/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r13.speaker: بعض العراقيين
SULAMI:v1p44/r13.claim: Amin expresses hope that God will answer the supplications just made.
SULAMI:v1p44/r13.anchor: وقال بعض العراقيين : آمين أي : راجين لإجابة هذه الدعوات

SULAMI:v1p44/r14.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r14.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p44/r14.claim: Amin can ask to be spared from one's requests because God's choice is better than one's own.
SULAMI:v1p44/r14.anchor: وقال بعضهم مستقيلين من جميع اسؤلتنا ؛ لأن حسن اختيارك لنا خير من اختيارنا

SULAMI:v1p44/r15.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p44/r15.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p44/r15.claim: Amin means being content with God's decree for and against the servants.
SULAMI:v1p44/r15.anchor: وقيل : آمين أي : راضين بما قضيت علينا ولنا .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the path of those favored as the way of those whom God favored.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : صراط الذين انعمت عليهم يقول : طريق من انعمت عليهم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those favored as obedient angels, prophets, truthful ones, and martyrs who worshipped God.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله انعمت عليهم يقول الملائكة والنبيين والصديقين والشهداء الذين اطاعوني وعبدوني

IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies those favored as the believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد : صراط الذين انعمت عليهم قال : هم المؤمنون

IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r4.claim: The Prophet identifies those under wrath as Jews and the astray as Christians; the author says exegetes do not disagree on this wording.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r4.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم قال : قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم : المغضوب عليهم : اليهود ، ولا الضالين : النصارى

IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r5.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r5.claim: The author says he knows no disagreement among exegetes over the identification of those astray as Christians and those under wrath as Jews.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r5.anchor: قال أبو سعيد : ولا اعلم بين المفسرين في هذا الحرف اختلافا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r6.claim: A second report from the Prophet likewise says the Jews incurred wrath and the Christians went astray.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r6.anchor: عن عباد بن حبيش ، عن عدي بن حاتم قال : اتيت رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو جالس في المسجد فقال : ان اليهود مغضوب عليهم ، والنصارى ضلال

IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the clause as avoiding the way of wrongdoers, especially Christians misled by their claims about God; he prays for the true religion and protection from the punishments of Jews and Christians through divine mercy.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس : وغير طريق الظالمين ، فهم النصارى الذين اضلهم الله بعزيتهم عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r8.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r8.claim: The author again says he knows no exegetical disagreement over this wording.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p31/r8.anchor: قال أبو محمد : ولا اعلم في هذا الحرف اختلافا بين المفسرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.claim: He reads the sura's annexation to Fatihat al-Kitab as descriptive: it means a sura characterized as the Book's opening, with no separate title needed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r1.anchor: إضافة السورة إلى فاتحة الكتاب من إضافة الموصوف إلى الصفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.claim: By contrast, Fatihat al-Kitab is a true annexation: al-Kitab here means the remainder of the Book apart from the sura called the Opening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r2.anchor: إضافة فاتحة إلى الكتاب فإضافة حقيقية باعتبار أن المراد من الكتاب بقيته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.claim: The names Umm al-Qur'an and Umm al-Kitab are established in the Sunna; “mother” denotes a thing's origin and source.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r3.anchor: وأما تسميتها أم القرآن وأم الكتاب فقد ثبتت في السنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.claim: A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says Abu Sa'id al-Khudri recited Umm al-Qur'an over a person suffering from a sting as a healing prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r4.anchor: أن أبا سعيد الخدري رقى ملدوغا فجعل يقرأ عليه بأم القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.claim: A sound hadith calls a prayer without Umm al-Qur'an deficient.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r5.anchor: كل صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم القرآن فهي خداج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.claim: One explanation of Umm al-Qur'an is that it begins and opens the Qur'an, making it like its origin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r6.anchor: أنها مبدؤه ومفتتحه فكأنها أصله ومنشؤه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.claim: A second explanation is that the sura gathers the Qur'an's three main aims: praise, commands and prohibitions, and promise and warning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r7.anchor: تشتمل محتوياتها على أنواع مقاصد القرآن وهي ثلاثة أنواع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r10.claim: The mention of those angered and astray also alludes to the Qur'an's narratives about misguided peoples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r10.anchor: يشير أيضا إلى نوع قصص القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.claim: The sura's three aims together represent the Qur'an's original purposes, while its remaining material elaborates them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r11.anchor: فهذه هي أنواع مقاصد القرآن كله ، وغيرها تكملات لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.claim: He also supports the sura's comprehensiveness by citing the sound report that al-Ikhlas counts as a third of the Qur'an because all its wording praises God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p132#2/r12.anchor: وقد يؤيد هذا الوجه بما ورد في الصحيح في : { قل هو الله أحد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.claim: A third explanation of Umm al-Qur'an is that it contains the Qur'an's theoretical wisdom and practical rulings, including theology, prophecy, admonition, worship, transactions, morals, and law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r1.anchor: تشتمل معانيها على جملة معاني القرآن من الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r10.claim: Those granted favor point to the good states of virtuous past nations and individuals; the angered and astray evoke the stories of deviant peoples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r10.anchor: يشير إلى أحوال الأمم والأفراد الماضية الفاضلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.claim: Taken explicitly and by implication, the sura gives a general outline of the Qur'an's aims and prompts readers to seek their fuller detail as able.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r11.anchor: يحصل من معاني الفاتحة تصريحا وتضمنا علم إجمالي بما حواه القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.claim: Requiring al-Fatiha in every rak'ah preserves recollection of the Qur'an's purposes contained within it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p133/r12.anchor: فرضت قراءة الفاتحة في كل ركعة من الصلاة حرصا على التذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r1.claim: Al-Fatiha stands first as the Qur'an's preface, both for its core purposes and for the rhetorical excellence of its opening.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r1.anchor: لأنها تنزل منها منزل ديباجة الخطبة أو الكتابب ، مع ما تضمنته من أصول مقاصد القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r2.claim: The majority agree that the sura is Meccan.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r3.speaker: كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r3.claim: Many say al-Fatiha was the first sura revealed; Ibn Ashur rejects that chronology, placing the opening of al-Alaq and then al-Muddaththir before it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r3.anchor: وقال كثير إنها أول سورة نزلت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur's preferred sequence has al-Alaq, then al-Muddaththir, and then al-Fatiha revealed before it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r4.anchor: والصحيح أنه نزل قبلها : { اقرأ باسم ربك } ( العلق : 1 ) وسورة المدثر ثم الفاتحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r5.claim: Other accounts put Nun and al-Muzzammil before al-Fatiha; another says al-Fatiha was the first complete sura, unlike al-Qalam, which came in portions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r5.anchor: وقيل نزل قبلها أيضا : { ن والقلم } ( القلم : 1 ) وسورة المزمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r6.claim: Some scholars say it was revealed when prayer became obligatory, and a report from Jabir ibn Zayd ranks it fifth in the order of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r6.anchor: وقد عدت في رواية عن جابر بن زيد السورة الخامسة في ترتيب نزول السور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r7.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r7.claim: The Prophet named it Fatihat al-Kitab and instructed that it be placed first in the Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r7.anchor: وأيا ما كان فإنها قد سماها النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتحة الكتاب وأمر بأن تكون أول القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r8.claim: Its first placement does not conflict with earlier revelations: it was put at the front once enough Qur'an had accumulated to form a Book.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r9.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r9.claim: Although the reciters and commentators agree on seven verses, Hasan al-Basri is reported to count eight; six is attributed to Amr ibn Ubayd and al-Husayn al-Ju'fi, and nine to an unspecified source.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r9.anchor: وهي سبع آيات باتفاق القراء والمفسرين ، ولم يشذ عن ذلك إلا الحسن البصري ، قال هي ثمان آيات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.claim: A hadith in both Sahihs from Abu Hurayra has God divide prayer between Himself and the servant, answering each portion of al-Fatiha and granting the servant's request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r10.anchor: قسمت الصلاة نصفين بيني وبين عبدي فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.claim: The verse division differs by region: Medinans exclude the basmala and count “those You favored” as a verse; Meccans and Kufans include the basmala and combine that phrase with its verse; Hasan counts both separately.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p135/r11.anchor: فعند أهل المدينة لا تعد البسملة آية وتعد : { أنعمت عليهم } آية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.claim: Important guidance requires preparing listeners, stirring their attention, and removing stubbornness, false assumptions, and satanic impulses that block learning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r1.anchor: ما بقي يخالجها العناد والبهتان ، وتخامر رشدها نزغات الشيطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.claim: Placed first by the Prophet's instruction, al-Fatiha trains readers in inner purification through its supplication from “You alone we worship” onward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r2.anchor: نبه الله تعالى قراء كتابه وفاتحي مصحفه إلى أصول هذه التزكية النفسية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r6.claim: Following those granted favor expresses the desire to adopt a good example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r6.anchor: الرابع الرغبة في التحلي بالأسوة الحسنة بما تضمنه { صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r7.claim: The prayer also expresses concern to avoid the plain error of those who incurred anger and those astray.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r7.anchor: الخامس التهمم بالسلامة من الضلال الصريح بما تضمنه { غير المغضوب عليهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r8.claim: “Those astray” additionally conveys concern that thought not become entangled in false claims disguised as truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r8.anchor: سلامة تفكيرهم من الاختلاط بشبهات الباطل المموه بصورة الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.claim: As a Qur'anic preface, al-Fatiha models an Arabic literary opening that improves understanding and attentive reception.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p152/r10.anchor: وهذا الأسلوب له شأن عظيم في صناعة الأدب العربي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.claim: Because the Qur'an guides people and reforms both worldly and future life, listeners must prepare by removing stubbornness, error, and low impulses before receiving its wisdom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r5.anchor: فلا مناص لها قبل استقبال تلك الحكمة والنظر من الاتسام بميسم الفضيلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r9.claim: The final distinction between the angered and astray wards off corruptions that can destroy sound knowledge or true revealed law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r9.anchor: الضلالات التي تعتري العلوم الصحيحة والشرائع الحقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.claim: These aims help explain why al-Fatiha is called Umm al-Qur'an.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p153/r10.anchor: ولأجل هذا سميت هاته السورة أم القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r1.claim: The straight path metaphorically means the truth that leads its follower to God's approval, the goal Islam came to seek.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r1.anchor: والصراط في هذه الآية مستعار لمعنى الحق الذي يبلغ به مدركه إلى الفوز برضاء الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r2.claim: Mustaqīm is the active participle of istaqāma and describes a route without bends; a straight highway brings travelers nearer without confusion or hesitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r2.anchor: والمستقيم اسم فاعل استقام مطاوع قومته فاستقام ، والمستقيم الذي لا عوج فيه ولا تعاريج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the straight path as the true religion and, in another report, the religion of Islam; Ibn ʿĀshūr reads the explanations together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن الصراط المستقيم دين الحق ، ونقل عنه أنه ملة الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r4.claim: The definite phrase identifies the mentally understood unique straight path; truth is one while misguidance has many forms, and Satan's speech confirms this usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r4.anchor: فالتعريف في ( الصراط المستقيم ) تعريف العهد الذهني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r5.claim: One explanation is that believers already received Islam and are taught this prayer to recognize God's favor, while later Quran and prophetic guidance continue to guide them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r5.anchor: وقد يوجه هذا التفسير بحصول الهداية إلى الإسلام فعلمهم الله هذا الدعاء لإظهار منته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r6.claim: He prefers all sound beliefs and deeds, with guidance calibrated to each person's capacity; everyone needs it continuously to avoid neglect and deviation, and Islamic guidance continues through law and inference.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p190#2/r6.anchor: والأظهر عندي أن المراد بالصراط المستقيم المعارف الصالحات كلها من اعتقاد وعمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r1.claim: The second phrase is either an appositive or explanatory substitute for the straight path; this general-to-specific restatement emphasizes the requested way and adds the merit of following the favored.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r1.anchor: بدل أو عطف بيان من { الصراط المستقيم } ، وإنما جاء نظم الآية بأسلوب الإبدال أو البيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r2.claim: The two grammatical labels have no semantic advantage over one another; explanatory apposition is a type of matching substitute.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r2.anchor: التحقيق عندي أن عطف البيان اسم لنوع من البدل وهو البدل المطابق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says substitution emphasizes by repetition, effectively repeating both the request and its governing verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r3.anchor: الكشاف ) : ( فإن قلت ما فائدة البدل ؟ قلت فائدته التوكيد لما فيه من التثنية والتكرير ) ا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r4.claim: The repeated phrase combines substitution's grammatical function with verbal emphasis; that dual rhetorical benefit depends on this artful wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192/r4.anchor: ومراده أن مثل هذا البدل وهو الذي فيه إعادة لفظ المبدل منه يفيد فائدة البدل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r1.claim: Repeating a noun before attaching a new qualification signals special care for its referent and creates rhetorical pleasure beyond mere emphasis; Quranic examples use the same pattern.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r1.anchor: إعادة الاسم في البدل أو البيان ليبنى عليه ما يراد تعلقه بالاسم الأول أسلوب بهيج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r2.speaker: ابن جني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r2.claim: Citing al-Aḥwaṣ, Ibn Jinnī says verb repetition is valid when the repeated verb takes a new prepositional complement that adds meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r2.anchor:
قال ابن جني في ( شرح مشكل الحماسة ) عند قول الأحوص :
فإذا تزول تزول عن متخمط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r3.claim: The repeated phrase in the verse about those led astray may be an appositive; he cannot determine why Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī objected and suggests he treated it as a new sentence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r3.anchor: فلعله امتنع من اعتبار { أغويناهم } بدلا من { أغوينا } وجعله استئنافا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r4.claim: Calling the favored people by a relative clause and ascribing their favor to God honors them in contrast with the other groups.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r4.anchor: وفي استحضار المنعم عليهم بطريق الموصول ، وإسناد فعل الإنعام عليهم إلى ضمير الجلالة ، تنويه بشأنهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r5.claim: Mentioning the favored path encourages a generous response and subtly asks to share their rank and imitate their causes of guidance; it also anticipates disavowal and offers hope and protection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p192#2/r5.anchor: فإن الكريم إذا قلت له أعطني كما أعطيت فلانا كان ذلك أنشط لكرمه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r1.claim: Niʿma derives from ease and pleasant living; the feminine noun denotes a good state, first bodily pleasure and later beneficial intellectual or spiritual goods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r1.anchor: والنعمة بالكسر وبالفتح مشتقة من النعيم وهو راحة العيش وملائم الإنسان والترفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r2.claim: The requested favor is complete good with no damaging aftermath: worldly and afterlife benefits, acquired or bestowed, spiritual or bodily, with the afterlife foremost.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r2.anchor: فالمراد من النعمة في قوله : { الذين أنعمت عليهم } النعمة التي لم يشبها ما يكدرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r3.claim: Most blessings resolve into guidance: guidance directs acquired worldly goods and all afterlife goods, and even bestowed gifts need guidance for proper use.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r3.anchor: والنعمة بهذا المعنى يرجع معظمها إلى الهداية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r4.claim: The favored are recipients of complete blessing, especially earlier messengers and prophets; substitution shows that guidance itself is a blessing and the fully blessed were guided.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r4.anchor: والذين أنعم الله عليهم هم خيار الأمم السابقة من الرسل والأنبياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r5.claim: The request fits Islam because true laws share sound principles and guidance; Islam preserves earlier sound paths and adds to them, or the favored may mean prophets whose state surpassed their peoples'.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r5.anchor: فسألوا دينا قويما يكون في استقامته كصراط المنعم عليهم فأجيبوا بدين الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r6.claim: Earlier peoples were treated leniently, while messengers exemplified fuller obedience; for example, prophets avoided even small amounts of intoxicating drink that earlier law permitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r6.anchor: فقد كان القدر غير المسكر منه مباحا وإنما يحرم السكر أو لا يحرم أصلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r7.claim: Whether the favored are prophets, their best followers, or earlier Muslims, the prayer asks for complete guidance as appropriate to each era's attained and un attained guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p193/r7.anchor: فسواء فسرنا المنعم عليهم بالأنبياء أو بأفضل أتباعهم أو المسلمين السابقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r1.claim: The meaning of the request for guidance remains acquisition, increase, or continued preservation according to the supplicants' circumstances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r1.anchor: والقول في المطلوب من { اهدنا } على هذه التقادير كلها كالقول فيما تقدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r2.claim: The prayer excludes blessings with a bad outcome: unbelievers have many gifts, but they are shadowed by fear of the end and followed by punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r2.anchor: والدعاء مبني على عدم الاعتداد بالنعمة غير الخالصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r3.claim: The dispute over whether an unbeliever is blessed has little value, so there is no reason to rehearse both sides' apparent proofs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p194/r3.anchor: فالخلاف المفروض بين بعض العلماء في أن الكافر هل هو منعم عليه خلاف لا طائل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r1.claim: All ten readers put ghayr in the genitive; it can modify the favored people or stand as a substitute, with no difference in intended meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r1.anchor: كلمة غير مجرورة باتفاق القراء العشرة ، وهي صفة للذين أنعمت عليهم ، أو بدل منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r2.claim: Adjectival analysis is strongest; substitution by a descriptive word is weaker because a substitute should be the same entity, though al-Zamakhsharī's gloss explains the sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r2.anchor: وإلا فإن جعل { غير المغضوب } صفة للذين هو الوجه وكذلك أعربه سيبويه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r3.claim: Ibn Hishām transmits from Ibn al-Sarrāj and al-Sīrāfī that ghayr can become definite when it negates the single opposite of its noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r3.anchor: هكذا نقل ابن هشام عن ابن السراج والسيرافي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r4.speaker: سيبوبه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r4.claim: Sībawayh explains that ghayr normally remains indefinite because it means different, like mathal, siwā, and ḥasb, but can become definite when permanence is intended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r4.anchor: ونقل عن سيبوبه أن غيرا إنما لم تتعرف لأنها بمعنى المغاير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r5.claim: The accounts converge when ghayr is added to the sole opposite of a description: that fixed contrast defines it, as in this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p195/r5.anchor: وكأن مآل المذهبين واحد لأن غيرا إذا أضيفت إلى ضد موصوفها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r1.claim: The description disavows peoples once guided who later misunderstood or neglected their religion, became complacent, distorted interpretation, or let worldly desires displace observance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r1.anchor: والتبرؤ من أن يكونوا مثلهم في بطر النعمة وسوء الامتثال وفساد التأويل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r2.claim: It also rejects the fate of people who received guidance but failed to preserve their course and became astray through poor understanding of the blessing of knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r2.anchor: فأصبحوا من الضالين بعد الهداية إذ أساءوا صفة العلم بالنعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r3.claim: The groups had apparently not earned divine wrath before Islam because their error was not deliberate; Jews exemplify the first and Christians the second, without exhausting either category.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r3.anchor: واليهود من جملة الفريق الأول ، والنصارى من جملة الفريق الثاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r4.claim: Angered people represent deliberate religious disregard or far-fetched interpretation, while astray people err through poor understanding or inattention; both are blameworthy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r4.anchor: فالمغضوب عليهم جنس للفرق التي تعمدت ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r5.claim: Reports identifying the angered with Jews and the astray with Christians allude to famous examples, not exclusive meanings; asking to avoid both escalates protection from the more severe fate to the lesser.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p196/r5.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى أن في الآية تعريضا بهذين الفريقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r1.claim: Human anger is a psychological aversion that can lead to harsh treatment and sometimes revenge; revenge is not essential to anger, whose intensity varies among people and customs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r1.anchor: وأن الغضب هو كيفية للنفس تعرض من حصول ما لا يلائمها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r2.claim: God cannot literally undergo anger or change; the attribution must mean its effects, such as punishment, humiliation, curse, or exclusion, or function as a representational metaphor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r2.anchor: فقد وجب على المؤمن صرف إسناد الغضب إلى الله عن معناه الحقيقي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r3.claim: Early scholars often left ambiguous attributes uninterpreted to focus on practice; later scholars used sound Arabic interpretations to answer false claims, and Ibn ʿĀshūr regards both approaches as rightly guided.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197/r3.anchor: وكان السلف في القرن الأول ومنتصفف القرن الثاني يمسكون عن تأويل هذه المتشابهات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.claim: Divine anger means God's treatment of those who leave guidance and disobey, culminating in punishment; anger, dislike, pleasure, and love differ from creative will.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r1.anchor: فغضب الله تعالى على العموم يرجع إلى معاملته الحائدين عن هديه العاصين لأوامره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.claim: Ethicists treat the irascible faculty as a root of courage within justice; its balanced form is bravery and magnanimity, while excess and deficiency yield distinct vices.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r2.anchor: فالغضب مبدأ الشجاعة إلا أن الغضب يعبر به عن مبدأ نفساني لأخلاق كثيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.claim: A prophetic report in al-Tirmidhī answers a man's repeated request for advice with the counsel not to become angry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r3.anchor: من جوامع كلم النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم ( أن رجلا قال له أوصني قال : لا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.claim: Anger for oneself is blameworthy, but anger defending public and religious interests is praiseworthy; the Prophet did not get angry for himself but did for God's limits.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p197#2/r4.anchor: ومن الغضب محمود وهو الغضب لحماية المصالح العامة وخصوصا الدينية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r1.speaker: مكي ابن أبي طالب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r1.claim: Makkī b. Abī Ṭālib says the repeated لا prevents readers from connecting those astray to the favored people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية ، قال مكي ابن أبي طالب إن دخول ( لا ) لدفع توهم عطف ( الضالين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr calls that explanation far-fetched: لا simply reinforces the negation already conveyed by ghayr in a normal negative coordination.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r2.anchor: فالحق أن ( لا ) مزيدة لتأكيد النفي المستفاد من لفظ ( غير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r3.speaker: السيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r3.claim: Al-Sayyid says repeating negation prevents the mistaken inference that only the two groups together are excluded, so either one could still be included.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r3.anchor: السيد في ( حواشي الكشاف ) لئلا يتوهم أن المنفي هو المجموع فيجوز ثبوت أحدهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r4.claim: This extra لا is only verbal reinforcement and keeps the meaning negative, unlike the particle in the command to Adam not to prostrate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r4.anchor: وليست زيادة ( لا ) هنا كزيادتها في نحو : { ما منعك أن لا تسجد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r5.claim: Misguidance is mistakenly taking a path other than the intended one, whether consciously or unknowingly; its religious use is metaphorical and ranges from neglecting sunnahs to disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r5.anchor: والضلال سلوك غير الطريق المراد عن خطإ سواء علم بذلك فهو يتطلب الطريق أم لم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r6.claim: Religious misguidance opposes complete faith and can culminate in sealing and veiling; the angered deliberately deviate under worldly desire, while astray groups distort true religions through error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p198/r6.anchor: والضالون جنس للفرق الذين حرفوا الديانات الحق عن عمد وعن سوء فهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r1.claim: The two descriptions form an ellipsis-like pairing: each group shares both traits, but those called astray are less deeply astray than those under severe wrath.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r1.anchor: فحصل شبه الاحتباك وهو أن كلا الفريقين نال حظا من الوصفين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r2.speaker: النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r2.claim: Jews exemplify the angered and Christians the astray; a ḥasan prophetic report in Jāmiʿ al-Tirmidhī supports the examples, not an exclusive interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r2.anchor: والنصارى من جملة الفريق الثاني كما ورد به الحديث عن النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r3.claim: Jews rebelled against prophets and scholars and deliberately altered law; Christians after the Apostles misunderstood Jesus' sanctification and claimed he was literally God's son.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r3.anchor: والنصارى ضلوا بعد الحواريين وأساءوا فهم معنى التقديس في عيسى عليه السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r4.claim: Calling the path straight signals Islam's clear proofs and sound route; juristic effort can still err with reward, and revelation distinguishes internal disagreement from error outside Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p199/r4.anchor: وفي وصف الصراط المسؤول في قوله : { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } بالمستقيم إيماء إلى أن الإسلام واضح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r1.claim: Most readers kasra the pronoun hāʾ after a silent yāʾ to avoid heaviness; this is the dialect of Qays, Tamīm, and Saʿd b. Bakr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r1.anchor: فالجمهور قرأوها بكسر الهاء تخلصا من الثقل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r2.speaker: حمزة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r2.claim: Ḥamza alone uses ḍamma in عليهم وإليهم ولديهم and kasra elsewhere; this reflects Quraysh and Hijazi speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة عليهم وإليهم ولديهم فقط بضم الهاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r3.speaker: يعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb uses ḍamma for every pronoun of this type when the letter before hāʾ is a silent yāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r3.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب كل ضمير من هذا القبيل مما قبل الهاء فيه ياء ساكنة بضم الهاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r4.claim: Most readers leave the plural mīm silent before a following vowel; Ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, and Qālūn in one transmission lengthen its ḍamma.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r4.anchor: فالجمهور قرأوا : { عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم } بسكون الميم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r5.speaker: لبيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r5.claim: Labīd's verse وهمو فوارسها وهم حكامها witnesses the dialect with a lengthened plural mīm; Warsh lengthens it only before hamza, and all readers silence it at pause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p200/r5.anchor:
وعليها قول لبيد :
وهمو فوارسها وهم حكامها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن الزبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r1.claim: ʿUmar and Ibn al-Zubayr read “the path of those whom You favored” as “the path of whom You favored.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r1.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب، وابن الزبير: «صراط من أنعمت عليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r2.claim: Alladhina is the plural of alladhi; its yāʾ is removed in the indefinite form but restored with the article, and its plural may also be declined by some Arabs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r2.anchor: والذين جمع الذي، وأصله «لذ» ، حذفت منه الياء للتنوين كما تحذف من عم، وقاض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وجمهور من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and most exegetes identify those favored as prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and the righteous, citing 4:66–69 to show that this group follows a straight path.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r3.anchor: إنه أراد صراط النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين، وانتزعوا ذلك من قوله تعالى: ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r4.claim: Another statement from Ibn ʿAbbas says the favored are believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: «المنعم عليهم هم المؤمنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r5.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r5.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan identifies the favored as the Companions of Muhammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: «المنعم عليهم أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r6.speaker: فرقة من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r6.claim: A group of exegetes says the favored are the believers among the Children of Israel, citing God's address to Israel in 2:40, 2:47, and 2:122.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r6.anchor: وحكى مكي وغيره عن فرقة من المفسرين أن المنعم عليهم مؤمنو بني إسرائيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also identifies the favored as Moses' followers before they changed their religion; the author says this matches the previous interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r7.anchor:
وقال ابن عباس: «المنعم عليهم أصحاب موسى قبل أن يبدلوا» .
قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا والذي قبله سواء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r8.speaker: قتادة بن دعامة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r8.claim: Qatada ibn Diʿama restricts the favored to prophets.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة بن دعامة: «المنعم عليهم الأنبياء خاصة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r9.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya identifies the favored as Muhammad, Abu Bakr, and ʿUmar; the author calls this stronger because naming the people as the path is figurative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r9.anchor: وحكى مكي عن أبي العالية أنه قال: «المنعم عليهم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r10.claim: If the favored are Muhammad, Abu Bakr, and ʿUmar, their persons metaphorically constitute the path; the author says this interpretation is stronger in meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r10.anchor: وهذا أقوى في المعنى، لأن تسمية أشخاصهم طريقا تجوز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r11.speaker: حمزة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r11.claim: Hamza reads ʿalayhim with ḍamma on hāʾ and a quiescent mīm; he does likewise for ladayhim and ilayhim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75/r11.anchor: فقرأ حمزة «عليهم» بضم الهاء وإسكان الميم، وكذلك لديهم وإليهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r1.claim: Nafiʿ is reported with a choice of ḍamma on the hāʾ and a silent mīm; the author infers that his customary reading was with mīm silent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r1.anchor: فروي عن نافع التخيير بين ضمها وسكونها. وروي عنه أنه كان لا يعيب ضم الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir joins a ḍamma-bearing mīm to a wāw after the hāʾ, whether that hāʾ is pronounced with ḍamma or kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r2.anchor: وكان عبد الله بن كثير يصل الميم بواو انضمت الهاء قبلها أو انكسرت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r3.speaker: ورش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r3.claim: Warsh reads hāʾ with kasra and leaves the mīm unvocalized, except when it precedes an original alif, when he inserts a wāw in pronunciation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ورش الهاء مكسورة والميم موقوفة، إلا أن تلقى الميم ألفا أصلية فيلحق في اللفظ واوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r4.claim: Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim, Ibn ʿAmir, and al-Kisaʾi read the hāʾ with kasra and the mīm silent; before a following consonant, their treatment of hāʾ and mīm vowels differs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r4.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو، وعاصم، وابن عامر، والكسائي، يكسرون، ويسكنون الميم، فإذا لقي الميم حرف ساكن اختلفوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r5.speaker: عاصم وابن كثير ونافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r5.claim: Before a consonant, ʿAsim, Ibn Kathir, and Nafiʿ keep hāʾ kasra and give mīm ḍamma, as in “upon them is humiliation.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r5.anchor: فكان عاصم، وابن كثير، ونافع يمضون على كسر الهاء وضم الميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r6.claim: Abu ʿAmr keeps both hāʾ and mīm with kasra in the same environment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r6.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو يكسر الهاء والميم فيقول: عليهم الذلة وإليهم اثنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r7.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r7.claim: Al-Kisaʾi gives both hāʾ and mīm ḍamma in the same environment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r7.anchor: وكان الكسائي يضم الهاء والميم معا، فيقرأ عليهم الذلة ومن دونهم امرأتين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r8.speaker: أبو بكر أحمد بن موسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r8.claim: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Musa says variation in hāʾ depends on whether it follows kasra or a quiescent yāʾ; elsewhere only ḍamma occurs, while mīm may be silent or have ḍamma in the stated contexts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r8.anchor: وكل هذا الاختلاف في كسر الهاء وضمها إنما هو في الهاء التي قبلها كسرة أو ياء ساكنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r9.speaker: صاحب الدلائل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r9.claim: The Dalāʾil source lists five transmitted combinations of hāʾ and mīm vowels, with or without a lengthened wāw or yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r9.anchor: قرأ بعضهم عليهم وبواو وضمتين، وبعضهم بضمتين وألغى الواو، وبعضهم بكسرتين وألحق الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r10.speaker: ابن جني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r10.claim: Ibn Jinni reports readings with and without a lengthened wāw and with mīm silent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r10.anchor: حكى أحمد بن موسى عليهم وو عليهم بضم الميم من غير إشباع إلى الواو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r11.speaker: الحسن وعمرو بن فائد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r11.claim: Al-Hasan and ʿAmr ibn Faʾid read ʿalayhimi with a final kasra on the mīm.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r12.speaker: الأعرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r12.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads the hāʾ and yāʾ with kasra and mīm with ḍamma, without lengthening the yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p75#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج: «عليهم» بكسر الياء وضم الميم من غير إشباع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r1.claim: Taken together, the source counts ten readings of the hāʾ-and-mīm sequence, in forms with ḍamma or kasra and differing ways of joining the vowel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r1.anchor: وهذه القراءات كلها بضم الهاء إلا الأخيرة وبإزاء كل واحدة منها قراءة بكسر الهاء فيجيء في الجميع عشر قراءات

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r2.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r2.claim: These canonical readers put kasra on the rāʾ of ghayr, while Ibn Kathir reads it with fatḥa and is also reported with kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r2.anchor: فقرأ نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بخفض الراء، وقرأ ابن كثير بالنصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r3.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r3.claim: Abu ʿAli explains jarr as either an appositive for alladhina or an adjective of an indefinite expression, since alladhina here is not used to specify particular people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r3.anchor: الخفض على ضربين: على البدل، من الذين، أو على الصفة للنكرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r4.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r4.claim: Abu ʿAli explains fatḥa as circumstantial (“not in a state of being angered”), exceptional (“except those angered”), or an implied “I mean”; al-Khalil is reported to agree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r4.anchor: والنصب في الراء على ضربين: على الحال كأنك قلت أنعمت عليهم لا مغضوبا عليهم، أو على الاستثناء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r5.claim: The pro-accusative argument is that ghayr is indefinite and cannot describe a definite noun; the author prefers the unambiguous genitive reading transmitted from Ibn Kathir and the canonical readers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r5.anchor: والاختيار الذي لا خفاء به الكسر. وقد روي عن ابن كثير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن السراج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sarraj says ghayr and mithl usually remain indefinite with a definite complement because their meanings allow endlessly many alternatives or likenesses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r6.anchor: وإنما تنكرت غير ومثل مع إضافتهما إلى المعارف من أجل معناهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r7.speaker: أبو بكر بن السراج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r7.claim: In this context ghayr can become definite when it contrasts two known, exclusive alternatives: one favored person either has been angered or has not.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p76/r7.anchor: فمتى كانت غير على هذه الصفة وقصد بها هذا المقصد فهي معرفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r1.claim: Abu Bakr keeps alladhina definite and allows ghayr to describe it because context makes ghayr definite; other grammarians treat alladhina as a common, near-indefinite term and allow an indefinite adjective.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r1.anchor: أبقى أبو بكر الذين على حد التعريف، وجوز نعتها ب غير لما بينه من تعرف غير في هذا الموضع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd identify those angered as Jews and those astray as Christians; ʿAdi ibn Hatim transmits this from the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r2.anchor: والمغضوب عليهم اليهود، والضالون النصارى. وهكذا قال ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، ومجاهد، والسدي، وابن زيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r3.claim: The Qur'an repeatedly associates divine wrath with Jews, including 2:61, 3:112, and 5:60; 2:65 identifies the people turned into apes as Sabbath violators.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r3.anchor: وذلك بين من كتاب الله تعالى، لأن ذكر غضب الله على اليهود متكرر فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r4.claim: God's anger means that he exposes them to trials, punishments, and humiliation, showing their decisive removal from his mercy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r4.anchor: وغضب الله تعالى عبارة عن إظهاره عليهم محنا وعقوبات وذلة ونحو ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r5.claim: Christians who followed their prior law went astray once Muhammad's law arrived; others had already gone astray through their divided claims about Jesus.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r5.anchor: والنصارى كان محققوهم على شرعة قبل ورود شرع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فلما ورد ضلوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r6.claim: The Qur'an says Christians followed desires of people who had previously strayed and misled many in 5:77.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r6.anchor: ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيرا وضلوا عن سواء السبيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r7.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r7.claim: Maki says the negative particle before “those astray” prevents them from being read as directly coordinated with “those whom You favored.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r7.anchor: قال مكي رحمه الله حكاية: دخلت لا في قوله ولا الضالين لئلا يتوهم أن الضالين عطف على الذين.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r8.claim: Some say la is emphatic and means ghayr, “other than.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r9.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r9.claim: Al-Tabari calls la redundant, parallel to a rajaz line and a verse by al-Ahwas.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p77/r9.anchor: وحكى الطبري أن لا زائدة، وقال: هي هنا على نحو ما هي عليه في قول الراجز:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
