IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r1.claim: The author rejects al-Tabari's reading of the al-Ahwas verse as lacking la; the poet means that the speakers wished not to love him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r1.anchor: وبيت الأحوص إنما معناه إرادة أن لا أحبه ف «لا» فيه متمكنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وأبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r2.claim: ʿUmar and Ubay read ghayr before both “those angered” and “those astray,” with reports varying between accusative and genitive on each.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r2.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب وأبي بن كعب: «غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r3.claim: Asked why each group receives a distinct description when Jews and Christians share both attributes, al-Tabari answers that God marks each by its most repeated designation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r3.anchor: فإن قال قائل أليس الضلال من صفة اليهود، كما أن النصارى عليهم غضب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r4.claim: The author finds this answer insufficient: Jewish aggression, defiance, disbelief despite signs, and killing prophets especially warrant wrath, while Christians strayed from the start without these specific acts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r4.anchor: أن أفاعيل اليهود من اعتدائهم، وتعنتهم، وكفرهم مع رؤيتهم الآيات، وقتلهم الأنبياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r5.claim: Calling Christians “astray” does not support Qadarite claims that they made themselves astray: the intransitive phrasing works like “the wall collapsed” or “the tree moved”; God created their error and they acquired it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r5.anchor: وليس في العبارة ب الضالين تعلق للقدرية في أنهم أضلوا أنفسهم لأن هذا إنما هو كقولهم تهدم الجدار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r6.speaker: أيوب السختياني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r6.claim: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani reads al-dallin with a non-lengthened hamza to avoid adjacent quiescent consonants, a dialect also reflected in other Arab forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r6.anchor: وقرأ أيوب السختياني: «الضألين» بهمزة غير ممدودة كأنه فر من التقاء الساكنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r7.speaker: أبو زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r7.claim: Abu Zayd's examples of dābbah and shābbah support the dialectal hamza that Ayyub uses in al-dallin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78/r7.anchor: حكى أبو زيد قال: سمعت عمرو بن عبيد يقرأ: «فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جأن»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78#2/r1.claim: A poetic line gives another dialectal example of the hamza form discussed for al-dallin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78#2/r1.anchor: وللأرض أما سودها فتجللت ... بياضا وأما بيضها فادهأمت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78#2/r2.claim: There is agreement that al-Fatiha has seven verses, counted as al-ʿalamin, al-Rahim, al-Din, nastaʿin, al-mustaqim, anʿamta ʿalayhim, and wa-la al-dallin; the earlier discussion noted anomalous contrary reports.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p78#2/r2.anchor: وأجمع الناس على أن عدد آي سورة الحمد سبع آيات: العالمين آية، الرحيم آية، الدين آية، نستعين آية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra and others report the Prophet instructing worshippers to say amin after the imam recites “those astray”; one who coincides with the angels is forgiven earlier sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r1.anchor: روى أبو هريرة وغيره عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: إذا قال الإمام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r2.speaker: جبريل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r2.claim: A report says Gabriel told the Prophet to say amin after teaching him the opening sura at its revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r2.anchor:
وروي أن جبريل عليه السلام لما علم النبي عليه السلام فاتحة الكتاب وقت نزولها فقرأها قال له:
«قل آمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r3.claim: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib calls amin the seal of the Lord of the worlds that closes a believing servant's supplication.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r3.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: «آمين خاتم رب العالمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r4.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r4.claim: The Prophet says a supplication is assured when sealed, and identifies amin as the seal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r4.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع رجلا يدعو فقال: «أوجب إن ختم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r5.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وثعلب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r5.claim: Most scholars, including al-Hasan and Thaʿlab, interpret amin as “O God, respond” or “Respond, Lord.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r5.anchor: ومعنى «آمين» عند أكثر أهل العلم: اللهم استجب، أو أجب يا رب، ونحو هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r6.speaker: جعفر بن محمد ومجاهد وهلال بن يساف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r6.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, Mujahid, and Hilal ibn Yasaf reportedly say Amin is one of God's names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: «هو اسم من أسماء الله تعالى» ، روي ذلك عن جعفر بن محمد ومجاهد وهلال بن يساف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r7.claim: Another report calls Amin the seal stamped on the books of the people of Paradise who receive them in faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r7.anchor: وقد روي أن «آمين» اسم خاتم يطبع به كتب أهل الجنة التي تؤخذ بالإيمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r8.claim: Given these reports, anyone praying or reciting al-Fatiha outside prayer should end the supplication with amin, but outside prayer it is not said aloud in the manner of formal recitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79/r8.anchor: فمقتضى هذه الآثار أن كل داع ينبغي له في آخر دعائه أن يقول: «آمين» وكذلك كل قارئ للحمد في غير صلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.claim: Every worshipper—leader, solitary, or follower—says amin after reciting or hearing the closing phrase.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r1.anchor: يقولها كل مصل من إمام وفذ ومأموم قرأها أو سمعها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.claim: In the Mudawwana, the imam does not say amin; followers say it quietly, while a solitary worshipper does say it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r2.anchor: وقال مالك في المدونة: «لا يقول الإمام «آمين» ولكن يقولها من خلفه ويخفون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.claim: A report from Malik allows the imam to say amin either silently or aloud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r3.anchor: عن مالك رضي الله عنه: أن الإمام يقولها أسر أم جهر.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.claim: Another report from Malik says the imam does not say amin during audible recitation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r4.anchor: وروي عنه: «الإمام لا يؤمن في الجهر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.speaker: ابن حبيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r5.claim: Ibn Habib says the imam says amin.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.speaker: ابن بكير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r6.claim: Ibn Bukayr says the imam has a choice.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.claim: The disagreement concerns the imam; solitary worshippers and followers are agreed upon apart from Ibn Nafi.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r7.anchor: فهذا الخلاف إنما هو في الإمام، ولم يختلف في الفذ ولا في المأموم إلا ابن نافع.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.speaker: ابن نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.claim: A follower says amin only if he hears the imam reach walā al-ḍāllīn; if too far away to hear, he omits it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r8.anchor: «لا يقولها المأموم إلا إن سمع الإمام يقول ولا الضالين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.speaker: ابن عبدوس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abdus advises estimating the length of the recitation and then saying amin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عبدوس: «يتحرى قدر القراءة ويقول آمين»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r10.claim: Amin is indeclinable with fatḥa because two vowelless letters meet; fatḥa with yā is the lightest pronunciation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r10.anchor: وهي لفظة مبنية على الفتح لالتقاء الساكنين، وكأن الفتح مع الياء أخف من سائر الحركات،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.claim: Some Arabs lengthen amin; the cited verse uses the long form and repeats it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r11.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول «آمين» فيمده، ومنه قول الشاعر:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.speaker: جبير بن الأضبط
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.claim: Some Arabs shorten amin, as illustrated by Jubayr ibn al-Adbat's verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r12.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول «أمين» بالقصر، ومنه قول الشاعر: [جبير بن الأضبط]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r13.claim: Reports explain the Prophet's promise about matching the angels as agreement in response, sincerity, or timing; Ibn Atiyya prefers matching the time with sincere, attentive supplication, after which the response follows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p79#2/r13.anchor: والذي يترجح أن المعنى فمن وافق في الوقت مع خلوص النية، والإقبال على الرغبة إلى الله تعالى بقلب سليم،

AKHFASH:v1p16/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p16/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p16/r3.claim: Ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim is accusative as an appositive to al-ṣirāṭ.

AKHFASH:v1p16/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p16/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p16/r4.claim: The alif in anʿamta is hamzat qaṭʿ because its imperfect is yanʿimu, with a ḍamma on the yāʾ.

AKHFASH:v1p16/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p16/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p16/r5.claim: Ghayr al-maghḍūbi can be an adjective for those blessed, though ghayr and mithl are ordinarily used with indefinites and can modify definite forms that carry an indefinite sense.
AKHFASH:v1p16/r5.anchor: قد احتيج اليهما في هذا الموضع فأجريتا صفة لما فيه الالف واللام

AKHFASH:v1p16/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p16/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p16/r6.claim: Apposition is better than the adjective analysis because alladhī and alladhīna remain definite; he argues that rajul mithluka is generic, while Zayd mithluka only works as apposition.
AKHFASH:v1p16/r6.anchor: أجود من الصفة، لان "الذي" و "الذين" لا تفارقهما الالف واللام

AKHFASH:v1p16/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p16/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p16/r7.claim: Ṣirāṭ has both sīn and ṣād forms; al-Akhfash prefers ṣād because that is how it is written throughout the Qurʾān.
AKHFASH:v1p16/r7.anchor: الا انا نختار الصاد لان كتابها على ذلك في جميع القرآن

AKHFASH:v1p16/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p16/r8.speaker: العرب
AKHFASH:v1p16/r8.claim: Arab usage can put al-jammāʾ al-ghafīr in the accusative despite its article, treating it like an indefinite expression.
AKHFASH:v1p16/r8.anchor: وقد قال العرب "هم فيها الجماء الغفير" فنصبوا

AKHFASH:v1p17/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p17/r1.speaker: قوم
AKHFASH:v1p17/r1.claim: Some readers construe ghayr al-maghḍūbi as an exception outside the initial statement.
AKHFASH:v1p17/r1.anchor: وقد قرأ قوم {غير المغضوب عليهم} جعلوه على الاستثناء

AKHFASH:v1p17/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p17/r2.speaker: أهل الحجاز
AKHFASH:v1p17/r2.claim: In the Hijaz dialect, an exception outside the initial statement after negation is accusative, as in mā fīhā aḥadun illā ḥimāran.
AKHFASH:v1p17/r2.anchor: في لغة أهل الحجاز فانه ينصب

AKHFASH:v1p17/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p17/r3.speaker: غيرهم
AKHFASH:v1p17/r3.claim: Other Arabs treat the exception as part of the initial statement and put it in the nominative.
AKHFASH:v1p17/r3.anchor: وغيرهم يقول: "هذا بمنزلة ما هو من الأول" فيرفع

AKHFASH:v1p17/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p17/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p17/r4.claim: A genitive form is explained by analogy to alladhī bi-l-rajul; al-Akhfash finds the adjective analysis weak and apposition better, as in the naṣiya example.
AKHFASH:v1p17/r4.anchor: وليس هو على الصفة بحسن ولكن على البدل

AKHFASH:v1p17/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p17/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p17/r5.claim: Ghayr may alternatively be accusative as a circumstantial expression because it is indefinite while its antecedent is definite.
AKHFASH:v1p17/r5.anchor: نصبا على الحال لانها نكرة والأول معرفة

AKHFASH:v1p17/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p17/r7.speaker: أهل الحجاز
AKHFASH:v1p17/r7.claim: The Hijaz dialect feminizes ṣirāṭ like al-ṭarīq, al-zuqāq, al-sabīl, al-sūq, and al-kalāʾ; Tamīm uses masculine forms, while Asad feminizes al-hudā.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies those favored by God as the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس هم النبيون والصديقون والشهداء والصالحون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r2.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r2.claim: Most readers pronounce the pronoun in ʿalayhim with kasra, as in ladayhim and ilayhim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأكثرون عليهم بكسر الهاء وكذلك لديهم و إليهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r3.speaker: حمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r3.claim: Ḥamza reads those pronouns with ḍamma on hāʾ; Ibn Kathīr joins the ḍamma of mīm with a following wāw.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r3.anchor: وقرأهن حمزة بضمها وكان ابن كثير يصل ضم الميم بواو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says grammarians record ten forms of ʿalayhim: six attested among reciters, with varying hāʾ/mīm vowels and added yāʾ or wāw, and four transmitted from Arabs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري حكى اللغويون في عليهم عشر لغات قرئ بعامتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r5.speaker: عدي بن حاتم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r5.claim: A report from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, from the Prophet, identifies the objects of anger as Jews and the astray as Christians.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r5.anchor: فهم اليهود والضالون النصارى رواه عدي بن حاتم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines ḍalāl as bewilderment and turning away from what is true.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r6.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة والضلال الحيرة والعدول عن الحق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r7.speaker: أبو الحسن علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r7.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn ʿUbayd Allāh says it is Sunnah for a Fātiḥa reader to follow it with āmīn, whether inside or outside prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r7.anchor: ومن السنة في حق قارىء الفاتحة ان يعقبها ب آمين قال شيخنا أبو الحسن علي ابن عبيد الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r8.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra, from the Prophet, says that when the congregation says āmīn after the imām, matching the angels, prior sins are forgiven.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r9.speaker: ابن الأنباري عن ابن عباس والحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r9.claim: One explanation makes āmīn mean “so be it,” as Ibn al-Anbārī relates from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r9.anchor: أحدها أن معنى آمين كذلك يكون حكاه ابن الأنباري عن ابن عباس والحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r10.speaker: الحسن والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r10.claim: A second explanation understands āmīn as “O God, answer,” held by al-Ḥasan and al-Zajjāj.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r10.anchor: والثاني أنها بمعنى اللهم استجب قاله الحسن والزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r11.speaker: مجاهد وهلال بن يساف وجعفر بن محمد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r11.claim: A third view treats āmīn as one of God's names, held by Mujāhid, Hilāl ibn Yasāf, and Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r11.anchor: والثالث أنه اسم من أسماء الله تعالى قاله مجاهد وهلال بن يساف وجعفر ابن محمد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r12.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r12.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains it as “O trustworthy one, answer our prayer,” with the vocative yāʾ omitted as in “Yūsuf, turn away from this” (12:29).
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r12.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة معناها يا أمين أجب دعاءنا فسقطت يا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r13.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r13.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī rejects the vocative analysis as grammatically wrong: a singular vocative after yāʾ should be nominative, but Arabs consistently give āmīn fatḥa on nūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r13.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري وهذا القول خطأ عند جميع النحويين لأنه إذا أدخل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r14.claim: The nūn is open in both pronunciations; āmīn has a short-vowel form amīn and a long-vowel form āmīn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p15/r14.anchor: وفي آمين لغتان أمين بالقصر وآمين بالمد والنون فيهما مفتوحة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r1.speaker: أبو العباس عن ابن الأعرابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r1.claim: A verse transmitted by Abū al-ʿAbbās from Ibn al-Aʿrābī uses āmīn in a prayer asking rain for a people and protection for a caravan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r1.anchor: أنشدنا أبو العباس عن ابن الاعرابي سقى الله حيا بين صارة والحمى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r2.speaker: أبو العباس عن ابن الأعرابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r2.claim: Another verse transmitted through Abū al-ʿAbbās has a speaker say āmīn after praying for distance from Faṭḥal and his mother’s son.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r2.anchor: وأنشدنا أبو العباس أيضا تباعد مني فطحل وابن أمه أمين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r3.speaker: أبو العباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r3.claim: A third poetic citation uses āmīn in a supplication that God never deprive the speaker of his beloved and have mercy on one who says āmīnā.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r3.anchor: وأنشدنا أبو العباس أيضا يا رب لا تسلبني حبها أبدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r4.speaker: أبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r4.claim: The author's father transmits a verse beginning āmīn and praying that harm strike the extremities of the one who gave a gift.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r4.anchor: وأنشدني أبي أمين ومن اعطاك مني هوداة رمى الله في أطرافه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r5.speaker: أبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r5.claim: A final verse transmitted by the author's father uses āmīn twice to close two lines about love and grief.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r5.anchor: وأنشدني أبي فقلت له قد هجت لي بارح الهوى أصاب حمام الموت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r6.speaker: الأكثرون عن أحمد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r6.claim: Most transmit from Aḥmad that al-Fātiḥa is required for a valid prayer, so one able to recite it who omits it has no valid prayer; this is Mālik's and al-Shāfiʿī's position.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r6.anchor: نقل الأكثرون عن أحمد أن الفاتحه شرط في صحة الصلاة فمن تركها مع القدرة عليها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة ورواية عن أحمد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r7.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says al-Fātiḥa is not specifically required, a position also reported from Aḥmad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا تتعين وهي رواية عن أحمد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r8.claim: The first position is supported by the Ṣaḥīḥayn report from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit: the Prophet said there is no prayer for one who does not recite the Opening of the Book.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p17/r8.anchor: ويدل على الرواية الأولى ما روي في الصحيحين من حديث عبادة بن الصامت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.speaker: الله تعالى
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.claim: In a divine report, God divides the prayer between Himself and His servant, responds to each recited section, calls 1:5 shared between them, and grants the servant's request.
IBNKATHIR:1:5/r11.anchor: قال : هذا بيني وبين عبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r1.claim: “Path of those You favored” explains the straight path; grammatically it may be apposition or explanatory apposition.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r1.anchor: مفسر للصراط المستقيم .   وهو بدل منه عند النحاة ،   ويجوز أن يكون عطف بيان

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r2.claim: The favored people are the four groups named in 4:69: prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and the righteous.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r2.anchor: هم المذكورون في سورة النساء ،   حيث قال :

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r3.claim: In al-Dahhak's report, the favored path is obedience and worship, including angels, prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous; Ibn Kathir calls this the broadest account.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r3.anchor: وقال الضحاك ،   عن ابن عباس : صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بطاعتك وعبادتك ،   من ملائكتك ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r4.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, through Abu Jaʿfar, identifies those favored as the prophets.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r4.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر ،   عن الربيع بن أنس : { صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم } قال : هم النبيون .

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, through Ibn Jurayj, and Mujahid identify the favored people as believers.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جريج ،   عن ابن عباس : هم المؤمنون .   وكذا قال مجاهد .

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r6.speaker: وكيع
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r6.claim: Wakiʿ identifies those favored as Muslims.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r6.anchor: وقال وَكِيع : هم المسلمون .   وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam identifies them as the Prophet and those with him.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم : هم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن معه .

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the earlier Ibn ʿAbbas account because it is broader and more comprehensive.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r8.anchor: والتفسير المتقدم ،   عن ابن عباس أعم ،   وأشمل ،   والله أعلم .

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r9.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r9.claim: The majority read ghayr in the genitive as an adjective modifying the path.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r9.anchor: قرأ الجمهور :  " غير "  بالجر على النعت ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports an accusative circumstantial reading of ghayr, attributed to the Prophet and ʿUmar and also transmitted from Ibn Kathir; its circumstantial referent is the pronoun in ʿalayhim.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r10.anchor: قال الزمخشري : وقرئ بالنصب على الحال ،   وهي قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعمر بن الخطاب ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r11.claim: The favored path belongs to people of guidance, uprightness, obedience to God and His messengers, and compliance with commands and prohibitions.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r11.anchor: وهم أهل الهداية والاستقامة والطاعة لله ورسله ،   وامتثال أوامره وترك نواهيه وزواجره ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r12.claim: Those subject to anger know the truth but turn away; the astray lack knowledge and wander without reaching the truth.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r12.anchor: الذين فسدت إرادتهم ،   فعلموا الحق وعدلوا عنه ،   ولا صراط الضالين وهم الذين فقدوا العلم

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r13.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r13.claim: The added negation marks two distinct corrupt routes, those of the Jews and Christians.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r13.anchor: وأكد الكلام بلا ليدل على أن ثَمّ مسلكين فاسدين ،   وهما طريقتا اليهود والنصارى .

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r14.speaker: بعض النحاة
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r14.claim: Some grammarians take ghayr as an exception, making it a disconnected exception because the angered are outside the favored group; Ibn Kathir says his own account is better.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r14.anchor: وقد زعم بعض النحاة أن { غير } هاهنا استثنائية ،   فيكون على هذا منقطعا

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r15.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r15.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers construing ghayr as “the path other than that of the angered,” with the omitted noun supplied by context.

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r16.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r16.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r16.claim: The Nabigha al-Dhubyani line illustrates omitting the described noun and retaining its adjective; here “path” is omitted before “other than the angered.”
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r16.anchor: وهكذا ،   { غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ } أي : غير صراط المغضوب عليهم .

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r17.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r17.speaker: بعض النحاة
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r17.claim: Some grammarians call la before the astray redundant and cite an al-ʿAjjaj line; Ibn Kathir rejects this and treats it as reinforcing the negation.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r17.anchor: ومنهم من زعم أن( لا ) في قوله : { ولا الضالين } زائدة ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r18.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r18.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r18.claim: ʿUmar read “and other than the astray”; Ibn Kathir says this report has a sound chain and treats it as explanatory, supporting emphatic negation and separation of the two paths.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r18.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب ،   رضي الله عنه : أنه كان يقرأ :  " غَيْرِ المَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَغَيْر الضَّالّين "  .   وهذا إسناد صحيح

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r19.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r19.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r19.claim: A similar reading is attributed to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb; Ibn Kathir understands it as explanatory rather than as the verse's wording.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r19.anchor: [ وكذا حكي عن أبي بن كعب أنه قرأ كذلك ]{[964]} وهو محمول على أنه صدر منه على وجه التفسير

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r20.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r20.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r20.claim: Jews are characterized by abandoning known truth and thus anger, while Christians seek a goal without knowledge of its way because they do not follow the true Messenger; each group is also both astray and under anger.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r20.anchor: فإن طريقة أهل الإيمان مشتملة على العلم بالحق والعمل به ،   واليهود فقدوا العمل ،   والنصارى فقدوا العلم

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r21.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r21.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r21.claim: The Qurʾan calls the Jews recipients of anger and specifically describes Christians as astray, supporting the verse's characteristic labels.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r21.anchor: وأخص أوصاف النصارى الضلال [ كما قال : { قَدْ ضَلُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ وَأَضَلُّوا كَثِيرًا

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r22.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r22.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r22.claim: Qurʾanic references to Jewish anger and wrongdoing support the identification: Israel's children incur anger for rejecting revelation and are condemned for sin and failure to stop wrongdoing.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r22.anchor: بئسما اشتروا به أنفسهم أن يكفروا بما أنزل الله بغيا أن ينزل الله من فضله

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r23.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r23.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r23.claim: In the report from ʿAdi ibn Hatim, the Prophet identifies the angered as Jews and the astray as Christians; al-Tirmidhi grades this route hasan gharīb, and Ibn Kathir notes other routes and wordings.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r23.anchor: وقال : «المغضوب{[974]} عليهم اليهود ،   وإن الضالين النصارى »{[975]} .   وذكر الحديث ،   ورواه الترمذي ،   من حديث سماك بن حرب

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r24.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r24.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r24.claim: At Wadi al-Qura the Prophet points to Jews as the angered and Christians as the astray; other transmitters send the report without naming the eyewitness, while ʿUrwa's route names Ibn ʿUmar.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r24.anchor: قال : «المغضوب عليهم - وأشار إلى اليهود - والضالون هم النصارى »{[978]} .

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r25.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r25.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r25.claim: A report from Abu Dharr gives the same Prophetic explanation; Ibn Hajar calls Ibn Mardawayh's chain hasan.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r25.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال : سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن المغضوب عليهم قال : «اليهود » ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r26.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r26.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r26.claim: Al-Suddi, transmitting from Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Masʿud, and Companions of the Prophet, identifies the Jews as angered and Christians as astray.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r26.anchor: وقال السُّدِّي ،   عن أبي مالك ،   وعن أبي صالح ،   عن ابن عباس ،   وعن مرة الهمداني ،   عن ابن مسعود ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r27.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r27.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r27.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, through al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj, gives the same identification; al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, and others agree, and Ibn Abi Hatim reports no disagreement among exegetes.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r27.anchor: وقال الضحاك ،   وابن جُرَيْج ،   عن ابن عباس : { غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ } اليهود ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r28.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r28.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r28.claim: A report about Zayd ibn ʿAmr says he refused Jewish or Christian conversion because each demanded a share in divine anger, remained on his natural disposition and avoided idols, while his companions became Christians; Waraqa later accepted the Prophet's revelation.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r28.anchor: عن زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل ؛ أنه لما خرج هو وجماعة من أصحابه إلى الشام يطلبون الدين الحنيف ،   قالت له اليهود :

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r29.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r29.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r29.claim: Scholars may excuse confusing dād and ẓāʾ because their articulation points are close and both are voiced, fricative, and emphatic; the saying “I am the most eloquent to pronounce dād” has no basis.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r29.anchor: والصحيح من مذاهب العلماء أنه يغتفر الإخلال بتحرير ما بين الضاد والظاء لقرب مخرجيهما ؛

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r30.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r30.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r30.claim: The surah praises and magnifies God through His names and attributes, recalls the afterlife, teaches supplication, disavowal of human power, sincere worship and divine oneness, and asks for guidance and steadfastness on the upright religion.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r30.anchor: اشتملت هذه السورة الكريمة وهي سبع آيات ،   على حمد الله وتمجيده والثناء عليه ،   بذكر أسمائه الحسنى

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r31.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r31.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r31.claim: The requested straight path leads to crossing the eschatological bridge and reaching Paradise with prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous; the surah urges good deeds and warns against false paths.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r31.anchor: وإلى سؤالهم إياه الهداية إلى الصراط المستقيم ،   وهو الدين القويم ،   وتثبيتهم عليه حتى يُفضي بهم ذلك إلى جواز الصراط الحسي

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r32.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r32.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r32.claim: The verse attributes favor directly to God, leaves the agent of anger unexpressed although God is its true agent, and assigns misguidance to those who embody it although He misleads by His decree; cited verses affirm His exclusive control of guidance and misguidance.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r32.anchor: وما أحسن ما جاء إسناد الإنعام إليه في قوله تعالى : { صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r33.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r33.speaker: الفرقة القدرية
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r33.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the Qadari claim that servants independently choose and cause guidance or misguidance: clear verses make God alone their controller, while innovators follow ambiguous passages and leave clear evidence.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r33.anchor: لا كما تقوله الفرقة القدرية ومن حذا حذوهم ،   من أن العباد هم الذين يختارون ذلك ويفعلونه{[3]} ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r34.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r34.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r34.claim: The Prophet warns that people who follow ambiguous verses are those named by God as having deviation in their hearts; Ibn Kathir says the Qurʾan gives no valid proof for innovation, since it has no contradiction and distinguishes guidance from error.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r34.anchor: وقد ورد في الحديث الصحيح : «إذا رأيتم الذين يتبعون ما تشابه منه ،   فأولئك الذين سمى الله فاحذروهم »{[5]} .

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r35.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r35.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r35.claim: It is recommended to say amin after al-Fatiha, pronounced either with a long or short first vowel; it means “O God, answer.” A report from Waʾil says the Prophet lengthened it, and al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r35.anchor: يستحب لمن قرأ الفاتحة أن يقول بعدها : آمين [ مثل : يس ]{[7]} ،   ويقال : أمين

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r36.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r36.speaker: وائل بن حجر
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r36.claim: Waʾil ibn Hujr reports hearing the Prophet say amin aloud after al-Fatiha; al-Tirmidhi grades the hadith hasan, and reports also come from ʿAli and Ibn Masʿud.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r36.anchor: عن وائل بن حجر ،   قال : سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ : { غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا الضَّالِّينَ } فقال :  " آمين "

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r37.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r37.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r37.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet said amin loudly enough for the first row to hear; Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah add that the mosque resounded, and al-Daraqutni calls the chain hasan.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r37.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة ،   قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا تلا { غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا الضَّالِّينَ } قال :  " آمين "  حتى يسمع من يليه من الصف الأول

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r38.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r38.speaker: بلال
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r38.claim: Bilal asked the Prophet not to say amin before him.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r38.anchor: وعن بلال أنه قال : يا رسول الله ،   لا تسبقني بآمين .   رواه أبو داود

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r39.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r39.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r39.claim: Al-Hasan and Jaʿfar al-Sadiq are reported to pronounce amin with a doubled mīm, like the Qurʾanic word in 5:2.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r39.anchor: ونقل أبو نصر القشيري{[15]} عن الحسن وجعفر الصادق أنهما شددا الميم من آمين مثل :

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r40.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r40.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r40.claim: Saying amin is recommended outside prayer and especially within it, whether alone, imam, or follower; the sound reports promise forgiveness when one's amin coincides with the angels'.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r40.anchor: قال أصحابنا وغيرهم : ويستحب ذلك لمن هو خارج الصلاة ،   ويتأكد في حق المصلي ،   وسواء كان منفردًا أو إمامًا أو مأمومًا

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r41.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r41.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r41.claim: In the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections, the Prophet says that when the imam says amin, worshippers should say it; agreement with the angels' amin brings forgiveness of prior sins.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r41.anchor: إذا أمن الإمام فأمنوا ،   فإنه من وافق تأمينه تأمين الملائكة ،   غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r42.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r42.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r42.claim: The matching between a worshipper's amin and the angels' may mean matching in time, in the response received, or in sincerity.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r42.anchor: قيل : بمعنى من وافق تأمينه تأمين الملائكة في الزمان ،   وقيل : في الإجابة ،   وقيل : في صفة الإخلاص

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r43.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r43.speaker: أبو موسى
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r43.claim: A Prophetic report in Muslim says that when the imam recites “nor the astray,” worshippers should say amin and God will answer them.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r43.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي موسى مرفوعا : «إذا{[19]} قال ،   يعني الإمام : { ولا الضالين } ،   فقولوا : آمين .   يجبكم الله

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r44.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r44.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r44.claim: A report through Juwaybir and al-Dahhak explains amin as “Lord, do”; al-Jawhari says “so let it be,” al-Tirmidhi says it means do not disappoint our hope, and most interpreters say “O God, answer us.”
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r44.anchor: وقال جُوَيبر ،   عن الضحاك ،   عن ابن عباس ،   قال : قلت : يا رسول الله ،   ما معنى آمين ؟ قال : «رب افعل »

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r45.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r45.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r45.claim: Mujahid, Jaʿfar al-Sadiq, and Hilal ibn Kaysan are reported to call amin one of God's names, but Ibn al-ʿArabi says the Prophetic report from Ibn ʿAbbas for this is unsound.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r45.anchor: وحكى القرطبي عن مجاهد وجعفر الصادق وهلال بن كيسان : أن آمين اسم من أسماء الله تعالى وروي عن ابن عباس مرفوعا ولا يصح

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r46.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r46.speaker: أصحاب مالك
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r46.claim: Malik's companions say the imam does not say amin but the follower does, citing Abu Hurayra's report that followers should say it when the imam reaches “nor the astray”; Ibn Kathir counters with reports that the Prophet himself said amin.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r46.anchor: وقال أصحاب مالك : لا يؤمن الإمام ويؤمن المأموم ،   لما رواه مالك عن سُمَيّ ،   عن أبي صالح ،   عن أبي هريرة

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r47.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r47.speaker: القول الجديد
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r47.claim: The new Shafiʿi position, also held by Abu Hanifa and one Maliki report, is that a follower does not say amin aloud when the imam does; it is a remembrance like other prayer remembrances.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r47.anchor: وحاصل الخلاف أن الإمام إن نسي التأمين جهر المأموم به قولا واحدًا ،   وإن أمَّن الإمام جهرًا فالجديد أنه لا يجهر المأموم

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r48.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r48.speaker: القول القديم
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r48.claim: The old Shafiʿi position, held by Ahmad and another Maliki report, is that the follower says amin aloud, based on the report that the mosque echoed with it.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r48.anchor: والقديم أنه يجهر به ،   وهو مذهب الإمام أحمد بن حنبل ،   والرواية الأخرى عن مالك

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r49.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r49.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r49.claim: A third position has the follower say amin quietly in a small mosque, where the imam can be heard, and aloud in a large mosque so it reaches its far sides.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r49.anchor: ولنا قول آخر ثالث : أنه إن كان المسجد صغيرًا لم يجهر المأموم{[26]} ،   لأنهم يسمعون قراءة الإمام ،

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r50.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r50.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r50.claim: A report from ʿAisha says Jews envy Muslims for Friday, the qibla, and saying amin behind the imam; Ibn Majah's wording adds greeting and amin.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r50.anchor: عن عائشة ،   رضي الله عنها ،   أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكرت عنده اليهود ،   فقال :  " إنهم لن يحسدونا

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r51.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r51.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r51.claim: A report urges frequent amin because Jews envy Muslims for it; Ibn Kathir notes its chain contains the weak Talha ibn ʿAmr.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r51.anchor: وله عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال :  " ما حسدتكم اليهود على شيء ما حسدتكم على قول : آمين

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r52.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r52.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r52.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits from Abu Hurayra a Prophetic report calling amin the Lord of the worlds' seal upon His believing servants.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r52.anchor: وروى ابن مَرْدُويه ،   عن أبي هريرة : أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : «آمين : خاتم رب العالمين على عباده المؤمنين »

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r53.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r53.speaker: أنس
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r53.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet was given amin in prayer and supplication; only Moses had it earlier, with Harun saying amin to Moses' prayer, so supplications should end with amin for acceptance.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r53.anchor: وعن أنس ،   قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «أعطيت آمين في الصلاة وعند الدعاء ،   لم يعط أحد قبلي إلا أن يكون موسى

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r54.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r54.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r54.claim: The account of Moses' prayer and the dual reply that “your two prayers” were answered implies that Harun said amin; this makes the person who says amin to a prayer like one who prayed it.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r54.anchor: فذكر الدعاء عن موسى وحده ،   ومن سياق الكلام ما يدل على أن هارون أمَّن ،   فنزل منزلة من دعا ،   لقوله تعالى :

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r55.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r55.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r55.claim: Some use this reasoning to argue that the follower need not recite aloud behind the imam because amin after al-Fatiha counts as recitation; they cite “whoever has an imam, the imam's recitation is his recitation” and Bilal's request not to be preceded in amin.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r55.anchor: فدل هذا المنزع على أن المأموم لا قراءة عليه في الجهرية ،   والله أعلم .

IBNKATHIR:1:7/r56.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r56.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r56.claim: A report through Kaʿb says that when the imam says amin and the amins of earth and heaven coincide, God forgives the worshipper; one who omits amin is compared to a warrior whose lot was not drawn.
IBNKATHIR:1:7/r56.anchor: عن كعب ،   عن أبي هريرة ،   قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا قال الإمام : { غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلا الضَّالِّينَ } فقال : آمين ،

FARRA:v1p4/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p4/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p4/r1.claim: The two pronunciations of the pronoun in ʿalayhim are both Arabic dialects.
FARRA:v1p4/r1.anchor:
معنى «ما» .
(عليهم) و (عليهم) وهما لغتان لكل لغة مذهب في العربية.

FARRA:v1p4/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p4/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p4/r2.claim: With ḍamma on the hāʾ, its original vowel is retained across nominative, accusative, and genitive forms.
FARRA:v1p4/r2.anchor: فأما من رفع الهاء فإنه يقول: أصلها رفع في نصبها وخفضها ورفعها

FARRA:v1p4/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p4/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p4/r3.claim: With kasra on the hāʾ, speakers ease the ḍamma after a silent yāʾ; the same two options occur after a preceding kasra, as in bihim.
FARRA:v1p4/r3.anchor:
استثقل الضمة في الهاء وقبلها ياء ساكنة، فقال:
«عليهم» لكثرة دور المكنى في الكلام.

FARRA:v1p4/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p4/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p4/r4.claim: After a yāʾ that has become a pronounced alif because its preceding vowel is fatḥa, the pronoun takes only ḍamma.
FARRA:v1p4/r4.anchor: فإذا انفتح ما قبل الياء فصارت ألفا في اللفظ لم يجز في «هم» إلا الرفع

FARRA:v1p7/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p7/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p7/r1.claim: Genitive ghayri is an adjective of alladhīna, not of the pronoun in ʿalayhim; its definite annexation permits this description because neither expression denotes a specified person.
FARRA:v1p7/r1.anchor: بخفض «غير» لأنها نعت للذين، لا للهاء والميم من «عليهم» . وإنما جاز أن تكون «غير» نعتا لمعرفة لأنها قد أضيفت إلى اسم فيه ألف ولام،

FARRA:v1p7/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p7/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p7/r2.claim: Ghayri can be accusative as a detached description of ʿalayhim, or genitive after repeating ṣirāṭ as “the path of those other than …”.
FARRA:v1p7/r2.anchor: «غير» ، تجعله قطعا من «عليهم» . وقد يجوز أن تجعل «الذين» قبلها في موضع توقيت، وتخفض «غير» على التكرير:

FARRA:v1p7/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p7/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p7/r3.claim: In wa-lā al-ḍāllīn, ghayr means lā, so lā is repeated; if ghayr meant “other than,” repeating lā would be ungrammatical.
FARRA:v1p7/r3.anchor: مجمل فإذا كانت «غير» بمعنى سوى لم يجز أن تكر عليها «لا»

FARRA:v1p7/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p7/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p7/r4.claim: Farra rejects the claim that ghayr in al-ḥamd means “other than” and lā is extra; extra lā requires a preceding negation.
FARRA:v1p7/r4.anchor: وقد قال بعض من لا يعرف العربية: إن معنى «غير» في «الحمد» معنى «سوى» ، وإن «لا» صلة في الكلام،

FARRA:v1p7/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p7/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p7/r5.claim: The verse “in a well without ḥawr” does not prove an extra lā: here lā is a true negation, while poetry allows an extra lā after an earlier negation.
FARRA:v1p7/r5.anchor: وهذا [غير] جائز لأن المعنى وقع على ما لا يتبين فيه عمله، فهو جحد محض.

FARRA:v1p7/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p7/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p7/r6.claim: In the cited phrase “a well that returns nothing,” ḥāra means that the action leaves no perceptible trace, like grinding that produces no result.
FARRA:v1p7/r6.anchor: أراد في: بئر ماء لا يحير عليه شيئا كأنك قلت: إلى غير رشد توجه وما درى.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r1.claim: Those granted favor on the straight path are the prophets and believers.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r1.anchor:
{صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} يعني الأنبياء والمؤمنين.
و {المغضوب عليهم} اليهود.
و

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r2.claim: Those under wrath are the Jews.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r2.anchor:
{صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} يعني الأنبياء والمؤمنين.
و {المغضوب عليهم} اليهود.
و

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r3.claim: Those who are astray are the Christians.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p38#5/r3.anchor:
أنعمت عليهم} يعني الأنبياء والمؤمنين.
و {المغضوب عليهم} اليهود.
و (الضالون) النصارى.

JISHUMI:v1p215/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p215/r3.speaker: حمزة
JISHUMI:v1p215/r3.claim: Ḥamza reads the hāʾ in ʿalayhim, ilayhim, and ladayhim with ḍamma throughout the Qur’an.
JISHUMI:v1p215/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة: (عليهم) و(إليهم) و(لديهم) بضم الهاء

JISHUMI:v1p215/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p215/r4.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v1p215/r4.claim: Yaʿqūb gives ḍamma to each hāʾ preceded by a vowelless yāʾ, including forms such as ʿalayhim and fīhim, and reportedly also where that yāʾ drops.
JISHUMI:v1p215/r4.anchor: وعن يعقوب ضم كل هاء قبلها ياء ساكنة، ك (عليهم)، و(إليهم)، و(فيهم)

JISHUMI:v1p215/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p215/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p215/r5.claim: Readers vary between kasra and ḍamma on the hāʾ, and between a vowelless, kasra, or ḍamma mīm of the plural, especially before a following hamzat al-waṣl; the author lists each school’s distributions.
JISHUMI:v1p215/r5.anchor: فأما من ضم الهاء، فلأنه يردها إلى الأصل، لأنك تقول: أعطيتموه

JISHUMI:v1p215/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p215/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p215/r6.claim: Ḍamma on hāʾ restores its underlying form; kasra is influenced by the preceding yāʾ, avoiding a heavy shift from ḍamma beside yāʾ, while ḍamma on mīm restores its base and appended wāw lengthens it.
JISHUMI:v1p215/r6.anchor: ومن كسرها فلأجل الياء الساكنة. ومن كسر الهاء وجزم الميم

JISHUMI:v1p215/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p215/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p215/r7.claim: Inʿām, iḥsān, and ifḍāl are near-synonyms, though one may act beneficently toward oneself but cannot bless oneself; niʿma derives from softness and denotes good intended benefit.
JISHUMI:v1p215/r7.anchor: الإنعام والإحسان والإفضال نظائر، وبين الإنعام والإحسان فرق

JISHUMI:v1p215/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p215/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p215/r8.claim: God blesses both believers and unbelievers; His first favor to a servant is creating that person alive for benefit.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r1.claim: The phrase is an explanatory substitute for the straight path and virtually repeats the verb, emphasizing and identifying the straight way with the Muslims' way.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r1.anchor: بدل من الصراط المستقيم وهو في حكم تكرير العامل كأنه قيل اهدنا الصراط المستقيم اهدنا صراط الذين انعمت عليهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r2.claim: The repeated, first-general-then-specific description makes the believers a clear, emphatic example of those who possess the praised qualities.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r2.anchor: فائدته التوكيد لما فيه من التثنية والتكرير والإشعار بأن الطريق المستقيم بيانه وتفسيره صراط المسلمين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r3.claim: Those blessed are believers, and the wording leaves blessing general because Islam gathers every blessing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r3.anchor: والذين انعمت عليهم هم المؤمنون وأطلق الإنعام ليشمل كل إنعام لأن من أنعم عليه بنعمة الاسلام لم تبق نعمة الا أصابته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those blessed as Moses's companions before they changed their religion; another view identifies them as prophets.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس هم أصحاب موسى قبل ان يغيروا وقيل هم الأنبياء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud reads the phrase as the path of those whom You blessed, using a relative pronoun instead of alladhina.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ( صراط من انعمت عليهم )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r1.claim: Ghayr al-maghḍūb may substitute for those blessed, describing them as safe from anger and error, or qualify them as combining faith with safety from both.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r1.anchor: بدل من الذين أنعمت عليهم على معنى ان المنعم عليهم هم الذين سلموا من غضب الله والضلال أو صفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r2.claim: Ghayr can qualify the definite phrase because alladhina is not temporally delimited and the contrary identities of the two groups remove its ambiguity; it can also be accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r2.anchor: ولأن المغضوب عليهم والضالين خلاف المنعم عليهم فليس في غير إذا الإبهام الذي يأبى عليه ان يتعرف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعمر بن الخطاب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r3.claim: A circumstantial accusative reading of ghayr is attributed to the Prophet and Umar, and also reported from Ibn Kathir.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r3.anchor: وقرىء بالنصب على الحال وهي قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعمر بن الخطاب ورويت عن ابن كثير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r4.claim: An unnamed view identifies the angered as Jews, citing the verse that says God cursed them and was angry with them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p58#3/r4.anchor: وقيل المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود لقوله عز وجل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r1.claim: God's anger means His will to take vengeance on sinners, punish them, and treat them as a king does those under his authority.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r1.anchor: هو إرادة الانتقام من العصاة وإنزال العقوبة بهم وان يفعل بهم ما يفعله الملك اذا غضب على من تحت يده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r2.claim: The first عليهم is parsed as an object and the second as a subject.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r2.anchor: الأولى محلها النصب على المفعولية والثانية محلها الرفع على الفاعلية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r3.claim: The negative lā before astray is included because ghayr already carries a negative sense.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r3.anchor: لما في غير من معنى النفي كانه قيل لا المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r4.speaker: عمر وعلي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r4.claim: Umar and Ali are reported to read wa-ghayr al-dallin, repeating the negative particle in a different construction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r4.anchor: وعن عمر وعلي رضي الله عنهما أنهما قرآ وغير الضالين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r5.speaker: أيوب السختياني
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r5.claim: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani reads al-dallin with hamza to avoid two adjacent silent consonants, as in dialect examples cited by Abu Zayd.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r5.anchor: وقرأ أيوب السختياني ( ولا الضألين ) بالهمزة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r6.claim: Amin is an indeclinable sound used for the verb respond; it has long and short forms, and a poetic line illustrates it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r6.anchor: آمين صوت سمي به الفعل الذي هو استجب كما ان رويد وحيهل وهلم أصوات سميت بها الأفعال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet explained Amin as meaning do it or answer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r7.anchor:
وعن ابن عباس
4 سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معنى آمين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r8.claim: The Prophet said Gabriel taught him Amin upon finishing al-Fatiha and called it like a seal on a book; it is not Quran because absent from the codices.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r8.anchor:
وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
5 ( لقنني جبريل عليه السلام آمين عند فراغي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r9.speaker: الحسن وأبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r9.claim: Hasan says the imam should not say Amin because he is the one supplicating; Abu Hanifa shares this view and is known to recite it quietly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p59/r9.anchor:
وعن الحسن لا يقولها الامام لأنه الداعي
وعن أبي حنيفة رحمه الله مثله والمشهور عنه وعن أصحابه انه يخفيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r1.claim: Wail ibn Hujr reports that the Prophet said Amin aloud after reciting wa-la al-dallin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r1.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان اذا قرأ ولا الضالين قال آمين ورفع بها صوته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r2.claim: The Prophet tells Ubayy ibn Ka'b that al-Fatiha has no equal in Torah, Gospel, or Quran and is the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Quran given to him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r2.anchor:
وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي بن كعب
7 ( ألا أخبرك بسورة لم ينزل في التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن مثلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r3.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r3.claim: Hudhayfa reports that God lifts an imminent calamity from a people for forty years after a child recites al-Fatiha and God hears it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p61/r3.anchor:
وعن حذيفة بن اليمان ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال
8 ( إن القوم ليبعث الله عليهم العذاب حتما مقضيا فيقرأ صبي من صبيانهم

MAJAZ:v1p24/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r1.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ means a road or clear, straight way; an unattributed line uses the phrase ṣirāṭ al-qāṣid.
MAJAZ:v1p24/r1.anchor: «الصراط» (5) : الطريق، المنهاج الواضح، قال: فصد عن نهج الصراط القاصد

MAJAZ:v1p24/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r2.claim: Jarīr’s verse describes the Commander of the Faithful as being on a ṣirāṭ that stays straight even when routes bend.
MAJAZ:v1p24/r2.anchor: وقال جرير: أمير المؤمنين على صراط ... إذا اعوج الموارد مستقيم

MAJAZ:v1p24/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r3.claim: Mawārid means roads or places one reaches for water, and also villages; the following verse uses ṣirāṭ as a road comparison.
MAJAZ:v1p24/r3.anchor: والموارد: الطرق، ما وردت عليه من ماء، وكذلك القرى وقال: وطئنا أرضهم بالخيل حتى ... تركناهم أذل من الصراط

MAJAZ:v1p24/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r4.claim: In ghayr al-maghḍūbi ʿalayhim wa-lā al-ḍāllīn, the first lā is an extra particle completing the phrase, effectively ‘and the straying.’
MAJAZ:v1p24/r4.anchor: «غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين» (7) مجازها: غير المغضوب عليهم والضالين، و «لا» من حروف الزوائد لتتميم الكلام،

MAJAZ:v1p24/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r5.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s phrase fī biʾr lā ḥawr has an extra lā; the intended sense is a well of ruin or destruction.
MAJAZ:v1p24/r5.anchor: وقال العجاج: فى بئر لا حور سرى وما شعر أي فى بئر خور أي هلكة،

MAJAZ:v1p24/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r6.claim: Abū al-Najm’s ألا تسخرا means أن يسخرن, showing an extra lā; al-qafandar means ugly and repulsive.
MAJAZ:v1p24/r6.anchor: وقال أبو النجم: فما ألوم البيض ألا تسخرا ... لما رأين الشمط القفندرا القفندر: القبيح الفاحش، أي فما ألوم البيض أن يسخرن،

MAJAZ:v1p24/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r7.claim: In the cited line, ‘they reproach me in amusement ألا أحبه’ means ‘that I love it,’ with lā treated as extra.
MAJAZ:v1p24/r7.anchor: وقال: ويلحيننى فى اللهو ألا أحبه ... وللهو داع دائب غير غافل والمعنى: ويلحيننى فى اللهو أن أحبه.

MAJAZ:v1p24/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r9.claim: In wa-lā al-ḍāllīn, lā reinforces the preceding negation; Arabic likewise says ‘without good or blessing’ and ‘no benefit nor defense.’
MAJAZ:v1p24/r9.anchor: «ولا الضالين» : «لا» تأكيد لأنه نفى، فأدخلت «لا» لتوكيد النفي، تقول: جئت بلا خير ولا بركة،

MAJAZ:v1p24/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p24/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p24/r10.claim: Abū Khirāsh’s verse supplies a further example of lā continuing a negative coordination in ولا البكر.
MAJAZ:v1p24/r10.anchor: قال أبو خراش: فإنك لو أبصرت مصرع خالد ... بجنب الستار بين أظلم فالحزم إذا لرأيت الناب غير رزية ... ولا البكر لاضطمت يداك على غنم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r12.claim: Those favored are variously identified as angels, prophets, believers in earlier scriptures, Muslims, or Muhammad and his Companions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r12.anchor: { الذين أنعمت عليهم } خمسة أقاويل : أحدها : أنهم الملائكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r13.speaker: وكيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r13.claim: He identifies those favored as Muslims.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r14.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r14.claim: He identifies those favored as Muhammad and the Companions with him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r15.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن الزبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r15.claim: They read sirat man anʿamta ʿalayhim instead of sirat alladhina anʿamta ʿalayhim.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r15.anchor: عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن الزبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r16.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r16.claim: He asked the Prophet who the angered and astray groups were; the Prophet identified them as Jews and Christians, respectively, as all exegetes agree.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r17.claim: One account understands divine anger as the anger known among human beings.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r18.claim: A second account interprets God's anger as a will to punish; anger linguistically means severity, a quality unsuitable for God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r18.anchor: في اللغة هو الغلظة , وهذه الصفة لا تجوز

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r19.claim: A third account interprets God's anger as His condemnation of them.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r20.claim: A fourth account calls a kind of punishment anger, just as God's bounty is called mercy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r20.anchor: نوع من العقوبة سمي غضبا , كما سميت نعمه رحمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r21.claim: Misguidance is the opposite of guidance, and Jews are singled out for anger because they are more intensely hostile.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r22.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r22.claim: He read the closing phrase with a repeated ghayr before wa-la al-dallin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p58/r22.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب ( غير المغضوب عليهم

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r5.claim: Those granted favor are the prophets, whom God favored with prophethood.
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r5.anchor: يعنى النبيين الذين أنعم الله عليهم بالنبوة

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r6.claim: The people under divine anger are the Jews, whom God turned into apes and pigs; the requested path is other than their religion.
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r6.anchor: غير اليهود الذين غضب الله عليهم، فجعل منهم القردة والخنازير

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r7.claim: The straying people are the polytheists, identified here as the Christians.
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r7.anchor: يقول: ولا دين المشركين، يعنى النصارى

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says the Prophet related that God divided this sūra between Himself and the servant: praise is thanks, the two mercy names are praise, the King verse is glorification, and the rest belongs to the servant; seeking help is God's special acknowledgment of the servant's plea.
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r8.anchor: عن أبى هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

MUQATIL:1:5-7/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r9.claim: Muqātil instructs a reader who reaches the closing words to say Āmīn; angels say it too, and if people's response coincides, the group's prior sins are forgiven.
MUQATIL:1:5-7/r9.anchor: عن مقاتل، قال إذا قرأ أحدكم هذه السورة فبلغ خاتمتها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r1.claim: “The path of those You favored” is an appositive restating the straight path, both reinforcing the point and identifying it as the Muslims' path; this emphatically attests to its uprightness.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r1.anchor: بدل من الصراط وهو فى حكم تكرير العامل وفائدته التأكيد والإشعار بأن الصراط المستقيم تفسيره صراط المسلمين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r2.claim: Those favored are the believers and prophets, or the people of Moses before they changed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r2.anchor: وهم المؤمنون والأنبياء عليهم السلام أو قوم موسى قبل أن يغيروا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r3.claim: “Other than those under anger” is an appositive: those favored are the ones spared God's anger and misguidance.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r3.anchor: بدل من الذين أنعمت عليهم يعنى أن المنعم عليهم هم الذين سلموا من غضب الله والضلال

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the phrase qualifies the favored, who combine the full blessing of faith with safety from divine anger and error; the source explains why “other than” can qualify a definite antecedent.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r4.anchor: أو صفة للذين يعنى أنهم جمعوا بين النعمة المطلقة وهى نعمة الإيمان

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r5.claim: The first “upon them” is an object and the second is a subject; God's anger means His will to exact revenge and impose punishment on deniers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r5.anchor: وعليهم الأولى محلها النصب على المفعولية ومحل الثانية الرفع على الفاعلية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r6.claim: A reported identification takes those under anger as Jews, citing the verse about those God cursed and angered.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r6.anchor: وقيل المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود لقوله تعالى من لعنه الله وغضب عليه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r7.claim: The reported identification takes the astray as Christians, citing the verse that says they went astray before.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r7.anchor: والضالون هم النصارى لقوله تعالى قد ضلوا من قبل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r8.claim: Basran grammarians take la as emphatic negation; Kufans take it to mean “other than.”
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r8.anchor: ولا زائدة عند البصريين للتوكيد وعند الكوفيين هى بمعنى غير

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r9.claim: Asked about Amin, Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet explained it as “respond” or “so be it”; the word is a built verbal noun with long and short vowel forms.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معنى آمين فقال افعل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r10.claim: The poet's evidence shows both long and short forms of Amin, and a Prophetic report says Gabriel taught Amin at the end of al-Fatiha, like a seal on a letter; it is not Qur'an because codices omit it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p8#2/r10.anchor: قال عليه السلام لقننى جبريل آمين عند فراغى من قراءة فاتحة الكتاب وقال إنه كالختم على الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r3.claim: ʿUmar and Ibn al-Zubayr read “the path of those whom You favored” as “the path of whom You favored.”
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r3.anchor: الموفية الثلاثين: قرأ عمر بن الخطاب وابن الزبير رضي الله عنهما «صراط من أنعمت عليهم».

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r4.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r4.claim: Most exegetes identify the favored people as prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and righteous people, based on the verse naming these groups as God’s companions.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r4.anchor: إنه أراد صراط النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r5.claim: The verse refutes Qadariyya, Muʿtazila, and Imamiyya claims that humans create their acts: repeated requests for guidance and protection from deviation show dependence on God.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7/r5.anchor: فلو كان الأمر إليهم والاختيار بيدهم دون ربهم لما سألوه الهداية

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r1.claim: Most interpreters identify those under wrath as Jews and those astray as Christians; the Prophet’s explanation to ʿAdi ibn Hatim supports it, as do verses about their wrath and error.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r1.anchor: فالجمهور أن المغضوب عليهم اليهود، والضالين النصارى

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r2.claim: Other interpreters identify those under wrath as polytheists and those astray as hypocrites.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r3.speaker: السلمي والماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r3.claim: A strained interpretation labels those omitting the Fatiha in prayer as under wrath and those missing its blessing as astray; al-Mawardi rejects it because disputed reports cannot support such a ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r3.anchor: وهذا وجه مردود لأن ما تعارضت فيه الأخبار وتقابلت فيه الآثار

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r4.claim: Another view calls innovators recipients of wrath and those who leave the sunnas astray; the author says this is good, though the Prophet’s interpretation is best.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r4.anchor: وهذا حسن وتفسير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أولى وأعلى وأحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r5.claim: Alayhim is grammatically understood as “wrath fell upon them”; wrath linguistically means severity, while in God’s attribute it is either His will to punish or punishment itself.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى الغضب في صفة الله تعالى إرادة العقوبة، فهو صفة ذات، وإرادة الله تعالى من صفات ذاته

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r6.claim: A hadith says charity extinguishes the Lord’s wrath, treating wrath as an attribute of action when it means the punishment.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r7.claim: Ḍalāl means leaving the proper course and the path of truth; milk disappearing in water illustrates the root’s sense of vanishing.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#2/r7.anchor: الضلال في كلام العرب هو الذهاب عن سنن القصد وطريق الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r1.claim: Poetry illustrates al-muḍallal for one gone missing; ḍalḍala is a smooth stone water rolls through a valley, and ghaḍba can mean a differently colored rock on a mountain.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r1.anchor: والضلضلة: حجر أملس يردده الماء في الوادي.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وأبي بن كعب
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r2.claim: ʿUmar and Ubayy read ghayr before both “those under wrath” and “those astray”; the two forms are read in genitive or accusative.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r2.anchor: الرابعة والثلاثون: قرأ عمر بن الخطاب وأبي بن كعب «غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين»

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r3.claim: The genitive may make ghayr an appositive to alladhina or to the pronoun in alayhim, or an adjective; although definite nouns usually are not modified by indefinite ones, alladhina is general here or ghayr is definite between exclusive opposites.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r3.anchor: فالخفض على البدل من «الذين» أو من الهاء والميم في «عليهم» أو صفة للذين

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r4.speaker: الفارسي والزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r4.claim: Two grammatical analyses for the reading’s genitive are attributed respectively to al-Farisi and al-Zamakhshari.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r5.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r5.claim: The accusative may be circumstantial, exceptive, or understood as “I mean,” a construction attributed to al-Khalil.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r5.anchor: ويجوز النصب بأعني وحكي عن الخليل

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r6.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r6.claim: Al-Tabari treats lā in “and not those astray” as redundant, as in the verse “what prevented you from not prostrating.”
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r6.anchor: الخامسة والثلاثون: «لا» في قوله «ولا الضالين» اختلف فيها، فقيل هي زائدة قاله الطبري.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r7.speaker: مكي والمهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r7.claim: Makki and al-Mahdawi say lā reinforces the separation so the astray are not mistaken for a group conjoined with the favored.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r7.anchor: وقيل: هي تأكيد دخلت لئلا يتوهم أن الضالين معطوف على الذين، حكاه مكي والمهدوي.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r8.claim: The Kufans say lā means “other than,” as in ʿUmar’s and Ubayy’s variant reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r8.anchor: وقال الكوفيون: «لا» بمعنى غير، وهي قراءة عمر وأبي وقد تقدم.

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r9.claim: The original form was al-ḍāllilīn; the first lām lost its vowel and assimilated into the next, and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani uses a hamza reading to avoid adjacent still consonants.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r9.anchor: السادسة والثلاثون: الأصل في «الضالين»: الضاللين حذفت حركة اللام الأولى ثم أدغمت اللام في اللام

QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r10.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r10.claim: Abu Zayd heard ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd read the verse about no human or jinn being asked of sin; he initially thought it a mistake until he heard Arabs use forms such as dābba and shābba.
QURTUBI-FULL:1:7#3/r10.anchor: حكى أبو زيد قال: سمعت عمرو بن عبيد يقرأ:

QURTUBI-FULL:1:1-7#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:1:1-7#4/r1.speaker: كثير
QURTUBI-FULL:1:1-7#4/r1.claim: The poet Kathir’s line “when the spearheads reddened with fresh blood” witnesses the hamza dialect.

NAHHAS:v1p174/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p174/r9.claim: Ṣirāṭ is an appositional substitute, and alladhīna is genitive by annexation and indeclinable so its middle does not inflect.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r9.anchor: بدل و الذين في موضع خفض بالإضافة وهو مبني لئلا يعرب الاسم من وسطه

NAHHAS:v1p174/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p174/r10.claim: Anʿamta ʿalayhim is the relative clause, and its pronoun refers back to alladhīna.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r10.anchor: ( أنعمت عليهم ) داخل في الصلة والهاء والميم يعود على الذين

NAHHAS:v1p174/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r11.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p174/r11.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads ʿalayhimu with a ḍamma and retained wāw, the original form.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r11.anchor: قرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ( أنعمت عليهمو ) بضم الهاء وإثبات الواو وهذا هو الأصل

NAHHAS:v1p174/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r12.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v1p174/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ʿalayhimī with kasra and a retained yāʾ, avoiding yāʾ next to ḍamma and changing wāw after kasra.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r12.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( أنعمت عليهمي ) بكسر الهاء وإثبات الياء وكسر الهاء لأنه كره أن يجمع بين ياء وضمة

NAHHAS:v1p174/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r13.speaker: أهل المدينة
NAHHAS:v1p174/r13.claim: The people of Medina read ʿalayhim with kasra on hāʾ and a still mīm, a Najdi dialect.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r13.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة ( عليهم ) بكسر الهاء وإسكان الميم وهي لغة أهل نجد

NAHHAS:v1p174/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r14.speaker: حمزة وأهل الكوفة
NAHHAS:v1p174/r14.claim: Ḥamza and the Kufans read ʿalayhum with ḍamma on hāʾ and still mīm, dropping the heavy wāw.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r14.anchor: قرأ حمزة وأهل الكوفة ( عليهم ) بضم الهاء وإسكان الميم فحذفوا الواو لثقلها

NAHHAS:v1p174/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r15.speaker: الأعرج
NAHHAS:v1p174/r15.claim: Al-Aʿraj reads ʿalayhimu with kasra on hāʾ and a retained wāw.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r15.anchor: واللغة الخامسة قرأ بها الأعرج ( عليهمو ) بكسر الهاء والواو

NAHHAS:v1p174/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r16.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v1p174/r16.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd rejects as impermissible two irregular forms with hāʾ and mīm both ḍamma or both kasra without wāw or yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r16.anchor: وحكي لغتنا شاذتان وهما ضم الهاء والميم بغير واو وكسرهما بغير ياء وقال محمد بن يزيد وهذا لا يجوز

NAHHAS:v1p174/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r17.speaker: أبو العباس
NAHHAS:v1p174/r17.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās says the kasra in minhu is possible because the nūn is still; Banū Bakr also use kasra in ʿalaykum, but he rejects the analogy as a grave error.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r17.anchor: قال أبو العباس وناس من بني بكر بن وائل يقولون عليكم فيكسرون الكاف

NAHHAS:v1p174/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r18.speaker: ابن كيسان
NAHHAS:v1p174/r18.claim: Ibn Kaysān permits ghayr al-maghḍūbi as an adjective or apposition to alladhīna, and also as apposition to their pronoun in ʿalayhim.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r18.anchor: قال ابن كيسان ويجوز أن يكون بد لا من الهاء والميم في عليهم

NAHHAS:v1p174/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r19.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير
NAHHAS:v1p174/r19.claim: A report from al-Khalīl says ʿAbd Allāh ibn Kathīr read ghayra al-maghḍūbi in the accusative.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r19.anchor: وروى الخليل رحمه الله عن عبد الله بن كثير ( غير المغضوب ) بالنصب

NAHHAS:v1p174/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r20.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p174/r20.claim: Al-Akhfash parses the accusative as a circumstantial accusative or an exception.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r20.anchor: قال الأخفش هو نصب على الحال وإن شئت على الاستثناء

NAHHAS:v1p174/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r21.speaker: أبو العباس
NAHHAS:v1p174/r21.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās calls it a detached exception rather than an exception from the preceding expression.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r21.anchor: قال أبو العباس هو استثناء ليس من الأول

NAHHAS:v1p174/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r22.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v1p174/r22.claim: The Kufans deny an exception parse because lā follows and, they say, lā is not superfluous in exceptions.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r22.anchor: قال الكوفيون لا يكون استثناءا لأن بعده ولا ولا تزاد لا في الاستثناء

NAHHAS:v1p174/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r23.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p174/r23.claim: The Kufan objection is not binding because lā here carries a negative sense.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r23.anchor: قال أبو جعفر وذا لا يلزم لأن فيه معنى النفي

NAHHAS:v1p174/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r24.speaker: ابن كيسان
NAHHAS:v1p174/r24.claim: Ibn Kaysān says al-maghḍūb is singular in form but plural in sense, like passive participles with a genitive complement.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r24.anchor: قال ابن كيسان هو موحد في معنى جمع وكذلك كل فعل المفعول إذا لم يكن فيه خفض

NAHHAS:v1p174/r25.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r25.speaker: البصريون
NAHHAS:v1p174/r25.claim: Basrans treat lā as extra; the Kufans understand it as ghayr.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r25.anchor: ( لا ) زائدة عند البصريين وبمعنى غير عند الكوفيين

NAHHAS:v1p174/r26.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r26.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p174/r26.claim: Al-ḍāllīn is coordinated with al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim; the Kufans call this coordination, while Sībawayh calls it sharing.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r26.anchor: و ( الضالين ) عطف على المغضوب عليهم والكوفيون يقولون نسق وسيبويه يقول إشراك

NAHHAS:v1p174/r27.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p174/r27.speaker: أيوب السختياني
NAHHAS:v1p174/r27.claim: The underlying form al-ḍāllīn is al-ḍāllilīn, with assimilated lām; Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī read the lām with hamza.
NAHHAS:v1p174/r27.anchor: والأصل في الضالين الضاللين ثم أدغمت اللام في اللام

QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r1.speaker: author
