QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r1.claim: Al-Fatiha is Meccan and has seven verses; Muslims recite it at least seventeen times daily, more with voluntary prayers, and may repeat it without limit.

QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله [ ص ]
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.claim: The Prophet says prayer is invalid without reciting the Opening of the Book; the report is in both Sahih collections.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r2.anchor: لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب

QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.claim: The short surah gathers core Islamic creed, worldview, feelings, and guidance, explaining its repetition in every rakʿa and why prayer without it is invalid.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:1/r3.anchor: ما يشير إلى طرف من حكمة اختيارها للتكرار

QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r1.claim: The straight path is that of people granted God's favor, not those who know truth and turn away in anger or those who never find guidance to truth.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r1.anchor: فهو طريق الذين قسم لهم نعمته

QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.speaker: رسول الله
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports in Sahih Muslim that God calls al-Fatiha a prayer divided between Himself and His servant: praise, mercy, and glorification are the Lord's; worship and aid are shared; guidance and the servant's request belong to the servant, who receives what he asks.
QUTB-ZILAL:1:7/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله [ ص ] :  "  يقول الله تعالى : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين

RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r4.claim: The path has a positive side, following those God favored—prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous—and a negative side, avoiding those corrupted in practice or belief.
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r4.anchor: صراط الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين

RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r5.claim: Some say specifying the path of the favored shows that a seeker needs a guiding shaykh, since most people lack sound judgment and need a perfected guide's intellect.
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r5.anchor: إنه لما قال ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾ لم يقتصر عليه بل قال

RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r6.claim: Razi says the surah sets out the covenants of lordship and servitude together, as in God's promise to fulfill each side of His covenant.
RAZI-FULL:v1p152/r6.anchor: هذه السورة وافية ببيان ما يجب معرفته من عهد الربوبية وعهد العبودية

RAZI-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.claim: A single soul is weaker than many united souls; joining the purified spirits seeking spiritual disclosures strengthens readiness to attain the path of those favored.
RAZI-FULL:v1p153#2/r5.anchor: فلهذا قال : ﴿ صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r1.claim: Connection with purified spirits increases strength, while connection with evil spirits brings failure and deprivation; Razi identifies those under wrath as immoral people and the astray as unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r1.anchor: وهم الفساق : ﴿ ولا الضالين ﴾ وهم الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: The law, path, and reality complete human ascent: worship, reliance on God, and guidance culminate in fellowship with the pure and distance from the wretched.
RAZI-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: أعني الشريعة المدلول عليها بقوله إياك نعبد والطريقة المدلول عليها بقوله وإياك نستعين

RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r7.claim: Humanity divides between those who serve, rely on, and seek good from God and those who depend on people; the servant asks to join the favored, not the lost parties.
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r7.anchor: إلهي اجعلني في زمرة الفرقة الأولى وهم الذين أنعمت عليهم بهذه الأنوار الربانية

RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r8.claim: Following the second, misguided party brings loss and destruction; Razi introduces the Quranic rebuke against worshipping what cannot hear, see, or help.
RAZI-FULL:v1p155/r8.anchor: فإن متابعة هذه الفرقة لا تفيد إلا الخسار والهلاك كما قال إبراهيم عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.speaker: أم سلمة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited al-Fatiha while counting the basmala as its first verse, followed by the rest of its verses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p161/r2.anchor: روى الشافعي رضي الله عنه عن مسلم عن ابن جريج عن ابن أبي مليكة عن أم سلمة أنها قالت

RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.claim: In the divided-prayer report, God calls the basmala glorification, al-Hamd praise, the two mercy names extolling, the Master of Judgment entrustment, and the remaining response a sharing and a request granted.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162/r2.anchor: فإذا قال العبد بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم قال الله سبحانه مجدني عبدي وإذا قال الحمد لله رب العالمين

RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.claim: The seven-verse count supports al-Shafi'i's division, with the basmala as one verse and the final phrase as one; Abu Hanifa denies the basmala verse and splits that final phrase, a weak view for Razi.
RAZI-FULL:v1p162#2/r5.anchor: وسنبين في مسألة مفردة أن قول أبي حنيفة مرجوح ضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r1.claim: One definition makes a blessing a benefit bestowed as kindness upon another.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r1.anchor: عبارة عن المنفعة المفعولة على جهة الإحسان إلى الغير

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r2.claim: Another definition adds that the benefit must be good, since only a good act merits gratitude.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r2.anchor: المنفعة الحسنة المفعولة على جهة الإحسان إلى الغير

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r3.claim: Razi rejects requiring the benefit to be good: gratitude for kindness and blame for sin concern different aspects and can coexist.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r3.anchor: هذا القيد غير معتبر لأنه يجوز أن يستحق الشكر بالإحسان وإن كان فعله محظورا

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r4.claim: A pure harm is not a blessing, because the definition requires a benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r4.anchor: أما قولنا المنفعة فلأن المضرة المحضة لا تكون نعمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r5.claim: The giver must intend kindness to the recipient; an apparent benefit pursued for the giver's own profit is not a blessing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r5.anchor: لو كان نفعا حقا وقصد الفاعل به نفع نفسه لا نفع المفعول به لا يكون نعمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r6.claim: Every benefit or removal of harm reaching creatures is ultimately from God, and blessings fall into three categories.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r6.anchor: أن كل ما يصل إلى الخلق من النفع ودفع الضرر فهو من الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r7.claim: Some blessings appear to come through another person, but God creates the gift, recipient, and benefactor's impulse; the human instrument is thanked while God is the true benefactor.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r7.anchor: إلا أنه تعالى لما أجرى تلك النعمة على يد ذلك العبد كان ذلك العبد مشكورا ولكن المشكور في الحقيقة هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r8.claim: Benefits received through obedience also come from God, who enables, assists, guides, and removes obstacles; therefore all blessings are truly from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r8.anchor: لولا أن الله سبحانه وتعالى وفقنا للطاعات وأعاننا عليها وهدانا إليها

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r9.claim: Life is God's first blessing: nothing can be enjoyed without life, and the Qur'an mentions bringing people to life before worldly provisions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r9.anchor: فثبت أن أصل جميع النعم هو الحياة

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r10.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r10.claim: Some of Razi's Ash'arite colleagues deny that God bestows any blessing on unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r10.anchor: فقال بعض أصحابنا ليس لله تعالى على الكافر نعمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r11.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r11.claim: The Mu'tazilites affirm that God gives unbelievers both religious and worldly blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r11.anchor: وقالت المعتزلة : لله على الكافر نعمة دينية ونعمة دنيويه

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r12.claim: Razi supports his colleagues: if unbelievers were among those favored, asking for the favored path would ask for their path; calling the phrase appositional to the straight path does not remove that consequence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r12.anchor: فكان التقدير اهدنا صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم وحينئذ يعود المحذور المذكور

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r13.claim: Razi also cites the verse saying unbelievers' respite increases their sin as evidence against calling their worldly lot a blessing.

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r14.claim: Worldly benefits are negligible beside everlasting afterlife punishment, as a small sweetness is not counted a benefit when mixed with much poison.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r14.anchor: نعم الدنيا في مقابلة عذاب الآخرة على الدوام قليلة كالقطرة في البحر

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r15.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r15.claim: The opposing evidence includes the command that all people worship their creator, who prepared the earth and sky for them, presenting these as universal blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r15.anchor: فنبه على أنه يجب على الكل طاعة الله لمكان هذه النعم العظيمة

RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r16.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r16.claim: They also cite God's bringing people to life as an act of grace, His reminder to Israel of His favor, and statements that few give thanks as evidence that blessings reach unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v1p208#2/r16.anchor: ذكر ذلك في معرض الامتنان وشرح النعم

RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r1.claim: The verse means asking for the path of those favored; 4:69 identifies them as prophets and the truthful, whose chief is Abu Bakr, so it supports his imamate and the propriety of following him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r1.anchor: ولا شك أن رأس الصديقين ورئيسهم أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r2.claim: The favor cannot mean worldly benefits; it means religious favor, and among these faith alone can exist without the other religious gifts.
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r2.anchor: ولما بطل الأول ثبت أن المراد منه نعمة الدين

RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r3.claim: Razi therefore identifies the favor in the verse specifically as faith.
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r3.anchor: فرجع حاصل القول في قوله اهدنا الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم أنه طلب لنعمة الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r4.claim: Because God is explicitly the giver of faith, He creates and grants it; otherwise the servant would bestow the greatest blessing and God's praise of His own favor would be misplaced, against the Mu'tazilites.
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r4.anchor: ثبت أن خالق الإيمان والمعطي للإيمان هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r5.claim: A believer cannot remain eternally in Hell, since the verse praises this gift as a great favor; a favor with no effect on endless punishment would be insignificant.
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r5.anchor: يجب أن لا يبقى المؤمن مخلدا في النار

RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r6.claim: God is not obligated to provide the best religious guidance: a required act would not count as a favor, whereas the verse calls it one.
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r6.anchor: لا يجب على الله رعاية الصلاح والأصلح في الدين

RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r7.claim: The favor cannot merely mean giving capacity, guidance, or removing excuses, since these are also given to unbelievers while the verse singles out some people.
RAZI-FULL:v1p209/r7.anchor: كل ذلك حاصل في حق الكفار

RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r1.speaker: المشهور
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r1.claim: The commonly reported identification makes those under wrath the Jews and those astray the Christians, citing the Qur'an's descriptions of each.
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r1.anchor: المشهور أن المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود

RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r2.claim: Razi calls this restricted identification weak, since deniers of the Creator and polytheists have worse creeds and should more obviously be disavowed.
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r2.anchor: هذا ضعيف ؛ لأن منكري الصانع والمشركين أخبث دينا من اليهود والنصارى

RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r3.claim: A broader reading takes those under wrath as people who err in outward deeds, including sinners, and those astray as people who err in belief; the wording is general and should not be restricted without cause.
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r3.anchor: المغضوب عليهم على كل من أخطأ في الأعمال الظاهرة وهم الفساق

RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r4.claim: Razi also offers a possible reading in which those under wrath are unbelievers and those astray are hypocrites, following the order of groups in the opening of al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يقال : المغضوب عليهم هم الكفار والضالون هم المنافقون

RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r5.claim: If God has judged a group astray, they cannot also be believers, since that would turn God's truthful report into a lie.
RAZI-FULL:v1p210/r5.anchor: امتنع كونهم مؤمنين وإلا لزم انقلاب خبر الله الصدق كذبا

RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r1.claim: The verse establishes the immunity of prophets and angels from actions or beliefs contrary to the favored path: otherwise they would stray and could not be models or belong among those favored.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r1.anchor: ولما كان ذلك باطلا علمنا بهذه الآية عصمة الأنبياء والملائكة عليهم السلام

RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r2.claim: Human anger is a bodily change, impossible for God; psychological terms applied to God signify their final effect, so divine anger means willing harm, while divine modesty means leaving an act.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r2.anchor: لفظ الغضب في حق الله تعالى لا يحمل على أوله الذي هو غليان دم القلب بل على غايته الذي هو إرادة الإضرار

RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r3.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue that divine anger proves people freely chose their sins, or God's anger would be unjust.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r3.anchor: غضب الله عليهم يدل على كونهم فاعلين للقبائح باختيارهم

RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r4.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r4.claim: Razi's Ash'arite school reads the sequence as God's anger causing their misguidance; the reverse would make a human attribute affect God, which is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r4.anchor: دل ذلك على أن غضب الله عليهم علة لكونهم ضالين

RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r5.claim: The surah begins by praising God and ends by censuring those who reject faith and obedience, showing that turning to God brings good while turning away brings affliction.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211/r5.anchor: مطلع الخيرات وعنوان السعادات هو الإقبال على الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r1.claim: The verse divides people into the obedient who are favored, sinners under wrath, and those ignorant of religion or unbelievers who are astray.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r1.anchor: أن المكلفين ثلاث فرق : أهل الطاعة وإليهم الإشارة بقوله : أنعمت عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r2.claim: Sinners are mentioned before unbelievers because everyone avoids unbelief, while people may fail to guard against sin, making the warning about sin more pressing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r2.anchor: لأن كل واحد يحترز عن الكفر أما قد لا يحترز عن الفسق

RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r3.claim: Razi poses the problem that divine anger follows knowledge of human sin: if God's knowledge is eternal, why create people destined for endless punishment and why create what He is angry with?
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r3.anchor: فهذا العلم إما أن يقال إنه قديم أو محدث فإن كان هذا العلم قديما

RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r4.claim: If that knowledge is new, God would be subject to temporal events and its creation would require a prior knowledge indefinitely; Razi answers that God does what He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r4.anchor: وجوابه يفعل الله ما يشاء ويحكم ما يريد

RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r5.claim: Since the favored cannot also be under wrath or astray, naming the rejected groups adds hope and fear: the first phrase gives complete hope, the latter phrases complete fear, completing faith.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r5.anchor: فقوله صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم يوجب الرجاء الكامل

RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r6.claim: Those with complete favor unite knowledge of truth for its own sake with doing good for its own sake; lacking practice makes sinners under wrath, while lacking knowledge makes people astray.
RAZI-FULL:v1p211#2/r6.anchor: فإن اختل قيد العمل فهم الفسقة وهم المغضوب عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r1.claim: This world is obscure and the afterlife pure: worldly realities need an afterlife original, while afterlife realities need a worldly example, or they would be empty illusion or unsupported claim.
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r1.anchor: عالم الدنيا عالم الكدورة وعالم الآخرة عالم الصفا

RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r2.claim: The spiritual realm has ranks and one supreme being obeyed by the others; correspondingly, the human realm has one supreme person, with the former as source and the latter as manifestation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r2.anchor: فالمطاع في عالم الأرواح هو المصدر والمطاع في عالم الأجسام هو المظهر

RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r3.claim: The spiritual messenger and human messenger meet and correspond, and together complete happiness in the afterlife and this world.
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r3.anchor: والمظهر هو الرسول البشري وبهما يتم أمر السعادات في الآخرة وفي الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r4.claim: The human messenger's call to God requires seven matters in 2:285–286: four concern knowledge of the origin, two concern servitude, and one concerns return to God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r4.anchor: فابتداء الأمر أربعة وفي الوسط صار اثنين وفي النهاية صار واحدا

RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r5.claim: The four matters of origin are knowledge of God, angels, books, and messengers, including not distinguishing among God's messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r5.anchor: وهي معرفة الله والملائكة والكتب والرسل

RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r6.claim: The two aspects of servitude are hearing and obeying as the starting point, then seeking forgiveness through trust and complete reliance on God rather than one's own works.
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r6.anchor: وأما الكمال فهو التوكل على الله والالتجاء بالكلية إليه

RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r7.claim: The seven petitions of 2:286 map onto the seven Fatiha phrases: protection from forgetfulness to the opening remembrance, burden to praise, and inability to mercy, through forgiveness, worship and aid, guidance, and refuge from the rejected paths.
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r7.anchor: وهو المراد من قوله غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r8.claim: The seven ranks at the end of al-Baqara were revealed to Muhammad in the spiritual realm during the ascent and expressed as al-Fatiha when he descended.
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r8.anchor: ذكرها محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام في عالم الروحانيات عند صعوده إلى المعراج

RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r9.claim: Reciting al-Fatiha in prayer sends the lights from manifestation back to their source, mirroring their descent to Muhammad; hence prayer is the believer's ascent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p212/r9.anchor: فمن قرأها في صلاته صعدت هذه الأنوار من المظهر إلى المصدر

RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r1.claim: The three original satanic entrances are desire, anger, and caprice: animalistic, predatory, and satanic respectively; anger is worse than desire, and caprice worse than anger.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r1.anchor: الشهوة بهيمية والغضب سبعية والهوى شيطانية

RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r2.claim: The prayer's prohibition of indecency, wrongdoing, and aggression addresses the effects of desire, anger, and caprice respectively.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r2.anchor: المراد منه آثار الغضب وقوله : ﴿ والبغي ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r3.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r3.claim: A prophetic report distinguishes three kinds of wrongdoing: shirk that is never forgiven, harm between people that is not left unaddressed, and self-wrong that God may forgive; Razi associates them with caprice, anger, and desire.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r3.anchor: الظلم ثلاثة : فظلم لا يغفر وظلم لا يترك وظلم عسى الله أن يتركه

RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r4.claim: Desire produces greed and stinginess, anger produces vanity and pride, and caprice produces unbelief and innovation; their combination produces envy, the worst human trait.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r4.anchor: فالحرص والبخل نتيجة الشهوة والعجب والكبر نتيجة الغضب والكفر والبدعة نتيجة الهوى

RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r5.claim: Envy closes the catalogue of human evils as satanic whispering closes satanic evils; Razi repeats a story in which Iblis tells Pharaoh that the envious are worse than either of them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r5.anchor: ولهذا السبب ختم الله مجامع الشرور الإنسانية بالحسد

RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r6.claim: Al-Fatiha has seven verses to counter these seven vices; its opening three names answer the three basic vices, and the Qur'an and moral traits branch from these foundations.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214/r6.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى سورة الفاتحة وهي سبع آيات لحسم هذه الآفات السبع

RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.claim: Knowing God turns one away from caprice, treated as a rival deity; a saying to Moses urges resisting desire because it contests God's sovereignty.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.anchor: يا موسى خالف هواك فإني ما خلقت خلقا نازعني في ملكي إلا الهوى

RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.claim: Knowing God as the Merciful removes anger, which arises from seeking rule; sovereignty belongs to the Merciful.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.anchor: ومن عرف أنه رحمن لا يغضب لأن منشأ الغضب طلب الولاية

RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r3.claim: Knowing God as Merciful calls a person to imitate mercy and so avoid self-wrong and animalistic behavior.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r3.anchor: ومن عرف أنه رحيم وجب أن يتشبه به في كونه رحيما

RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r4.claim: The names Lord and King are close to Merciful and All-Merciful; the three names in the closing surah answer desire, anger, and caprice in that order.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r4.anchor: التقدير كأنه قيل : إن أتاك الشيطان من قبل الشهوة فقل

RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.claim: The seven Fatiha verses remove seven vices: praise dispels desire, Lord of the worlds greed, Judgment Day anger, worship and aid pride and vanity, guidance caprice, the favored path unbelief and doubt, and the final phrase innovation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.anchor: فثبت أن هذه الآيات السبع دافعة لتلك الأخلاق القبيحة السبعة

RAZI-FULL:v1p215/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p215/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p215/r1.claim: Al-Fatiha gathers what people need to know about the origin, the middle of servitude, and the return; Razi begins its proof of the Creator from human creation, citing Abraham and Moses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p215/r1.anchor: في تقرير أن سورة الفاتحة جامعة لكل ما يحتاج الإنسان إليه في معرفة المبدأ والوسط والمعاد

RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r10.claim: The favored are complete in knowledge and practice, the condemned neglect righteous deeds, and the astray lack sound belief; asking for the favored path seeks the example of the sound group.
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r10.anchor: ثم إن أهل العالم ثلاث طوائف : الطائفة الأولى

RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.claim: Human knowledge grows through one's own reasoning or through receiving predecessors' discoveries: “guide us” asks for the first, and the path of the favored for the second.
RAZI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.anchor: وقوله : ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾ إشارة إلى القسم الأول

RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.claim: The seven Fatiha verses correspond to the seven bodily prayer acts—standing, bowing, rising, first prostration, rising between prostrations, second prostration, and sitting—as soul to body.
RAZI-FULL:v1p219/r4.anchor: أن آيات الفاتحة سبع والأعمال المحسوسة أيضا في الصلاة سبعة

RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r7.claim: The favored path corresponds to sitting: after utmost humility God honors the servant by seating him before Him, a great favor; the Prophet's ascension and words of greeting model this believer's ascent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r7.anchor: وهو أن أمره بالقعود بين يديه وذلك إنعام عظيم من الله على العبد

RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.claim: The seven Fatiha verses are the soul of the seven prayer acts, themselves the soul of seven stages of human formation; God is the soul of souls and light of lights.
RAZI-FULL:v1p220/r8.anchor: روح الأرواح ونور الأنوار هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.claim: Muhammad's ascent has a bodily journey from Mecca to Jerusalem and then the high kingdom, and a spiritual journey from the visible to the unseen and from the unseen to the unseen of the unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r1.anchor: أما ما يتعلق بعالم الأرواح فله معراجان

RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.claim: The spiritual ascent rises through human spirits, the spirits of the heavens, angels, throne-bearers, and pure spirits detached from bodies, whose worship and love of God exceed human comprehension.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r2.anchor: ثم تترقى فتنتهي إلى الأرواح المقدسة عن التعلقات بالأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.claim: The ascent continues through ever-higher spiritual ranks until God, the source of all good and mercy; thus the spirit-world is the unseen and God's presence the unseen of the unseen.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221/r3.anchor: فثبت أن عالم الأرواح هو عالم الغيب وحضرة جلال الربوبية هي غيب الغيب

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.claim: A prophetic report says God has seventy veils of light; if unveiled, the splendor of His face would burn everything perceived by sight, and only prophetic light reveals the number.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.anchor: إن لله سبعين حجابا من النور لو كشفها لأحرقت سبحات وجهه كل ما أدرك البصر

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.claim: Prayer was given to Muhammad as a gift for his community because it joins bodily ascent through actions with spiritual ascent through remembrances.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.anchor: إن تحفة أمتك الصلاة وذلك لأنها جامعة بين المعراج الجسماني وبين المعراج الروحاني

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.claim: Before beginning the ascent, the worshipper purifies body and clothing for the holy presence and chooses which of opposing companions—angel or devil, reason or desire, truth or falsehood, and so forth—to follow, since settled companionship is hard to break.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.anchor: فإنه إذا استحكمت المرافقة تعذرت المفارقة

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.claim: Raising the hands signals leaving both worlds and directing all inner faculties toward God; “God is greatest” means He exceeds all beings, knowledge, comparison, and even the claim that He is simply greater.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.anchor: فاقطع نظرك عنهما بالكلية ووجه قلبك وروحك وسرك وعقلك وفهمك

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.claim: The opening glorification reveals the lights of divine majesty and moves from declaring God's transcendence to praising Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.anchor: ثم قل : سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك وفي هذا المقام تجلى لك نور سبحات الجلال

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.claim: “Blessed is Your name” unveils pre-eternity and eternity, since blessing here indicates abiding beyond extinction and nonexistence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.anchor: لأن قوله تبارك إشارة إلى الدوام المنزه عن الإفناء والإعدام

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.claim: “Exalted is Your majesty” signifies that God's knowledge and greatness exceed every stated measure.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.anchor: أعلم وأعظم من أن تكون صفات جلاله ونعوت كماله محصورة في القدر المذكور

RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.claim: “There is no god but You” means every attribute of majesty and perfection belongs only to God; ultimately reason, speech, understanding, and imagination fail before Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.anchor: كل صفات الجلال وسمات الكمال له لا لغيره

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r1.claim: The opening glorification links the worshipper's prayer to the ascent of the angels and Muhammad, while Abraham's formula supplies another prophetic ascent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r1.anchor: سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك معراج الملائكة المقربين

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r2.claim: Seeking refuge after these praises guards the worshipper against self-admiration.

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r3.claim: The prayer opens a gate of knowledge, followed by remembrance in the basmala and gratitude in the praise of God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r3.anchor: باب المعرفة والباب الثاني هو باب الذكر

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r4.claim: The names al-Rahman and al-Rahim signify the gates of hope, while Master of Judgment signifies fear.
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r4.anchor: الباب الرابع الرجاء وهو قولك الرحمن الرحيم والباب الخامس باب الخوف

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r5.claim: The declaration that God alone is worshipped and sought for help is the gate of sincerity, grounded in knowing servanthood and lordship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r5.anchor: باب الإخلاص المتولد من معرفة العبودية ومعرفة الربوبية

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r6.claim: The request for the straight path is the gate of supplication and humble appeal, supported by Qur'anic calls to pray.

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r7.claim: The final clause is the gate of following and being guided by pure spirits.
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r7.anchor: باب الاقتداء بالأرواح الطيبة الطاهرة والاهتداء بأنوارهم

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r8.claim: Reciting the surah with insight opens eight gates of paradise, identified with the doors of Eden and spiritual knowledge.

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r9.claim: Bodily prayer begins with standing like the Companions of the Cave and the people at resurrection, then the prescribed invocations and Fatiha.

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r10.claim: The worshipper should view worship from God's perspective and so regard it as inadequate, never suppose that personal worship gives one a claim on God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r10.anchor: أن تنظر من الله إلى عبادتك حتى تستحقرها

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r11.claim: The soul is softened by awe like wood before fire; bend it in bowing, then let it straighten and practice religion gently.
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r11.anchor: النفس الآن جارية مجرى خشبة عرضتها على نار خوف الجلال

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r12.claim: The bow and two prostrations overcome three ruinous obstacles: desire, anger, and caprice.
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r12.anchor: بالركوع تنجو عن عقبة الشهوات وبالسجود الأول

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r13.claim: In the closing sitting, greetings are offered by the tongue, prayers by the limbs, and good words by the heart and faith.

RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r14.claim: The worshipper's spirit meets Muhammad's spirit in this station, prompting a greeting to the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v1p222/r14.anchor: فيتلاقى الروحان ويحصل هناك الروح والراحة والريحان

RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r1.claim: The exchange of greetings prompts the worshipper to testify that all blessings come from God, while honoring Muhammad as guide and Abraham for asking that a messenger be sent.
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r1.anchor: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأشهد أن محمدا رسول الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r2.claim: After the testimony, the worshipper asks God to bless Muhammad and Abraham, then declares that every blessing ultimately comes from the Praiseworthy and Glorious God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r2.anchor: بل من الحميد المجيد إنك حميد مجيد

RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r3.claim: A divine report says God remembers a servant in a gathering better than the servant's; the angels then long to visit, and the worshipper greets them on both sides.
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r3.anchor: إذا ذكرني عبدي في ملأ ذكرته في ملأ خير من ملئه

RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r4.claim: This greeting anticipates the angels entering upon the believer in paradise from every gate and welcoming their patient arrival.
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r4.anchor: الملائكة يدخلون عليه من كل باب فيقولون : سلام عليكم بما صبرتم

RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r5.claim: Space and time are the most imposing created realities: space is boundless expanse, while time is an imagined span from eternity past to eternity future.
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r5.anchor: أعظم المخلوقات جلالة ومهابة المكان والزمان

RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r6.claim: First and last describe time, and manifest and hidden describe space; God encompasses both dimensions and is therefore beyond space and time.
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r6.anchor: كان مدبر المكان والزمان هو الحق تعالى كان منزها عن المكان والزمان

RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r7.claim: The Throne is associated with time and the Kursi with space; there is no space beyond the Kursi or time beyond the Throne.
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r7.anchor: فلا مكان وراء الكرسي ولا زمان وراء العرش

RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r8.claim: Divine highness and greatness are levels of perfection, with greatness above highness and majesty above both; the report makes grandeur God's garment and greatness His mantle.
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r8.anchor: درجة العظمة أكمل وأقوى من درجة العلو

RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r9.claim: Majesty is God's unique reality, beyond resemblance to any possible being, and the ground of His divinity.
RAZI-FULL:v1p223/r9.anchor: تقدسه في حقيقته المخصوصة وهويته المعينة عن مناسبة شيء من الممكنات

RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r1.claim: The Prophet's invocation to call on God as possessor of majesty and honor frames prayer as seeking God's face.

RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r2.claim: Entering prayer requires purification at several levels: repentance from sins, renunciation of worldly things, and progressively leaving attachment to one's works, good deeds, and everything besides God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r2.anchor: ومن كان في مقام الزهد كانت طهارته من الدنيا حلالها وحرامها

RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r3.claim: The degrees of purification are many and unequal, like the differing ranks of those oriented toward the primordial religion.
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r3.anchor: فالمقامات كثيرة والدرجات متفاوته كأنها غير متناهية

RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r4.claim: Before the opening takbir, the worshipper should mentally survey all bodily and natural creation, then the heavens and the Throne, and finally the earthly and celestial spirits.
RAZI-FULL:v1p224/r4.anchor: استحضر في عقلك جملة ما في هذا العالم من أنواع المعادن والنبات والحيوان

RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r1.claim: The contemplation includes angels filling every handbreadth of the heavens, the Throne's attendants, and God's forces beyond the created world.
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r1.anchor: ما في السموات موضع شبر إلا وفيه ملك قائم أو قاعد

RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r2.claim: The first meaning of Allahu akbar is that God brought all things into existence and perfected their qualities, while remaining incomparable to them and beyond rational comparison.
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r2.anchor: منزه عن أن يحكم العقل بجواز مقايسته بها

RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r3.claim: Another meaning is that God is too great to fail to see or hear the worshipper, as described in the hadith of ihsan.
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r3.anchor: الله أكبر من أن لا يراني ومن أن لا يسمع كلامي

RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r4.claim: A third meaning is that God surpasses the reach of human intellect, imagination, and understanding; Ali defines divine unity as not imagining God.

RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r5.claim: A fourth meaning is that no creature can discharge the full right of worship, praise, or knowledge of God's essence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p225/r5.anchor: طاعاتهم قاصرة عن خدمته وثناؤهم قاصر عن كبريائه

RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r1.claim: A prophetic supplication says thought cannot reach God's depth and no observer's gaze reaches Him; created descriptions fall beneath His majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r1.anchor: لا ينالك غوص الفكر ولا ينتهي إليك نظر ناظر

RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r2.claim: The worshipper uses Fatiha as a mirror of creation, afterlife, divine mercy and majesty, law, spiritual way, truth, and the ranks of the blessed and damned.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r2.anchor: واجعل سورة الفاتحة مرآة لك تبصر فيها عجائب عالم الدنيا والآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r3.claim: The clause about those God favored reveals the ranks of the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous; the next clauses disclose the ranks of sinners and unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r3.anchor: درجات أرباب السعادات وأصحاب الكرامات من النبيين والصديقين

RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r4.claim: After spiritual insight into these stations, the worshipper must return to acknowledging God's grandeur and personal lowliness with another takbir.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r4.anchor: فلا تظنن أنك بلغت الغور والغاية بل عد إلى الإقرار للحق بالكبرياء

RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r5.claim: The difference between 'great' in bowing and 'highest' in prostration has subtle meanings the author declines to disclose.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r5.anchor: ما جاء سبحان ربي الأعظم وإنما جاء سبحان ربي العظيم

RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r6.claim: After bowing, pray for those sharing one's standing; God's help to the worshipper follows from helping another Muslim.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226/r6.anchor: لا يزال الله في عون العبد ما دام العبد في عون أخيه المسلم

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.claim: The formula 'God hears whoever praises Him' is a station of intercession, so it has no takbir associated with it; takbir instead expresses awe and fear.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r1.anchor: لأن التكبير مأخوذ من الكبرياء وهو مقام الهيبة والخوف

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.claim: Prostration expresses more humility than bowing, so its wording uses the superlative 'highest' while bowing uses the ordinary 'great.'
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r2.anchor: السجود أكثر تواضعا من الركوع لا جرم الذكر المذكور في السجود

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.claim: A report says an angel named Hizqil flew for three spans of thirty thousand years without crossing the Throne, then praised God as the Highest.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r3.anchor: لله تعالى ملكا تحت العرش اسمه حزقيل

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r4.claim: One interpretation makes the first prostration for eternity past and the second for eternity future, with worldly life between them.

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation says the first prostration recognizes worldly life ending in the afterlife, while the second recognizes the afterlife's passing when God's majesty appears.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r5.anchor: اعلم بالسجدة الأولى فناء الدنيا في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.claim: A third interpretation sees the first prostration as the annihilation of all things and the second as their continued existence through God's sustaining act.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r6.anchor: الثالث : السجدة الأولى فناء الكل في نفسها

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r7.claim: A fourth interpretation assigns the first prostration to the submission of the visible world and the second to the submission of the spiritual world.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r7.anchor: السجدة الأولى تدل على انقياد عالم الشهادة لقدرة الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r8.claim: A fifth interpretation makes the first prostration gratitude for knowledge of God and His attributes and the second an admission of inability to fulfill His rights.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r8.anchor: السجدة الأولى سجدة الشكر بمقدار ما أعطانا من معرفة ذاته وصفاته

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r9.claim: God is not great by bodily size, high by spatial direction, or great by duration: He transcends body, location, and time, while time itself is created.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r9.anchor: فهو عظيم لا بالجثة عال لا بالجهة كبير لا بالمدة

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r10.claim: God's greatness, exaltedness, and majesty exceed all sensory images, imagined forms, and human descriptions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r10.anchor: فهو أجل من أن يشابه المحسوسات ويناسب المخيلات

RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r11.claim: When thought rises to the highest names and angelic praises, the worshipper should recite the declaration that God is above what they describe.
RAZI-FULL:v1p226#2/r11.anchor: سبحان ربك رب العزة عما يصفون

RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet says Abraham asked the reward for praising God; God answered that praise begins and ends gratitude, and so begins revelation and ends the speech of paradise's people.
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r1.anchor: روي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن إبراهيم الخليل عليه السلام سأل ربه

RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r2.claim: A report attributed to Ali says God created intellect from a hidden light, endowed it with virtues, and had it first speak praise; God said no creature was dearer to Him.
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r2.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام أنه قال : خلق الله العقل من نور مكنون مخزون

RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r3.claim: Another report says Adam's first words after sneezing were praise of God.
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r3.anchor: نقل أن آدم عليه السلام لما عطس فقال : الحمد لله

RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r4.claim: Because praise is the first speech of both the first and last created beings, God made it the opening of Muhammad's revealed Book and named the Prophet Ahmad and Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v1p227/r4.anchor: فلا جرم جعلها الله فاتحة كتابه

RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r1.claim: The Prophet is called Ahmad in heaven and Muhammad on earth: heavenly beings praise God and the Prophet, while God praises earthly believers.
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r1.anchor: أنا في السماء أحمد وفي الأرض محمد

RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r2.claim: Since praise accompanies receipt of mercy, its place at the start implies mercy is God's first act; a report says His mercy precedes His anger.

RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r3.claim: Ahmad means the greatest of those praising, and greater praise follows from greater blessing; Muhammad therefore received exceptional mercy and is mercy to all worlds.
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r3.anchor: أن الرسول اسمه أحمد ومعناه أنه أحمد الحامدين

RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r4.claim: Al-Rahman and al-Rahim name God's mercy; Muhammad and Ahmad likewise imply being shown mercy and being most merciful through their relation to praise.
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r4.anchor: قولنا محمد وأحمد جار مجرى قولنا مرحوم وأرحم

RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r5.claim: Some reports add al-Hamd, al-Hamid, and al-Mahmud among the Prophet's names, making five names associated with mercy; paired with five divine mercy terms, they give the sinner ten oceans of mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r5.anchor: أن من أسماء الرسول : الحمد والحامد والمحمود فهذه خمسة

RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r6.claim: The five divine names in Fatiha correspond to five human acts: worship, seeking help, guidance, steadfastness, and asking for blessing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r6.anchor: انطبقت تلك الأسماء الخمسة على هذه الأحوال الخمسة

RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r7.claim: The five names address five human constituents: the rational spirit, satanic soul, irascible soul, appetitive soul, and body, restraining each by a fitting divine name.
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r7.anchor: الإنسان مركب من خمسة أشياء : بدنه ونفسه الشيطانية

RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p228/r8.claim: These constituents answer in reverse order through Fatiha, from the body's worship to the purified spirits asking to join the spiritually blessed.

RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r1.claim: The five pillars correspond to the five names: testimony to God, prayer to Lord, almsgiving to the Merciful, fasting to the Compassionate, and pilgrimage to Master of Judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r1.anchor: فشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله حاصلة من تجلي نور اسم الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r2.claim: Fasting under the name al-Rahim evokes the poor person's hunger and loosens attachment to sensory pleasures, easing their departure at death.
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r2.anchor: إذا جاع تذكر جوع الفقراء فيعطيهم ما يحتاجون إليه

RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r3.claim: Pilgrimage corresponds to Master of Judgment because leaving home and family and traveling barefoot resembles the journey and condition of resurrection.

RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r4.claim: Five kinds of qibla—Jerusalem, the Kaaba, the Frequented House, the Throne, and God's presence—are assigned to the five names.
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r4.anchor: أنواع القبلة خمسة : بيت المقدس والكعبة والبيت المعمور

RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r5.claim: The five senses receive moral discipline from verses about reflection, listening well, wholesome food, Joseph's scent, and chastity; divine-name lights help repel their harms.
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r5.anchor: الحواس خمس : أدب البصر بقوله : ﴿ فاعتبروا يا أولي الأبصار

RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r6.claim: The first half of Fatiha sends the lights of five divine names down and the second half sends the servant's five petitions upward, with the transition at Master of Judgment and You alone we worship.
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r6.anchor: هو الحد الفاصل بين قوله : ﴿ مالك يوم الدين

RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r7.claim: Human requests include worldly benefit and protection, escape from hell and attainment of paradise, plus the highest aim of worshipping God for His own sake.
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r7.anchor: طلب خدمة الله وطاعته وعبوديته لما هو هو

RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r8.claim: The five names direct different requests: God alone, paradise, worldly goods, protection from afterlife harms, and protection from worldly sins that lead to punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r8.anchor: إن شاهدت نور اسم الله لم تطلب من الله شيئا سوى الله

RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r9.claim: The names also map to five familiar remembrances: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa-la quwwata illa billah.
RAZI-FULL:v1p229/r9.anchor: قولنا سبحان الله فهو فاتحة سورة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r1.claim: Divine self-disclosure has three levels: through acts and signs to ordinary people, through attributes to God's friends, and through the essence to eminent prophets and angels.
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r1.anchor: يتجلى لعقول الخلق إلا أن لذلك التجلي ثلاث مراتب

RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r2.claim: The name Allah most powerfully indicates disclosure of the essence: its wording is evident, yet its meaning escapes minds and its secrets remain inaccessible.
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r2.anchor: أظهر الأسماء في اللفظ وأبعدها معنى عن العقول

RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r3.claim: Al-Hallaj's verse depicts people lost in the name Allah and unable to reach its reality without the one who first disclosed it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r3.anchor: اسم الله مع الخلق قد تاهوا به ولها

RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r4.claim: Al-Rahman signifies disclosure through God's exalted attributes, whereas al-Rahim signifies disclosure through His acts and signs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p231/r4.anchor: وأما اسمه الرحمن فهو يفيد تجلى الحق بصفاته العالية

RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r1.claim: The five names correspond to stages of human life: creation, worldly nurture, knowledge of origin, knowledge of return, and transfer from bodies to the abode of recompense.
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r1.anchor: مراتب أحوال الخلق خمسة : أولها الخلق وثانيها التربية

RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r2.claim: God, Lord, al-Rahman, al-Rahim, and King respectively govern those five stages; arrival at the final stage turns speech from third-person reference to direct address.
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r2.anchor: اسم الله منبع الخلق والإيجاد والتكوين والإبداع

RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r3.claim: The repeated pairing of worship and seeking help relates each divine name to its fitting role as creator, provider, merciful giver, or sovereign.
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r3.anchor: إياك نعبد لأنك الله الخالق وإياك نستعين لأنك الرب الرازق

RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r4.claim: Because the Day of Judgment is a long journey, worship is its provision; the servant admits personal deeds are insufficient and asks for God's store of mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r4.anchor: لا بد لذلك اليوم من زاد واستعداد وذلك هو العبادة

RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r5.claim: The difficult journey has many paths, so the servant asks God to guide him along the straight path and chooses the prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous as guides and companions.

RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r6.claim: The final plea seeks protection from two veils separating people from God: the fiery veil of the material world and the luminous veil of the spirit world.
RAZI-FULL:v1p231#2/r6.anchor: الحجب عن الله قسمان : الحجب النارية - وهي عالم الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v1p232/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p232/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p232/r1.claim: Fatiha's two phrases attached to God's name serve the beginning and end of actions: the basmala is remembrance, praise is gratitude, and each merits mercy from a different divine name.
RAZI-FULL:v1p232/r1.anchor: فقوله بسم الله لبداية الأمور وقوله الحمد لله لخواتيم الأمور

RAZI-FULL:v1p232/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p232/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p232/r2.claim: Lordship marks the beginning of human existence, al-Rahman its middle, and the King its end, from the primordial covenant to the final declaration of God's sole sovereignty.
RAZI-FULL:v1p232/r2.anchor: فالربوبية لبداية حالهم بدليل قوله ﴿ ألست بربكم قالوا بلى ﴾

SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r1.claim: Ṣirāṭ alladhīna is a complete apposition, a definite noun replacing another definite noun.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { صراط الذين }: بدل منه بدل كل من كل، وهو بدل معرفة من معرفة

SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r2.claim: Grammarians enumerate seven kinds of apposition; the first three are undisputed, while some assert apposition of clarification and cite a prayer report, which does not apply to Qur'anic wording.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r2.anchor: أما الأقسام الثلاثة الأول فلا خلاف فيها، وأما بدل البداء فأثبته بعضهم

SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r3.speaker: ذي الرمة
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r3.claim: Dhū al-Rumma's line is cited for apposition by mistake or forgetfulness because ḥawa is pure black and laʿas is black tinged with red; the author says these do not occur in eloquent speech.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r3.anchor: قال: لأن الحوة السواد الخالص، واللعس سواد يشوبه حمرة.

SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r4.claim: Arguments for whole-from-part apposition in the Ṭalḥa and Imruʾ al-Qays lines fail: the first reflects an omitted annexed noun, and the second treats a day as a time-span.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r4.anchor: ولا حجة في البيتين، أما الأول: فإن الأصل: أعظما دفنوها أعظم طلحة

SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r5.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r5.claim: Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad says the second ṣirāṭ differs from the first and denotes knowledge of God; the author finds the required omitted conjunction problematic.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن الصراط الثاني غير الأول والمراد به العلم بالله تعالى، قاله جعفر بن محمد

SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r6.claim: Apposition may be definite or indefinite, overt or pronominal in several combinations; its function is clarification after ambiguity and semantic emphasis through an implied repetition of the governing word.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7/r6.anchor: وفائدة البدل: الإيضاح بعد الإبهام، ولأنه يفيد تأكيدا من حيث المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r1.claim: Alladhīna is genitive through annexation, a relative plural requiring a clause and resumptive; it usually has yāʾ in all cases, though some raise it with wāw, as in the cited verse.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r1.anchor: و " الذين " في محل جر بالإضافة، وهو اسم موصول لافتقاره إلى صلة وعائد

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r2.claim: A poetic form uses alladhūna with nominative wāw, and another deletes the relative's nūn to lengthen its clause; the plural is restricted to rational beings unlike singular alladhī.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r2.anchor: وبعضهم يرفعه بالواو جريا له مجرى جمع المذكر السالم ومنه:

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r3.claim: Anʿamta is the relative clause: tāʾ is its attached nominative second-person subject, and ʿalayhim is governed by the verb and supplies the resumptive pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r3.anchor: وأنعمت: فعل وفاعل صلة الموصول، والتاء في " أنعمت " ضمير المخاطب

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r4.claim: The causative hamza in anʿamta normally makes the object directly governed, but here the verb is cast with the prepositional government of tafaḍḍala.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r4.anchor: والهمزة في " أنعمت " لجعل الشيء صاحب ما صيغ منه فحقه أن يتعدى بنفسه

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r5.claim: The hamza pattern afʿala has many meanings: causation, abundance, becoming, assistance, removal, offering, finding, reaching number, time or place, and lexical relations to other patterns.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r5.anchor: ولأفعل أربعة وعشرون معنى، تقدم واحد، والباقي: التعدية نحو: أخرجته، والكثرة

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r6.claim: Further afʿala meanings include naming, prayer, deserving, conveying, greeting, arriving with something, distinguishing forms, and attacking; the passage illustrates each with examples.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#2/r6.anchor: والتسمية نحو: أخطأته أي سميته مخطئا، والدعاء نحو: أسقيته أي قلت له

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r1.claim: ʿAlā primarily signals literal or figurative elevation; it can also mean ʿan, bi, fī, accompaniment, causation, min, or be augmentative, with Qur'anic and poetic examples.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r1.anchor: و " على " حرف استعلاء حقيقة أو مجازا، نحو: عليه دين، ولها معان أخر

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r2.claim: ʿAlā can be a noun meaning above when preceded by a preposition, and may be nominal where treating it as a preposition would produce an impermissible link between detached and attached pronouns.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r2.anchor: فتكون اسما في موضعين، أحدهما: أن يدخل عليها حرف الجر

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r3.claim: The claim that ʿalā is also a verb because ʿalā Zayd means Zayd rose confuses unrelated words: the verb derives from ʿuluww, unlike the noun or preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r3.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن " على " مترددة بين الاسم والفعل والحرف:

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r4.claim: The pronoun hāʾ is normally damma, but non-Hijazis use kasra after a silent yāʾ or kasra; mīm is usually silent before a vowel and kasra before silence when hāʾ is kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#3/r4.anchor: والأصل في هاء الكناية الضم، فإن تقدمها ياء ساكنة أو كسرة كسرها غير الحجازيين

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r1.speaker: أبو بكر ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r1.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī records ten pronunciations of ʿalayhim, including variations in hāʾ and mīm vowels and added wāw or yāʾ; some were read in Qur'anic recitation.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r1.anchor: وفي " عليهم " عشر لغات قرئ ببعضها: عليهم الهاء وضمها مع سكون الميم

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r2.claim: Ghayr is an indefinite apposition to alladhīna; calling it an adjective is difficult because ghayr is indefinite and the relative is definite.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r2.anchor: و " غير " بدل من " الذين " بدل نكرة من معرفة، وقيل: نعت للذين وهو مشكل

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r3.speaker: some grammarians
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r3.claim: Two defenses of adjectival ghayr are offered: it becomes definite between opposites, per Ibn al-Sarrāj's weak view, or the relative resembles an indefinite through ambiguity.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r3.anchor: وأجابوا عنه بجوابين: أحدهما: أن " غير " إنما يكون نكرة إذا لم يقع بين ضدين

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r4.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r4.claim: Makkī says ghayr replaces the attached pronoun in ʿalayhim; the author objects that deleting the replaced pronoun would leave the relative clause without its resumptive.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن " غير " بدل من الضمير المجرور في " عليهم " ،

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r5.claim: Al-maghḍūb is genitive by annexation and a passive participle; the prepositional phrase supplies its agent, and the relative al means those who were angered.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r5.anchor: و " المغضوب ": خفض بالإضافة، وهو اسم مفعول، والقائم مقام الفاعل الجار والمجرور

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r6.claim: Ghayr remains masculine singular, though its verb may be feminine when it refers to a woman; it is inherently adjectival and does not become definite through annexation.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r6.anchor: واعلم أن لفظ " غير " مفرد مذكر أبدا، إلا أنه إن أريد به مؤنث جاز تأنيث فعله

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r7.claim: Ghayr can function like illā for exception, as an adjective by analogy with illā, or like lā for negation, permitting its governed object to precede it.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#4/r7.anchor: وقد يستثنى بها حملا على " إلا " ، كما يوصف بإلا حملا عليها

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r1.claim: The poetic line places the object before negative ghayr, meaning the speaker is not unremembered by the beloved despite distance.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r1.anchor: إن امرأ خصني عمدا مودته على التنائي لعندي غير مكفور

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r2.claim: Object-fronting is not permitted when ghayr is non-negative; grammarians also differ between a general ban and a distinction for oath responses.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r2.anchor: ولا يجوز ذلك فيها إذا كانت لغير النفي، لو قلت: جاء القوم زيدا غير ضارب

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r3.claim: Ghayr must be annexed overtly or implicitly, so putting the definite article on it is incorrect.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r3.anchor: وهي من الألفاظ الملازمة للإضافة لفظا أو تقديرا، فإدخال الألف واللام عليها خطأ.

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r4.claim: Ghayr is also read in the accusative as a circumstantial from alladhīna or ʿalayhim, or as a disjoint exception; al-Farrāʾ rejects the latter because lā lacks a preceding negation.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r4.anchor: وقرئ " غير " نصبا، فقيل: حال من " الذين " وهو ضعيف

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r5.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ argues lā is only augmentative after an earlier negation; the cited lines are offered in reply as cases without one.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r5.anchor: ومنعه الفراء قال: لأن " لا " لا تزاد إلا إذا تقدمها نفي

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r6.claim: Calling lā augmentative does not by itself answer al-Farrāʾ; the reply should show examples where it is augmentative without prior negation, while another analysis makes lā the object of abā.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#5/r6.anchor: وفي هذا الجواب نظر، لأن الفراء لم يقل إنها غير زائدة

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r1.speaker: الخليل
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r1.claim: Al-Khalīl is reported to parse accusative ghayr with an omitted aʿnī, meaning I mean those other than the angered ones.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r1.anchor: وقيل: إن نصب " غير " بإضمار أعني، ويحكى عن الخليل.

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r2.claim: An omitted ṣirāṭ after ghayr is proposed, but this adjective analysis is weak because when an adjective and apposition coexist, the adjective ordinarily comes first; ghayr can instead modify ṣirāṭ alladhīna.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r2.anchor: وهذا ضعيف، لأنه متى اجتمع البدل والوصف قدم الوصف

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r3.claim: Accusative ghayr may also replace either ṣirāṭ, despite a possible repeated-apposition problem, or serve as a circumstantial from either one.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون بدلا من { الصراط المستقيم } أو من { صراط الذين }

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r4.claim: If ghayr is adjectival, the analysis must either treat ghayr as definite or treat its relative antecedent as indefinite-like through ambiguity.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r4.anchor: حيث جعلنا " غير " صفة فلا بد من القول بتعريف " غير " أو بإبهام الموصوف

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r5.claim: Lā reinforces the negation already carried by ghayr and blocks reading al-ḍāllīn as coordinated with those blessed; Kufans instead equate it with ghayr, and ʿUmar reportedly read that way.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r5.anchor: و " لا " في قوله: { ولا الضآلين } زائدة لتأكيد معنى النفي المفهوم من " غير "

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r6.claim: A rare hamzated reading of al-ḍāllīn is supported by dialectal examples; al-Zamakhsharī says it avoids two quiescent consonants, but examples without that environment suggest a regular dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r6.anchor: وقرئ شاذا: الضألين بهمز الألف، وأنشدوا:

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r7.claim: The past-tense relative clause presents God's blessing as established, while the noun after al generalizes across times; passive wording tactfully avoids attributing anger directly to the deity.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#6/r7.anchor: قيل: ليدل ذلك على ثبوت إنعام الله عليهم وتحقيقه لهم، وأتى بصلة أل اسما

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r1.claim: Inʿām is delivering benefit to another and is said only of rational recipients, not horses or donkeys.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r1.anchor: والإنعام: إيصال الإحسان إلى الغير، ولا يقال إلا إذا كان الموصل إليه الإحسان من العقلاء

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r2.claim: Anger is described as the heart's blood surging in intent to take revenge; a prophetic report warns against anger and describes its bodily signs.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r2.anchor: والغضب: ثوران دم القلب إرادة الانتقام، ومنه قوله عليه السلام:

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r3.claim: When attributed to God, anger means retribution; غضبت لفلان is said of a living person and غضبت به of a dead one.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r3.anchor: وإذا وصف به الباري تعالى فالمراد به الانتقام لا غيره

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r4.claim: Alternative definitions make anger a heart's change toward something disliked, or distinguish divine action-attribute when it means punishment from essential attribute when it means the will to punish.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r4.anchor: وقيل: إن أريد بالغضب العقوبة كان صفة فعل، وإن أريد به إرادة العقوبة كان صفة ذات.

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r5.claim: Ḍalāl may mean concealment or disappearance, destruction, deviation from the straight path, or forgetfulness; the forgetfulness sense in 2:282 is supported by its following remembrance clause.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r5.anchor: والضلال: الخفاء والغيبوبة، وقيل: الهلاك، فمن الأول قولهم:

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r6.claim: Amin is not part of the Quran by consensus; it means respond and is an indeclinable imperative noun.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r6.anchor: القرآن إجماعا، ومعناها: استجب، فهي اسم فعل مبني على الفتح

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa rejects treating Amin as a divine name because a singular definite vocative should take damma and divine names require transmitted authorization.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r7.anchor: وضعف أبو البقاء هذا بوجهين: أحدهما: أنه لو كان كذلك لكان ينبغي أن يبنى على الضم

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r8.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r8.claim: Al-Farisi explains the divine-name reading by an implicit pronoun referring to God within the imperative noun; the author calls this a good analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r8.anchor: ووجه الفارسي قول من جعله اسما لله تعالى على معنى أن فيه ضميرا يعود على الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r9.claim: Amin has long and short forms, each attested in poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#7/r9.anchor: وفي آمين لغتان: المد والقصر، فمن الأول قوله:

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r1.claim: Some treat the long form as foreign because its pattern resembles Qābīl and Hābīl; geminating mīm is commonly called erroneous, though transmitted from al-Ḥasan and Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r1.anchor: وقيل: الممدود اسم أعجمي، لأنه بزنة قابيل وهابيل.

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r2.speaker: الجوهري
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r2.claim: Al-Jawhari transmits the common judgment that geminating mim is erroneous, though the reading is also reported from al-Hasan and Jafar al-Sadiq.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r2.anchor: وهل يجوز تشديد الميم؟ المشهور أنه خطأ نقله الجوهري، ولكنه قد روي عن الحسن وجعفر الصادق التشديد

SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r3.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r3.claim: Al-Ḥusayn b. al-Faḍl derives the geminated form from amma, to intend or aim toward God, as in the Qur'anic phrase about those intending the Sacred House.
SAMIN-DURR:1:7#8/r3.anchor: وهو قول الحسين بن الفضل من أم إذا قصد، أي نحن قاصدون نحوك، ومنه ولا آمين البيت الحرام

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.claim: Most scholars place al-Fātiḥah among the earliest sūrahs revealed in Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r1.anchor: to have been revealed in Makkah

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.speaker: Mujāhid
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.claim: Mujāhid says al-Fātiḥah was revealed in Madinah.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r2.anchor: According to Mujāhid (d. 104/722–23), one of the leading scholars among the second generation of Muslims, this sūrah was revealed in Madinah

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.claim: Most scholars reject a Medinan origin because Muslims needed the sūrah to perform obligatory prayers.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r3.anchor: Most scholars claim that this is impossible, however, as the Muslims would not have been able to perform their required prayers without it

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.claim: Al-Fātiḥah means The Opening: it opens the Book, each prayer cycle, many everyday acts, and may open the breast to faith.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r4.anchor: The primary meaning of al-Fātiḥah is “The Opening,” which indicates the sūrah’s function as “the opening of the Book”

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.claim: The sūrah is seen as a synthesis and the Quran’s most important chapter, hence Umm al-kitāb; the title also refers to 3:7 and the celestial archetype of scripture.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r5.anchor: has been given the title Umm al-kitāb, “Mother of the Book,” a
