STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.claim: It is called the Mother of the Quran because it contains the meaning of the entire Quran.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r6.anchor: It is also known as “The Mother of the Quran” (IK, Ṭ), a reference to its containing the meaning of the entire Quran

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r7.claim: Another title, The Seven Oft-Repeated, is linked to 15:87.

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.claim: The title The Cure reflects its reputed healing power for body and soul.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r8.anchor: is said to have healing powers for both body and soul

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.claim: The title The Foundation reflects the Fātiḥah’s role as a foundation for the whole Quran.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r9.anchor: because it serves as a foundation

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.claim: As Sūrat al-Ḥamd and Sūrat al-Ṣalāh, the Fātiḥah begins each prayer cycle for Sunnis and many Shiites.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r10.anchor: the Fātiḥah is recited at the beginning of each

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.claim: Shiite law permits reciting the Fātiḥah in the third and fourth cycles or an alternative formula praising God.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r11.anchor: In Shiite law one is allowed to recite the Fātiḥah

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.claim: Muslims recite the Fātiḥah at diverse life events; funeral services are called fātiḥah in some lands as an opening from one life to another.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r12.anchor: It is also recited by Muslims on occasions as diverse as a funeral, a wedding, the birth of a child, the inauguration of an official event

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.claim: The Prophet identifies the Fātiḥah as the greatest sūrah, calling it Praise be to God and the seven oft-repeated, and linking it to 15:87.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r13.anchor: the Prophet told a man that he would teach him the greatest sūrah; when asked what it was, the Prophet responded

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.speaker: God
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.claim: In a hadith qudsī, God responds to the servant’s praise, magnification, and glorification during the prayer, which is divided between them.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r14.anchor: I have divided the prayer between Myself and My

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.claim: The Fātiḥah is a prayer encapsulating metaphysical and eschatological realities and teaches the proper human disposition toward God.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r15.anchor: the Fātiḥah is more than the confessional prayer of Muslims. It is a prayer that encapsulates all the metaphysical and eschatological realities

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.claim: Its structure moves from God’s nature in the first three verses, through the God-human relationship, to human states in the final three.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r16.anchor: The Fātiḥah thus has a threefold structure: the first three verses deal with the nature of God, the middle verse deals with the relationship between God and human beings

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.claim: A report says nothing like the Fātiḥah was revealed in the Torah, Psalms, Gospel, or Quran.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r17.anchor: In one the Prophet says, “By Him in Whose Hand lies my soul, in neither the Torah, the Psalms, the Gospel, nor the Quran was the like of it revealed”

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.speaker: Mujāhid
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.claim: One attribution says Satan was frightened when the Fātiḥah was revealed, among four events; others attribute the saying to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r18.anchor: attributed by some to Mujāhid (Q) and by

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.claim: The Fātiḥah’s exalted status generated many independent commentaries, often showing how the Quran as a whole is contained in it.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r19.anchor: The exalted status of the Fātiḥah has resulted in numerous independent commentaries upon it, some numbering hundreds of pages

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.claim: A saying attributed to ʿAlī compresses the Quran into the Fātiḥah, the basmalah, its opening bāʾ, and the diacritical point beneath it.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r20.anchor: a famous saying attributed to ʿAlī ibn AbīṬālib

STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.claim: The point beneath bāʾ can symbolize the Divine Pen’s first drop of ink, which inscribed all archetypes on the Preserved Tablet before creation; thus basmalah marks both Quranic and cosmic beginnings.
STUDYQURAN:1:intro/r21.anchor:
This point can be understood to represent the first
drop of ink

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r1.claim: Some accounts divide the final verse into two verses, with the first ending at hast blessed.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r1.anchor: According to some accounts, this verse is in fact two verses, the first of which ends with hast blessed

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r2.claim: Those God blessed are identified in 4:69 as prophets, truthful ones, witnesses, and righteous people, excellent companions.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r2.anchor: Whosoever obeys God and the Messenger, they are with those whom God has blessed, the prophets, the truthful ones, the witnesses, and the righteous

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r3.claim: The blessed are also described as purified for attaining God or as observing the Law while realizing spiritual truths without exceeding knowledge or its decrees.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r3.anchor: Those who are blessed by God are also said to be those whom God has purified, so that they are able to attain unto Him

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r4.claim: Ghayr may attach grammatically to the path or to those, but both readings yield the same meaning.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r4.anchor: Not of renders the exceptive particle ghayr, which is understood as being attached to the path

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r5.claim: Some commentators identify those incurring wrath with idolaters and those astray with hypocrites.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r5.anchor: According to some, those who incur wrath are the idolaters, and those who are astray are the hypocrites

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r6.claim: Another interpretation associates disbelief with wrath and lesser sins with straying.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r6.anchor: Others relate the terms to two categories of sin in which disbelief incurs wrath and lesser sin results from being astray

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r7.claim: Others associate the terms with moral shortcomings such as heedlessness and profligacy, broadly encompassing spiritual debasement and worldly preoccupation.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r7.anchor: Still others relate the terms to those who exhibit various moral shortcomings, such as those who are heedless and those who are profligate

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r8.claim: Other Quranic passages describe divine wrath against disbelief, disputants, hypocrites, idolaters, and murderers of believers.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r8.anchor: Regarding those who incur wrath, 16:106 says, Whosoever opens his breast unto disbelief, upon them shall be the Wrath of God

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r9.claim: The Quran frequently describes disbelievers, those who exchange belief for disbelief, and caprice-followers without guidance as astray.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r9.anchor: Regarding those who are astray, a far more prevalent Quranic concept, 3:90 states

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r10.claim: The verse prays to follow those whom God elevates in belief, knowledge, and uncorrupted faith, and to avoid disbelievers, some astray and some under wrath.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r10.anchor: the final verse of this sūrah can be understood as a prayer (1) to follow the way of those whom God raises in degrees

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r11.claim: Verses 6–7 depict humanity’s journey toward God and request an honorable approach rather than a disgraced one, echoing the image of walking upright on a straight path.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r11.anchor: vv. 6–7 refer to the manner in which all human beings are moving toward their Lord

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r12.claim: Past-tense blessedness conveys completed certainty, while passive wrath leaves room for repentance and avoids attributing injustice to God, who does not wrong people.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r12.anchor: Those whom Thou hast blessed conveys an action performed by God in the past tense, thus giving a sense of finality and certitude

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r13.claim: Straying may be intentional or mistaken; Moses called himself astray before his mission, and God says He found Muhammad astray and guided him, so the term can cover those not living by revelation.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r13.anchor: Being astray can result from something intentional or something done by mistake

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r14.claim: On a vertical ascent reading, wrath represents descent from God and straying represents horizontal wandering; together they symbolize three spatial dimensions and human possibilities.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r14.anchor: those who incur wrath can be understood as a reference to those upon a path of descent away from God

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r15.claim: A prophetic saying, not considered highly authentic, identifies those under wrath as Jews and those astray as Christians.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r15.anchor: Based upon a saying attributed to the Prophet, though not considered to be of the highest degree of authenticity

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r16.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r16.claim: A hadith promises forgiveness of past sins when a worshipper’s Āmīn coincides with the angels’ Āmīn.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r16.anchor: According to a ḥadīth, “When the prayer leader says

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r17.claim: Sunnis customarily say Āmīn after the Fātiḥah; it is recommended, not obligatory, and scholars differ whether it should be said aloud or quietly.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r17.anchor: Upon the completion of the Fātiḥah, it is thus customary among Sunni Muslims to say Āmīn

STUDYQURAN:1:7/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r18.claim: Āmīn is commonly a supplication meaning O God, answer us; others call it a divine Name or say Thus shall it be, akin to Hebrew Amen as an affirmation and seal of prayer.
STUDYQURAN:1:7/r18.anchor: Most understand āmīn to mean, “O God! Answer us,” which functions as a supplication

TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r1.claim: The phrase those You favored explains which straight path is meant: the way of angels, prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous who obey and worship God, as in the promise of Qur'an 4:67–69.
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r1.anchor: إبانة عن الصراط المستقيم، أي الصراط هو إذ كان كل طريق من طرق الحق صراطا مستقيما

TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r2.claim: The requested guidance is to the path God described; whoever follows it obediently will be brought to the company and dwelling of those favored, and God never breaks His promise.
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r2.anchor: ووعد من سلكه فاستقام فيه طائعا لله ولرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أن يورده مواردهم، والله لا يخلف الميعاد

TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says those favored include obedient worshippers among angels, prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous.
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r3.anchor: يقول: طريق من أنعمت عليهم بطاعتك وعبادتك من الملائكة والنبيين

TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r4.speaker: ربيع
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r4.claim: Rabīʿ interprets those favored as the prophets.

TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p176#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets those favored as believers.

TAB-FULL:v1p178/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p178/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p178/r1.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says those favored are Muhammad and those with him.
TAB-FULL:v1p178/r1.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن معه

TAB-FULL:v1p178/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p178/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p178/r2.claim: The verse clearly shows that obedience is attained only through God's favor and enabling, since the verse attributes their guidance, obedience, and worship to His blessing.
TAB-FULL:v1p178/r2.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل واضح على أن طاعة الله جل ثناؤه لا ينالها المطيعون إلا بإنعام الله بها عليهم وتوفيقه إياهم لها

TAB-FULL:v1p178/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p178/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p178/r3.claim: The wording omits the explicit object of bestowed favor because the preceding request and the adjacent phrase identifying the straight path make that favor—the upright path—clear; Arabic likewise omits words recoverable from context, as in lines by al-Nābigha and al-Farazdaq.
TAB-FULL:v1p178/r3.anchor: قد قدمنا البيان فيما مضى من كتابنا هذا عن اجتزاء العرب في منطقها ببعض من بعض

TAB-FULL:v1p180/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p180/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p180/r1.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line omits the pronoun hum, recoverable from the preceding word; similarly, the nearby wording those You favored suffices without restating the understood favor or path.
TAB-FULL:v1p180/r1.anchor: يريد: متقلديها هم، فحذف هم إذ كان الظاهر من قوله: أرباقهم دالا عليها

TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r1.claim: The first genitive parse makes ghayr an adjective for alladhīna: the relative phrase is not a fully specified proper name but indefinite-like, so it can take this adjective.
TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r1.anchor: والذين معرفة وغير نكرة؛ لأن الذين بصلتها ليست بالمعرفة المؤقتة كالأسماء التي هي أمارات بين الناس

TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r2.claim: The second genitive analysis treats alladhīna as a fully specified definite phrase and supplies a repeated ṣirāṭ: the path of those favored, the path of those outside the objects of wrath.
TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r2.anchor: وإذا وجه إلى ذلك، كانت غير مخفوضة بنية تكرير الصراط الذي خفض الذين عليها

TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r3.claim: The two genitive parses have nearly the same implication: those truly favored with guidance to the true religion are not under God's anger and are not astray.
TAB-FULL:v1p180#2/r3.anchor: وإن اختلفا باختلاف معربيهما، فإنهما يتقارب معناهما

TAB-FULL:v1p182/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p182/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p182/r1.claim: Even if ghayr repeats ṣirāṭ rather than qualifying those favored, their evident description as guided by God already implies they are neither objects of His anger nor astray.
TAB-FULL:v1p182/r1.anchor: لأن الصفة الظاهرة التي وصفوا بها قد أنبأت عنهم أنهم كذلك وإن لم يصرح وصفهم به

TAB-FULL:v1p182/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p182/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p182/r2.claim: An accusative reading of ghayr is grammatically possible but al-Ṭabarī dislikes it because it departs from the established, widely transmitted reading; it would qualify the object pronoun in عليهم and mean not objects of anger or misguidance.
TAB-FULL:v1p182/r2.anchor: وإن كنت للقراءة بها كارها لشذوذها عن قراءة القراء

TAB-FULL:v1p182/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p182/r3.speaker: بعض نحويي البصريين
TAB-FULL:v1p182/r3.claim: One Basran grammarian takes accusative ghayr as an exception from those favored: exclude those not favored or guided, and do not make us among them.
TAB-FULL:v1p182/r3.anchor: وقد كان بعض نحويي البصريين يزعم أن قراءة من نصب غير

TAB-FULL:v1p183/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r1.speaker: بعض نحويي البصريين
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r1.claim: The Basran exception analysis appeals to al-Nābigha's poem, where the awārī are excepted although they are plainly not part of the preceding group of people.
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r1.anchor: والأواري معلوم أنها ليست من عداد أحد في شيء

TAB-FULL:v1p183/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r2.speaker: نحويو الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r2.claim: Kufan grammarians reject exception: coordinating the negative wa-lā al-ḍāllīn with an exception is unattested, since Arabic coordinates exception with exception and negation with negation.
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r2.anchor: وأما نحويو الكوفيين فأنكروا هذا التأويل واستخطئوه

TAB-FULL:v1p183/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r3.claim: He prefers the universally transmitted genitive reading, taking ghayr as an adjective of those favored or as repeated ṣirāṭ; either parse is sound, and he explains the grammatical alternatives because they produce different interpretations.
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول في تأويله وقراءته عندنا القول الأول،

TAB-FULL:v1p183/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r4.claim: Those under anger are the people God describes as cursed and punished in Qur'an 5:60; He informs believers of their fate and shows them the route to salvation out of mercy.
TAB-FULL:v1p183/r4.anchor: هم الذين وصفهم الله جل ثناؤه في تنزيله فقال:

TAB-FULL:v1p188/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p188/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عدي بن حاتم
TAB-FULL:v1p188/r1.claim: The Prophet identifies those under wrath as the Jews in reports transmitted from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim.
TAB-FULL:v1p188/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " المغضوب عليهم: اليهود

TAB-FULL:v1p188/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p188/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عبد الله بن شقيق
TAB-FULL:v1p188/r2.claim: Reports from the Prophet at the siege of Wādī al-Qurā identify the besieged people under wrath as Jews.
TAB-FULL:v1p188/r2.anchor: أن رجلا أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو محاصر وادي القرى

TAB-FULL:v1p188/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p188/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p188/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses those under wrath as Jews whom God has been angry with.
TAB-FULL:v1p188/r3.anchor: يعني اليهود الذين غضب الله عليهم

TAB-FULL:v1p189/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r1.speaker: السدي عن أبي مالك وأبي صالح عن ابن عباس ومرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r1.claim: The report attributed through al-Suddī to these early authorities identifies those under wrath as Jews.
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r1.anchor: وعن ناس من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] هم اليهود

TAB-FULL:v1p189/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies those under wrath as Jews.
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] قال: هم اليهود

TAB-FULL:v1p189/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r3.speaker: ربيع
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r3.claim: Rabīʿ says those under wrath are the Jews.
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r3.anchor: عن ربيع: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] قال: اليهود

TAB-FULL:v1p189/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise identifies them as Jews.
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال ابن عباس: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] قال: اليهود

TAB-FULL:v1p189/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says those under wrath are the Jews; he also transmits the same identification from his father.
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] اليهود

TAB-FULL:v1p189/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r6.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r6.claim: One theological account says God's anger is the imposition of punishment in this life or the next, citing the drowning of Pharaoh's people and the punishment described in Qur'an 5:60.
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r6.anchor: فقال بعضهم: غضب الله على من غضب عليه

TAB-FULL:v1p189/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r7.claim: A second account understands divine anger as blame for their conduct and verbal reproach or insult.
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: غضب الله على من غضب عليه من عباده ذم منه لهم ولأفعالهم،

TAB-FULL:v1p189/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r8.claim: A third account treats anger as a real divine attribute, intelligible by affirmation but unlike human anger, which involves agitation, pain, or harm; it is an attribute like knowledge and power without creaturely limitations.
TAB-FULL:v1p189/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الغضب منه معنى مفهوم، كالذي يعرف من معاني الغضب

TAB-FULL:v1p190/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p190/r1.speaker: بعض أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v1p190/r1.claim: Some Basrans say lā before those astray is an expendable filler, appealing to poetry and to Qur'an 7:12, which they read as meaning What kept you from prostrating.
TAB-FULL:v1p190/r1.anchor: كان بعض أهل البصرة يزعم أن لا مع الضالين أدخلت تتميما للكلام والمعنى إلغاؤها

TAB-FULL:v1p190/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p190/r2.speaker: بعض أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v1p190/r2.claim: The same Basran analysis takes ghayr as meaning other than, so the favored are those other than the objects of wrath and the astray.
TAB-FULL:v1p190/r2.anchor: أنه كان يتأول غير التي مع المغضوب عليهم أنها بمعنى سوى

TAB-FULL:v1p190/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p190/r3.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v1p190/r3.claim: A Kufan grammarian rejects ghayr meaning other than because lā cannot coordinate with سوى absent a prior negative; he also rejects starting lā with an omitted-negation sense without previous negation.
TAB-FULL:v1p190/r3.anchor: لأن سوى ليست من حروف النفي والجحود

TAB-FULL:v1p192/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r1.speaker: نحوي من الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r1.claim: The Kufan answer reads al-ʿAjjāj's lā as genuine negation and explains the other poems' apparent filler lā by the negative earlier in each sentence, as in the line about Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r1.anchor: إنما جاز أن تكون لا بمعنى الحذف، لأن الجحد قد تقدمها في أول الكلام،

TAB-FULL:v1p192/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r2.claim: He prefers the Kufan analysis: lā cannot begin as an omitted negative or coordinate with other than or an exception; since ghayr can mean exception, negation, or other than, the only valid reading here is negation, making the verse ask to avoid both groups.
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r2.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وهذا القول الآخر أولى بالصواب من الأول، إذ كان غير موجود في كلام العرب

TAB-FULL:v1p192/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r3.claim: The astray are exemplified by Qur'an 5:77's People of the Book who exceed the truth, follow the desires of already astray people, and stray from the path.
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r3.anchor: هم الذين وصفهم الله في تنزيله، فقال:

TAB-FULL:v1p192/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عدي بن حاتم
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r4.claim: The Prophet identifies those astray as Christians when asked about the verse.
TAB-FULL:v1p192/r4.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {ولا الضالين} [الفاتحة: 7] قال: النصارى

TAB-FULL:v1p195/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عدي بن حاتم
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r1.claim: The Prophet tells ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim that those astray are Christians; further routes repeat this identification.
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r1.anchor: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الضالين: النصارى

TAB-FULL:v1p195/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عبد الله بن شقيق
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r2.claim: Reports from a questioner during the siege at Wādī al-Qurā have the Prophet identify the people asked about as Christians, the astray.
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r2.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو محاصر وادي القرى قال: قلت: من هؤلاء؟ قال: " هؤلاء الضالون: النصارى

TAB-FULL:v1p195/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies those astray as Christians.

TAB-FULL:v1p195/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the astray as Christians whom God led astray through their fabrication about Him; the prayer asks for the true monotheistic faith, protection from Jewish wrath and Christian error, and mercy to prevent their punishment.
TAB-FULL:v1p195/r4.anchor: قال: وغير طريق النصارى الذين أضلهم الله بفريتهم عليه.

TAB-FULL:v1p197/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وناس من أصحاب النبي وربيع وعبد الرحمن بن زيد وأبوه
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r1.claim: The cited authorities—through Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī's report, Rabīʿ, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd and his father—identify those astray as Christians.
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r1.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: " {ولا الضالين} [الفاتحة: 7] النصارى

TAB-FULL:v1p197/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r2.claim: In Arabic, anyone deviating from the intended road is astray; Christians are so called because they miss the truth and take a religious route other than the straight one.
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r2.anchor: وكل حائد عن قصد السبيل وسالك غير المنهج القويم فضال عند العرب

TAB-FULL:v1p197/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r3.claim: Both Jews and Christians are astray and under wrath, but God labels each by a true, recognizable characteristic, without listing every blameworthy trait of either group.
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r3.anchor: إن كلا الفريقين ضلال مغضوب عليهم، غير أن الله جل ثناؤه وسم كل فريق منهم من صفته لعباده

TAB-FULL:v1p197/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r4.speaker: بعض أهل الغباء من القدرية
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r4.claim: Some Qadariyyah wrongly infer from calling Christians astray and Jews objects of wrath that human acts belong only to people and that God does not cause their misguidance; al-Ṭabarī says this betrays ignorance of Arabic attribution and the many verses naming God as guide and misguider.
TAB-FULL:v1p197/r4.anchor: وقد ظن بعض أهل الغباء من القدرية أن في وصف الله جل ثناؤه النصارى بالضلال

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r1.claim: Arabic attributes an act sometimes to its immediate agent and sometimes to its cause: although God creates an act, it is properly attributed to the person who acquires it by power and choice and to God as its creator; Qur'an 10:22 illustrates attribution of sailing to ships though another causes their motion, and 45:23 calls God the guide and misguider.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r1.anchor: ومن شأن العرب إضافة الفعل إلى من وجد منه، وإن كان مسببه غير الذي وجد منه أحيانا،

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.claim: Answering why al-Fātiḥa has seven verses if two contain its meanings: earlier scriptures each included only some meanings, while the Qur'an gathers all of them for Muhammad's community and adds many more.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r2.anchor: إن الله تعالى ذكره جمع لنبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولأمته بما أنزل إليه من كتابه معاني لم يجمعهن بكتاب

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.claim: The Torah is admonition and detailed instruction, Psalms praise and glorification, and Gospel admonition and reminder, but none has a miracle proving its recipient; the Qur'an contains these meanings and more.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r3.anchor: كالتوراة التي هي مواعظ وتفصيل، والزبور الذي هو تحميد وتمجيد، والإنجيل الذي هو مواعظ وتذكير؛ لا معجزة في واحد منها

TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.claim: Among the Qur'an's distinctive merits is its miraculous arrangement and composition: rhetoricians cannot compose even a sura as short as one of its chapters.
TAB-FULL:v1p199/r4.anchor: نظمه العجيب، ورصفه الغريب، وتأليفه البديع، الذي عجزت عن نظم مثل أصغر سورة منه الخطباء

TAB-FULL:v1p203/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p203/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p203/r1.claim: Al-Fātiḥa’s extended, distinctive form and combined praise, commands, warnings, stories, arguments, and examples establish Muhammad’s prophethood and teach God’s greatness, blessings, dependence on Him, and fear of disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v1p203/r1.anchor: أراد أن يجمع برصفه العجيب، ونظمه الغريب، المنعدل عن أوزان الأشعار، وسجع الكهان

TAB-FULL:v1p203/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p203/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة عن رسول الله
TAB-FULL:v1p203/r2.claim: The Prophet reports God praises the servant’s recitation of praise, mercy, and sovereignty, then says the invocation from You alone we worship through the end belongs to the servant.
TAB-FULL:v1p203/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا قال العبد: {الحمد لله رب العالمين}

TABATABAI:1:6-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r1.claim: Straight path, road, and way are near synonyms; the requested straight way is the route followed by those God blessed, and thus the goal of worship: that pure worship occur upon it.
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r1.anchor: فالصراط الذي من شأنه ذلك هو الذي سئل الهداية إليه وهو بمعنى الغاية للعبادة

TABATABAI:1:6-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r2.claim: All creatures travel toward God and meet Him; the Qur'an distinguishes the straight way of worship from the opposing way of following Satan.

TABATABAI:1:6-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r3.claim: The way of divine worship is near because God is near and responds to supplication, while those who disbelieve call from a distant place, making their destination far.
TABATABAI:1:6-7/r3.anchor: فبين تعالى أنه قريب من عباده وأن الطريق الأقرب إليه تعالى طريق عبادته ودعائه

TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r1.claim: The Qur'an depicts an upward route and a downward route; those struck by wrath fall, while misguidance is associated with shirk, producing three groups: believers, the wrathful, and the wandering astray.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r1.anchor: وعند ذلك تقسم الناس في طرقهم ثلثه أقسام من طريقه إلى فوق

TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r2.claim: The straight path is the believers' way, excluding the wrathful and the astray, but the believers themselves have ranks and divisions.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r2.anchor: يدل على أن نفس الطريق الأول أيضا يقع فيه انقسام

TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#2/r3.claim: Shirk, injustice, and error are coextensive in their actual instances; therefore the straight path contains none of them, inwardly or outwardly, and represents complete knowledge and practice of tawhid.

TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r1.claim: The description of believers free of injustice in 6:82 confirms safety on the path and promises complete guidance; the author reads the active participle as referring to the future.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r1.anchor: وفيه تثبيت للأمن في الطريق ووعد بالاهتداء التام

TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r2.claim: The blessed are those who obey God and the Messenger: prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and righteous people, described by complete outward and inward submission.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r2.anchor: من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين وحسن أولئك رفيقا

TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r3.claim: Ordinary faithful are with the blessed in a lower rank, not yet among them; the similar joining of believers to martyrs and truthful ones is likewise a future association.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r3.anchor: وفي صف دون صفهم لمكان مع ولمكان قوله وحسن أولئك رفيقا

TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r4.claim: People of the straight path have a higher station than ordinary believers; if the latter's remaining deficiency were completed, they could rise from companionship to that rank, perhaps through knowledge of God.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#3/r4.anchor: لو تمت فيهم كانوا من الذين أنعم الله عليهم، وارتقوا من منزلة المصاحبة معهم إلى درجة الدخول فيهم

TABATABAI:1:6-7#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#4/r1.claim: The straight-path people receive a gift higher than complete faith; God names one straight path but many ways, which differ with their travelers and may lead into or constitute that path.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#4/r1.anchor: فالصراط المستقيم أصحابه منعم عليهم بنعمة هي أرفع النعم قدرا، يربو على نعمة الإيمان التام

TABATABAI:1:6-7#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#4/r2.claim: Because some people combine belief with shirk, an individual way can contain error whereas the singular straight path cannot; each way bears its own degree of deficiency or distinction.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#4/r2.anchor: فبين أن من الشرك وهو ضلال ما يجتمع مع الإيمان وهو سبيل، ومنه يعلم أن السبيل يجامع الشرك

TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r1.claim: The straight path is the spirit shared by the many ways, like one soul persisting through the changing stages of a body; individual ways can suffer flaws that do not characterize the path itself.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r1.anchor: فمثل الصراط المستقيم بالنسبة إلى سبل الله تعالى كمثل الروح بالنسبة إلى البدن

TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r2.claim: Ways differ in purity and proximity and can mix with shirk or error, but they all connect with or realize the straight path at some level.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r2.anchor: فللسبيل مراتب كثيرة من جهة خلوصه وشوبه وقربه وبعده

TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r3.claim: The rain-and-valleys parable shows that hearts receive heavenly knowledge according to their differing capacities, despite a single source of provision.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#5/r3.anchor: فبين أن القلوب والأفهام في تلقي المعارف والكمال مختلفة، مع كون الجميع متكئة منتهية إلى رزق سماوي واحد

TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r1.claim: Paths to God differ in rank and proximity to the source of reality; the author lists faith, worship, sincerity, and humility and their opposites, and says receptivity to divine knowledge varies by capacity.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r1.anchor: أن الطرق إلى الله مختلفة كمالا ونقصا وغلاء ورخصا

TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r2.claim: Those firmly established on the straight path also govern the other ways and are entrusted by God with guiding His servants.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r2.anchor: فكذلك أصحابه الذين مكنهم الله تعالى فيه وتولى أمرهم وولاهم أمر هداية عباده

TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r3.claim: The Sahih lexicon defines guidance as indication; Hijazis take a second object directly, while others use ila, and the author accepts the latter grammatical description.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#6/r3.anchor: أن الهداية هي الدلالة على ما في الصحاح، وفيه أن تعديتها لمفعولين لغة أهل الحجاز

TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r1.claim: Proponents cite the verse saying the Prophet does not guide whom he loves to argue that his guidance differs from guidance belonging to God.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r1.anchor: إنك لا تهدي من أحببت ولكن الله يهدي من يشاء

TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r2.claim: The author replies that the verse about the Prophet not guiding his beloved negates complete guidance that belongs to God, not guidance altogether.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#7/r2.anchor: وفيه أن النفي المذكور نفي لحقيقة الهداية التي هي قائمة بالله تعالى، لا نفي لها أصلا

TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r5.claim: A follower of the final, fullest law may still be below Noah or Abraham in realized divine knowledge and spiritual station; asking for the latter's rank is therefore coherent.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#8/r5.anchor: وليس ذلك إلا أن حكم الشرائع والعمل بها غير حكم الولاية الحاصلة من التمكن فيها والتخلق بها

TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r1.claim: Some commentators answer that religion and core beliefs are one across revelations, while the final law has wider legal coverage and earlier communities serve as examples because they preceded us.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r1.anchor: أن دين الله واحد وهو الإسلام، والمعارف الأصلية وهي التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد

TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r2.claim: The author rejects that answer's assumptions that spiritual realities have no degrees and prophets equal ordinary believers in real perfection, with rank arising only from legislated status.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r2.anchor: فأفضل الأنبياء المقربين مع أخس المؤمنين من حيث الوجود وكماله الخارجي التكويني على حد سواء

TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r3.claim: He traces that error to materialism or to neglecting reflective Qur'anic interpretation in favor of ordinary surface understanding.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#9/r3.anchor: إما القول بالاكتفاء بالحس اعتمادا على العلوم المادية وإما إلغاء التدبر في القرآن

TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r1.claim: The pure word that ascends to God is belief and knowledge; righteous action raises and supports it but does not itself ascend to Him.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#10/r1.anchor: فالذي يصعد إليه تعالى هو الكلم الطيب وهو الاعتقاد والعلم، وأما العمل الصالح فشأنه رفع الكلام الطيب

TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r5.speaker: علي
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r5.claim: Ali says the blessed are those favored with success in religion and obedience, not merely wealth or health, since disbelievers and sinners may also enjoy those worldly gifts.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r5.anchor: أنعمت عليهم بالتوفيق لدينك وطاعتك، لا بالمال والصحة

TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.claim: The Prophet transmits God's division of al-Fatiha between Himself and the servant: each phrase receives divine acknowledgement and a tailored promise of blessing, mercy, ease of judgment, reward, help, and fulfillment of the servant's requests.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#11/r6.anchor: قسمت فاتحة الكتاب بيني وبين عبدي فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي، ولعبدي ما سأل

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the whole Fātiḥa is divine speech voiced on the worshipper’s behalf as praise and confession of servitude in prayer.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r1.anchor: السورة بتمامها كلام تكلم به الله سبحانه في مقام النيابة عن عبده فيما يقوله إذا وجه وجهه إلى مقام الربوبية

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r2.claim: The Fātiḥa is uniquely divided: one half belongs to God and the other half to the servant.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r2.anchor: أنها مقسمة قسمين، فنصف منها لله ونصف منها للعبد

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r3.claim: In a concise, clear form, the Fātiḥa contains the Qurʾān’s central teachings, branches, promises, warnings, stories, and guidance.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r3.anchor: تشتمل على جميعها في أوجز لفظ وأوضح معنى

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r4.claim: Al-Ṣadūq reports a similar narration from al-Riḍā; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says it supports his reading of the Fātiḥa as prayer speech for the worshipper.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r4.anchor: وروى قريبا منه الصدوق في العلل عن الرضا عليه السلام، والرواية كما ترى تفسر سورة الفاتحة في الصلاة

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r5.claim: He contrasts the Fātiḥa with the Christian Lord’s Prayer, criticizing its father-language, political-sounding petitions, reciprocal forgiveness, and requests to escape testing as incoherent with earthly life as a trial.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r5.anchor: ولكن من الذي يستجيب هذا الدعاء الذي هو بشعارات الأحزاب السياسية أشبه؟

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r6.claim: He objects that asking God to exchange forgiveness for forgiveness makes overlooking right conditional, and that asking to avoid trial misunderstands life as a place of testing and growth.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r6.anchor: فالدار دار الامتحان والاستكمال وما معنى النجاة لولا الابتلاء والامتحان

TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r7.claim: He questions the claim that Islam has no intellectual superiority because all divine laws teach monotheism, virtue, and good deeds, leaving only social fruits to distinguish religions.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#12/r7.anchor: إن جميع شرائع الله تدعو إلى التوحيد وتصفية النفوس بالخلق الفاضل والعمل الصالح، وإنما تتفاضل الأديان في عراقة ثمراتها الاجتماعية

TABATABAI:1:6-7#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:1:6-7#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:1:6-7#14/r1.claim: Reports applying Qurʾānic verses to the Imams or their enemies are abundant, sometimes numbering in the hundreds, so he generally omits them unless useful to the discussion.
TABATABAI:1:6-7#14/r1.anchor: ربما تبلغ المئين، ونحن بعد هذا التنبيه العام نترك إيراد أكثرها في الأبحاث الروائية لخروجها عن الغرض في الكتاب

TABRISI:1:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7/r1.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
TABRISI:1:7/r1.claim: Hamza pronounces the hā in ʿalayhim and its parallels with ḍamma and the mīm quiescent; Yaqub uses ḍamma on hā preceded by a silent yā in duals and masculine and feminine plurals.
TABRISI:1:7/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة عليهم بضم الهاء وإسكان الميم وكذلك لديهم وإليهم وقرأ يعقوب بضم كل هاء قبلها ياء ساكنة

TABRISI:1:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7/r2.claim: Other transmitted forms vary the hā and mīm, add or omit a linking wāw, or connect it only before a following consonant; the regions and readers differ in these choices.
TABRISI:1:7/r2.anchor: وقرئ في الشواذ: عليهموا قراءة ابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى الثقفي وعليهمي قراءة الحسن البصري

TABRISI:1:7/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعمرو بن عبد الله الزبيري
TABRISI:1:7/r3.claim: They read the phrase as 'the path of those on whom You bestowed favor'; this form is also reported from the Prophet's household.
TABRISI:1:7/r3.anchor: وقرأ صراط من أنعمت عليهم عمر بن الخطاب وعمرو بن عبد الله الزبيري وروي ذلك عن أهل البيت

TABRISI:1:7/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7/r4.speaker: الأعرج
TABRISI:1:7/r4.claim: A noncanonical variant reads ghayr al-maghdubi in the accusative.
TABRISI:1:7/r4.anchor: وقرئ أيضا في الشواذ غير المغضوب عليهم بالنصب

TABRISI:1:7/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعلي
TABRISI:1:7/r5.claim: Umar reads ghayr al-ḍāllīn, and the same form is also reported from Ali.
TABRISI:1:7/r5.anchor: وقرأ: غير الضالين عمر بن الخطاب وروي ذلك عن علي ع

TABRISI:1:7/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7/r6.speaker: السراج
TABRISI:1:7/r6.claim: The ḍamma on hā in ʿalayhim restores the original form hum; al-Sarraj calls it the old recitation and a Qurayshi and Hijazi dialect.
TABRISI:1:7/r6.anchor: قال السراج وهي القراءة القديمة ولغة قريش وأهل الحجاز ومن حولهم

TABRISI:1:7/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7/r7.claim: Hamza singles out these forms because their preceding yā was historically an alif, which does not permit a kasra on the hā.
TABRISI:1:7/r7.anchor: وإنما خص حمزة هذه الحروف الثلاثة بالضم لأن الياء قبلها كانت ألفا

TABRISI:1:7/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7/r8.claim: Some reciters connect the hā's ḍamma to a wāw, while forms without wāw lighten the ending; other variants assimilate or preserve vowels according to ease and the preceding yā.
TABRISI:1:7/r8.anchor: ومن قرأ عليهموا فإنه اتبع الهاء ما أشبهها وهو الياء وترك ما لا يشبه الياء

TABRISI:1:7#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#2/r1.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:1:7#2/r1.claim: Sibawayh explains kasra on hā after yā or kasra as phonetic lightening and likens it to imāla; a following silent wāw changes to yā after kasra.
TABRISI:1:7#2/r1.anchor: قال سيبويه: الهاء تكسر إذا كان قبلها ياء أو كسرة لأنها خفيفة وهي من حروف الزيادة

TABRISI:1:7#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#2/r2.claim: Ṣirāṭ alladhīna is either an adjective of al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm or its apposition; apposition implies repeating the syntactic governor, unlike an adjective.
TABRISI:1:7#2/r2.anchor: { صراط الذين } صفة لقوله: { الصراط المستقيم } ويجوز أن يكون بدلا عنه

TABRISI:1:7#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#2/r3.claim: Alladhīna is a relative noun, and anʿamta ʿalayhim is its relative clause; together they form a genitive noun annexed to ṣirāṭ.
TABRISI:1:7#2/r3.anchor: والذين موصول وأنعمت عليهم: صلة وقد تم بها اسما مفردا يكون في موضع جر بإضافة صراط إليه

TABRISI:1:7#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#2/r4.claim: In the genitive, ghayr may be an apposition to the pronoun in ʿalayhim or to alladhīna, or an adjective of the relative phrase despite ghayr usually modifying an indefinite noun.
TABRISI:1:7#2/r4.anchor: وأما غير المغضوب عليهم ففي الجر فيه ثلاثة أوجه: أحدها: أن يكون بدلا من الهاء والميم

TABRISI:1:7#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:1:7#3/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows ghayr as an adjective of alladhīna because the relative phrase does not target named individuals, much like a generic man like you.
TABRISI:1:7#3/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: وإنما جاز ذلك لأن الذين ههنا ليس بمقصود قصدهم

TABRISI:1:7#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#3/r2.speaker: علي بن عيسى الرماني
TABRISI:1:7#3/r2.claim: Al-Rummani allows the adjective because alladhīna with its clause functions like a common noun rather than a proper name.
TABRISI:1:7#3/r2.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى الرماني: إنما جاز أن يكون نعتا للذين

TABRISI:1:7#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#3/r3.speaker: أبو بكر السراج
TABRISI:1:7#3/r3.claim: Al-Sarraj says ghayr becomes definite when its definite complement has one known opposite: the favored people are the ones other than those under anger.
TABRISI:1:7#3/r3.anchor: والذي عندي أن غير في هذا الموضع مع ما أضيف إليه معرفة لأن حكم كل مضاف إلى معرفة أن يكون معرفة

TABRISI:1:7#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#3/r4.speaker: أبو بكر السراج
TABRISI:1:7#3/r4.claim: In the accusative, ghayr may be a circumstantial qualifier, a disconnected exception, or an explanatory specification meaning 'I mean'.
TABRISI:1:7#3/r4.anchor: وفي نصب غير ثلاثة أوجه أيضا: أحدها أن يكون نصبا على الحال

TABRISI:1:7#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#3/r5.claim: The word maghdūb need not be pluralized because the plural pronoun in ʿalayhim already marks those who incur anger.
TABRISI:1:7#3/r5.anchor: ولم يجز أن يقال غير المغضوبين عليهم لأن الضمير قد جمع في عليهم فاستغنى عن أن يجمع المغضوب

TABRISI:1:7#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#3/r6.speaker: البصريون
TABRISI:1:7#3/r6.claim: The Basran grammarians take lā as an emphatic extra particle of negation, eliminating an ambiguity that could otherwise allow separate readings of the coordinated words.
TABRISI:1:7#3/r6.anchor: فذهب البصريون إلى أنها زائدة لتوكيد النفي وذهب الكوفيون إلى أنها بمعنى غير

TABRISI:1:7#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#3/r7.speaker: الكوفيون
TABRISI:1:7#3/r7.claim: The Kufans interpret lā as meaning ghayr, so the phrase excludes both the angered and the astray.
TABRISI:1:7#3/r7.anchor: وذهب الكوفيون إلى أنها بمعنى غير

TABRISI:1:7#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#3/r8.speaker: علي بن عيسى الرماني
TABRISI:1:7#3/r8.claim: Al-Rummani explains lā in the exception reading as an extra particle, like in the line about a pit of destruction and the Qur'anic phrase 'that you should not prostrate'.
TABRISI:1:7#3/r8.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى الرماني من نصب على الاستثناء جعل لا صلة كما أنشد أبو عبيدة

TABRISI:1:7#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#4/r1.claim: The favored people are those who obey God and the Messenger, as identified in the verse listing prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous.
TABRISI:1:7#4/r1.anchor: معنى الآية بيان الصراط المستقيم أي: صراط من أنعمت عليهم بطاعتك وهم الذين ذكرهم الله تعالى

TABRISI:1:7#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#4/r2.claim: The root of niʿma carries the sense of intensification or addition, as in grinding medicine thoroughly.
TABRISI:1:7#4/r2.anchor: وأصل النعمة المبالغة والزيادة يقال دققت الدواء فأنعمت دقه أي بالغت في دقه

TABRISI:1:7#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#4/r3.speaker: جميع المفسرين
TABRISI:1:7#4/r3.claim: Commentators broadly identify those under anger as Jews, supported by verses about divine anger and the Sabbath violators turned into apes.
TABRISI:1:7#4/r3.anchor: وأراد بالمغضوب عليهم اليهود عند جميع المفسرين الخاص والعام

TABRISI:1:7#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#4/r4.claim: The astray are identified as Christians, supported by the warning against those who went astray and led many astray.
TABRISI:1:7#4/r4.anchor: وأراد بالضالين النصارى بدلالة قوله تعالى

TABRISI:1:7#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#4/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
TABRISI:1:7#4/r5.claim: Hasan says both Jews and Christians are both astray and under anger, though God marks each group by a distinguishing epithet despite their shared traits.
TABRISI:1:7#4/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: إن الله تعالى لم يبرئ اليهود من الضلالة

TABRISI:1:7#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#4/r6.claim: Other interpreters take both descriptions as applying to all unbelievers, with the two attributes conveying different benefits.
TABRISI:1:7#4/r6.anchor: وقيل المراد بالمغضوب عليهم والضالين جميع الكفار وإنما ذكروا بالصفتين لاختلاف الفائدتين

TABRISI:1:7#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#4/r7.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
TABRISI:1:7#4/r7.claim: Al-Jurjani instead reads the language generically as a prayer to avoid a state like that of the angered, not a reference to a particular people.
TABRISI:1:7#4/r7.anchor: واختار الإمام عبد القاهر الجرجاني قولا آخر قال: إن حق اللفظ فيه أن يكون خرج مخرج الجنس

TABRISI:1:7#5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#5/r1.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
TABRISI:1:7#5/r1.claim: Al-Jurjani says a speaker may ask to join those favored or be spared the state of the angered without referring to any known group; Antara's beloved is likewise not compared to a third person.
TABRISI:1:7#5/r1.anchor: إنه لم يرد أن يشبهها بإنسان هو محب مكرم عنده أو عند غيره ولكنه أراد أن يقول

TABRISI:1:7#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#5/r2.claim: Divine anger is God's will to impose deserved punishment, curse the people, and disavow them; its root denotes severity.
TABRISI:1:7#5/r2.anchor: وأما الغضب من الله تعالى فهو إرادته انزال العقاب المستحق بهم ولعنهم وبراءته منهم وأصل الغضب الشدة

TABRISI:1:7#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#5/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#5/r3.claim: Ḍalāl fundamentally means destruction and, in religion, departure from truth; the author cites 'we were lost in the earth' and 'He destroyed their works'.
TABRISI:1:7#5/r3.anchor: وأصل الضلال الهلاك ومنه قوله إذا ضللنا في الأرض أي هلكنا

TABRISI:1:7#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#5/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#5/r4.claim: The wording avoids saying that those favored are simply other than the angered, out of courtesy and preference for refined expression.
TABRISI:1:7#5/r4.anchor: وإنما لا يقال الذين أنعمت عليهم غير الذين غضبت عليهم مراعاة للأدب في الخطاب واختيارا لحسن اللفظ المستطاب

TABRISI:1:7#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#5/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:1:7#5/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Muslim reports al-Sadiq's explanation that the seven oft-repeated verses are the Opening of the Book.
TABRISI:1:7#5/r5.anchor: في تفسير العياشي رحمه الله روى محمد بن مسلم عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

TABRISI:1:7#5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#5/r6.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:1:7#5/r6.claim: The Prophet says God bestowed the Opening of the Book from a treasure of Paradise, including the basmala and the verse about people turning away when God alone is mentioned.
TABRISI:1:7#5/r6.anchor:
وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إن الله تعالى من علي بفاتحة الكتاب من كنز الجنة

TABRISI:1:7#6/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#6/r1.claim: Al-ḥamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin is described as the utterance of Paradise's people when they thank God for their good reward.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r1.anchor: و { الحمد لله رب العالمين } دعوى أهل الجنة حين شكروا لله حسن الثواب

TABRISI:1:7#6/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r2.speaker: جبرائيل
TABRISI:1:7#6/r2.claim: Gabriel says that whenever a Muslim says 'Lord of the Worlds', God and the inhabitants of heaven affirm him.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r2.anchor: قال جبرائيل عليه السلام ما قالها مسلم إلا صدقه الله تعالى وأهل سمائه

TABRISI:1:7#6/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#6/r3.claim: Iyyaka naʿbudu expresses pure worship, iyyaka nastaʿīn is the best way to seek needs, and the straight path is the path of the prophets.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r3.anchor: إياك نعبد إخلاص للعبادة وإياك نستعين أفضل ما طلب به العباد حوائجهم اهدنا الصراط المستقيم صراط الأنبياء

TABRISI:1:7#6/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#6/r4.claim: This explanation identifies the angered as Jews and the astray as Christians.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r4.anchor: وهم الذين أنعم الله عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم اليهود ولا الضالين النصارى

TABRISI:1:7#6/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:1:7#6/r5.claim: Al-Halabi reports that al-Sadiq read Malik yawm al-din and ihdina ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm; another narration interprets the latter as referring to Ali, the Commander of the Faithful.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r5.anchor: وروى محمد الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام أنه كان يقرأ ملك يوم الدين ويقرأ اهدنا صراط المستقيم

TABRISI:1:7#6/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:1:7#6/r6.claim: Jamil reports al-Sadiq's instruction that a follower behind an imam should say al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin when the imam finishes al-Fatiha.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r6.anchor: وروى جميل عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال: إذا كنت خلف إمام ففرغ من قراءة الفاتحة

TABRISI:1:7#6/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:1:7#6/r7.claim: Fudayl ibn Yasar reports al-Sadiq's instruction to say al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-alamin after finishing al-Fatiha.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r7.anchor: وروى فضيل بن يسار عنه عليه السلام قال: إذا قرأت الفاتحة ففرغت من قراءتها فقل الحمد لله رب العالمين

TABRISI:1:7#6/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#6/r8.claim: The sura's sequence begins with recognition of God's visible favors, so the worshiper starts with the basmala as invocation and acknowledgment of the benefactor's divinity and mercy.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r8.anchor: إذا عرف نعم الله سبحانه بالمشاهدة وكان له من نفسه بذلك أعدل شاهد وأصدق رائد ابتدأ بآية التسمية استفتاحا باسم المنعم

TABRISI:1:7#6/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#6/r9.claim: Recognition of God's favors to oneself and others leads to praise and recognition that He is Lord of all creatures.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r9.anchor: اشتغل بالشكر له والحمد فقال الحمد لله ولما رأى نعم الله تعالى على غيره واضحة كما شاهد آثارها على نفسه لائحة عرف أنه رب الخلائق أجمعين

TABRISI:1:7#6/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#6/r10.claim: Universal grace and provision lead to the name Rahman; despite people's shortcomings, God forgives, delays punishment, and does not withdraw His blessings, so He is Rahim.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r10.anchor: لما رأى شمول فضله للمربوبين وعموم رزقه للمرزوقين قال الرحمن لما رأى تقصيرهم في واجب شكره

TABRISI:1:7#6/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#6/r11.claim: Because people oppress one another, the worshiper acknowledges a future day when the wronged receive justice from the wrongdoer and says Malik yawm al-din.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r11.anchor: ولما رأى ما بين العباد من التباغي والتظالم والتكالم والتلاكم وأن ليس بعضهم من شر بعض بسالم على أن وراءهم يوما ينتصف فيه للمظلوم من الظالم

TABRISI:1:7#6/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#6/r12.claim: Knowing God as Creator, provider, and merciful giver establishes that He alone is worthy of worship; the speaker shifts to direct address as if seeing a king face-to-face.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r12.anchor: ولما صار الموصوف بهذا الوصف كالمدرك له بالعيان المشاهد بالبرهان تحول عن لفظ الغيبة إلى لفظ الخطاب فقال: إياك نعبد

TABRISI:1:7#6/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#6/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#6/r13.claim: Conflicting desires, doubts, and opinions leave no helper but God, so the worshiper requests assistance for obedience with all its causes.
TABRISI:1:7#6/r13.anchor: ولما رأى اعتراض الأهواء والشبهات وتعاور الآراء المختلفات ولم يجد معينا غير الله تعالى سأله الإعانة على الطاعات بجميع الأسباب

TABRISI:1:7#7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#7/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#7/r1.claim: Having reached knowledge of truth, the worshiper asks for lasting guidance and protection from error because he lacks infallibility; the request includes knowledge of rulings, Islamic practice, and following the divinely appointed Imams.
TABRISI:1:7#7/r1.anchor: وتبين له أنه بلغ من معرفة الحق المدى واستقام على منهج الهدى ولم يأمن العثرة لارتفاع العصمة سأل الله تعالى التوفيق للدوام عليه والثبات

TABRISI:1:7#7/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:1:7#7/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:1:7#7/r2.claim: The worshiper asks to join God's chosen beneficiaries and be protected from those who oppose truth, blind themselves to guidance, or doubt clear proofs and stray from the right way.
TABRISI:1:7#7/r2.anchor: فسأله أن يلحقه بهم ويسلك به سبيلهم وأن يعصمه عن مثل أحوال الزالين المزلين والضالين المضلين ممن عاند الحق

THALABI:v1p121#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p121#2/r1.claim: The phrase is an appositive to the first ṣirāṭ: those favored are guided and cared for in affirmation of divine unity; the author identifies them as prophets and believers and cites 4:69.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r1.anchor: صراط بدل من الأول الذين أنعمت عليهم يعني: طريق الذين أنعمت عليهم بالتوفيق والرعاية

THALABI:v1p121#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p121#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies them as the people of Moses and Jesus before they changed God's favors upon them.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم قوم موسى وعيسى من قبل أن يغيروا نعم الله عليهم

THALABI:v1p121#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r3.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
THALABI:v1p121#2/r3.claim: Shahr ibn Ḥawshab identifies them as the Prophet's companions and his household.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r3.anchor: وقال شهر بن حوشب هم أصحاب الرسول صلى الله عليه ورضي عنهم وأهل بيته (عليهم السلام) .

THALABI:v1p121#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v1p121#2/r4.claim: ʿIkrima says they were granted steadfastness in faith and uprightness.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r4.anchor: وقال عكرمة: أنعمت عليهم) بالثبات على الإيمان والاستقامة

THALABI:v1p121#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r5.speaker: علي بن الحسين بن داود
THALABI:v1p121#2/r5.claim: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Dāwūd says they give thanks in ease and patience in hardship.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r5.anchor: وقال علي بن الحسين بن داود: أنعمت عليهم بالشكر على السراء والصبر على الضراء

THALABI:v1p121#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r6.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
THALABI:v1p121#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faḍl understands the favor as God completing His blessing upon them.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r6.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: يعني أتممت عليهم النعمة

THALABI:v1p121#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p121#2/r7.claim: Niʿma originally conveys increase or doing something thoroughly; the usage أنعما for Abū Bakr and ʿUmar means they surpassed others in good.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r7.anchor: وأصل النعمة المبالغة والزيادة، يقال: دققت الدواء فأنعمت دقه

THALABI:v1p121#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r8.speaker: الصادق
THALABI:v1p121#2/r8.claim: Al-Ṣādiq reads the phrase as ‘the path of those whom You favored’; ʿAmr ibn al-Zubayr and ʿAlī also read it this way, with lām governing the following word.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الصادق: (صراط من أنعمت عليهم) ، وبه قرأ عمرو بن الزبير وعلي

THALABI:v1p121#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p121#2/r9.claim: The common reading has ʿalayhim with kasra on hāʾ and a still mīm.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r9.anchor: الأولى: عليهم- بكسر الهاء وجزم الميم- وهي قراءة العامة

THALABI:v1p121#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r10.speaker: الأعمش
THALABI:v1p121#2/r10.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read ʿalayhum with ḍamma on hāʾ and a still mīm; a report attributes it to the Prophet and ʿUmar as well.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r10.anchor: الثانية: عليهم- بضم الهاء وجزم الميم- وهي قراءة الأعمش وحمزة

THALABI:v1p121#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r11.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
THALABI:v1p121#2/r11.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read with ḍamma on both hāʾ and mīm and an added wāw.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r11.anchor: الثالثة: عليهم- بضم الهاء والميم وإلحاق الواو- وهي قراءة عيسى بن عمر

THALABI:v1p121#2/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r12.speaker: ابن كثير
THALABI:v1p121#2/r12.claim: Ibn Kathīr and al-Aʿraj read with kasra on hāʾ, ḍamma on mīm, and an appended wāw.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r12.anchor: الرابعة: عليهمو- بكسر الهاء وضم الميم وإلحاق الواو- وهي قراءة ابن كثير

THALABI:v1p121#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p121#2/r13.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p121#2/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads with kasra on both hāʾ and mīm and an appended yāʾ.
THALABI:v1p121#2/r13.anchor: الخامسة: عليهم- بكسر الهاء والميم وإلحاق الياء- وهي قراءة الحسن

THALABI:v1p122/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p122/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عطاء الخفاف
THALABI:v1p122/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAṭāʾ al-Khaffāf transmits from Abū ʿAmr a kasra on hāʾ and a lightly articulated ḍamma on mīm.
THALABI:v1p122/r1.anchor: والسادسة: عليهم- بكسر الهاء وضم الميم مضمومة مختلسة- وهي رواية عبد الله بن عطاء الخفاف

THALABI:v1p122/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p122/r2.speaker: عمرو بن حامد
THALABI:v1p122/r2.claim: ʿAmr ibn Ḥāmid reads the word with kasra on both hāʾ and mīm.
THALABI:v1p122/r2.anchor: والسابعة: عليهم- بكسر الهاء والميم- وهي قراءة عمرو بن حامد

THALABI:v1p122/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p122/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p122/r3.claim: The variants arise from the original ḍamma, neighboring yāʾ favoring kasra, the heaviness of ḍamma beside a still yāʾ, assimilation, easing, and appending wāw or yāʾ for vowel harmony.
THALABI:v1p122/r3.anchor: فمن ضم الهاء رده إلى الأصل لأنه لو أفرد كان مضموما عند الابتداء به

THALABI:v1p122/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p122/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p122/r4.claim: Ghayr functions as an adjective for alladhīna despite the usual definiteness mismatch, because alladhīna here is not a fully specified definite but means whoever is truthful rather than lying.
THALABI:v1p122/r4.anchor: غير: صفة الذين. والذين معرفة ولا توصف المعارف بالنكرات

THALABI:v1p122/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p122/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p122/r5.claim: The intended sense is ‘other than the path of those upon whom You were angry.’
THALABI:v1p122/r5.anchor: ومعنى كلامه: غير صراط الذين غضبت عليهم

THALABI:v1p123/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p123/r1.speaker: قوم
THALABI:v1p123/r1.claim: One group explains God's anger as His will to take vengeance on sinners.
THALABI:v1p123/r1.anchor: فقال قوم: هو إرادة الانتقام من العصاة

THALABI:v1p123/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p123/r2.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p123/r2.claim: Another explanation calls anger a kind of punishment opposite to divine pleasure.
THALABI:v1p123/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو جنس من العقاب يضاد والرضا

THALABI:v1p123/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p123/r3.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p123/r3.claim: A third explanation defines anger as condemnation of sinners for the ugliness of their acts.
THALABI:v1p123/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو ذم العصاة على قبح أفعالهم

THALABI:v1p123/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p123/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p123/r4.claim: God's anger does not reach sinful believers; it reaches unbelievers.
THALABI:v1p123/r4.anchor: ولا يلحق غضب الله تعالى العصاة من المؤمنين بل يلحق الكافرين

THALABI:v1p123/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p123/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p123/r5.claim: The misguided are those who have strayed from guidance; the root suggests loss or disappearance, and a poetic line uses it of a people who lost their way.
THALABI:v1p123/r5.anchor: وأصل الضلال الهلاك، يقال ضل الماء في اللبن إذا خفي وذهب

THALABI:v1p123/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p123/r6.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v1p123/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj says lā may coordinate with ghayr because ghayr already carries negation, effectively meaning neither those angered nor those astray; this is not possible when ghayr means ‘other than.’
THALABI:v1p123/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج وغيره: وإنما جاز أن يعطف ب (لا) على غير لأن غير متضمن معنى النفي

THALABI:v1p123/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p123/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
THALABI:v1p123/r7.claim: Khalīl ibn Aḥmad transmits Ibn Kathīr's accusative reading of ghayr al-maghḍūb.
THALABI:v1p123/r7.anchor:
وروى الخليل

 بن أحمد عن ابن كثير: غير المغضوب نصبا

THALABI:v1p123/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p123/r8.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v1p123/r8.claim: ʿUmar and ʿAlī read ‘and not those astray.’
THALABI:v1p123/r8.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب وعلي بن أبي طالب- رضي الله عنهما-: (وغير الضالين)

THALABI:v1p123/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p123/r9.speaker: السختياني
THALABI:v1p123/r9.claim: Al-Sakhtiyānī reads lā al-ḍāllīn with hamza to break the meeting of two unvowelled consonants.
THALABI:v1p123/r9.anchor: وقرأ السختياني (ولأ الضالئين) بالهمزة لالتقاء الساكنين

THALABI:v1p124/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p124/r1.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v1p124/r1.claim: In a report from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, the Prophet identifies those angered with the Jews and those astray with the Christians.
THALABI:v1p124/r1.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: غير المغضوب عليهم قال: «اليهود

THALABI:v1p124/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p124/r2.speaker: رسول الله
THALABI:v1p124/r2.claim: At Wādī al-Qurā, the Prophet points to Jews fighting him as those angered and to Christians as the other party, those astray.
THALABI:v1p124/r2.anchor: وهو بوادي القرى على فرسه فسأله رجل من القين، فقال: يا رسول الله، من هؤلاء الذين يقاتلونك

THALABI:v1p124/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p124/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p124/r3.claim: The author links divine anger against Jews to 5:60 and the description of Christians as astray to 5:77.
THALABI:v1p124/r3.anchor: وتصديق هذا الحديث حكم الله تعالى بالغضب على اليهود في قوله: هل أنبئكم بشر

THALABI:v1p124/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p124/r4.speaker: الواقدي
THALABI:v1p124/r4.claim: Al-Wāqidī glosses those angered as people who oppose and disobey, and those astray as people who leave religion and faith.
THALABI:v1p124/r4.anchor: وقال الواقدي: غير المغضوب عليهم بالمخالفة والعصيان، ولا الضالين عن الدين والإيمان

THALABI:v1p124/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p124/r5.speaker: التستري
THALABI:v1p124/r5.claim: Al-Tustarī identifies innovation with those angered and departure from Sunna with those astray.
THALABI:v1p124/r5.anchor: وقال التستري: غير المغضوب عليهم البدعة، ولا الضالين عن السنة

ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n3/r1.claim: The blessed are those given prophetic guidance and enabled to benefit from it.
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n3/r1.anchor: by vouchsafing to them prophetic guidance and enabling them to avail themselves thereof

ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r1.claim: Nearly all commentators equate God's condemnation with the harmful consequences people incur by knowingly rejecting guidance and disobeying its commands.
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r1.anchor: According to almost all the commentators, God's "condemnation" (ghadab, lit., "wrath") is synonymous

ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r2.claim: Zamakhshari reads the final two descriptions as qualifying the blessed people: they were not condemned and did not go astray.
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r2.anchor: Some commentators (e.g., Zamakhshari) interpret this passage as follows

ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r3.speaker: Baghawi and Ibn Kathir
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r3.claim: Baghawi and Ibn Kathir reject Zamakhshari's qualification reading and take the final phrases as distinct groups on a wrong course, as Asad does.
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r3.anchor: Other commentators (e.g., Baghawi and Ibn Kathir) do not subscribe to this interpretation

ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r4.speaker: Al-Ghazali and Muhammad 'Abduh
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r4.claim: They distinguish informed rejection of a recognized message from straying when truth never arrived or arrived too corrupted to recognize.
ASAD-NOTES:1:6#n4/r4.anchor: Al-Ghazali or, in recent times, Muhammad 'Abduh) held the view that the people described

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r1.claim: Ṣirāṭ in ṣirāṭ alladhīna is an appositive restating the first ṣirāṭ in meaning, like calling one's father by the name Zayd.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {صراط الذين}: (صراط) بدل من (الصراط) # الأول (¬1)، وهو بدل الشيء من نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r2.claim: Relative pronouns such as alladhī and alladhīna are incomplete until their clause supplies a predicate, verb, circumstance, or conditional structure; that clause must contain a pronoun referring back.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r2.anchor: وقوله: {الذين} النحويون يسمون (الذي والتي) وتثنيتهما، وجمعهما: الأسماء الموصولة، والأسماء النواقص، والأسماء المبهمة، وذلك لأنها (¬4) أسماء لا تتم إلا بصلاتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r3.claim: Alladhīna is indeclinable across nominative, accusative, and genitive because it remains incomplete without its relative clause and thus resembles a particle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r3.anchor: و (الذين) لا يظهر فيه # الإعراب (¬1)، تقول (¬2) في الرفع والنصب والجر: (الذين)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r4.claim: A singular indeclinable relative gains case marking in the dual because particles are not dualized, but the plural is again a single form like hāʾulāʾ and remains indeclinable.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r4.anchor: قيل: إن جميع ما لا يعرب في الواحد مشبه بالحرف الذي جاء لمعنى، فإذا ثنيته بطل شبه الحرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq, following Sībawayh, al-Khalīl, and al-Akhfash, says the original form of alladhī was ladh on the faʿl pattern.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وأصل (الذي)، (لذ) على وزن (عم)، كذلك قال سيبويه والخليل والأخفش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r6.speaker: أبو الفتح الموصلي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r6.claim: Abū al-Fatḥ al-Mawṣilī says the alif and lām in alladhī and related forms are fixed additions: other relatives such as man, mā, and ayy are definite without them, and the relative clause itself identifies alladhī.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p530/r6.anchor: وأما الألف واللام فيه (¬2)، فقال أبو الفتح الموصلي (¬3): (الألف واللام) في (الذي) و (التي)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r1.claim: The added lām is retained because alladhī enables a clause to describe a definite noun: ordinary clauses are indefinite, and the particle alif-lām cannot attach directly to a clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r1.anchor: قيل: إن (الذي) (¬1) إنما وقع في الكلام توصلا إلى وصف المعارف بالجمل، وذلك أن الجمل نكرات.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r2.claim: Alladhī turns the sentence into a relative clause and marks the description as definite, as in the construction Zayd alladhī abūhu munṭaliq.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r2.anchor: فجاؤوا ب (الذي) متوصلين به إلى وصف المعارف بالجمل، وجعلوا (¬6) الجملة التي كانت صفة للنكرة صلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r3.claim: In the verse, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim means the road of those on whom You bestowed favor; the clause could describe an indefinite qawm directly, but not a definite group.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p533/r3.anchor: وبيان ما ذكرنا (¬1) من الآية أن معنى قوله: {صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} صراط القوم الذين أنعمت عليهم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r1.claim: God's inʿām is His favor and gift; niʿma is a verbal noun used in place of the infinitive inʿām, as nafaqa stands for infāq.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {أنعمت عليهم}، إنعام الله تعالى: منه (¬9) وعطاؤه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r2.claim: The hāʾ in ʿalayhim may be pronounced with either kasra or ḍamma; kasra follows because yāʾ is related to kasra and the lighter transition is preferred.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {عليهم} يجوز كسر (الهاء) فيه وضمه (¬1). فمن كسر فلأن الياء أخت الكسرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
