WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r3.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r3.claim: Sībawayh says wāw was added after masculine hāʾ just as alif was added after feminine hāʾ, balancing their added endings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r3.anchor: زعم (¬5) سيبويه أن (¬6) (الواو) زيدت على (الهاء) في المذكر، كما زيدت (الألف)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says wāw was added to make the faint throat-produced hāʾ clearer with a labial long vowel; the connecting wāw drops in pause and changes to yāʾ after kasra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: و (¬1) القول في هذه (الواو (¬2)) أنها زيدت لخفاء (الهاء)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r5.claim: Because hāʾ is a weak barrier, the preceding kasra acts as if it directly preceded the added wāw; that explains kasra in ʿalayhi and its retention in ʿalayhim.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p535/r5.anchor: وبهذه (¬2) العلة كسرت الهاء في (عليه) وكان الأصل (عليهو) (¬3) فقلبت (¬4) الواو

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r1.speaker: ابن السراج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r1.claim: Ibn al-Sarrāj explains the plural mīm's sukūn as lightening: the dual's alif already signals two, while the indispensable plural mīm lets speakers drop wāw without ambiguity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r1.anchor: وقال ابن السراج (¬3): إنما أسكنوا لأنه قد أمن اللبس، إذ كانت (الألف) في التثنية قد دلت على الاثنين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r2.speaker: ورش عن نافع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r2.claim: Warsh from Nāfiʿ pronounces plural mīm with ḍamma and links a following initial hamza with wāw; dropping hamza and moving its vowel requires the mīm to recover its original ḍamma and lengthen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r2.anchor: وروى ورش (¬5) عن نافع (¬6) ضم الميم ووصلها بواو إذا (¬7) استقبلها # همزة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r3.claim: Warsh lengthens before an open hamza rather than transferring its fatḥa to mīm, which could make the plural resemble the dual; he follows the same pattern before other hamza vowels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r3.anchor: فلما مدها عند الهمزة المفتوحة ولم ينقل حركتها إليها مخافة الالتباس فعل ذلك به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r4.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī pronounce hāʾ and mīm with ḍamma at a following hamzat al-waṣl: mīm returns to its original vowel to break two sukūns, then hāʾ follows it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r4.anchor: وكان حمزة والكسائي يضمان (¬7) (الهاء) و (الميم) عند ألف الوصل (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses kasra for mīm as the usual vowel when breaking two sukūns and also gives hāʾ kasra to avoid a heavy kasra-to-ḍamma transition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r5.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو (¬2) يكسرها عند ألف الوصل؛ لأنه يكسر الميم على أصل تحريك الساكن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r6.claim: Readers who keep hāʾ kasra but give mīm ḍamma restore mīm to its original vowel without restoring hāʾ, which was not forced by the context.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r6.anchor: وأما من كسر (الهاء) وضم (الميم) عند ألف الوصل (¬4)، فإنه يقول: لما احتجت إلى حركة الميم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says those given favor were the people of Moses and Jesus before they changed God's blessings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p541/r7.anchor: فأما التفسير: فقال ابن عباس: {الذين أنعمت عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7]: هم قوم موسى وعيسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r1.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r1.claim: ʿIkrima says God favored them by keeping them firm in faith and steadfast.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r1.anchor: وقال عكرمة: أنعمت عليهم بالثبات على الإيمان والاستقامة (¬8).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r2.claim: Another interpretation identifies them with the people in 4:69 who obey God and the Messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r2.anchor: وقيل: هم الذين ذكرهم الله في قوله (¬1) سبحانه: {ومن يطع الله والرسول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r3.speaker: محمد بن جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r3.claim: Ibn Jarīr says the verse is elliptical: guide us along the path of those You favored with guidance to the path, since Arabic omits words when context supplies them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r3.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: في الآية اختصار، معناه: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بالهداية إلى الصراط.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r4.claim: Ghayr can be genitive as an appositive to alladhīna or as its adjective; the adjective is valid because the relative phrase here is not a particular, singled-out group.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {غير المغضوب عليهم} (غير) (¬3) ينخفض على ضربين (¬4):

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r5.claim: Ghayr may instead be accusative as a circumstantial expression or an exception meaning except those under wrath; as a circumstantial phrase it means not those under wrath.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r5.anchor: ويجوز (النصب) على ضربين: على الحال، والاستثناء (¬1)، أما الاستثناء:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r6.speaker: ابن السراج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sarrāj additionally allows accusative as an implied aʿnī, I mean; al-Khalīl reportedly allowed it as a detached form of praise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r6.anchor: قال ابن السراج (¬4): ويجوز عندي النصب على (¬5) (أعنى).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r7.claim: The author chooses genitive: although ghayr and mithl are usually indefinite even when annexed to a definite word, a known thing with one known opposite makes ghayr definite.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r7.anchor: والاختيار الكسر (¬1). ولا يلزم وصف المعرفة بالنكرة؛ لأن حكم كل مضاف إلى معرفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r8.claim: If a known thing has one known opposite, ghayr annexed to that opposite is definite, as in movement versus stillness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p543/r8.anchor: فأما إذا كان شيء معرفة له ضد واحد، وأردت إثباته ونفي ضده، وعلم السامع (¬5) ذلك الضد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r1.speaker: صاحب الحجة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r1.claim: The author of al-Ḥujja says genitive ghayr is either apposition or adjective; apposition implies repeating the governing factor, as the repeated prepositions in 7:75 show.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r1.anchor: قال صاحب (¬7) "الحجة": أما الخفض في (¬8) (غير) فعلى البدل أو الصفة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r2.speaker: صاحب الحجة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r2.claim: Apposition differs from an adjective because an indefinite can replace a definite and an expressed noun can replace a pronoun, neither of which is allowed for modifiers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r2.anchor: وأيضا (¬3) فإن النكرة تبدل من المعرفة، والمظهر من المضمر (¬4)، وهذا مما لا يجوز في الصفة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r3.speaker: صاحب الحجة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r3.claim: Apposition also repeats the understood governing case factor, while both apposition and adjective clarify the first noun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r3.anchor: وكما أعيدت اللام الجارة في البدل (¬6)، فكذلك يكون العامل الناصب (¬7) والرافع في تقدير التكرير.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r4.speaker: صاحب الحجة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r4.claim: As apposition, ghayr has a clear meaning whether construed definite or indefinite, since both definite and indefinite apposition are accepted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r4.anchor: فمن جعل (¬1) (غير) في الآية (¬2) بدلا، كان تأويله بينا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r5.speaker: صاحب الحجة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r5.claim: As an adjective, ghayr can modify alladhīna here only because the relative phrase does not single out a particular group, making it like an indefinite description.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r5.anchor: وأما من قدر (غير) صفة و (الذين (¬7) فإنما جاز أن يصف (الذين) ب (غير)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r6.speaker: صاحب الحجة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r6.claim: A parallel is the definite al-rajul described by mithluka: the article does not identify a particular man, so the description remains nonspecific.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r6.anchor: قولهم: قد أمر (¬2) بالرجل مثلك فيكرمني (¬3)، فوصف الرجل بمثلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r7.claim: In the verse, ghayr al-maghḍūb describes the favored people and is definite because one favored with faith is not under wrath.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p546/r7.anchor: وكذلك قوله: {أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم} فغير المغضوب عليهم، هم الذين أنعم عليهم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r1.claim: In 4:95, ghayr can modify the believers sitting out: the intended contrast is healthy nonparticipants versus those who strive.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r1.anchor: ومما (¬5) جاء (غير) فيه صفة (¬6) قوله: {لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ rejects accusative ghayr as an exception, arguing that a positive exception cannot be followed by negative lā in coordination.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r2.anchor: وأما من نصب (غير) على الاستثناء، فإن الفراء ينكر جواز (¬10) ذلك،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r3.claim: Those allowing exception say an exception resembles negation, so all came except Zayd can mean all came, not Zayd; lā can coordinate by meaning or be an addition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r3.anchor: ومن أجاز (¬4) الاستثناء فإنه يقول: لا يمتنع دخول (لا) (¬5) بعد الحرف العاطف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r4.claim: The author concludes al-Farrāʾ's objection has no force, since lā can follow exception under either of those analyses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r4.anchor: وإذا جاز دخول (لا) (¬1) مع الاستثناء لهذين الوجهين (¬2) فلا وجه لقول من أنكره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r5.claim: Lā may also be added after ghayr as a circumstantial expression, adjective, or appositive; the Qur'an uses it in 57:29.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r5.anchor: وكذلك (¬4) يجوز زيادة (لا) في قول من جعل (غير) حالا أو صفة أو بدلا.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r6.speaker: some grammarians
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r6.claim: Some allow added lā only after a preceding negation, but the author rejects that restriction and cites Saʿida al-Hudhalī's affirmative example.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p550/r6.anchor: والذين يجوزون زيادة (لا) يقولون: إنما تجوز إذا تقدمه نفي (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r1.claim: Before an indefinite, lā may be extra; if not extra, it either joins the noun as one genitive compound or contributes negation without affecting the noun's case.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r1.anchor: وهذا الحرف (¬6) -أعني: (لا) - يدخل (¬7) في النكرة على وجهين:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r2.claim: Examples of the compound include min lā shayʾ and bi-lā māl; lā plus noun functions as a single expression, like fifteen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r2.anchor: وذلك نحو قولهم: (غضب من لا شيء، وجئت بلا مال) ف (لا) مع الاسم المنكور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r3.claim: The non-compounding negator leaves case untouched, as in al-Nābigha's no uncle and al-Shammākh's sleepless night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r3.anchor: والآخر: ألا تعمل (¬4) (لا) في اللفظ، ويراد بها معنى النفي،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r4.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says lā in wa-lā al-ḍāllīn prevents misreading al-ḍāllīn as coordinated with those favored; it marks coordination with ghayr, which implies negation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r4.anchor: وقال صاحب "النظم" (¬2): دخلت (لا) في قوله: {ولا الضالين} لمعنى من المعاني،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r5.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r5.claim: He illustrates the disambiguating role with a poem: lā before ʿUmar keeps him inside the Prophet's disapproval clause instead of starting a new sentence praising Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p553/r5.anchor: أدخل (لا) (¬6) في قوله: (ولا عمر)؛ لأنه لو لم يدخل لاحتمل أن يكون انقطاع القصة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r1.claim: The root of ḍalāl is disappearance: water disappears into milk, and a disbeliever disappears from the path of truth; 32:10 uses the word for bodies lost in earth after death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ولا الضالين} أصل الضلال في اللغة الغيبوبة، يقال: ضل الماء في اللبن إذا غاب،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r2.claim: Aḍalla can mean to hide or bury something, as in al-Mukhabbal's poem about Banū Qays losing their leader.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r2.anchor: ويقال: أضللت الشيء إذا غيبته، [وأضللت الميت إذا غيبته] (¬6) في التراب ودفنته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r3.claim: Thus the astray person is absent from truth and has deviated from right guidance; the verb has reported variant forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r3.anchor: فالضال هو الغائب عن الحق الزائغ عن الرشد، ويقال: ضل يضل، وضل يضل لغتان،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r4.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r4.claim: A report from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, attributed to the Prophet, identifies those under wrath as Jews and the astray as Christians; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r4.anchor: فأما التفسير فروى عدي بن حاتم (¬3) عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في تفسير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r5.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r5.claim: A second report says the Prophet at Wādī al-Qurā was asked by a man from Bali about two groups; he pointed to Jews as those under wrath and Christians as astray; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r5.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان بوادي القرى (¬5) على فرسه (¬6)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود ومجاهد وغيرهم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r6.claim: Commentators support this interpretation by citing God's anger against Jews in 5:60 and the description of people who strayed in 5:77; Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and Mujāhid hold it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r6.anchor: قال المفسرون: وتصديق هذا حكم الله عز وجل بالغضب على اليهود (¬5) في قوله:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r7.claim: The identification also fits a rare accusative reading of ghayr as exception, excluding Jews and Christians from those favored; the author notes that this reading is anomalous.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r7.anchor: وهذا التفسير يوافق في ظاهر اللفظ قراءة من قرأ (غير) بالنصب على

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r8.claim: For the standard reading, the sense is the path of those favored who are neither under wrath nor astray; denying these traits implicitly attributes them to others, supporting implication in discourse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r8.anchor: وتصحيح هذا التفسير على القراءة المعروفة هو أن (¬5) المعنى: اهدنا صراط المنعم عليهم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r9.claim: The Prophet and the exegetes have already identified who are under wrath and who are astray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p557/r9.anchor: قد بينه النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وذكره المفسرون (¬4).

WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r1.claim: Those favored with guidance are the people of Moses and Jesus before they changed God's favor.
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r1.anchor: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم بالهداية وهم قوم موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام قبل أن يغيروا نعم الله

WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r2.claim: Another view identifies the favored people with those named in the verse about being with those God favored.
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r2.anchor: وقيل هم الذين ذكرهم الله عز وجل في قوله تعالى فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم الآية

WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r3.claim: Those under wrath are Jews; God's wrath means His willing punishment.
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r3.anchor: غير المغضوب عليهم أي غير الذين غضبت عليهم وهم اليهود ومعنى الغضب من الله تعالى إرادة العقوبة

WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r4.claim: Those astray are Christians, and Muslims ask to avoid both their error and the Jews' incurred wrath.
WAHIDI-QT:1:7/r4.anchor: ولا الضالين أي ولا الذين ضلوا وهم النصارى فكأن المسلمين سألوا الله تعالى أن يهديهم طريق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r4.claim: Those granted favor are the followers of Moses and Jesus before they changed God's favor.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r4.anchor: وهم قوم موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام قبل أن يغيروا نعم الله عز وجل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r5.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r5.claim: Another identification is those described as being with the people God favored in 4:69.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r5.anchor: وقيل: هم الذين ذكرهم الله عز وجل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r6.claim: Those under divine anger are the Jews; God's anger means His willing punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r6.anchor: وهم اليهود، ومعنى الغضب من الله تعالى: إرادة العقوبة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r7.claim: The people who went astray are the Christians; Muslims ask to avoid their deviation from truth as well as the Jews' incurred anger.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:1:5-7/r7.anchor: فكأن المسلمين سألوا الله تعالى أن يهديهم طريق الذين أنعم عليهم

ELMALILI:1:7/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r1.speaker: Sâhib-i Keşşâf
ELMALILI:1:7/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf prefers reading the verb as an absolute act of bestowing, with no expressed object.
ELMALILI:1:7/r1.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf evvelkini, İbn Cerîr Taberî ikinciyi tercih etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:1:7/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r2.speaker: İbn Cerîr Taberî
ELMALILI:1:7/r2.claim: Ibn Jarir prefers supplying an implicit object, construing the phrase as bestowing something upon them.
ELMALILI:1:7/r2.anchor: Sâhib-i Keşşâf evvelkini, İbn Cerîr Taberî ikinciyi tercih etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:1:7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7/r3.claim: Elmalılı finds the objectless reading safer from ellipsis and rhetorically eloquent, although the second reading is the verb's more apparent construction.
ELMALILI:1:7/r3.anchor: Haziften selâmet itibariyle evvelkisi evlâ ve beliğ ve fakat bir kinaye mâhiyetindedir.

ELMALILI:1:7/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir uses the following worship covenant to construe the implied object as obedience and worship; Elmalılı instead finds the path itself the more apparent object.
ELMALILI:1:7/r4.anchor: Ancak İbn Cerîr Taberî bu mef‘ûlü إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ karînesiyle tâat ve ibadete ircâ‘ederek

ELMALILI:1:7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7/r5.claim: Elmalılı's final reading supplies no pronoun: unrestricted bestowal is a rhetorical indirect expression for bestowing the path.
ELMALILI:1:7/r5.anchor: Ve en doğrusu burada zamiri takdir

ELMALILI:1:7/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7/r6.claim: This construal makes the path itself a supreme blessing, its bestowal a supreme divine aid, and the path theirs through divine gift and their following it.
ELMALILI:1:7/r6.anchor: Bunda câlib-i dikkat üç nokta vardır. Evvelâ, bizzat tarîk ve sırâtın ehemm-i ni‘âm olan bir ni‘met-i ‘uzmâ olduğu anlaşılır.

ELMALILI:1:7/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7/r7.claim: Receiving the route or means to a blessing secures repeated access to it, unlike receiving a single instance of the blessing.
ELMALILI:1:7/r7.anchor: Çünkü herhangi bir nimetin tarîkine, kanununa nâil olmak

ELMALILI:1:7/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7/r8.claim: Asking for a single benefit is a small request; asking for its path and steadfastness brings it repeatedly, so the opening prayer asks for the straight path.
ELMALILI:1:7/r8.anchor: burada ibtidâ “bize nimet ver” denmeyip de ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ duasıyla doğru yol istemenin tâlim buyurulması

ELMALILI:1:7/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7/r9.claim: The greatest path is the route by which divine aid arrives; without God's enabling, even a known and followed route may fail to reach its goal.
ELMALILI:1:7/r9.anchor: Tarîkin en büyüğü de me‘ûnet-i ilâhiyenin tarîk-i vürûdudur. Bunun en kısası da müstakīm olan tarîktir.

ELMALILI:1:7/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7/r10.claim: The straight path is a religion and community that carries people through the worship covenant; its beneficiaries are a historically witnessed, successful example, as the next phrase specifies.
ELMALILI:1:7/r10.anchor: Bu yol إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ahdinde sebat ile yürütecek olan bir din ve millettir.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r1.claim: The recipients of blessing are not one bounded historical group but innumerable people and communities appearing across human history under God's nurture.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r1.anchor: İbtidâ-i beşeriyetten bu âna kadar peyderpey gelmiş

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r2.claim: Their existence is certain, and asking for their path proceeds from that certainty; their specific members can be identified mentally according to what blessing means.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r2.anchor: Bu nokta yakīnîdir. Ve ‘ale’l-ıtlâk bunların sırâtını talep etmek de bu yakīn ile harekettir.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r3.claim: Qur'an 4:69 names prophets, the truthful, martyrs, the righteous, and their believing companions as the truly blessed; this is the fullest listing, initially viewed from early Islam.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r3.anchor: Kur’an bize bu cinsten birçok cemaatler gösterecektir ki وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r4.claim: For Muslims, Muhammad and his Companions form an unambiguous historical example of the blessed community, whose worldly and otherworldly success had no historical parallel.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r4.anchor: Bize gelince; bu numunenin bütün ibhamlarından ârî bir ‘ahd-i hâricîsi vardır ki o da Hâtemü’l-Enbiyâ Muhammed Mustafâ

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r5.claim: Umar's humble patched garment amid conquests and justice exemplifies the companions' spiritual joy and stature above imperial luxury.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r5.anchor: Ömer’in sırtındaki yamalı bir gömlek âlemin gözüne kisrâların, kayserlerin tâc-ı haşmetlerinden çok yüksek bir hiss-i ibtihâc saçıyordu.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r6.claim: When Umar seemed shaken on the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr emerged and guided him and the community back onto Muhammad's path.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r6.anchor: Hazret-i Sıddîk bütün sıddîkiyetiyle ibrâz-ı vücûd ederek onu ve herkesi irşad etmiş ve cemaati kemâ fi’s-sâbık sırât-ı Muhammedîde yürütmüştü.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r7.claim: During the Hijra cave crisis, Muhammad reassured the grieving Abu Bakr that God was with them, citing Qur'an 9:40.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r7.anchor: diye onu tesliye ve tatmin eden ancak Hazret-i Muhammed olmuş idi.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r8.claim: Many earlier and later exegetes explain the path as Muhammad's and his Companions' way and Sunna; considered within the wider class, they remain its exemplary community.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r8.anchor: Hazret-i Muhammed’in ve ashâb-ı kirâmının tarîki, sünneti ile tefsir etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r9.claim: Grammatically, the relative phrase qualifies those under wrath and indicates the source of Islam's quality of piety.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r9.anchor: “ٱلَّذِينَ,”غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ’nin sıfatıdır. Ve İslâm’daki haslet-i takvânın menşe’ini gösterir.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r10.claim: Because adjectives agree with their nouns in definiteness, while gayr is indefinite unless annexed to a complete opposite, the adjective reading signals a mentally specified antecedent.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r10.anchor: Arapça’da sıfat ile mevsuf arasında ta‘rîf veya tenkîr cihetinden dahi mutabakat şarttır.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r11.claim: Some who appear blessed are actually subject to wrath or astray, so gayr excludes these and restricts the blessed to those enjoying sound, safe blessing.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r11.anchor: Mün‘âmun ‘aleyh görünenler içinde hakikatte mahkûm-i gazab veya dâll olan nice kimseler de bulunur.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r12.claim: If blessing is taken absolutely, gayr cannot be an adjective and may instead be read as a substitute; Elmalılı will reject that analysis in favor of the adjective.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r12.anchor: in‘âm ıtlâkıyla mülâhaza edilir ve الذ�ن de bu sıla ile cinsen veya ‘ahd-i hâricî ile ma‘rife tanılır ise “gayr” ona sıfat olamaz, belki bedel olabilir.

ELMALILI:1:7#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r13.claim: Al-Kashshaf, followed by Qadi and others, allows treating gayr as a substitute; Elmalılı reports Ebussuud's rejection.
ELMALILI:1:7#2/r13.anchor: vesâire bu bedeliyeti tecviz etmişlerdir. Fakat Ebussuud tefsirinde bunu bihakkın reddeylemiştir.

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r1.claim: Anger is the soul's agitation toward retaliation at something disliked, opposed to satisfaction; Turkish equivalents include anger, indignation, and wrath.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r1.anchor: “Gazab” nefsin bir mekruh karşısında irâde-i intikām ile heyecânıdır ki rızânın zıddıdır.

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r2.claim: When attributed to God, anger means its ultimate end, the will to retaliate or impose punishment, and is compatible with merciful lordship: punishing an oppressor serves mercy to the oppressed.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r2.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah’a nisbet edildiği zaman gazab infi‘âlât-ı nefsâniyeden tecrid ile müntehâ ve gayesinde isti‘mâl edilir de irâde-i intikam veya inzâl-i ukūbet mânası murad olunur.

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r3.claim: A temporary punishment or pain that prepares future blessings does not make someone one of those under wrath; outcomes determine the judgment, as 2:155 illustrates.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r3.anchor: وَلَنَبْلُوَنَّكُم بِشَىْءٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْخَوْفِ وَٱلْجُوعِ وَنَقْصٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْأَمْوَٰلِ وَٱلْأَنفُسِ

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r4.claim: Dalaal means straying from the right path, intentionally or accidentally, opposite guidance; it can progress from heedlessness or bewilderment to loss and ruin.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r4.anchor: Dalâl” ve “dalâlet”, doğru yoldan ‘amden veya hatâen sapmaktır ki “hüdâ”nın mukabilidir.

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r5.claim: The term first concerns departure from a physical route and extends to mental and spiritual matters; Turkish usage distinguishes religious dalalet from intellectual or verbal sapıklık.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r5.anchor: Esasında mahsüs ve maddî yoldan sapmaktır. Ve sonra ma‘neviyyât ve ma‘kūlâtta da müte‘âref olmuştur.

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r6.claim: The definite articles in the wrath and deviation phrases most naturally mark generic, comprehensive categories, excluding every unbelieving path from the fully safe blessing.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r6.anchor: Burada gerek ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ ve gerek ٱلضَّآلِّينَ’deki harf-i ta‘rîflerin istiğrak veya cins için olduğu zâhirdir.

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, the definite articles may refer to the earliest external examples; excluding even their minimum certain cases rhetorically entails avoiding all worse cases.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r7.anchor: harf-i ta‘rîflerin akdem olan ‘ahd-i hâricî mânasına hamllerinde dahi aynı mânayı dolayısıyla istihsâl mümkindir.

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r8.claim: Qur'an also attributes divine wrath to disbelievers generally and describes those who reject God's way as far astray, supporting the comprehensive reading.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r8.anchor: وَلَٰكِن مَّن شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًۭا فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r9.claim: The Qur'an explicitly says that those who disbelieve and obstruct God's way have gone far astray, extending the category beyond specific communities.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r9.anchor: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَصَدُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ قَدْ ضَلُّوا۟ ضَلَٰلًۢا بَعِيدًا

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r10.claim: The Quran associates Jews with wrath and Christians with deviation, citing 2:61 for Jews; 5:77 separately identifies Christians with deviation.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r10.anchor: Yehûd hakkında ekseriya وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r11.claim: The Quran describes Christians as having strayed from the right way, citing 5:77.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r11.anchor: Nasârâ hakkında da قُلْ يَٰٓأَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ لَا تَغْلُوا۟ فِى دِينِكُمْ غَيْرَ ٱلْحَقِّ

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r12.claim: Jews and Christians remain distinguishable from other unbelievers in close dealings, such as permission to eat their slaughter and marry their daughters, and are Islam's nearest opposite.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r12.anchor: Yehûd ile Nasârâ’nın kestiklerini yemek ve kızlarını nikâh edebilmek gibi yakın mu‘âmelâtta diğer ehl-i şirkten farklarını

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r13.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim, as quoted by al-Durr al-Manthur, says he knows of no exegetical disagreement identifying those under wrath as Jews and those astray as Christians.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r13.anchor: demiştir ki: “‘Mağdûbun ‘aleyhim’in Yehûd ve ‘dâllîn’in Nasârâ ile tefsîrinde beyne’l-müfessirîn hilâf bilmiyorum.”

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r14.claim: Elmalılı says Ibn Hibban and Hakim judged the relevant reports sound, Tirmidhi judged them fair, and many hadith scholars transmitted them.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r14.anchor: Tirmizî de hüsnüne hükmetmiş ve bunları birçok muhaddisîn tahric eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r15.claim: Some exegetes object that restricting the Qur'anic wording to two groups would violate its generality, and prefer treating Jews and Christians as examples.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r15.anchor: bazı müfessirîn buna ilişmiş ve nassın umûmiyet üzere ibkāsıyla Yehûd ve Nasârâ’yı birer misâl olarak telakkī etmeyi muvâfık görmüştür.

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r16.claim: Elmalılı accepts the external-reference reading only if Jews and Christians are minimum certain examples, so exclusion of them implies exclusion of all others; limiting the verse to them alone contradicts reason and decisive reports.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r16.anchor: bunlar ednâ-yı müteyakkan olarak tasavvur edilirse diğerlerinden ihtirâz-ı ‘âm bi’l-evleviyye sâbit olacağı

ELMALILI:1:7#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r17.claim: The worship covenant already clearly excludes polytheists, while this verse explicitly excludes Jews and Christians and implicitly excludes the others, a rhetorically apt distinction.
ELMALILI:1:7#3/r17.anchor: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ’de şirkleri zâhir olan müşrikîn-i sâireden vâzıhan

ELMALILI:1:7#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r1.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r1.claim: Elmalılı cites a hadith that Tirmidhi grades hasan, transmitted from Adi b. Hatim, in which the Prophet says Jews are under wrath and Christians are astray.
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r1.anchor: Aleyhi’s-salâtü ve’s-selâm Efendimiz’in “Yehûd mağdûbun ‘aleyhim, Nasârâ da dullâldir” buyurduğunu Tirmizî Sahîh’inin

ELMALILI:1:7#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r2.speaker: Adî b. Hâtim
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r2.claim: Adi recounts that the Prophet welcomed him, took his hand, helped a woman and child with their need, then spoke with him about faith; Adi subsequently professed Islam.
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r2.anchor: Cemaat ‘İşte bu Adî b. Hâtim’dir’ dediler. Ben ise emansız, mükâtebesiz gelmiştim

ELMALILI:1:7#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r3.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r3.claim: The Prophet warns listeners to give charity, however little, as protection from Hell; at judgment God will ask what they prepared from the gifts they received.
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r3.anchor: Resûlullah kalktı, namaz kıldı, ba‘dehu onları tergībe başladı. Diyordu ki: ‘Velev bir sâ‘, velev yarım sâ‘

ELMALILI:1:7#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r4.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r4.claim: The Prophet says that if a person cannot give even half a date, a kind word can serve as protection; he reassures the audience that God's help removes fear of poverty.
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r4.anchor: Her biriniz Allah’a varacak, O da ona şu söyleyeceğimi söyleyecektir: «Ben size göz kulak vermedim mi?»

ELMALILI:1:7#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r5.speaker: Adî b. Hâtim
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r5.claim: Adi recalls thinking about how the Prophet's assurances compared with the bandits of the Tay mountains.
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r5.anchor: Adî b. Hâtim hazretleri bunu rivayet ettikten sonra şunu da ilâve etmiş: “Bunu dinlerken ben gönlümden

ELMALILI:1:7#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r6.claim: Saying that Jews are among those under wrath is not equivalent to saying that all those under wrath are Jews; the hadiths make them examples, not the exhaustive referent.
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r6.anchor: Fakat “Yehûd mağdûbun ‘aleyhimdir” deme kle “el-mağdûbi ‘aleyhim Yehûd’dur” demek arasında büyük fark vardır.

ELMALILI:1:7#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r7.claim: Because an external-reference reading is plausible without restricting the Qur'an to non-mutawatir reports, both interpretations of the hadiths should be applied; the external reading implies comprehensive exclusion.
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r7.anchor: takyîd-i nas mahzûru vârid olmayacağı cihetle

ELMALILI:1:7#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r8.claim: The generic reading excludes all others explicitly, while the external-reference reading excludes other unbelievers implicitly; Elmalılı finds the latter more consistent with the Qur'anic context because it distinguishes polytheists from People of the Book.
ELMALILI:1:7#4/r8.anchor: ikincide ise bu fark dahi gösterilmiş olur ki biz bunu siyâk-ı Kur’ân’a daha muvâfık buluyoruz.

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r1.claim: Although Christians then ruled major powers and could appear blessed, Elmalılı says their true condition and afterlife were perilous.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r1.anchor: Nasârâ’ya gelince; o zaman bunlar Roma’nın vârisi, İstanbul’un sâhibi olarak yer yüzündeki iki büyük devletin biri

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r2.claim: Christianity abandoned divine unity for the Trinity and idols, though its recognition of a Father-God retained a limited unitarian element compared with Manichaeans and Zoroastrians.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r2.anchor: Evvelemirde tevhîd-i Hakk’a bedel ‘akīde-i teslîse saplanmışlar

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r3.claim: Its doctrine made God both one and three through the union of three persons, violating the law of noncontradiction and stunting intellectual development.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r3.anchor: hem bir, hem üç idi. Böyle aklın tenakuz kanununu da çiğneyen bir ‘akīde-i teslîs

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r4.claim: Elmalılı says Christians derailed inherited sciences and abandoned proof for emotional inclination, using psychology and popular sentiment to influence ordinary people and rationalize excess.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r4.anchor: vâris oldukları bütün ulûm u fünûnu çığırından çıkarmış ve tarîk-i isbâttan ayrılıp sadece zevk-i kalbîye

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r5.claim: Christian legal thought severed right and law from truth, treating law neither as divine or scientific nor as dependent on the people's will.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r5.anchor: Nazarlarında hak, şeriat mefhûmunun hakikatle alakası yoktu; bunlar ilmî, hakīkī ve ilâhî bir mefhum değil idi.

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r6.claim: Clergy and councils made law by will rather than knowledge or interpretation, allowing arbitrary rules and joining divine and human realms incoherently.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r6.anchor: vaz‘ı idi. Ve bunlar hak üzerinde bir fikr-i ilmî ve ictihâdî ile değil

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r7.claim: This arbitrary law denied non-Christians a right to live, undermined social order, and eventually collapsed because emotional pleasures cannot sustain injustice to human rights.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r7.anchor: Hıristiyanlardan mâ‘adâsına hiçbir suretle hakk-ı hayat tanımaması hey’et-i ictimâ‘iyeyi büyük sukūtlara ihzar ediyordu.

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r8.claim: Elmalılı sets aside sins not arising from doctrine, distinguishing personal misconduct from the religious traits under discussion.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r8.anchor: Burada akideden neş’et etmeyen ve akide hilâfında vâki‘olan fısk u fücûrdan bahse lüzum görmüyoruz.

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r9.claim: The defining Christian traits he lists amount to departure from the prophetic truth, whose consequence is punishment and misguidance despite outward worldly prosperity.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r9.anchor: teslis, ta‘kīm-i ‘ukūl, sayd-ı kulûb, şeriatsızlık, vicdan darlığı ve hâsılı bir kelime ile hakk u hakikatten tebâ‘üd

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r10.claim: God gave Muslims Islam as a safe path to complete blessing; its rapid early success established the promise, and those steadfast on it will have the same outcome eternally.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r10.anchor: pek az bir zaman içinde de bununla tedeyyün edenlere vaad ve in‘âm-ı ilâhî şekk ü şüpheden âzâde olarak tahakkuk etti

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r11.claim: The Fatiha's opening treats knowledge of God, its middle establishes divine relation and social and legal principles, and its last three verses define Islam's path with comprehensive eloquence.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r11.anchor: üç âyette de tarîk-i hakkın, dîn-i İslâm’ın efrâdını câmi‘, ağyârını mâni‘bir hadd-i tâmmını tasvîrine doyulmaz bir belâgat ile tesbit etmiş

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r12.claim: Islam is the clear, straight, safe road that leads to God and His blessings without wrath or misguidance, followed by people historically witnessed to attain true happiness and gratitude.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r12.anchor: Gazaba uğratmadan, dalâlete düşürmeden doğruca ve selâmetle Allah’a ve

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r13.claim: Religious practice begins by knowing God and making a fully monotheistic covenant, then asking for guidance to a straight divine law that teaches duties and enables their steadfast practice.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r13.anchor: Bu din ile tedeyyünün, diyânetin mebde’i evvelâ Allah teâlâ’yı tanımak ve O’na إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ diye

ELMALILI:1:7#5/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r14.claim: Human beings make the request and practice; God gives religion, law, and two forms of guidance: intellectual instruction from the Qur'an and practical enabling through accepting it.
ELMALILI:1:7#5/r14.anchor: taleb ve diyânet bizden; din, şeriat, hidâyet Allah’tandır ve bu hidâyet iki nevidir.

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r1.claim: The Fatiha substantiates Islam through observation, experience, and historical testimony after its rational and spiritual guidance, requiring no further proof.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r1.anchor: Fâtiha bunu târif ederken mazmûnunu isbat için bidâyetteki irşâdât-ı akliye ve kalbiyeden sonra müşahede ve tecribeyi

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r2.claim: The Prophet and his Companions provide a visible historical example of the greatness and sanctity of divine blessings attained through Islam.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r2.anchor: Hâtemü’l-enbiyâ Muhammed Mustafâ sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Efendimiz’le ashâb-ı kirâmının bu sâyede mazhar oldukları ni‘am-ı ilâhiyenin azamet

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r3.claim: Because the Qur'an is preserved letter for letter and Prophetic practice is preserved, Islam has suffered no deviation; the Qur'an is Muhammad's clearest miracle and history testifies to his truth.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r3.anchor: kitâb-ı ilâhî bir harfine bile halel gelmeksizin aynen mevcut ve sünen-i nebeviye mahfuz olduğundan

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r4.claim: Religious knowledge joins reason and transmitted tradition; societies that apply it sincerely can expect the same results confirmed by experience, and denying this is to reject induction.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r4.anchor: bizim için ilm-i dîn akıl ve nakil ile memzucdur. Bunları sıdk u ihlâs ile tatbik edecek olan hey’et-i ictimâ‘iyelerin

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r5.claim: Europeans mislead inquiry by testing Islam among currently declining Muslims instead of investigating its genuine sources and comparing present practice with past practice.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r5.anchor: şimdiki inhitat içinde yuvarlanan Müslümanlarda arıyorlar.

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r6.claim: Those who genuinely follow the straight path advance, while those who do not decline; the divine law is true even when religious practice is incomplete or insincere.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r6.anchor: Demek ki sâdıklar müterakkī, gayr-i sâdıklar mütedennîdirler. Demek ki din kānûn-ı hak lâkin diyânet nâtamam ve gayr-i sâdıktır.

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r7.claim: Failure to apply arithmetic or hygiene does not discredit those sciences; likewise, people are responsible for conforming to true law rather than bending it to themselves.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r7.anchor: İnsanlar kendilerini kānûn-ı hakka uydurmakla mükellef iken o kānûn-ı hakkı kendilerine uydurmaya çalışırlarsa kusur o kanunun değil

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r8.claim: Those who knowingly disobey incur divine wrath, while the unwitting are misguided and ultimately face the same consequence.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r8.anchor: Gazab-ı ilâhî evvelâ bunu bilerek yapanlar içindir. Bilmeyerek yapanlar da dâllîndirler

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r9.claim: Modern people seek to fit true law to themselves, causing human distress to grow despite advances in science; only following the right path can end that distress.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r9.anchor: bütün âlemde ıztırâbât-ı beşeriyenin sûret-i umûmiyede gittikçe artmasının sebebi de budur. Bu ıztırabâtı ancak tarîk-i hakka sülûk

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r10.claim: Amin is an imperative-like noun of action meaning 'answer' or 'accept'; it is not part of Qur'anic wording and therefore is not written in the codex.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r10.anchor: “Âmin” icâbet et, kabul et mânasına bir ism-i fiildir. “Âmin” demeye de “te’mîn” denilir.

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r11.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r11.claim: A Bukhari and Muslim hadith instructs everyone to say amin when the imam says waladdallin; agreement with the angels' amin brings forgiveness of past sins.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r11.anchor: İmam ‘veleddâllîn’ dediği zaman hepiniz ‘âmin’ deyiniz. Çünkü melekler ‘âmin’ derler.

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r12.claim: A separate suspended report says the ranks of the people on earth align with the heavenly ranks, and earthly amin coinciding with heavenly amin brings forgiveness.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r12.anchor: Ehl-i arzın saflarını ehl-i semânın safları vely eder. Binâen‘aleyh yerdeki ‘âmin’ gökteki ‘âmîn’e tevâfuk ederse

ELMALILI:1:7#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r13.claim: Amin is established by Sunna and should be said quietly by the imam, congregation, and a person praying alone.
ELMALILI:1:7#6/r13.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh âmin sünnet ile sâbittir. Hem imam ve hem cemaat tarafından sırren yapılmalıdır.

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r1.claim: The concatenated specification of the right path distinguishes it from rival paths to God, while leaving the groups’ identities partly open.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die mit Konkatenation an den vorausgehenden Vers angeschlossene Spezifizierung des rechten Weges dient der Abgrenzung gegen konkurrierende Gruppen

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r2.claim: Those favored by God can mean righteous people generally, but here may refer especially to middle Meccan Christians whose protagonists are linked with divine favor and mercy.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r2.anchor: hier könnte aber speziell an die in Mittelmekka in den Vordergrund tretenden Christen gedacht sein

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r3.claim: The phrase may also include monotheistic predecessors generally, favored by God.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r3.anchor: Ebenso kann aber auch generell an von Gott ausgezeichnete monotheistische Vorläufer der Gemeinde gedacht sein

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r4.speaker: Nöldeke
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r4.claim: On the hypothesis that the Fātiḥa draws on Christian traditions, Nöldeke’s reading takes the second group as Jews, stereotyped in Christian polemic as subject to divine wrath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r4.anchor: Nöldeke (GdQ I, S. 110–117) vertritt – an christliche Traditionen anknüpfen

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r5.claim: Identifying the wrath-stricken with Jews would be anachronistic for the Fātiḥa’s first proclamation: this image appears only in Medina and never becomes a Quranic stereotype.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r5.anchor: Die Identifizierung der Zornbelasteten mit den Juden wäre daher in der Fātiḥa für die Zeit ihrer Erstverkündigung ein Anachronismus

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r6.claim: The category may inherit a preexisting topos stripped of political targeting; since Jewish opponents were not yet in view, hearers fill in its referent.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r6.anchor: Die Formulierung reflektiert vielleicht die Aufnahme eines vorgefundenen Topos, jedoch unter Ausblendung der religionspolitischen Spitze

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r7.claim: Al-ḍāllīn is a standard middle Meccan designation for pagan opponents, already found in early Meccan passages.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r7.anchor: Aḍ-ḍāllīn (»die Irregehenden«) ist dagegen in Mittelmekka als Standardbezeichnung für die paganen Gegner eindeutig

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r8.speaker: Winkler and Goitein
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r8.claim: They note the Fātiḥa’s relationship to the Christian Lord’s Prayer, especially its kingdom and deliverance-from-evil motifs.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r8.anchor: Die Verwandtschaft zum christlichen Vaterunser (Mt 6,9–13) ist früh betont worden (siehe Winkler 1928 und Goitein 2009)

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r9.speaker: Martin Bauschke
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r9.claim: Bauschke argues more strongly that the Fātiḥa records Muhammad’s authentic engagement with Christ and traces anonymous traces of Jesus into Islam’s principal prayer.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r9.anchor: Martin Bauschke (2013:67–69) betont noch stärker als Winkler, daß mit der Fātiḥa

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r10.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r10.speaker: Josef van Ess
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r10.claim: Van Ess highlights a theological difference: the Fātiḥa locates evil in the individual soul, which must be protected from temptation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r10.anchor: Josef van Ess hat auf die ganz verschiedene Verortung des Bösen in beiden Texten hingewiesen

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r11.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r11.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r11.claim: The Fātiḥa and Lord’s Prayer differ theologically: the Quran makes keeping the right path salvific, unlike Christian redemption from sin; their strongest common ground is the genre of community prayer.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r11.anchor: Ganz geht die Gleichung zwischen den beiden Texten also nicht auf; man wird das Hauptargument für die Ähnlichkeit der Fātiḥa mit dem Vaterunser daher am ehesten auf die gemeinsame Gattung des Gemeindegebets begrenzen

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r12.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r12.speaker: Anton Baumstark
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r12.claim: Baumstark reconstructs a monotheistic liturgical genealogy for the Fātiḥa, whose formula and structure reflect an early Christian daily-prayer doxology.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r12.anchor: Ihr Anfang bildet nach Baumstark (1927: 242–248) in Formelhaftigkeit und Struktur einen altchristlichen Lobpreis ab

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r13.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r13.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r13.claim: If the Basmala is omitted in worship, the Fātiḥa opens with a universalized doxology like the beginnings of the Chrysostom and Basil liturgies.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r13.anchor: Denn geht man davon aus, daß, wie in einzelnen Riten bis heute üblich, die Fātiḥa im Kultus ohne die Basmala auskommt

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r14.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r14.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r14.claim: The Greek doxology and response together parallel praise, eschatological kingship, rule over present and eternity, and mercy in the first part of the Fātiḥa.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r14.anchor: alle wesentlichen Elemente des ersten Teils der Fātiḥa enthält: die Preisung

CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r15.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r15.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r15.claim: Parallels between the Fātiḥa’s second half and the litany after the hymn strengthen the view that it opens worship; it likely functioned both as community prayer and liturgical preface during Quranic formation.
CORPUSCORANICUM:1:7:kommentar/r15.anchor: so daß die Annahme, die Fātiḥa stehe als Gottesdiensteinleitung in der Tradition älterer Gottesdienstanfangsteile

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r1.claim: History offers evidence for the sound and unsound paths: seekers should study those who found happiness by following prophets and those who rejected divine guidance and incurred wrath.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r1.anchor: dönüp tarihe bakmak, gerçek mutluluğu bulanlarla sapanlar ve Allah’ın gazabına uğrayanların yol ve yöntemlerini incelemek durumundadırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r2.claim: Some reports identify the strayed as Christians and those under wrath as Jews; the author says these are nearby examples in time and place, not an exhaustive identification.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r2.anchor: Bazı rivayetlerde sapanların “hıristiyanlar”, ilâhî gazaba uğrayanların da “yahudiler” olarak açıklanması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r3.speaker: Allah Teâlâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r3.claim: A sacred hadith in Muslim presents Fatiha as divided between God and the worshipper: God answers each praise or request, and grants the servant’s plea for guidance.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r3.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın, “Namazı (Fâtiha’yı) kulumla kendi aramda yarı yarıya paylaştım ve kulum dilediğini alacaktır”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r4.claim: Amin means asking that the prayer be accepted; it is not part of Fatiha or a verse, and hadiths say the Prophet said it after Fatiha and instructed others to do so.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r4.anchor: Bu cümle Fâtiha sûresine dahil olmadığı gibi âyet de değildir. Birçok hadiste Resûlullah’ın Fâtiha’dan sonra “âmin” dediği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r5.claim: Hadiths say angels also say amin with the worshipper and that the prayer is accepted in both the visible and unseen realms.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r5.anchor: aynı zamanda meleklerin de “âmin” dedikleri, hem şehâdet hem de gayb âlemlerinde aynı anda dile getirilen bu duanın Allah tarafından kabul buyurulacağı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:1:7/r6.claim: Because sound hadiths support saying amin aloud after audible Fatiha, most legal schools adopt that practice; Hanafis always say it silently in prayer.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.claim: Invoking the congregation’s mercy, the worshipper praises, worships, seeks help, asks guidance, follows the righteous, and flees the rejected as a group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p56/r2.anchor: سمعت رسولك يقول: (الجماعة رحمة والفرقة عذاب) فلما أردت تحميدك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r2.claim: The blessed are those who have followed the straight path, while those astray are lost from it; the Quran often pairs guidance and misguidance as opposites.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p58/r2.anchor: والهدى ضد الضلال، وكثيراً ما يجمع القرآن بين الهدى والضلال على أنهما متضادان،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r4.claim: The next phrase identifies the straight path as the way of the blessed, excluding the angry and the astray and encompassing every accountable person.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p60/r4.anchor: ثم زاد هذا الصراط بياناً وتوضيحاً، فقال:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r1.claim: People are either blessed, or wretched in two ways: knowing truth but violating it, or lacking knowledge of truth and being astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r1.anchor: فهم إما أهل السعادة، وهم الذين أنعم الله عليهم.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r2.speaker: البيضاوي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r2.claim: One proposed reading identifies the angry as sinners and the astray as those ignorant of God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r2.anchor: ويتجه أن يقال: المغضوب عليهم: العصاة، والضالين: الجاهلون بالله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r3.claim: No accountable person falls outside these categories: the blessed know and obey, while the wretched are sinners or ignorant.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r3.anchor: ولا يخرج أصناف المكلفين عن هؤلاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r4.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r4.claim: Al-Razi classifies accountable people as obedient, sinful, or ignorant of religion and unbelieving, corresponding to the three Quranic groups.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p61/r4.anchor: دلت هذه الآية على أن المكلفين ثلاث فرق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r1.speaker: الرازي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r1.claim: Complete blessing combines knowing truth and acting on it; lacking action makes one sinful and angry upon, while lacking knowledge makes one astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r1.anchor: أن الذين كملت نِعَمُ الله عليهم، هم الذين جمعوا بين معرفة الحق لذاته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r2.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r2.claim: People divide by knowledge and practice: the knowledgeable doer is blessed, the knowledgeable follower of desire is angry upon, and the ignorant is astray; the first is more deserving of anger.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r2.anchor: فالعالم بالحق العامل به هو المنعم عليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r3.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r3.claim: Corrupt knowledge produces misguidance and corrupt intention produces anger; these are the two root diseases of the heart.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p62/r3.anchor: فإن مدار اعتلال القلوب وأسقامها على أصلين: فساد العلم وفساد القصد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.claim: Living out worship and seeking aid in knowledge, action, and inward state cures corruption of the heart and intention.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r1.anchor: والتحقق بـ {إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ} علماً ومعرفة وعملاً وحالاً يتضمنُ الشفاءَ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r3.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r3.claim: Asking for the straight path cures ignorance; healing these spiritual diseases makes a person among the blessed, unlike those corrupt in intention or knowledge.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r3.anchor: ومن مرض الجهل بـ {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} عُوفيَ من أمراضه وأسقامه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r4.claim: The past tense in You blessed identifies established recipients, including prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and righteous people.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r4.anchor: المقصود صراط الذين ثبت إنعام الله عليهم وتحقق وهم الأنبياء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r5.claim: Using a past verb for the blessed, then nominal forms for the angry and astray, distinguishes established past beneficiaries from the enduring qualities of the latter groups.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r5.anchor: فعبر عن المنعم عليهم بالفعل الماضي، ثم قال:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r6.claim: A present-tense blessing would omit the earlier prophets and righteous, imply no established past recipients, and obscure continuity in one path from Adam onward.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p63/r6.anchor: لأغفلَ كُلَّ مَنْ مضى من رسل الله والصالحين،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r1.claim: The past tense allows the community of the blessed to grow as each present recipient joins those already blessed; the present tense could imply only a small current group.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r1.anchor: لأن الحاضر يلتحق بالماضي، وهكذا تتسع دائرة المنعَم عليهم بمرور الزمن

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r2.claim: The noun forms angry upon and astray cover all times and make those conditions enduring.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r3.claim: Calling them the blessed ones would not name the benefactor; the greatness of a gift and the honor it confers depend on who bestowed it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p64/r3.anchor: لم يبيّن المُنعِم الذي أنعم عليهم، والنعمة إنما تقدر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r1.claim: Attributing blessing to the greatest giver magnifies both the gift and the recipient’s honor, as a ruler’s favor exceeds a lesser official’s.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r1.anchor: فإن كان المنعِم عظيماً عَظُمتْ نعمتهُ، وإن كان أدنى من ذلك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r2.claim: God attributes good and favor to Himself but leaves evil’s agent unmentioned, as in the saying that all good is in God’s hands and evil is not from Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r2.anchor: فنسب النعمة إلى نفسه ولم ينسب إلى نفسه الشر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r3.claim: All blessing truly comes from God, so the Quran attributes the act of bestowing blessing to Him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p65/r3.anchor: ولذلك ينسب النعم كلها إلى نفسه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r1.claim: The sole Quranic attribution of blessing to someone besides God occurs when the Prophet’s special favor to Zayd is mentioned after God’s favor to him.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r1.anchor: ولم يسند فعل النعمة إلى غير الله، إلا في قوله تعالى:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r2.claim: The passive angry upon leaves the agent broad, including God and those angry for Him; even former allies disown and curse the condemned in the afterlife.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r2.anchor: فقد بناه للمفعول ليعم الغضب عليهم: غضب الله، وغضب الغاضبين لله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r3.claim: The passive avoids attributing anger directly to the God being addressed in a humble request for favor and also prepares the ending’s parallelism and rhyme.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p66/r3.anchor: لأن من طلب منه الهداية ونسب الإنعام إليه لا يناسبه نسبة الغضب إليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r1.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r1.claim: Blessing is good and favor, while anger is retribution; God names the more complete and prior quality and leaves the contrasting agent unstated, as elsewhere in the Quran.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r1.anchor: أن النعمةَ هي الخير والفضل، والغضب من باب الانتقام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r2.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r2.claim: God alone is the source of blessing, while angels, prophets, messengers, and allies also share anger at His enemies; the passive wording signals this.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r2.anchor: إن الله سبحانه هو المتفرد بالنعم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r3.speaker: التفسير القيم
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r3.claim: Omitting the agent of anger belittles its targets, while naming the giver of blessing honors the recipients.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r3.anchor: إن في حذف فاعل الغضب من الإشعار بإهانة المغضوب عليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r4.claim: The nominal forms make anger and misguidance fixed conditions that persist in this world and the next, unlike temporary verb forms.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p67/r4.anchor: المغضوب عليهم والضالين اسماً، وذلك للدلالة على الثبوت

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r1.claim: Adding lā before the astray makes the exclusion apply to either group separately, rather than only excluding people who combine anger and misguidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r1.anchor: لئلا يفهم أن المباينة لمن جمع الغضب والضلال دون من لم يجمعهما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r2.speaker: حاشية الجرجاني على الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r2.claim: In negation, the added lā after the coordinating conjunction explicitly attaches negation to each item and prevents reading only the combined pair as negated.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r2.anchor: أن (لا) المسماة بالمزيدة عند البصريين، إنما تقع بعد الواو العاطفة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r3.claim: The verse’s order prompts the question why the angry are named before the astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r3.anchor: وقد تقول: ولمَ قدّم الغضبَ على الضلال، فقال:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r4.claim: The knowing rebel is more culpable than the ignorant because knowledge followed by denial brings a graver sin and punishment.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p68/r4.anchor: أن المغضوب عليه أشد ضلالاً وجرماً وعقوبة لأنه علم وجحد،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r1.claim: A sound hadith identifies the angry as Jews and the astray as Christians; the Jews came earlier, fitting their precedence in the verse.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r1.anchor: جاء في الحديث الصحيح أن المغضوب عليهم اليهود والضالين النصارى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r2.claim: The knowing disobedience of Iblis was the first sin; after it, he vowed to mislead humanity, so anger appropriately precedes misguidance.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r2.anchor: وهي معصية إبليس، ذلك أنه كان عالماً بالحق عارفاً له،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r3.claim: The first sin on earth was Cain’s deliberate killing of his brother after their offerings, another case of wrongdoing by a knowing person.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r3.anchor: وهي قتل ابن آدم أخاه، بعد أن قَرَّبا قرباناً،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r4.claim: The angry contrast directly with the recipients of blessing, as one may say a ruler blessed one person and was angered by another, unlike the unrelated verb strayed.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p69/r4.anchor: فلان أنعم عليه الخليفة، وفلان غضب عليه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r1.claim: After praising God and declaring worship and reliance, a person who strays is among those angry upon, so distance from that group is requested first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r1.anchor: إذا زاغ كان من المغضوب عليهم، لأنه علم وخالف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r2.claim: After asking for guidance, it is fitting to ask distance from misguidance; this order also suits the verse endings.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r2.anchor: وأما سؤال الهداية بعد ذلك وهو قوله:

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r3.speaker: البحر المحيط
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r3.claim: Although anger results from misguidance, anger is placed beside blessing because blessing and retribution correspond semantically; the final wording also suits the rhyme.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r3.anchor: وقدم الغضب على الضلال، وإن كان الغضب من نتيجة الضلال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r4.claim: Unrestricted praise and the enduring nominal descriptions of the angry and astray all suggest timeless, lasting states.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r4.anchor: أن الحمد مطلق غير مقيد بزمن ولا بفاعل معين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r5.claim: Anyone who fails to praise God, recognize Him as Lord, or receive the mercy of the Most Merciful is angry upon and astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p70/r5.anchor: أنَّ مَنْ لم يحمد الله، فهو مغضوب عليه وضال،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r1.claim: Failure to believe in the Day of Judgment and God’s ownership of it makes a person angry upon and astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r1.anchor: ومن لم يؤمن بيوم الدين، وأن الله مالك ذلك اليوم،

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r2.claim: Anyone who does not devote worship and reliance to God alone, or follow the straight path of the blessed, is angry upon and astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r2.anchor: ومَنْ لم يَخُصَّ اللهَ بالعبادة والاستعانة، فهو مغضوبٌ عليه وضال.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r7.claim: The straight path is known through prophets and messengers; acceptable worship comes from revelation, not from each person’s preference.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p71/r7.anchor: فإن الصراط المستقيم الذي يريده الله إنما يعرف من طريق الأنبياء والرسل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.claim: The guidance request ties the chapter together: Rabb guides, Rahman and Rahim show mercy, worship and reliance require the path, and the favored oppose the astray.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p26/r1.anchor: هذا الدعاء ارتبط بأول السورة وبوسطها وآخرها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r1.claim: The definite, construct, singular, straight path is one route to God's pleasure; other paths do not reach the goal, and scripture consistently uses sirat in the singular.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r1.anchor: مما يدل على انه صراط واحد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r2.claim: Sirat is singular while sabil can be plural because the many paths lead into the one broad path; following other paths fragments people away from it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p27/r2.anchor: الصراط هو الأوسع وهو الذي تفضي إليه كل السبل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p28/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p28/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p28/r1.claim: The closing description covers all accountable people: the favored know and follow truth, the angered know but oppose it (some exegetes call them sinners), and the astray do not know it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p28/r1.anchor: ولا يخرج المكلفون عن هذه الأصناف الثلاثة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p28/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p28/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p28/r2.claim: The past أنعمت identifies people whose favor has already been realized, including prophets and righteous predecessors, and links them across generations; 4:69 names them.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p28/r2.anchor: ليتعين زمانه ليبين صراط الذين تحققت عليهم النعمة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p29/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p29/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p29/r1.claim: Past أنعمت encompasses earlier and later generations who join the already favored; the present تنعم could suggest only a smaller group favored at one time.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p29/r1.anchor: كان قوله سبحانه أنعمت عليهم أوسع وأشمل واعم من الذين تنعم عليهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p29/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p29/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p29/r2.claim: Angered and astray are expressed as enduring states, while the verb for favor conveys renewal; this contrasts the lasting groups with an ongoing act of benefaction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p29/r2.anchor: الاسم يدل على الشمول ويشمل سائر الأزمنة من المغضوب عليهم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r1.claim: Saying أنعمت names God as giver, making the greatness of the gift clear; Quranic usage attributes good to God and often leaves evil's agent unstated or assigns it elsewhere.
