SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r1.anchor: أراد سبحانه وتعالى أن يبين المنعم ليبين قدرة النعمة وعظيمها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r2.claim: The Quran attributes blessings to God, as in 28:17, 43:59, and 17:83; 33:37 uniquely says both God and the Prophet bestowed a particular favor.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r2.anchor: ولم ينسب سبحانه النعمة لغيره إلا في آية واحدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r3.claim: The passive المغضوب عليهم leaves the agent open so the condemned face anger from God, angels, people, and even their own skins.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p30/r3.anchor: ليعم الغضب عليهم من الله والملائكة وكل الناس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r1.claim: Repeating لا ensures exclusion of either condemned group on its own; without it the wording might exclude only those who combine anger and error, as the two-part prohibition analogy shows.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r1.anchor: إذا حذفت (لا) يمكن أن يُفهم أن المباينة والابتعاد هو فقط للذين جمعوا الغضب والضلالة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r2.claim: The angered precede the astray because they know truth and reject it, are more culpable than the ignorant, and Jews preceded Christians; an authentic hadith identifies the groups accordingly.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r2.anchor: وفي الحديث الصحيح أن المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود وأما النصارى فهم الضالون

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r3.claim: Knowing defiance was the first sin in heaven with Iblis and the first on earth with Cain's murder of his brother; 4:93 also associates murder with God's anger.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r3.anchor: وصفة المغضوب عليهم هي أول معصية ظهرت في الوجود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r4.claim: The angered oppose the favored just as anger opposes grace; the chapter's ending gathers its opening praise, judgment, exclusive worship, reliance, and guidance into the fates of the condemned.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p31/r4.anchor: خاتمة سورة الفاتحة هي مناسبة لكل ما ورد في السورة من أولها إلى آخرها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r1.claim: Ḥamza alone uses a damma on the hāʾ and a still mim in ʿalayhim, ladayhim, and ilayhim; the others use a kasra on hāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة وحده (عليهم) بضم الهاء وكذلك (لديهم)، (وإليهم) هذه الثلاثة الأحرف بالضم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr joins the plural mim to a wāw after either a kasra or damma on hāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r2.anchor: فكان عبد الله بن كثير يصل الميم بواو، انضمت الهاء قبلها أو انكسرت

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r3.speaker: إسماعيل بن جعفر وابن جماز وقالون والمسيبي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r3.claim: Some Nāfiʿ transmitters allow either a damma or still mim after kasra hāʾ; Aḥmad b. Qālūn infers Nāfiʿ read with still mim, as did Aḥmad b. Mūsā.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r3.anchor: الهاء مكسورة، والميم مضمومة، أو منجزمة، أنت فيها مخير

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r4.speaker: ورش
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r4.claim: Warsh keeps hāʾ kasra and mim still, but inserts a wāw when an original alif follows, as in sawāʾ ʿalayhumu.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r4.anchor: وقال ورش : الهاء مكسورة والميم موقوفة إلا أن تلقى الميم ألف أصلية

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r5.claim: Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, and al-Kisāʾī generally use kasra hāʾ and still mim; before a following sukūn, readers differ over mim and sometimes hāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r5.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو، وعاصم، وابن عامر، والكسائي يكسرون الهاء، ويسكنون الميم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r6.speaker: أحمد بن موسى
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r6.claim: Aḥmad b. Mūsā says the variation of hāʾ depends on whether it follows kasra or silent yāʾ; elsewhere it is damma, while mim is damma or still.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p57/r6.anchor: وكل هذا الاختلاف في كسر الهاء وضمها إنما هو في الهاء التي قبلها كسرة، أو ياء ساكنة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r1.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r1.claim: Sibawayh reports that some say ʿalayhumu by assimilating to the preceding yāʾ; Abū Ḥātim identifies it as al-Aʿraj’s reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم: (عليهمو) أتبع الياء ما أشبهها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r2.claim: One defense says hāʾ shares yāʾ’s articulation, so the hāʾ should follow the yāʾ; another treats hāʾ as related to yāʾ by its articulation.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r2.anchor: إن الهاء من جنس الياء، لأن الهاء تنقطع إلى مخرج الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r3.speaker: عاصم وأبو عمرو والكسائي وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r3.claim: Their kasra-hāʾ, still-mim reading deletes wāw because the plural mim itself prevents confusion with the dual, and deletion lightens speech.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r3.anchor: إنه أمن اللبس، إذ كانت الألف في التثنية قد دلت على الاثنين، ولا ميم في الواحد

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r4.speaker: عاصم وأبو عمرو والكسائي وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r4.claim: They preserve kasra on hāʾ because it is the same pronoun hāʾ as in ʿalayhi and its cause for kasra remains unchanged after mim is added.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r4.anchor: لما كانت الهاء في (عليهم) هي الهاء التي كانت في عليه وجب إقرارها على ما كانت عليه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r5.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r5.claim: Ḥamza treats damma hāʾ as original, like hum when independent; the waw reading is described as old and Qurayshī, Ḥijāzī, and Yemeni eloquent usage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r5.anchor: ضم الهاء هو الأصل، وذلك أنها إذا انفردت من حروف تتصل بها قيل: هم فعلوا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r6.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r6.claim: Ḥamza limits damma to these three forms because before a visible noun, ʿalā, ladā, and ilā end in alif and hāʾ is not kasra after alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r6.anchor: لأنهن إن أولاهن ظاهرا صارت ياءاتهن ألفات مثل: على القوم، ولدى القوم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r7.claim: Damma on a mim before a following sukūn restores its original vowel after movement becomes necessary; this is common in the two Holy Cities.

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r8.claim: Kasra mim before a following sukūn assimilates kasra to kasra, avoiding the heaviness of damma after kasra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p59/r8.anchor: أتبعت الكسر الكسر، لثقل الضم بعد الكسر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r1.speaker: الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī keeps hāʾ kasra unless the mim meets a following sukūn, then restores both hāʾ and mim to damma to avoid switching from kasra to damma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r1.anchor: إذا رد الميم إلى أصلها رد الهاء أيضا إلى أصلها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r2.claim: The author prefers kasra on hāʾ because it is easier to pronounce and is the majority reading.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r2.anchor: والاختيار (عليهم) بالكسر، لأنها أخف على اللسان، وهي قراءة الأكثر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r3.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r3.claim: Sibawayh explains kasra hāʾ after yāʾ or kasra by its hidden quality and closeness to yāʾ and alif; adjacent kasra also changes wāw to yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r3.anchor: الهاء تكسر إذا كان قبلها ياء أو كسرة، لأنها خفية، كما أن الياء خفية

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r4.claim: When the next word begins with sukūn, kasra mim is preferred as lighter; it restores an original vowel, and Ḥasan’s alayhimi preserves the connecting yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p61/r4.anchor: والاختيار- إذا لقيها ساكن- كسر الميم، وذلك أنه أخف

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī argues that hāʾ resembles alif in articulation and hiddenness, so a preceding kasra or yāʾ draws its damma toward kasra as imāla draws alif toward yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r1.anchor: فأمالوا الفتحة التي قبلها نحو الكسرة، كما أمالوها إذا كانت قبل الألف نحو الكسرة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r2.claim: The pronunciation ḍarabtu ḍarbih shows hāʾ can trigger imāla even without a preceding kasra or yāʾ, like imāla in some proper names.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r2.anchor: إن ذلك يشبه من الإمالة ما أميل لغير سبب موجب للإمالة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r3.claim: Hāʾ and alif both clarify a preceding vowel in pause; al-Khalīl permits either hāʾ or alif after a consonant, supporting their parallel treatment in ʿalayhim.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r3.anchor: ومما يؤكد شبه الهاء بالألف اجتماعهما في تبيين الحركة نحو: (أنا) و (حي هلا)

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r4.claim: The optional hāʾ or alif suffix is allowed because each resembles and can stand for the other; alif also occurs in the same pause pattern after bāʾ, tāʾ, and thāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r4.anchor: جمع بينهما لمشابهة كل واحد منهما الآخر فيما ذكرنا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r5.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r5.claim: Although hāʾ lacks the sustained sound of alif, their shared hiddenness, weakness, and articulation allow one to be brought near the other.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p63/r5.anchor: فإنها توافقها في الخفاء، والضعف، واتفاق المخرج

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r1.claim: Hāʾ can replace other letters in pause just as alif can, another sign of their similarity.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r1.anchor: ومما يبين شبه الهاء بالألف أنهم قد غيروا بها بعض الحروف في الوقف

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r2.claim: Pronoun hāʾ’s hiddenness is shown by movements inserted before it in pause, and by their disappearance in liaison when hāʾ itself makes the vowel clear.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r2.anchor: إذا كانت إضمار مذكر بعد حرف ساكن أو مجزوم، حركوا الساكن

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r3.claim: The reported phrase lam aḍribihimā is treated as liaison pronounced like pause, not as a general rule for inflectional sukūn; inflectional endings do not assimilate freely.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r3.anchor: فهذا على أنه أجرى الوصل مجرى الوقف نحو: «سبسبا»

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r4.claim: A jussive consonant may move to avoid a following sukūn, as in the cited yattaqihi form, unlike a freely altered inflectional ending.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p64/r4.anchor: ألا تراه حرك اللام المنجزمة بالفتح، لالتقاء الساكنين

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r1.claim: The phrase اشتر لنا سويقا can be explained by treating the liaison as pause, among the analyses of movement before pronoun hāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r1.anchor: ووجه ثالث: وهو أن يجرى الوصل في قوله: اشتر لنا، مجرى الوقف

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r2.claim: Hāʾ behaves like weak letters: it can be deleted word-finally, as in shāh, shafah, and sanah, and shared rules strengthen the analogy.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك أنهم حذفوها لاما كما حذفوا الياء وأختها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r3.claim: Hāʾ substitutes for yāʾ in ذه/هذه; Ḥijāzī and Tamīmī dialects differ in whether it drops or becomes yāʾ in pause and liaison.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك أنهم أبدلوها من الياء، كما أبدلوا منها الألف في «طائي»

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r4.claim: Hāʾ also alternates with yāʾ under doubling, as in dahdayt for dahdaht and related forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك أنهم أبدلوا الياء منها في التضعيف

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r5.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r5.claim: Abū Zayd records the forms māhat and tamūhu/tamīhu, and a poetic line using māh as a word for a heart softened by tears.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r5.anchor: قالوا: ماهت الركية تموه وتميه وأماهها صاحبها إماهة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r6.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r6.claim: Some speakers kasra hāʾ despite an intervening consonant, as in minhum; this weaker analogy still supports kasra when yāʾ is adjacent.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p67/r6.anchor: أن ناسا كسروها مع حجز الحرف بينها وبين الكسرة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r1.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r1.claim: Abū Zayd reports a Bakrī speaker saying minhu, minhuma, and minhumī, breaking the pronoun in both connected and paused speech.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r1.anchor: أن رجلا من بني بكر بن وائل قال: أخذت هذا منه ومنهما ومنهمي

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r2.claim: Other Bakrī speakers say bikum and faḍlu aḥlāmikum with kasra on kāf, since kāf shares hāʾ’s whispering and pronoun function.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r2.anchor: ومما يؤكد كسر الهاء أن ناسا من بكر بن وائل قالوا: بكم

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r3.claim: The attachment of weak vowels to kāf and hāʾ further supports kasra in ʿalayhim because hāʾ has many similar features.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r3.anchor: فإتباع الهاء الكسرة للمشابهات التي فيها من حروف اللين وكثرتها أولى

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r4.claim: An objection says damma is the default for genitive pronoun hāʾ, as its accusative counterpart is damma and damma works in more environments than kasra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r4.anchor: إن الضمة هي الأصل في عليهم وبهم ونحو ذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r5.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r5.claim: The author replies that proximity can override a default vowel; Arabic regularly abandons original sounds for harmony or ease, including ṣād in ṣirāṭ and several broken forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p69/r5.anchor: إن كون الضم الأصل ليس مما يجب من أجله أن يختار على الكسر

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r1.claim: Numerous forms depart from their expected morphology: ʿīd has plural aʿyād, dunya’s pattern is otherwise abandoned, and Adam/Akhir form plurals with wāw despite an expected hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r1.anchor: والأصل في عيد كذلك أيضا، ومن ثم كسر على أعياد، ولم يكن كالأرواح

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r2.claim: The expected form of qasī is abandoned in three respects, illustrating that a linguistic default need not prevail when analogy or ease favors another form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r2.anchor: فهذه كلمة قد ترك الأصل فيها في ثلاثة مواضع

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r3.claim: Hamza’s reading in buyūt shows that kasra can replace a default damma because of nearby yāʾ; Sibawayh’s diminutive bayyit supports the same allowance.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r3.anchor: قراءة حمزة في (بيوت) ونحو ذلك على أن سيبويه حكى في تحقير بيت: بييت

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r4.claim: Because diminutive and broken plural formation are analogous processes, adjacent kasra may replace damma in a plural; this supports kasra in ʿalayhim for harmony and ease.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p71/r4.anchor: فإذا جاز إبدال الضمة كسرة في التحقير لمكان الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r1.claim: Poetic rhyme treats moving hāʾ as a connective following the rhyme, like silent alif, wāw, and yāʾ; named examples include al-Aʿshā’s verse.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r1.anchor: تحركها بمنزلة الألف والواو والياء والهاء والسواكن

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r2.claim: The hāʾ in bihi and ʿalayhi can therefore follow kasra or yāʾ just as alif does, despite being pronounced with a movement.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r2.anchor: كذلك يكون في قولهم : بهي وعليهي، وإن كانت متحركة بمنزلة الألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r3.claim: A moving hāʾ is often ignored as a separator: imāla occurs before it in yadribahā, yanziʿahā, and baynī wa-baynahā, as before alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r3.anchor: فأمالوا الفتحة التي قبل الهاء كما يميلها إذا قال: يريد أن ينزعا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r4.claim: The shared opening of the doubled dāl in raddahā and raddā likewise shows that hāʾ does not block the alif-like pattern.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r4.anchor: اجتمعوا على فتح الدال فيما حكى من يوثق به، كما يجمعون على فتحها إذا لم يحل بينها وبين الألف شيء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r5.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r5.claim: These analogies lead to the reading that deletes the weak glide after the plural mim rather than counting moving hāʾ as a separator.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p73/r5.anchor: ومن هاهنا كان الوجه في القراءة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r1.claim: When moving hāʾ is not counted, retaining its following yāʾ or wāw would leave two adjacent sukūns; deletion is therefore favored in fīhi hudan and khudhūhu.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r1.anchor: أن يحذف الحرف اللين اللاحق للهاء، لأن الاعتداد في هذين الموضعين لم يقع بها متحركة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r2.claim: Weak letters are deleted in many settings where other letters remain, including suffixes, possessive forms, pauses, and rhyme, so deleting the glide after mim is ordinary.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r2.anchor: فإن وجه ذلك أن هذه الحروف قد تستثقل فتحذف في مواضع لا يحذف فيها غيرها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r3.claim: Poetic examples demonstrate deletion of weak endings in verse and rhyme; the text also reports a variant wording for the line with sawāfa.

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r4.claim: Deleting waw or yāʾ after ʿalayhim is light and unambiguous because these suffixes are often dropped, even when nothing remains to mark them.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r4.anchor: كذلك حذفوهما في عليهم ونحوه، للخفة في اللفظ، وأمن اللبس

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r5.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r5.claim: Repeated deletion of weak endings makes it legitimate to apply the same deletion to nouns as well as other forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p76/r5.anchor: ولما استمر ذلك فيها وكثر، جعلوا ما كان اسما بمنزلة غيره في استجازة حذفها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r1.claim: Final alif is retained in pauses and rhyme while yāʾ may be deleted; exceptional deletion of alif is poetic necessity, so it does not refute the rule.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r1.anchor: فلا يحذف الألف من الفواصل كما يحذف الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r2.claim: Since plural mim can take alif, wāw, or yāʾ and alif is not deleted, loss of wāw or yāʾ creates no ambiguity.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r2.anchor: والألف لا تحذف، علم أن الذي يلحقه الحذف الواو أو الياء المنقلبة عنها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r3.claim: Both lexical and grammatical weak endings are deleted elsewhere, even without a surviving marker; that makes deletion from ʿalayhim especially fitting.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r3.anchor: فإذا كانوا قد حذفوا القبيلين جميعا، وحذفوا التي للضمير

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r4.claim: Retaining the mim vowel could restore the missing glide through vowel lengthening, so a still mim best realizes the intended lightening.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p78/r4.anchor: كره أن تبقى الكسرة أو الضمة، لأنهما قد يكونان بمنزلة الياء والواو

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r1.claim: A kasra or damma may be lengthened into the very yāʾ or wāw that was deleted; still mim prevents that reversal and preserves the lighter form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r1.anchor: إذا ثبتتا قد يشبعان فيلحقهما الواو والياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r2.claim: Plural mim always follows a kasra or damma, both heavy, unlike singular pronoun hāʾ, which can follow fatha or sukūn; this licenses still mim.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r2.anchor: أن الميم في عليهم، وعليكم، ودارهم، وبهم، لا يخلو ما قبلها من أن يكون ضما أو كسرا

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r3.claim: The shared deletion in pause follows naturally because plural glide deletion already occurs in liaison, and pause permits still more changes.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p80/r3.anchor: فلما اتفقا في الحذف في الوصل وكان الوقف يحذف فيه ما لا يحذف في الوصل

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r1.claim: A vowelled mim would create four or five consecutive moving syllables, a sequence avoided in Arabic word patterns and poetic meters; deleting its vowel prevents that sequence.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r1.anchor: لأدى ذلك إلى اجتماع أربع متحركات وخمس، وذلك مما قد كرهوه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r2.claim: Arabic meter alternates deletions in mustafʿilun to avoid five consecutive movements, an analogy for removing mim’s vowel.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r2.anchor: فلما كان يؤدي إلى ما قد تركوه، واطرحوه، حذفوا الحركة فيه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r3.claim: Ḥamza’s damma reading treats the derived yāʾ as nonessential, like alif, so hāʾ takes damma as it does after alif; forms ʿalāk and ilāk support this.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p82/r3.anchor: لما وجد هذه الياءات غير لازمة، وما كان غير لازم من الحروف فقد لا يقع الاعتداد به

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r1.claim: Arabic alternations such as ḥāḥayt, ṭāʾī, and ḥārī support the close relation of yāʾ and alif; alif from wāw is comparatively rare.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r1.anchor: وقالوا في النسب إلى طيئ: طائي وفي الحيرة: حاري

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r2.claim: Against the claim that dāwiya has an alif derived from wāw, Abū ʿAlī suggests it may derive from daw with a nisba ending, supported by a cited poetic use.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه يجوز أن يكون بنى من الدو فاعلا كالكاهل والغارب

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r3.claim: The common analogy should prevail over a rare alternative unless evidence forces the exception; poetic shortening of nisba yāʾ does not do so.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r3.anchor: فإن الحمل على القياس والأمر العام أولى

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r4.claim: Abū Zayd reports an eloquent Arab saying ḍarabat yadāh and waḍaʿtuhu ʿalāh; al-Khalīl used such speech to explain forms with alif-like treatment.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p84/r4.anchor: زعم أبو زيد أنه لقي أعرابيا فصيحا: يقول: ضربت يداه، ووضعته علاه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r1.claim: Ṭayyiʾ uses yāʾ where other dialects use final alif in both pause and liaison, as in afʿay for afʿā; this supports treating yāʾ in ʿalayhim like alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r1.anchor: وجعلت طيئ الحرف في الوصل والوقف ياء كما جعل أهل الحجاز وغيرهم من قيس آخر الكلمة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r2.claim: Ḥijāz and Qays use final hāʾ in both pause and liaison, paralleling Ṭayyiʾ’s yāʾ substitution and strengthening the analogy.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r2.anchor: كما جعل أهل الحجاز وغيرهم من قيس آخر الكلمة في الوصل والوقف هاء فقالوا: هذه وهذهي أمة الله

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r3.claim: The attested dialect and the analogous Ḥijāzī/Tamīmī alternations establish the language and make its use for Ḥamza’s reading legitimate.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r3.anchor: فإذا عضد ما ذكرنا من السماع الذي وصفناه من القياس

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r4.claim: Replacing alif with wāw is weaker than replacing it with yāʾ because it is less attested and less supported by analogy.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r4.anchor: إبدال الواو منها ليس بقوي من جهة القياس قوة إبدال الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r5.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r5.claim: Poetic meter balances duration, so the longer alif cannot share the rhyme position of yāʾ and wāw.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p87/r5.anchor: فلما كان المد في الألف أكثر من المد الذي في كل واحد منهما لم تجتمع معهما الألف في الردف

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r1.claim: Unlike long alif, short fatha can precede a rhyme with damma or kasra; examples from Abū al-Ḥasan show the distinction.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r1.anchor: ألا ترى أن الفتحة لما خالفت الألف فيما ذكرنا لم تمتنع

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r2.claim: Alif’s greater duration appears in how hamza is softened after alif but not after yāʾ or wāw, strengthening its distinct treatment.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r2.anchor: ومما يدلك على زيادة المد في الألف، استجازتهم تخفيف الهمزة بعدها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r3.claim: Yāʾ and wāw do not assimilate into alif because alif is long and always still; sibilants likewise resist stops because their extra hiss is absent from stops.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r3.anchor: ولم يجز إدغام الياء والواو في الألف لأنها لا تكون إلا ساكنة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r4.claim: A derived letter can retain the behavior of its source: yāʾ originating from alif in ʿalayhim is treated as alif, so hāʾ is rounded as after alif.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p89/r4.anchor: إذا كانت منقلبة عن الياء قربت منها فصارت مشابهة لها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r1.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r1.claim: Examples such as ruwiya, ruwiyya, and nuwwi show that a replacement wāw can inherit the behavior of its source; bīs similarly keeps its original kasra after hamza is dropped.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r1.anchor: فجعلوا [حكم الواو] حكم الحرف المنقلب عنه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r2.claim: Therefore the yāʾ in ʿalayhim may behave as the alif from which it derives, supporting Ḥamza’s damma on hāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r2.anchor: فكذلك يكون حكم الياء في عليهم حكم الحرف المنقلب عنه

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r3.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r3.claim: Yāʾ can also be fixed across case positions like alif, preserving one surface form; he cites ayādī sabā, bādī badā, qālī qalā, and maʿdīkarib.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r3.anchor: ومن تشابه الياء والألف أن الياء قد أجريت مجرى الألف، فأسكنت في موضع النصب

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r4.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r4.claim: These fixed-yāʾ forms occur in accusative position, whether analyzed as one of the cited nominal patterns or as an attached ending.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p91/r4.anchor: فالأول من هذه الأشياء في موضع فتح

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r1.speaker: أبو بكر أحمد بن موسى
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r1.claim: Abū Bakr counts seven transmitted vocalizations of the pronoun in عليهم; al-Akhfash adds three, yielding ten forms, five with hāʾ ḍamma and five with kasra.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r1.anchor: وزاد أبو الحسن سعيد بن مسعدة الأخفش1 على ما قال أبو بكر ثلاثة أوجه، فصار الجميع عشرة أوجه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r2.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق ومسلم بن جندب والأعرج وعيسى الثقفي وعبد الله بن يزيد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r2.claim: These readers transmit عليهمو; al-Ḥasan and ʿAmr b. Fāʾid transmit عليهمي, while al-Aʿraj is also reported with two unextended forms.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r2.anchor: قرأ "عليهمو" ابن إبي إسحاق2 ومسلم بن جندب3 والأعرج4 وعيسى الثقفي5

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r3.claim: Ibn Jinnī regards the plural wāw as original: mīm marks more than one, including the dual, while wāw specifically marks the plural.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r3.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: أما "عليهمو" فهي الأصل؛ لأنها رسيلة7 عليهما في التثنية

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r4.claim: He derives عليهمي from kasra spreading from the preceding yāʾ to the weak, nearby hāʾ, then to mīm; the wāw becomes yāʾ after a kasra.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p43/r4.anchor: كذلك كسرت الهاء، فكان انكسار الهاء للياء قبلها تغييرا لحقها لهما، كما أن انقلاب الألف ياء

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p62#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p62#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p62#2/r3.claim: The sīn form preserves the word’s original consonant; ṣād replaces sīn to harmonize its hissing quality with ṭāʾ’s emphatic articulation.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p62#2/r3.anchor: قرله تعالى ﴿ الصراط ﴾ تقرأ بالصاد والسين واشمام الزاي فالحجة لمن قرأ بالسين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p104/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p104/r5.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p104/r5.claim: The sīn reading of الصراط is transmitted from Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr through named reciters, while Ibn Kathīr also has transmissions with ṣād; Abū ʿAmr is reported with all three sibilant realizations.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p104/r5.anchor: وروى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو أنه قرأ / الزراط / بالزاي خالصة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r1.speaker: عريان بن أبي سفيان عن أبي عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r1.claim: One transmission from Abū ʿAmr places the sound between ṣād and zāy; the ordinary reading preserves clear ṣād, while Ḥamza’s imāla approaches zāy and cannot be represented precisely in writing.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r1.anchor: وروى عريان بن أبي سفيان عن أبي عمرو أنه كان يقرأ بين الصاد والزاي مثل حمزة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r2.speaker: الكسائي عن حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r2.claim: Reports differ on whether Ḥamza shades only quiescent ṣād toward zāy or also moving ṣād; some say he gives the zāy outright only when ṣād is quiescent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r2.anchor: وقال الكسائي عن حمزة إنه كان يفعل ذلك بالصاد الساكنة خاصة ولا يفعله بالمتحركة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r3.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī follows Ḥamza in ṣād before dāl in قصد and related forms; he says sīn is more common in Arabic but reads ṣād to follow the written Qurʾānic text.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r3.anchor: وكان الكسائي يتابع حمزة في ﴿ قصد ﴾ و ﴿ يصدر الرعاء ﴾ وما كان مثل ذلك

IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r4.claim: Sīn is etymologically original, but scribes and readers use ṣād to ease articulation beside emphatic ṭāʾ: both sounds can be made with the tongue raised, unlike sīn and ṭāʾ together.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p106/r4.anchor: والسين الأصل والكتاب بالصاد وإنما كتبت بالصاد ليقربوها من الطاء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r1.claim: Shading ṣād toward voiced zāy matches the voicing of ṭāʾ while retaining a sibilant; the same voicing rationale applies to the cited ṣād+dāl words.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r1.anchor: وأما إمالة الصاد إلى الزاي فلأن الصاد وإن كانت من حروف الإطباق فهي مهموسة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r2.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r2.claim: Ḥamza pronounces hāʾ with ḍamma and mīm quiescent in عليهم, إليهم, and لديهم; other readers use kasra on hāʾ.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108/r2.anchor: فقرأ ﴿ عليهم ﴾ بضم الهاء حمزة وكذلك ﴿ إليهم ﴾ و ﴿ لديهم ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr connects plural mīm to wāw whether the preceding hāʾ is kasra or ḍamma.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r1.anchor: فكان ابن كثير يصل الميم بواو انضمت الهاء قبلها أو انكسرت

IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r2.claim: Nafiʿ has reports allowing raised or quiescent mīm; the author’s own recitation uses sukūn. Warsh keeps hāʾ kasra and joins mīm to wāw before an initial vowel.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r2.anchor: واختلفوا عن نافع في الميم فقال إسماعيل بن جعفر وابن جماز وقالون والمسيبي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r3.speaker: عاصم ونافع وابن كثير وابن عامر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r3.claim: With a following consonant, these readers keep hāʾ kasra and raise mīm; Abū ʿAmr raises neither, while Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī raise both.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r3.anchor: فكان عاصم ونافع وابن كثير وابن عامر يمضون على كسر الهاء ويضمون الميم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r4.claim: Kasra on hāʾ follows a preceding kasra or yāʾ because hāʾ is close to yāʾ; plural wāw is retained as the original plural marker, parallel to dual alif in عليهما.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p108#2/r4.anchor: فأما من كسر الهاء ووصل الميم بواو وهو قول ابن كثير ونافع في أحد قوليه فإنه استثقل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r1.speaker: عاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r1.claim: These readers keep hāʾ kasra and mīm sukūn; the dual alif already distinguishes two, while plural mīm distinguishes many, so wāw can be omitted for ease.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r1.anchor: وأما من كسر الهاء وأسكن الميم وهو قول عاصم وأبي عمرو وابن عامر والكسائي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r2.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r2.claim: Ḥamza’s ḍamma on hāʾ reflects its underlying form, since the pronoun begins with ḍamma in هم.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r2.anchor: وأما الضمة في الهاء من ﴿ عليهم ﴾ وهو قول حمزة فهي أصل الهاء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r3.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r3.claim: When mīm meets a following consonant it must move; some restore its original ḍamma while leaving hāʾ kasra, others match kasras to avoid a heavy ḍamma after kasra.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r3.anchor: وأما من ترك الهاء مكسورة وضم الميم عند لقائها الساكن فلأن الميم لا بد

IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r4.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī restores both mīm and hāʾ to ḍamma before a following consonant, avoiding the transition from kasra to ḍamma.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r4.anchor: وأما من كسر الهاء إذا لم يلق الميم ساكن وضمها إذا لقي الميم ساكن وهو قول الكسائي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r5.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r5.claim: Ḥamza limits hāʾ-ḍamma to عليهم, إليهم, and لديهم: when followed by an overt noun, their yāʾ becomes alif, which cannot follow a kasra, so the pronoun follows the overt form.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p110/r5.anchor: وإنما خص حمزة هذه الأحرف الثلاثة بالضم أعني ﴿ عليهم ﴾ و ﴿ لديهم ﴾ و ﴿ إليهم ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r1.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r1.claim: These readers take غير المغضوب عليهم in the genitive as an adjective of الذين; Ibn Kathīr is reported with a different form, though another transmission agrees with the majority.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r1.anchor: قرأ ﴿ غير المغضوب عليهم ﴾ بخفض الراء نافع وعاصم وأبو عمر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r2.speaker: الخليل بن أحمد
IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r2.claim: Al-Khalīl permits Ibn Kathīr’s form as a detached adjective or as an accusative circumstantial phrase; he also allows repeating صراط before غير.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r2.anchor: وقال الخليل وهي جائزة على وجه الصفة للذين أنعم الله عليهم يعني بالصفة القطع من ذكر الذين

IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r3.speaker: الأخفش
IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash analyzes the accusative as an exception, but Ibn Mujāhid explicitly calls this mistaken; genitive غير is the adjective of الذين.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p111/r3.anchor: وقد قال الأخفش نصب غير على الاستثناء وهذا غلط

QIRAAT-ER:1:7:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:1#1/r1.claim: Replacing ṣād with sīn leaves the surface meaning unchanged and makes the sound closer to the cognate sabīl.
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:1#1/r1.anchor: same surface meaning but phonetically closer to sabīl cognate

QIRAAT-ER:1:7:1#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:1#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:1#2/r1.claim: Ishmām colors ṣād with zāy, producing a transitional articulation between ṣ and s.
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:1#2/r1.anchor: ishmām (ṣ with z-color); transitional articulation between ṣ and s

QIRAAT-ER:1:7:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:4#1/r1.claim: This reading lengthens the pronoun vowel through ṣilat al-mīm; it is phonetic.
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:4#1/r1.anchor: lengthened pronoun vowel (silat al-mīm); phonetic variant

QIRAAT-ER:1:7:4#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:4#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:4#2/r1.claim: This reading uses a short ḍamma on the pronoun instead of kasra.
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:4#2/r1.anchor: short ḍamma pronoun vowel instead of kasra

QIRAAT-ER:1:7:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:1:7:7#1/r1.claim: The canonical variant gives the pronoun a ḍamma vowel.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p37#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p37#2/r1.speaker: النبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p37#2/r1.claim: The Prophet points to Jews as those under divine anger, in response to a question at Wādī al-Qurā.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p37#2/r1.anchor: عن بديل العقيلي قال أخبرني عبد الله بن شقيق أنه أخبره من سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بوادي القرى

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p37#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p37#2/r2.speaker: النبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p37#2/r2.claim: The Prophet identifies Christians as the astray when asked who they are at Wādī al-Qurā.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r2.claim: Alladhīna is a relative pronoun, usually yāʾ in every case but sometimes wāw in the nominative; it refers to rational beings, unlike alladhī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r2.anchor: والأفصح كونه بالياء في أحواله الثلاثة، وبعض العرب يجعله بالواو في حالة الرفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r3.claim: Deleting the nūn of the relative pronoun is allowed, though some grammarians restrict it to poetic necessity unless it is not for specification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r3.anchor: واستعماله بحذف النون جائز، وخص بعضهم ذلك بالضرورة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r4.claim: Niʿma is ease and comfort; anʿamta makes someone possess a blessing, with ʿalā arising through an added sense of gracious favor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r4.anchor: النعمة: لين العيش وخفضه، ولذلك قيل للجنوب النعامى للين هبوبها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r5.claim: Anʿama illustrates one of the twenty-four meanings of form IV, making its object a possessor of the root's meaning, here a blessing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p45/r5.anchor: والهمزة في أنعم بجعل الشيء صاحب ما صيغ منه، إلا أنه ضمن معنى التفضل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r1.claim: Most grammarians treat ʿalā as a preposition, but Sībawayh treats it as a locative noun except in set uses; its main sense is literal or figurative elevation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r1.anchor: على: حرف جر عند الأكثرين، إلا إذا جرت بمن، أو كانت في نحو هون عليك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r2.claim: ʿAlā can also mean about, with, in, alongside, because of, from, or serve as an extra particle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r2.anchor: وزيد أن تكون بمعنى عن، وبمعنى الباء، وبمعنى في، وللمصاحبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r3.claim: The pronoun hum is masculine plural and rational, and is inflected for nominative, accusative, and genitive positions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r3.anchor: هم ضمير جمع غائب مذكر عاقل، ويكون في موضع رفع ونصب وجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r4.speaker: حمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r4.claim: Among ten reported forms of ʿalayhim, Ḥamza reads the hāʾ with ḍamma and the mīm quiescent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r4.anchor: وحكى اللغويون في عليهم عشر لغات ضم الهاء، وإسكان الميم، وهي قراءة حمزة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r5.claim: The majority read the hāʾ of ʿalayhim with kasra and leave the mīm quiescent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r5.anchor: وكسرها وإسكان الميم، وهي قراءة الجمهور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan lengthens the kasra of hāʾ and mīm with a following yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r6.anchor: وكسر الهاء والميم وياء بعدها، وهي قراءة الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r7.speaker: ابن كثير وقالون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr and, in one report, Qālūn use kasra on hāʾ, ḍamma on mīm, and a following wāw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r7.anchor: وكسر الهاء وضم الميم وواو بعدها، وهي قراءة ابن كثير، وقالون بخلاف عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r8.speaker: الأعرج والخفاف عن أبي عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān lists forms that lengthen the mīm with wāw or omit it, and other combinations of hāʾ and mīm vowels, among the ten reported ʿalayhim readings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p46/r8.anchor: وكسر الهاء وضم الميم بغير واو وضم الهاء والميم وواو بعدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r1.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r1.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq reads “straight path” in annexation, meaning the religion that is upright.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r1.anchor: وقرأ جعفر الصادق: صراط مستقيم بالإضافة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r2.claim: On al-Ḥasan’s and al-Ḍaḥḥāk’s reading, “the path of those” is a definite apposition to an indefinite, like “a straight path, God’s path.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r2.anchor: فعلى قراءة الحسن والضحاك يكون صراط الذين بدل معرفة من نكرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r3.claim: On al-Ṣādiq’s and the majority’s readings, “the path of those” is an apposition of one definite to another, clarifying the previously somewhat vague “straight path.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r3.anchor: وعلى قراءة الصادق وقراءات الجمهور تكون بدل معرفة من معرفة صراط الذين بدل شيء من شيء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r4.claim: This apposition restates the request for guidance, making it firmer and more emphatic by directing it to the path of those God favored.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r4.anchor: وجيء بها للبيان لأنه لما ذكر قبل اهدنا الصراط المستقيم كان فيه بعض إبهام،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r5.claim: A rare interpretation says the second path is not the first, as though a conjunction had been read; interpreters differ over its identification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r5.anchor: ومن غريب القول أن الصراط الثاني ليس الأول، بل هو غيره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r6.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r6.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad identifies the favored path as knowledge of God and understanding from Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r6.anchor: قيل هو العلم بالله والفهم عنه، قاله جعفر بن محمد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r7.claim: Another interpretation identifies the path as fulfilling religious obligations and following the Prophetic sunna.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r7.anchor: وقيل التزام الفرائض واتباع السنن، وقيل هو موافقة الباطن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r8.claim: Another interpretation makes the path harmony between inward and outward states in the fullness of divine favor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r8.anchor: وقيل هو موافقة الباطن للظاهر في إسباغ النعمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, ʿUmar, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read “the path of those whom You favored” without the relative pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r9.anchor: وقرأ: صراط من أنعمت عليهم، ابن مسعود، وعمر، وابن الزبير، وزيد بن علي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to identify those favored as believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r10.anchor: أو المؤمنون، قاله ابن عباس. أو الأنبياء والمؤمنون،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r11.speaker: وكيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r11.claim: Wakīʿ identifies those favored as prophets and believers, or as Muslims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r11.anchor: أو الأنبياء والمؤمنون، أو المسلمون، قاله وكيع، أقوال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attributes the majority’s identification to the four groups named in 4:69, and also records Ibn ʿAbbās’s view that they are believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: والجمهور أراد صراط النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r13.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the favored people as the Companions of Muḥammad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن: أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r14.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r14.claim: One group identifies them as the believing Israelites.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also identifies them as Moses’s followers before they altered the message.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r15.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أصحاب موسى قبل أن يبدلوا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r16.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r16.claim: Qatāda restricts those favored to the prophets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p48/r16.anchor: وقال قتادة: الأنبياء خاصة. وقال أبو العالية:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies those favored as Muḥammad, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r1.anchor: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر، انتهى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r2.claim: The wording leaves divine favor unrestricted, so it encompasses every kind of favor; the text supplies no basis for narrowing it to a particular favor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r2.anchor: ولم يقيد الأنعام ليعم جميع الأنعام، أعني عموم البدل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r3.claim: Some say God favored them by creating them for felicity; others say He rescued them from ruin, or guided them to follow the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r3.anchor: وقيل أنعم عليهم بخلقهم للسعادة، وقيل بأن نجاهم من الهلكة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r4.claim: Sufi writers add many restrictions, but the wording does not support assigning the favor one particular restriction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r4.anchor: وروي عن المتصوفة تقييدات كثيرة غير هذه، وليس في اللفظ ما يدل على تعيين قيد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilites affirm that God bestows favor on unbelievers, while others deny it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r5.anchor: واختلف هل لله نعمة على الكافر؟ فأثبتها المعتزلة ونفاها غيرهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r6.claim: “Upon them” is syntactically accusative, as are prepositional phrases attached to an active verb or equivalent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r6.anchor: وموضع عليهم نصب، وكذا كل حرف جر تعلق بفعل، أو ما جرى مجراه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r7.claim: The active “You favored” gently appeals to God’s prior generosity to secure acceptance of the plea for continued guidance, like reminding a benefactor of his customary kindness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r7.anchor: وبناء أنعمت للفاعل استعطاف لقبول التوسل بالدعاء في الهداية وتحصيلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r8.claim: The usual Arabic construction changes the verb’s person with an attached pronoun, though another dialect keeps it unchanged.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r8.anchor: وانقلاب الفاعل مع المضمر هي اللغة الشهرى، ويجوز إقرارها معه على لغة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r10.claim: “Ghayr” is masculine singular by default; feminine agreement may follow its form or its meaning, and it denotes some kind of difference.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r10.anchor: غير مفرد مذكر دائما وإذا أريد به المؤنث جاز تذكير الفعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r11.claim: “Ghayr” is originally an adjective, can mark exception, must be annexed, and cannot take the definite article or become definite merely through annexation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r11.anchor: ومدلوله المخالفة بوجه ما، وأصله الوصف، ويستثنى به ويلزم الإضافة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r12.speaker: ابن السراج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r12.claim: Ibn al-Sarrāj holds that “ghayr” becomes definite by annexation when the thing it differs from is a single definite referent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r12.anchor: ومذهب ابن السراج أنه إذا كان المغاير واحدا تعرف بإضافته إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r13.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r13.claim: Sībawayh allows a normally non-defining annexation to become defining when it is intended as such, making “ghayr” definite with a definite complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r13.anchor: وتقدم عن سيبويه أن كل ما إضافته غير محضة، قد يقصد بها التعريف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r14.speaker: البيانيون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r14.claim: Rhetoricians say “ghayr” or “mithl” is nearly required before the predicate in examples where it means anyone sharing the stated quality.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r14.anchor: وزعم البيانيون أن غير أو مثلا في باب الإسناد إليهما مما يكاد يلزم تقديمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r15.claim: The rhetoricians mean that anyone sharing the described quality is expected by analogy and custom to act in the stated way.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p49/r15.anchor: ولكنهم يعنون أن كل من كان مثله في الصفة كان من مقتضى القياس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r1.claim: “Al-maghdūb ʿalayhim” means those incurred anger; anger can also mean turning away because that is one of its consequences.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r1.anchor: المغضوب عليهم، الغضب: تغير الطبع لمكروه، وقد يطلق على الإعراض لأنه من ثمرته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r2.claim: The particle lā serves negation, command, or redundancy; contrary to the Kufans, it is not a noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r2.anchor: لا حرف يكون للنفي وللطلب وزائدا، ولا يكون اسما خلافا للكوفيين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r3.claim: The root of ḍalāl carries senses including perishing, disappearing, being lost or ignorant, straying, bewilderment, and wavering; Qurʾanic uses can mean lack of detailed knowledge or love.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r3.anchor: والضلال سلوك سبيل غير القصد، ضل عن الطريق سلك غير جادتها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r4.claim: The non-majority genitive reading of “ghayr”; al-Khalīl reports Ibn Kathīr’s accusative reading, also attributed to ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿūd, ʿAlī, and Ibn al-Zubayr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r4.anchor: وروى الخليل عن ابن كثير النصب، وهي قراءة عمر، وابن مسعود، وعلي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r5.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r5.claim: Abū ʿAlī analyzes the genitive as an apposition to “those” or to the pronoun in “upon them,” but Abū Ḥayyān says both are weak because “ghayr” is adjectival.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r5.anchor: فالجر على البدل من الذين، عن أبي علي، أو من الضمير في عليهم، وكلاهما ضعيف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r6.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r6.claim: Sībawayh permits the genitive as an adjective, taking “ghayr” as definite through annexation; Abū Ḥayyān also reports Ibn al-Sarrāj’s narrower rationale and rejects a generic-plural rationale.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r6.anchor: أو على النعت عن سيبويه، ويكون إذ ذاك غير تعرفت بما أضيفت إليه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r7.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r7.claim: Al-Mahdawī and others take the accusative as a circumstantial accusative from “those”; Abū Ḥayyān rejects it because the annexed complement has no syntactic position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r7.anchor: أو من الذين قاله المهدوي وغيره، وهو خطأ، لأن الحال من المضاف إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r8.claim: The poetic line means its speaker is unlike people easily deceived; reversing the placement of “ghayr” reverses the intended meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p50/r8.anchor: غيري بأكثر هذا الناس ينخدع غرضه أنه ليس ممن ينخدع ويغتر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r1.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash, al-Zajjāj, and others treat the accusative as a disconnected exception; al-Qurrāʾ object because of the following lā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r1.anchor: على الاستثناء، قاله الأخفش، والزجاج وغيرهما، وهو استثناء منقطع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r2.speaker: القراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r2.claim: Al-Qurrāʾ allow lā to be extra only after a prior negation, citing poetic usage and 17:61; Abū Ḥayyān discusses competing analyses of the cited poems.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r2.anchor: قال لأن لا، لا تزاد إلا إذا تقدم النفي، نحو قول الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r3.claim: Against interpreters who call lā redundant in the verse about “my generosity,” he argues it is the object of “refused”; “al-bukhl” is an apposition or purpose object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r3.anchor: بل الأظهر أن لا مفعول بأبى، وأن لفظة لا لا تتعلق بها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r4.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r4.claim: A further analysis attributed to al-Khalīl supplies an implied “I mean” before “ghayr.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r4.anchor: وقيل انتصب غير بإضمار أعني وعزى إلى الخليل، وهذا تقدير سهل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r5.claim: “Upon them” is nominative as the passive subject of “incurred anger”; grammarians discuss when a prepositional phrase may stand as passive subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r5.anchor: وعليهم في موضع رفع بالمغضوب على أنه مفعول لم يسم فاعله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r6.claim: The lā before “those astray” reinforces negation; placing it in the coordination prevents “those astray” from being mistaken as part of “those You favored.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r6.anchor: ولا في قوله: ولا الضالين لتأكيد معنى النفي، لأن غير فيه النفي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r7.speaker: عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r7.claim: ʿUmar and Ubayy read “and not those astray” with “ghayr”; variants are also reported for the case ending of rāʾ, distinguishing the two groups.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r7.anchor: وقرأ عمر وأبي وغير الضالين، وروي عنهما في الراء في الحرفين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī introduces a grammatical example to illustrate the semantic closeness of ghayr and lā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p51/r8.anchor: أتى الزمخشري بمسألة ليبين بها تقاربهما فقال: وتقول أنا زيدا غير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that “ghayr” allows an object before it, just as lā does, and uses this to establish their grammatical and semantic similarity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r1.anchor: لكنهم تسمحوا في العامل المضاف إليه غير، فأجازوا تقديم معموله على غير إجراء لغير مجرى لا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls al-Zamakhsharī’s argument very weak: the construction is disputed, similarity in meaning does not transfer syntax, and “أنا زيدا غير ضارب” is unattested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r2.anchor: وهذا الذي ذهب إليه الزمخشري مذهب ضعيف جدا، بناه على جواز أنا زيدا لا ضارب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r3.claim: Supplying an omitted “path” before “ghayr” yields weak analyses, including an adjective before its apposition or repeated apposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r3.anchor: وقدّر بعضهم في غير المغضوب محذوفا، قال التقدير غير صراط المغضوب عليهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r4.speaker: أيوب السختياني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r4.claim: Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī reads “wa-laḍ-ḍāllīn” with a hamza in place of the long vowel to avoid two adjacent vowelless letters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r4.anchor: وقرأ أيوب السختياني: ولا الضألين، بإبدال الألف همزة فرارا من التقاء الساكنين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r5.claim: The hamza substitution occurs in words such as dāba and shāba, but it is too rare to be treated as a productive rule, despite Abū al-Fatḥ’s dialect argument.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r5.anchor: ومع ذلك فلا ينقاس هذا الإبدال لأنه لم يكثر كثرة توجب القياس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r6.speaker: أبو زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r6.claim: Abū Zayd records dāba and shāba as dialect examples; he first thought ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd had misread until he heard the forms from Arabs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52/r6.anchor: قال أبو زيد: سمعت عمرو بن عبيد يقرأ فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r1.claim: Putting favor in the verbal relative clause of “those” fixes it to an established act, while the participial “incurred anger” leaves its time broad; the past verb specifies confirmed favor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r1.anchor: وجعل الإنعام في صلة الذين، والغضب في صلة أل، لأن صلة الذين تكون فعلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r2.claim: The passive “incurred anger” avoids directly attributing anger to God in a humble plea for kindness, and prepares the parallel ending “those astray.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r2.anchor: وبناه للمفعول، لأن من طلب منه الهداية ونسب الإنعام إليه لا يناسب نسبة الغضب إليه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r3.claim: The intended favor is religious; “those angered” and “those astray” are general categories of everyone who incurs anger and goes astray.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالإنعام، الإنعام الديني، والمغضوب عليهم والضالين عام في كل من غضب عليه وضل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Suddī, and Ibn Zayd identify those angered as Jews and those astray as Christians.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r4.anchor: وقيل المغضوب عليهم اليهود، والضالون النصارى، قاله ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، ومجاهد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r5.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r5.claim: This Jews-and-Christians interpretation is also reported from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim from the Prophet; Abū Ḥayyān says it must be followed if authentic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r5.anchor: وروي هذا عن عدي بن حاتم، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r6.claim: Other identifications say the angered are Jews and polytheists; Sufi restrictions also circulate but are not supported by the verse’s wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r6.anchor: وقيل اليهود والمشركون، وقيل غير ذلك. وقد روي في كتب التفسير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r7.claim: Divine anger can mean the will to punish, an attribute of essence given God’s prior knowledge, or the act of inflicting punishment, an attribute of action.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r7.anchor: والغضب من الله تعالى إرادة الانتقام من العاصي لأنه عالم بالعبد قبل خلقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r8.claim: Anger precedes misguidance despite resulting from it because it is paired antithetically with favor; the order also suits the verse-ending cadence and the conjunction itself implies no sequence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r8.anchor: وقدم الغضب على الضلال، وإن كان الغضب من نتيجة الضلال ضل عن الحق فغضب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r9.claim: If the groups mean Jews and Christians, Jews come first because they appeared earlier or are more hostile.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r9.anchor: فالتقديم إما للزمان أو لشدة العداوة، لأن اليهود أقدم وأشد عداوة من النصارى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r10.claim: The cited poetry illustrates the hamza substitution; if it is a dialect as Abū al-Fatḥ says, Abū Ḥayyān reasons that the substitution should be productive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p52#2/r10.anchor: إذا ما العوالي بالعبيط احمأرت وقول الآخر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p53/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p53/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p53/r6.claim: Some analyses posit omitted “path” before “not angered,” while other syntactic choices create many further ellipses in the sūra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p53/r6.anchor: ومنه حذف صراط من قوله غير المغضوب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r1.claim: The sūra uses fronting and delay in “we worship, we seek help” and in “those angered, those astray.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r1.anchor: التقديم والتأخير، وهو في قوله نعبد، ونستعين، والمغضوب عليهم، والضالين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r2.claim: The apposition “the path of those whom You favored” is explicit clarification after the initially vague “straight path.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r2.anchor: النوع السابع: التفسير، ويسمى التصريح بعد الإبهام، وذلك في بدل صراط الذين من الصراط المستقيم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r8.speaker: الجمهور المكيون والكوفيون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r8.claim: The Meccan and Kufan majority count the basmala as a verse and do not count “whom You favored” separately; other counters reverse those choices.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p54/r8.anchor: عد الجمهور المكيون والكوفيون بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم آية، ولم يعدوا أنعمت عليهم،

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r1.claim: The second ṣirāṭ is a complete appositive for the first; apposition reinforces the relation and explains the straight path as the path of Muslims, powerfully affirming its soundness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r1.anchor: بدل من الصراط الأول بدل الكل من الكل وهو الذي يسميه إبن مالك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r2.speaker: إبن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r2.claim: Ibn Malik calls this a matching apposition to avoid calling God part of a whole in phrases such as the path of God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r2.anchor: وهو الذي يسميه إبن مالك البدل الموافق أو المطابق تحاشيا من إطلاق الكل على الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r3.claim: Some take the second path as an adjective; an unusual report treats it as distinct from the first and offers several interpretations.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r3.anchor: وقيل صفة له ومن غريب المنقول أن الصراط الثاني غير الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r4.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r4.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad interprets the second path as knowledge of God and understanding from Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r4.anchor: فمن جعفر بن محمد هو العلم بالله والفهم عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r5.claim: Other reported interpretations make it inward agreement with outward gratitude, or observance of religious duties and sunnas; Alusi dismisses the latter as a departure from the straight path.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r5.anchor: وقيل موافقة الباطن للظاهر في إسباغ النعمة وقيل إلتزام الفرائض والسنن ولايخفى أن هذا القول خروج عن الصراط المستقيم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r6.speaker: إبن مسعود وزيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Zayd ibn ʿAli read “the path of those whom You favored” as “the path of whom You favored”; the reading is also transmitted from ʿUmar and the Prophet's Household.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r6.anchor: وقرأ إبن مسعود وزيد بن علي صراط من أنعمت عليهم وهو المروي عن عمر وأهل البيت

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r7.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r7.claim: Al-Shihab infers that the variant allows ambiguous names such as “who” to be applied to God; Alusi says the inference is mistaken because the annexed pronoun is the object, not agent, of the favor.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r7.anchor: قال الشهاب : وفيه دليل على جواز إطلاق الأسماء المبهمة ( كمن ) على الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r8.claim: Divine favor is conveying benefit to rational beings; hence one does not say that God favored a horse, and the blessing is defined as an unmotivated benefit to a human.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r8.anchor: والأنعام إيصال الإحسان إلى الغير من العقلاء كما قاله الراغب فلا يقال أنعم على فرسه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r9.claim: Reported identifications of the favored include believers generally, prophets, the followers of Moses and Jesus before textual alteration and abrogation, Muhammad's Companions, or Muhammad with Abu Bakr and ʿUmar.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r9.anchor: وأختلف في هؤلاء المنعم عليهم فقيل المؤمنون مطلقا وقيل الأنبياء وقيل أصحاب موسى وعيسى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r10.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r10.claim: Alusi prefers Ibn ʿAbbas's broad interpretation: prophets, angels, martyrs, the truthful, and everyone who obeys and worships God, as in 4:69; the unqualified blessing embraces God's innumerable favors.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r10.anchor: عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن المراد بالذين أنعمت عليهم الأنبياء والملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r11.claim: Other explanations say God favored them by creating them for felicity, saving them from destruction, or guiding them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r11.anchor: وقيل أنعم عليهم بخلقهم للسعادة وقيل بأن نجاهم من الهلكة وقيل بالهداية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r12.claim: The first-person past tense “You favored” appeals tenderly to God's prior favor and asks Him to complete it by answering the prayer for guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r12.anchor: وفي بناء أنعمت للفاعل إستعطاف فكأن الداعي يقول أطلب منك الهداية إذ سبق إنعامك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r13.claim: The source lists ten transmitted pronunciations of عليهم, including variants in vowel on the hāʾ and mīm, whether mīm is still or followed by a vowel or glide.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p93/r13.anchor: وحكى اللغويون في ( عليهم ) عشر لغات ضم الهاء وإسكان الميم وهي قراءة حمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r1.claim: The remaining transmitted forms of عليهم vary the hāʾ and mīm vowels and whether a following wāw or yāʾ is pronounced; named transmitters include al-Aʿraj, Muslim ibn Jundub, Ibn Hurmuz, and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r1.anchor: وهي قراءة الأعرج ومسلم بن جندب وجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r2.claim: The set of ten forms comprises combinations of still, lengthened, or unlengthened mīm and differing hāʾ/mīm vowels; their arguments are treated in grammar books.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r2.anchor: وحاصلها ضم الهاء مع سكون الميم أو ضمها بإشباع أو دونه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r3.claim: “Other than those who incurred anger” is a complete appositive for “those whom You favored”; taking it as an appositive for their pronoun is semantically awkward, though the relative clause remains grammatically attached.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r3.anchor: ( غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين ( بدل من الذين بدل كل من كل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r4.claim: Sibawayh treats ghayr as an explanatory or restrictive adjective of “those”; Alusi argues the partly specified group can function like an indefinite despite the relative phrase's definiteness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p94/r4.anchor: وعن سيبويه أنها صفة الذين مبينة أو مقيدة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r1.speaker: العلامة الساليكوتي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r1.claim: Al-Salikuti and others offer an analysis of ghayr's definiteness through the partly specified group; Alusi says their explanation has a difficulty.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r1.anchor: قاله العلامة الساليكوتي وغيره ولايخلو عن دغدغة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r2.speaker: المحققين من علماء العربية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r2.claim: Alusi adopts the view that ghayr can become definite by annexation when it lies between two definite opposites, such as motion and stillness; another rule permits definiteness when the annexed term has one opposite.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r2.anchor: أن ( غير ) هنا معرفة لأن المحققين من علماء العربية قالوا إنها قد تتعرف بالإضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r3.speaker: عمر إبن الخطاب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r3.claim: ʿUmar read ghayra in the accusative; it is also transmitted irregularly from Ibn Kathir, most plausibly as a circumstantial accusative referring to the pronoun in “upon them.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r3.anchor: وقرأ عمر إبن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه ( غير ) بالنصب وروى ذلك شاذا عن إبن كثير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r4.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash allows the accusative as a connected or disconnected exception if “favor” is broad; al-Farraʾ forbids joining negative lā to an exceptive phrase meaning “other than.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r4.anchor: الأخفش أن يكون النصب على الإستثنأء المنقطع أو المتصل إن فسر الأنعام بما يعم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r5.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r5.claim: Al-Khalil's analysis, which Alusi endorses, supplies an omitted verb meaning “I mean”; Alusi rejects the circumstantial analysis because it requires indefiniteness or a strained sense of ghayr.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r5.anchor: وعند الخليل النصب بفعل محذوف أعني أعني وبه أقول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r6.claim: An alternative analysis supplies “path” before “those who incurred anger,” but Alusi prefers avoiding ellipsis; the supplied phrase could then be adjective, apposition, or circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم في الآية حذف والتقدير غير صراط المغضوب عليهم وهو ممكن على هذه القراءة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r7.claim: The source gives several technical definitions of anger: a movement arising from desire for vengeance, the will to exact vengeance, or an inward condition producing outward movement; a report likens anger to a glowing ember in the heart.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r7.anchor: وفسر تارة بحركة للنفس مبدؤها إرادة الإنتقام كما في شرح المفتاح للسعد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r8.speaker: الكشاف
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains God's anger as His will to exact vengeance and punish sinners, acting as an angry ruler acts toward a subordinate.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95/r8.anchor: وفي الكشاف معنى غضب الله تعالى إرادة الإنتقام من العصاة وإنزال العقوبة بهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r1.claim: Alusi follows the early community: anger is a divine attribute befitting God, whose reality and manner are unknown, like mercy; “My mercy precedes My anger” concerns the greater or earlier manifestation of mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r1.anchor: قال سلف الأمة هو صفة لله تعالى لائقة بجلال ذاته لا أعلم حقيقتها ولا كيف هي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r2.claim: Ḍalāl originally means destruction, as in 32:10, and in religion means departure from truth; the text also cites a usage where God “destroys” deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r2.anchor: وأصل الضلال الهلاك ومنه قوله تعالى : ( أئذا ضللنا في الأرض ) أي هلكنا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r3.speaker: أبو أيوب السختياني
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r3.claim: Abu Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani read the alif of wa-lā al-ḍāllīn as hamza to avoid adjacent quiescent letters, although that meeting is allowed; comparable dialect forms and a line of poetry are cited.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو أيوب السختياني ( ولا الضالين ) بإبدال الألف همزة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعبدالله بن الزبير
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r4.claim: A reading attributed to ʿUmar and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr adds ghayr before “those astray”; the canonical reading is otherwise, and al-Kufis treat ghayr as negation reinforcing the phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r4.anchor: وروى عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه وعبدالله بن الزبير أنهما كانا يقرآن وغير الضالين والمتواتر لا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r5.claim: The Prophet identifies those under anger as Jews and those astray as Christians; Ahmad transmits it and Ibn Hibban grades it sound, and Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Masʿud also transmit the interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r5.anchor: وقد روى ذلك أحمد في مسنده وحسنه إبن حبان في صحيحه مرفوعا إلى رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r6.speaker: إبن أبي حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim says he knows no disagreement among exegetes that the angry are Jews and the astray are Christians; Alusi rejects replacing this with generic categories of sinners and doctrinally mistaken people.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r6.anchor: وقال إبن أبي حاتم : لا أعلم فيه خلافا للمفسرين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r7.speaker: الرازي
