ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r7.claim: Al-Razi proposes that the angry are unbelievers and the astray are hypocrites, paralleling the opening of al-Baqara; Alusi rejects the analogy against the Prophet's explicit report.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p95#2/r7.anchor: أنه زاد في الشطرنج بغلا فقال ويحتمل أن يقال المغضوب عليهم هم الكفار والضالون هم المنافقون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r1.claim: Qur'anic citations can support the Jewish and Christian identifications, but anger and straying also describe unbelievers generally; Alusi says the hadith is the better proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r1.anchor: والأولى الإستدلال بالحديث لأن الغضب والضلال وردا جميعا في القرآن لجميع الكفار على العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r2.claim: The angry are named before those astray because Jews preceded Christians historically; alternatively, favor contrasts semantically with retribution, or Jews are more hostile and corrupt.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r2.anchor: وإنما قدم سبحانه المغضوب عليهم على الضالين مع أن الضلال في باديء النظر سبب للغضب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r3.speaker: السلفي والديلمي وإبن عدي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r3.claim: A report says whoever lacks charity should curse the Jews; Alusi cites it in support of judging Jewish hostility more severe than that of Christians.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r3.anchor: وورد في الحديث من لم يكن عنده صدقة فليلعن اليهود رواه السلفي والديلمي وإبن عدي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r4.claim: Alusi argues Jews rejected both Jesus and Muhammad, whereas Christians rejected Muhammad; he also rejects the claim that Christian trinitarianism is worse than Jewish claims that God is poor, constrained, or has a son.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r4.anchor: مما يدل على أن اليهود أسوأ حالا من النصارى أنهم كفروا بنبيين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وعيسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r5.claim: Alusi says the claim that Christians are worse, based on “Dalāʾil al-asrār,” mistakes signs' inner meanings and cannot be settled by blind imitation because this is not a subsidiary legal question.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p96/r5.anchor: وقول النصارى بالتثليث ليس أفظع من قول اليهود إن الله فقير ونحن أغنياء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r1.claim: Some say “those astray” comes last to match the verse endings; Alusi allows this as one factor but rejects it as a sufficient explanation by itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم : تأخير الضالين لموافقة رؤوس الآي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r2.claim: God is directly credited with favor to draw near in prayer, but anger is phrased impersonally as a matter of decorum; the supplicant seeks a path whose blessing is already established.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r2.anchor: وإنما أسند النعمة إليه تعالى تقربا والمقصود طلب الهداية إلى صراط من ثبت إنعام الله تعالى عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r3.speaker: إبن كثير والتنوخي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir and al-Tanukhi classify passive wording after direct address as an unusual kind of rhetorical turn; Alusi says this fits older “variegation” usage, or can be called a turn under al-Sakkaki's broader definition.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r3.anchor: وقد عد إبن كثير في كنز البلاغة والتنوخي في الأقصى للقريب بناء الفعل للمفعول بعد خطاب فاعله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r4.speaker: أبو ميسرة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r4.claim: Abu Maysara reports that Gabriel taught the Prophet to say amin after al-Fatiha; the Prophet then said it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r4.anchor: فقد روى إبن أبي شيبة في مصنفه والبيهقي في الدلائل عن أبي ميسرة أن جبريل أقرأ النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r5.speaker: رسول الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r5.claim: The Prophet instructed congregants to say amin after the imam recites the ending of al-Fatiha, saying God will love them; Hanafis say it quietly, while Shafiʿis say it aloud.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r5.anchor: إذا قرأ يعني الإمام غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين فقولوا آمين يحبكم الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r6.speaker: علي وعبدالله بن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r6.claim: Quiet amin is attributed to ʿAli and Ibn Masʿud and is the Hanafi position; Shafiʿis vocalize it, Hasan says the imam should omit it, and one uncommon report from Abu Hanifa also favors concealment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r6.anchor: وإخفاؤها مذهب ساداتنا الحنفية وهو مذهب أمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وعبدالله بن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r7.claim: Amin is not part of the Qur'an by consensus, so a brief pause separates it from the next sura; the view attributed to Mujahid that it belongs to al-Fatiha is false.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r7.anchor: وليست من القرآن إجماعا ولذا سن الفصل بينها وبين السورة بسكتة لطيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r8.claim: Amin is an Arabic indeclinable imperative-noun meaning “respond”; other views call it broader in meaning, foreign, a divine name, or a form with a doubled mīm, which the source discusses and disputes.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r8.anchor: والصحيح أنها كلمة عربية ومعناها أستجيب وقيل موضوعة لما هو أعم منه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r9.claim: A sound report from Abu Hurayra says the Prophet taught Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that al-Fatiha has no equal in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an and is the seven oft-repeated verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r9.anchor: ما روى بأسانيد صحيحة عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج على أبي بن كعب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r10.claim: Alusi calls al-Fatiha the Mother of the Book and a treasury of hidden knowledge and says some spiritual masters derive cosmic events and rulers' histories from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p97/r10.anchor: فهي أم الكتاب والحاوية من دقائق الأسرار العجب العجاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p98/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p98/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p98/r5.claim: Al-Baqara follows al-Fatiha's sequence: knowledge of the Lord, worship, and requests for worldly and spiritual needs; al-Fatiha's request for guidance is echoed by “guidance for the God-conscious” at its opening.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p98/r5.anchor: ووجه مناسبتها لسورة الفاتحة أن الفاتحة مشتملة على بيان الربوبية أولا والعبودية ثانيا وطلب الهداية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r1.claim: All agree the Fatiha has seven verses, but those counting the basmala begin the final verse at ‘those You favored’; others begin it at ‘not those under wrath.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r1.anchor: واتفقوا على أن الفاتحة سبع آيات فالآية الأولى عند من يعدها من الفاتحة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r2.claim: Those counting the basmala cite its Quranic-script placement and a report from Ibn Abbas through Saʿid b. Jubayr: it is the seventh of the seven oft-repeated verses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r2.anchor: هي أم القرآن قال أبي وقرأها علي سعيد بن جبير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r3.claim: In the same report, Ibn Abbas says the basmala was reserved for this community and not disclosed to anyone before it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p51/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فذخرها لكم فما أخرجها لأحد قبلكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.claim: Ikrima says those favored were granted guidance and steadfastness in faith and right conduct, and identifies them as the prophets.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r1.anchor: قال عكرمة: مننت عليهم بالثبات على الإيمان والاستقامة وهم الأنبياء عليهم السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.claim: Another view includes all prophets and believers whom God kept firm in faith, linked with the verse describing those blessed alongside the prophets.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: هم كل من ثبته الله على الإيمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as the people of Moses and Jesus before they changed their religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هم قوم موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام قبل أن غيروا دينهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.claim: Abd al-Rahman b. Zayd says they are the Prophet and those with him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن ابن زيد: هم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن معه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies them as the Prophet’s family, Abu Bakr, and Umar.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: هم آل الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.claim: Shahr b. Hawshab says they are the Prophet’s Companions and household.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r6.anchor: وقال شهر بن حوشب: هم أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأهل بيته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.claim: Hamza reads the hāʾ of ʿalayhim, ladayhim, and ilayhim with ḍamma; Yaʿqub does so for dual and plural forms preceded by a silent yāʾ, with a stated exception.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r7.anchor: قرأ حمزة: عليهم ولديهم وإليهم بضم هاءاتها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r8.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Jaʿfar fully prolong the plural mīm in connected recitation unless a following consonant is silent; Nafiʿ may choose.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r8.anchor: وضم ابن كثير وأبو جعفر كل ميم جمع مشبعا في الوصل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r9.speaker: ورش وحمزة والكسائي وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r9.claim: The readers differ on hāʾ and plural-mīm vowels before a hamzat al-waṣl: Warsh lengthens at hamzat al-qaṭʿ, while Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, Abu Amr, and Yaʿqub follow the stated preceding-vowel conditions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p54#2/r9.anchor: ونافع يخير، ويضم ورش عند ألف القطع، فإذا تلقته ألف وصل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r1.claim: Those under wrath are people whose path incurred God’s anger; divine anger is the will to punish sinners, but does not befall sinful believers, only disbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r1.anchor: والغضب هو إرادة الانتقام من العصاة، وغضب الله تعالى لا يلحق عصاة المؤمنين إنما يلحق الكافرين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r2.claim: The straying ones are those who departed from guidance; the root sense of straying is perishing or disappearing, like water disappearing into milk.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r2.anchor: أي وغير الضالين عن الهدى. وأصل الضلال الهلاك والغيبوبة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r3.claim: Here ghayr functions as ‘not,’ which permits coordination with lā; if it meant ‘other than,’ such coordination would be ungrammatical.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r3.anchor: وغير هاهنا بمعنى لا ولا بمعنى غير ولذلك جاز العطف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r4.claim: Umar’s reading says ‘the path of those You favored, not those under wrath, and not the straying ones.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r4.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: صراط من أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r5.claim: A reported identification makes the objects of wrath Jews and the straying ones Christians, supported by Quranic descriptions of each group.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r5.anchor: وقيل: المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود والضالون: هم النصارى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r6.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r6.claim: Sahl b. Abd Allah interprets those under wrath as innovators and the straying ones as people departing from the Sunnah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r6.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله: غير المغضوب {عليهم} (1) بالبدعة، ولا الضالين عن السنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r7.claim: The reciter should say Amin after a separate pause; the word is normally light, though grammarians allow a long or short vowel, and means ‘God, hear and answer.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r7.anchor: والسنة للقارئ أن يقول بعد فراغه من قراءة الفاتحة "آمين" بسكتة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada gloss Amin as ‘so be it.’
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: معناه كذلك يكون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r9.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r9.claim: Mujahid says Amin is one of God’s names.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد هو اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r10.claim: Other explanations call Amin the seal of a supplication or God’s seal protecting servants from harm, like a seal protecting a letter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r10.anchor: وقيل: هو طابع الدعاء. وقيل هو خاتم الله على عباده يدفع به الآفات عنهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r11.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when the imam says Amin, worshippers should do so too; angels also say it, and agreement with them brings forgiveness of past sins. Al-Baghawi grades it sound.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p55/r11.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا قال الإمام

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r2.claim: The apposition identifies the believers' path as straight in the strongest way, making its soundness appear self-evident.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r2.anchor: وفائدته التوكيد والتنصيص على أن طريق المسلمين هو المشهود عليه بالاستقامة

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r3.claim: The favored are variously identified as prophets; the Prophet and his Companions; or the uncorrupted, un-abrogated followers of Moses and Jesus.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r3.anchor: وقيل: { الذين أنعمت عليهم } الأنبياء، وقيل: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r4.claim: Divine favors fall into worldly and afterlife kinds; worldly favors are bestowed or acquired, with spiritual and bodily branches, while acquired favors include virtue, good character, adornment, status, and wealth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r4.anchor: ونعم الله وإن كانت لا تحصى كما قال:

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r5.claim: The intended favor is the final afterlife good and whatever leads to it, including forgiveness, divine approval, and residence in the highest ranks; other favors are shared with unbelievers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7/r5.anchor: والمراد هو القسم الأخير وما يكون وصلة إلى نيله من الآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r1.claim: “Not those angered nor astray” may be an apposition to “those You favored,” or a qualifying description showing that true favor joins faith with safety from anger and error.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r1.anchor: بدل من { الذين } على معنى أن المنعم عليهم هم الذين سلموا من الغضب والضلال

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r2.claim: The adjective-like reading is possible if the relative is treated as indefinite or if غير becomes definite by annexation to the unique opposite group.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r2.anchor: وذلك إنما يصح بأحد تأويلين، إجراء الموصول مجرى النكرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads غير in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier or by an implied verb, and it can also be an exception if favors include both groups.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r3.anchor: وعن ابن كثير نصبه على الحال من الضمير المجرور والعامل أنعمت

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r4.claim: Divine anger denotes its ultimate effect, punishment; عليهم is a passive-subject phrase, unlike the earlier construction, and لا reinforces the negation in غير.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r4.anchor: والغضب: ثوران النفس إرادة الانتقام، فإذا أسند إلى الله تعالى أريد به المنتهى

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r5.claim: A recitation adds و before الضالين, and another uses hamza in الضألين to avoid two adjacent still consonants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r5.anchor: وقرىء { وغير الضالين } والضلال: العدول عن الطريق السوي

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r6.claim: A reported interpretation identifies those under anger as Jews and those astray as Christians, linking them to 5:60 and 5:77; the identification is also transmitted as a Prophetic report.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r6.anchor: قيل: { المغضوب عليهم } اليهود لقوله تعالى فيهم:

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r7.claim: A further interpretation calls deliberate sinners angered and those ignorant of God astray: failure of action is impiety, while failure of understanding is error.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r7.anchor: ويتجه أن يقال: المغضوب عليهم العصاة والضالين الجاهلون بالله،

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r8.claim: The favored combine knowledge of truth with doing good; the contrasting groups each lack one of the rational or active faculties.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#2/r8.anchor: لأن المنعم عليه من وفق للجمع بين معرفة الحق لذاته والخير للعمل به

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r1.claim: Āmīn is an imperative noun meaning “answer/accept”; a report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet explained it as “do so.” It is built on fatḥa to avoid two adjacent still consonants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r1.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معناه فقال

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r2.claim: Āmīn is not Qur'an, but ending the sura with it is recommended because Gabriel taught it to the Prophet as a seal on the book; ʿAlī similarly calls it the seal of the Lord of the worlds.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r2.anchor: لكن يسن ختم السورة به لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r3.speaker: وائل بن حجر
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r3.claim: The Prophet said آمين aloud after ولا الضالين; al-Bayḍāwī cites this for an imam's audible response in audible prayers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r3.anchor: لما روي عن وائل بن حجر

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r4.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa is reported not to say آمين, though the better-known report says he says it quietly; a congregant says it with the imam.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r4.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه أنه لا يقوله، والمشهور عنه أنه يخفيه

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r5.claim: A Prophetic report calls al-Fātiḥa unparalleled in Torah, Gospel, and Qur'an, and identifies it as the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur'an.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r5.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبي

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r6.claim: A visiting angel gave the Prophet two lights unavailable to earlier prophets—the opening of the Book and the end of al-Baqara—and each letter recited brings a gift.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال:

BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r7.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r7.claim: A report says recitation of الحمد لله رب العالمين by a child among a people under destined punishment caused God to lift it from them for forty years.
BAYDAWI-FULL:1:7#3/r7.anchor: وعن حذيفة بن اليمان أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.speaker: أبو الفضل محمد المشدالي المغربي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.claim: Al-Mashdali's method for Qur'anic coherence is to identify a surah's purpose, its prerequisites and their distance from the goal, then answer expectations raised as the discourse unfolds.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r2.anchor: قال شيخنا الإمام المحقق أبو الفضل محمد بن العلامة القدوة أبي عبد الله محمد ابن العلامة القدوة أبي القاسم محمد المشدالي المغربي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.claim: A surah's name summarizes its purpose, as a title signals the details within; Adam demonstrated this naming principle when he named things before the angels.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r3.anchor: أن اسم كل سورة مترجم عن مقصودها هلأن أسم كل شيء تظهر المناسبة بينه وبين مسماه عنوانه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.claim: The Fatiha's many titles converge on مراقبة: it is the Mother of the Book, foundation, oft-repeated, treasure, healing, sufficing, complete, protecting, incantation, praise, thanks, supplication and prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r4.anchor: فمدار هذه الأسماء كما ترى على أمر خفي كاف لكل مراد وهو المراقبة التي سأقول إنها مقصودها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.claim: The Fatiha is a treasure, cure, sufficiency, fulfillment, protection and incantation; it gathers praise, gratitude and supplication, with prayer as their greatest assembly.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p11#2/r5.anchor: فكل شيء لا يفتتح بها لا اعتداد به ، وهي كنز لكل شيء شافية لكل داء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.claim: The Fatiha's purpose is to establish God's exclusive right to all praise and perfection, sovereignty over both worlds, worship and aid, and to ask for the path of the successful rather than the doomed; its center is مراقبة.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p12/r1.anchor: الغرض الذي سبقت له الفاتحة وه إثبات استحقاق الله تعالى لجميع المحامد وصفا الكمال ، واختصاصه بملك الدنيا والآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.claim: The basmala relates to the Fatiha as the Fatiha relates to the Qur'an: each is a compact synthesis of what the larger whole details.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p13/r2.anchor: وأشد منه أنه لما كانت نسبة البسملة من الفاتحة نسبة الفاتحة من القرآن صدرت بها الفاتحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.claim: Al-Harali says all Qur'an is God's speech, but some verses voice what creatures at different levels ought to say yet cannot express; God teaches them words that fulfill their duty.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r5.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهذه الآيات أى هذه وما بهدها مما جاء كلام الله فيه جارياعلى لسان خلقه فإن القرآن كله كلام الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.claim: Al-Harali explains the sound report that God divided prayer between Himself and His servant: the first three verses are God's praise, which He accepts from the reciting servant as praise and glorification.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p16/r6.anchor: وتلك هي صلاتهم المقسمة التى عبر عنها فيما صح عنه علية الصلاة والسلام من قوله تعالى : ( قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r1.claim: Al-Harali defines the condemned as those who intentionally oppose guidance and thereby incur divine wrath, or those who turn toward guidance then stray without intending to.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r1.anchor: وأما من هدى وجهة ما فضل عن مرجععها فهو ضلال مذموم لأنه ضالال بعد هدى وهو يكون عن اعوجاج في الجبلة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r2.claim: The requested path is that of God's messengers; because blessing reaches every creature, the request seeks the mercy-specific path of those honored by God, not merely existence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r2.anchor: فأشار إلى أن الاعتصام به في اتباع رسله , ولما كان سبحانه عام النعمة لكل موجود عدواكان أو وليا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r3.claim: Removing the object of bestowed favor broadens the wording; the negation excludes the angry and astray as separate failures, one in action and the other in knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r3.anchor: وان حذف المنعم به لإرادة التعميم من باب تقليل اللفظ لتكثير المعنى فكان من المعلوم أن محط السؤال بعض أهل دمشق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r4.claim: The author reads the angry as a group that rejects action obstinately and the astray as a group deprived of felicity through failure in knowledge, warning against both.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r4.anchor: فعرف أنهم قسمان : قسم أريد للشقاوة فعاند في إخلاله بالعمل فاستوجب الغضب , وقسم لم يرد للسعادة فضل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r5.claim: Using غير rather than an exception marks exclusion from the outset, making clear that the requested universal blessing means the special honor granted to the faithful, not the general gift of existence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18/r5.anchor: فعرف أن المسؤول إنما هو طريق أهل النعمة بصفة الرحيمية تشوقت النفوس إلى معرفتهم فميزهم ببيان أضدادهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r1.claim: Al-Harali says the condemned intentionally show defiance, while the astray turn toward guidance and deviate without intending it; Amin expresses a decisive plea for a response.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r1.anchor: قال الحرالي : { المغضوب عليهم } الذين ظهر منهم المراغمة وتعمد الخالفة فيوجب ذلك الغضب من الأعلى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r2.claim: Amin means the petitioner trusts God not to reject the plea, since nothing can overcome or restrain Him; the word asks Him to respond.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r2.anchor: آمين كلمة عزم من الأمن , مدلولها أن المدعو مأمون منه أن يرد من دعاه لأنه لايعجز شىء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.claim: The Qur'an's arrangement is miraculous, so the Fatiha must retain its required order in prayer; rearrangement or insertion of foreign material invalidates it. Al-Isfahani locates its clearest inimitability in order.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : فإن القرآن معجز والركن الأبين الإعجاز يتعلق بالنظم والترتيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.claim: The spiritual seeker passes through awe of God's attributes, recognizes many perilous paths and the lack of guidance or safety apart from God, then asks for the straight path, its blessed companions and protection from both condemned groups.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.anchor: فلما أشرف وستنار وعرف مواقع الأسرار بالأقدار كأنه قيل له : ماذا تطلب وفي أي مذهب تذهب ؟

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.speaker: مسعود التفتازاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.claim: Al-Taftazani maps the Fatiha's blessings to two creations and two preservations: creation in Rabb al-alamin, preservation in mercy, second creation in judgment, and afterlife preservation in worship onward.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.anchor: كما قال العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي . إلى جميع النعم فغنها ترجع إلى إيجاد وإبقاء ثانيافي دار الفناء والبقاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.claim: Al-Harali says the seven repeated verses are the Qur'an's gathered essence and its contents will be disclosed at creation's completion; earlier scriptures progress from changeable scrolls and lasting books to the Qur'an, which completes religion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p18#2/r7.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي في مفتاح الباب القفل لفهم القرآن المنزل في أخر الباب التاسع منه : ولننه هذه الأبواب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.claim: Al-Harali contrasts the Qur'an's detailed, dispersed sequence with the Fatiha's seven complete universals, and makes the Fatiha a mirror of the servant's move from misguidance to guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r1.anchor: ووجه فوت أم القرآن مقصود تنزيله التفصيل والجوامع , فيه نجوم مبثوثة غير منتظمة , وحداة إثر واحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.claim: A Prophetic report says he was sent to complete noble character; the author links this completion with the Fatiha's comprehensive opening and the Qur'an's culmination.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r2.anchor: بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق . أن إلى ربك المنتهى .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.claim: Al-Harali describes the Qur'an's majesty through rulings spanning immediate and deferred realities, witnessed experience, and reports of the past and patterns that recur in time.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r3.anchor: ومن مجيده وهو ما حربت أحكامه من بين عاجل ما شهد وآجل ما علم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.claim: Al-Harali distinguishes gradual descent that moves understanding between states and rulings from descent from high to low, which may occur with or without intermediaries.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r4.anchor: وما كان منه بتدريج وتقريب للأفهام ففاءت من حال إلى حال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.claim: The passage names al-Baqara 2:281 as the last revealed verse and says its recitation position between the debt verse and the verse before it shows revelation and recitation order can differ.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p21/r5.anchor: وجعلوها بين آية الدين والآية قبلها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an's sevenfold gathering in Muhammad's heart relates to the Mother of Qur'an's universals as the Qur'an's gathering in his heart relates to the Mother.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r1.anchor: وأما الجمع ففي قلبه نسبة جوامعه السبع في أم القرآن إلى القرآن بمنزلة نسبة جمعه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an reached the Prophet on his tongue over the span of the prophetic mission, after its descent to the lowest heaven.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r2.anchor: وعلى لسانه في أمد أيام النبوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.claim: Aisha reports that Muhammad's character was the Qur'an, making his conduct the visible form of its inner reality.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r3.anchor: قالت عائشة رضى الله عنها : كان خلقه القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.claim: Al-Harali says the Fatiha is the Qur'an's mother: its first three verses encompass the divine names and attributes, while its last three cover the creature's way to God, mercy or failure.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r4.anchor: فالآيات الثلاث الول قال شاملة لكل معنى تضمنته الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.claim: Recitation order can differ from revelation chronology; the verse allowing the Prophet to marry certain women was placed before a later restriction.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r5.anchor: فقد يتطابق قرآن الأمر وتطور الخلق وقد لا يتابق والله يتولى إقامتها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.claim: In the authentic report in Muslim and the four Sunan, God says the Fatiha is divided between Himself and His servant: He answers praise, glorification and worship, and grants the servant's final requests.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p22/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضى الله عنه قال : سمعت زسول الله صلى اله عليه وسلم يقول

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.claim: Al-Baqara aims to prove the Book is guidance to follow; belief in the unseen, especially resurrection and the afterlife, is its greatest guidance and organizing theme.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r1.anchor: مقصودها إقامة الدليل على أن الكتاب هدى ليتبع يفي كل ما قال ، وأعظم ما يهدي إليه الإيمالن بالغيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.claim: The cow story makes the surah's title apt because resurrection occurs through an apparently slight human cause; it is a clearer sign of divine power than Abraham's story or earlier Israelite resurrections.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r2.anchor: فلذلك سميت بها السورة وكانت بذلك أحق من قصة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنها في نوع البشر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.claim: The following comparison of hearts and stones shows the guided and astray: hearts become hard and wretched, while stones display fear and yield benefit that reaches God's servants.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r3.anchor: ولا سيما وقد اتبعت بوصف القلوب والحجارة بما عم اللمهتدين بالكتاب والضالين فوصفها بالقسوة الموجبة للشقوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.claim: The Book functions like a caliph from the resolute messengers, guiding every matter to the right exit: rejecting it fails, hesitation nearly perishes, and accepting it brings piety and excellence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r4.anchor: وفيها إشارة إلى أن هذا الكتاب فينا كما لو كان فينا خليفة من أولي العزم من الرسل يرشدنا في كل أمر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.claim: Al-Baqara is also called the Radiant and the Hump: it illuminates guidance and sufficiency, brightens believers' faces at judgment, and exalts belief in the afterlife above every other good after monotheism.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p24/r5.anchor: وسميت الزهراء لإنارتها طريق الهداية والكفاية في الدنيا والآخرة ، ولأيجابها إسفار الوجوه يفي يوم الجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.claim: Because praise is the seventh inclusive letter, the Fatiha begins with it and gathers the seven universals diffused through the Qur'an, as the Qur'an gathers earlier scriptures.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r1.anchor: ولما كان حرف الحمد هو سابعها الجامع افتتح الله به سبحانه وتعالى الفاتحة أم القرآن وأم الكتاب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.claim: The fifth verse's request returns to praise, the sixth to the grace of lawful and forbidden provisions, and the seventh to the sovereign's command; together these complete all seven letters.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p28/r6.anchor: وعادتت مسألة الآيةى الخاتمسة على حرف الحمد ومسألة الآية السادسة على آية النعمة من حرفي الحلال والحرام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.claim: Baqara answers the Fatiha's plea for guidance by directing worshippers to the Book, describing the guided and denied groups as patterns to follow or avoid; its pious are the straight path and its others the path of ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r3.anchor: وأما منسبة ما بعد ذلك للفاتحة فهو أنه لما أخبلا سبحانه وتعالى أن عباده المخلصين سألوا في الفاتحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.claim: Alternatively, the surah's purpose is solely to describe the Book; it establishes the truth of its meaning, exposes disbelief and hypocrisy to show that inward faith matters, then proves its inimitable form and authority for teaching law.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p31/r4.anchor: وإن شئت قلت : مقصود هذه السورة وصف الكتاب فقط وما عدا ذلك فتوابع ولوازم

DURR-FULL:v1p25/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r3.claim: Those granted favor are prophets and believers whom God favored with Islam and prophethood.
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r3.anchor: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} يعني به النبيين والمؤمنين الذين أنعم الله عليهم بالإسلام والنبوة

DURR-FULL:v1p25/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r4.claim: The people under anger are Jews and the misguided are Christians; the account links their fate to the cited description of apes, swine, and evil destination.
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r4.anchor: غير المغضوب عليهم} يقول: أرشدنا غير دين هؤلاء الذين غضبت عليهم وهم اليهود {ولا الضالين} وهم النصارى

DURR-FULL:v1p25/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r5.claim: The Prophet tells worshippers to say amin when the imam says “not those astray,” promising God's love; the prayer is described as salvation from the Fire for Muhammad's community and followers.
DURR-FULL:v1p25/r5.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: فإذا قال الإمام {ولا الضالين} فقولوا

DURR-FULL:v1p35/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p35/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p35/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says the Prophet read “maalik” with an alif and read “ghayri al-maghdub” with the genitive ending.
DURR-FULL:v1p35/r8.anchor:
عن ابن مسعود
أنه قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {مالك يوم الدين} بالألف {غير المغضوب عليهم} خفض

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r1.claim: Umar read “the path of those whom You favored” with “min” and repeated “ghayr” before “the astray.”
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r1.anchor: أنه كان يقرأ / صراط من أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr used the same variant in prayer, with “min” and repeated “ghayr.”
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير قرأ / صراط من أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين / في الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r3.claim: Al-Hasan read “alayhim” with kasra on the ha and mim and an added ya.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r3.anchor: عن الحسن أنه كان يقرأ / عليهمي / بكسر الهاء والميم واثبات الياء

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r4.speaker: الأعرج
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r4.claim: Al-Araj read “alayhumu” with damma on both letters and an added waw; Ibn Kathir is also reported to use a waw variant.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r4.anchor: عن الأعرج أنه كان يقرأ / عليهمو / بضم الهاء والميم وإلحاق الواو

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r5.speaker: ابن إسحق
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq read “alayhum” with both ha and mim in damma and no added waw.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r5.anchor: عن ابن إسحق أنه قرأ {عليهم} بضم الهاء والميم من غير إلحاق واو

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra counts “those You favored” as the sixth verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال {أنعمت عليهم} الآية السادسة

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies those favored as obedient angels, prophets, truthful ones, martyrs, and righteous people.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} يقول: طريق من أنعمت عليهم من الملائكة والنبيين

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r8.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas glosses those favored as believers.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} قال: المؤمنين

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r9.speaker: أبو زيد
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r9.claim: Abu Zayd says “those of the path” means the Prophet and those with him.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r9.anchor: عن أبي زيد في قوله {صراط الذين} قال: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن معه

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r10.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r10.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas identifies the favored as prophets, those under anger as Jews, and the astray as Christians.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r10.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس في قوله {صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم} قال: النبيون {غير المغضوب عليهم} قال: اليهود

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r11.claim: Mujahid identifies those under anger as Jews and the astray as Christians.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد {غير المغضوب عليهم} قال: اليهود {ولا الضالين} قال: النصارى

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r12.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the two descriptions refer collectively to Jews and Christians.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r12.anchor:
عن سعيد بن جبير {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين}
قال: اليهود والنصارى

DURR-FULL:v1p40/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r13.claim: Asked at Wadi al-Qura who the people under anger and those astray were, the Prophet answered Jews and Christians respectively.
DURR-FULL:v1p40/r13.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شقيق قال: أخبرني من سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بوادي القرى

DURR-FULL:v1p42/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r1.claim: Several reports from questions at Wadi al-Qura say the Prophet identified those under anger as Jews and the other group as Christians who are astray.
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شقيق العقيلي قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يحاصر أهل وادي القرى فقال له رجل

DURR-FULL:v1p42/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r2.claim: Asked by Abu Dharr, the Prophet identifies the maghdub as Jews and the dalin as Christians.
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r2.anchor:
عن {المغضوب عليهم} قال: اليهود
قلت {الضالين} قال: النصارى

DURR-FULL:v1p42/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r3.claim: A report through a man of Balayn likewise records the Prophet's answer: Jews are under anger and Christians astray.
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r3.anchor: عن رجل من بلعين عن ابن عم له أنه قال أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بوادي القرى

DURR-FULL:v1p42/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r4.claim: Reports from Ismail ibn Abi Khalid, Adi ibn Hatim, Ibn Masud, and Mujahid repeat the identification of Jews with anger and Christians with misguidance.
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r4.anchor: عن إسمعيل بن أبي أبي خالد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال {المغضوب عليهم} اليهود والضالون هم النصارى

DURR-FULL:v1p42/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r5.claim: The Prophet rebuked al-Shurayd for sitting with his left hand behind his back, calling it the sitting posture of those under anger.
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r5.anchor: عن الشريد قال: مر بي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا جالس هكذا وقد وضعت يدي اليسرى خلف ظهري

DURR-FULL:v1p42/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r6.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r6.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim says he knows of no disagreement among exegetes that the maghdub are Jews and the dalin are Christians.
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r6.anchor: قال ابن أبي حاتم: لا أعلم خلافا بين المفسرين في تفسير {المغضوب عليهم} باليهود {الضالين} بالنصارى

DURR-FULL:v1p42/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r7.speaker: جبريل
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r7.claim: Abu Maysara says Gabriel taught the Prophet to say amin when reaching “nor those astray.”
DURR-FULL:v1p42/r7.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة قال: لما أقرأ جبريل رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v1p43/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r1.speaker: وائل بن حجر
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r1.claim: Wail ibn Hujr heard the Prophet say amin after the final words of al-Fatiha, prolonging his voice.
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r1.anchor: قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين} فقال {آمين} يمد بها صوته

DURR-FULL:v1p43/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r2.speaker: وائل بن حجر
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r2.claim: Another report from Wail says the Prophet added “Lord, forgive me” before amin; a further report says he said amin three times after al-Fatiha.
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r2.anchor: عن وائل بن حجر أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قال {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين} قال: رب اغفر لي {آمين

DURR-FULL:v1p43/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r3.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r3.claim: Ali says the Prophet said amin when he recited “nor those astray.”
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r3.anchor: عن علي سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قال {ولا الضالين} قال {آمين

DURR-FULL:v1p43/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r4.claim: The Prophet instructs the congregation to say amin after the imam recites the final phrase, promising God's love.
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r4.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قرأ - يعني الإمام - {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين} فقولوا {آمين

DURR-FULL:v1p43/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r5.claim: When the imam says amin, worshippers should say it too; whoever's amin coincides with the angels' is forgiven previous sins.
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إذا أمن الإمام فأمنوا فإنه من وافق تأمينه تأمين الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v1p43/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r6.claim: A good-chain report says the followers' amin meets that of heaven's inhabitants, while the person who omits it resembles a warrior whose lot never wins.
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r6.anchor: بسند جيد عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قال الإمام {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

DURR-FULL:v1p43/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r7.speaker: أبو زهير النميري
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r7.claim: Abu Zuhayr recommends ending supplication with amin, like a seal on a page; the Prophet said a persistent supplicant had secured an answer when he sealed his prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p43/r7.anchor: بسند حسن عن أبي زهير النميري وكان من الصحابة أنه كان إذا دعا الرجل بدعاء قال: اختمه بآمين

DURR-FULL:v1p45/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r1.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r1.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai recommended saying “God, forgive me; amin” after the imam recites the closing words.
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r1.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي قال: كان يستحب إذا قال الإمام {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين} أن يقال: اللهم اغفر لي {آمين

DURR-FULL:v1p45/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r2.claim: Mujahid recommends asking for Paradise and refuge from the Fire after the imam's recitation.
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: إذا قال الإمام {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين} فقل: اللهم إني أسألك الجنة وأعوذ بك من النار

DURR-FULL:v1p45/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r3.speaker: الربيع بن خيثم
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r3.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Khaytham says to use any supplication one wishes at this point.
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r3.anchor: عن الربيع بن خيثم قال: إذا قال الإمام {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين} فاستعن من الدعاء ماشئت

DURR-FULL:v1p45/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r4.claim: Ibn Shahin transmits Ubayy ibn Kab's variant with a repeated “ghayr” and amin; al-Hasan explains amin as “O God, respond.”
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r4.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن مسلم قال: في حرف أبي بن كعب / غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين آمين

DURR-FULL:v1p45/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r5.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r5.claim: A report from Anas promises that after reading the basmala and al-Fatiha, saying amin brings forgiveness prayers from every nearby angel.
DURR-FULL:v1p45/r5.anchor: من قرأ {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم} ثم قرأ فاتحة الكتاب ثم قال آمين

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: Sībawayh analyzes ghayr in 1:7 as an adjective meaning other than, not as an exceptive construction.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: He argues that deleting the noun رجل from لو كان معنا رجل إلا زيد makes the intended exception impossible, so إلا زيد here functions descriptively.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.anchor: لو قلت لو كان معنا إلا زيد لهلكنا وأنت تريد الاستثناء لكنت قد أحلت

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: He adduces 21:22 as a parallel in which إلا الله is understood adjectivally, like non-exceptive ghayr.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.anchor: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line uses إلا بغامها descriptively in place of غير بغامها, demonstrating a non-exceptive use of إلا.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: He cites 4:95, غير أولي الضرر, as another Quranic example of ghayr used as an adjective.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.anchor: لا يستوى القاعدون من المؤمنين غير

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: Labīd's phrase غير الجمل supplies a poetic example of ghayr used descriptively to mean other than the camel.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: In another Labīd line, the second ghayr is an adjective for the first; the intended point is that events cannot alter the sharp sword.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: After ما أتاني أحد, Sībawayh permits إلا زيد to be parsed either as an appositive or as an adjective.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.anchor: جعلت إلا زيد بدلا وإن شئت جعلته صفة

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: Without an antecedent noun, ما أتاني إلا زيد cannot be treated like the preceding construction; only the descriptive analysis is available.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.anchor: تريد أن تجعل الكلام بمنزلة مثل وإنما يجوز ذلك صفة

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: Amr ibn Maʿdīkarib's verse is paraphrased as كل أخ غير الفرقدين, with the ghayr phrase qualifying كل.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: Al-Shammākh's verse gives another poetic example of a ghayr phrase qualifying a noun, rather than forming an exception.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.claim: He disallows raising Zayd by ellipsis here, since the noun completed by the phrase cannot be left unexpressed in this analysis.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكلوكانمعنارجلإلازيدلغلبن.anchor: لأنك لا تضمر الاسم الذي هذا من تمامه

RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r7.claim: The blessed are those granted favor in every condition and station; the excluded are people of ignorance and error.
RAZI-FULL:v1p15/r7.anchor: من أهل الجهالات والضلالات والصلاة على محمد المؤيد بأفضل المعجزات

RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r5.claim: The stations of those favored by God are exalted; the preceding explanations let a reader glimpse the beginnings of their states.
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r5.anchor: وأما قوله جل جلاله ﴿ صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين ﴾ فما أجل هذه المقامات وأعظم مراتب هذه الدرجات !

RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r6.claim: The sūra contains limitless discussions and secrets; saying it contains ten thousand problems is an expression suited to its audience's understanding.
RAZI-FULL:v1p20/r6.anchor: فقد ظهر بالبيان الذي سبق أن هذه السورة مشتملة على مباحث لا نهاية لها وأسرار لا غاية لها وأن قول من يقول هذه السورة مشتملة على عشرة آلاف مسئلة

TAB:1:7/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r1.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r1.claim: The phrase specifies which straight path is meant: the path of those God favored through obedience and worship, including angels, prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and the righteous.
TAB:1:7/r1.anchor: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم إبانة عن الصراط المستقيم أي الصراط هو

TAB:1:7/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r2.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r2.claim: God promises to bring those who follow this path steadfastly in obedience to Him and His Messenger into the company of the favored.
TAB:1:7/r2.anchor: أن يورده مواردهم ، والله لا يخلف الميعاد

TAB:1:7/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:7/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, transmitted through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, identifies the favored as obedient worshippers among the angels, prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous.
TAB:1:7/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : ( صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ) يقول :

TAB:1:7/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB:1:7/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says the favored are the prophets.
TAB:1:7/r4.anchor: عن ربيع : ( صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ) قال : النبيون

TAB:1:7/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:7/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in a report through Ibn Jurayj, identifies the favored as believers.
TAB:1:7/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ( أنعمت عليهم ) قال : المؤمنين

TAB:1:7/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r6.speaker: وكيع
TAB:1:7/r6.claim: Wakīʿ identifies the favored as Muslims.

TAB:1:7/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
TAB:1:7/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says the favored are the Prophet and those with him.
TAB:1:7/r7.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد في قول الله : ( صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم )

TAB:1:7/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r8.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r8.claim: Obedience and guidance come to the obedient only through God's favor and enabling; the verse attributes their guidance, worship, and obedience to His beneficence.
TAB:1:7/r8.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل واضح على أن طاعة الله جل ثناؤه لا ينالها المطيعون إلا بإنعام الله

TAB:1:7/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r9.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r9.claim: The verse leaves the blessing unstated because the nearby phrase already makes clear that the blessing is guidance to the upright path; Arabic can omit what context supplies.
TAB:1:7/r9.anchor: اجتزاء العرب في منطقها ببعض من بعض إذا كان البعض الظاهر دالا على البعض الباطن وكافيا منه

TAB:1:7/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r10.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r10.claim: Al-Nābigha's line illustrates omission: saying someone is among the camels of Banū Uqays conveys the omitted noun, a camel.
TAB:1:7/r10.anchor: يريد كأنك من جمال بني أقيش جمل يقعقع خلف رجليه بشنّ ، فاكتفى بما ظهر من ذكر الجمال

TAB:1:7/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r11.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r11.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line illustrates omission of “they” after “their collars,” since the possessive phrase already indicates the pronoun.
TAB:1:7/r11.anchor: يريد : متقلديها هم ، فحذف «هم » إذ كان الظاهر من قوله : «أرباقهم » دالاّ عليها

TAB:1:7/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r12.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r12.claim: The reciters unanimously read ghayr with a genitive ending.
TAB:1:7/r12.anchor: والقراء مجمعة على قراءة «غير » بجرّ الراء منها

TAB:1:7/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r13.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r13.claim: On one parsing, ghayr is an adjective of alladhīna: the relative phrase is not a specific proper-name-like definite, so an indefinite adjective can describe it.
TAB:1:7/r13.anchor: أحدهما أن يكون غير صفة للذين ونعتا لهم فتخفضها ، إذ كان «الذين » خفضا

TAB:1:7/r14.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r14.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r14.claim: Alternatively, ghayr is genitive by an understood repetition of ṣirāṭ: “the path of those You favored, the path of those not under wrath.”
TAB:1:7/r14.anchor: غير مخفوضة بنية تكرير الصراط الذي خفض الذين عليها

TAB:1:7/r15.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r15.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r15.claim: The two genitive parses are close in meaning: those favored with true guidance are not under God's wrath or astray; the adjectival parse states this directly.
TAB:1:7/r15.anchor: هذان التأويلان في غير المغضوب عليهم ، وإن اختلفا باختلاف معربيهما ، فإنهما يتقارب معناهما

TAB:1:7/r16.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r16.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r16.claim: Although a grammatical route for reading ghayr in the accusative exists, al-Ṭabarī rejects it as anomalous against the reciters' transmitted consensus.
TAB:1:7/r16.anchor: وقد يجوز نصب «غير » في غير المغضوب عليهم وإن كنت للقراءة بها كارها لشذوذها عن قراءة القراء

TAB:1:7/r17.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r17.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r17.claim: The possible accusative parse treats ghayr as a detached adjective of the pronoun in ʿalayhim, which is syntactically governed by anʿamta.
TAB:1:7/r17.anchor: أن يكون صفة للهاء والميم اللتين في «عليهم » العائدة على «الذين »

TAB:1:7/r18.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r18.speaker: بعض نحويي البصريين
TAB:1:7/r18.claim: A Basran grammarian takes the accusative as an exception: ask for the path of the favored, excluding those not favored in religion, by analogy with al-Nābigha's exception.
TAB:1:7/r18.anchor: كان بعض نحويي البصريين يزعم أن قراءة من نصب «غير » في غير المغضوب عليهم على وجه استثناء

TAB:1:7/r19.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r19.speaker: نحويو الكوفة
TAB:1:7/r19.claim: The Kufans reject the exception analysis: “nor” is a negative conjunction, and Arabic coordinates a negative with a negative, not a negation with an exception.
TAB:1:7/r19.anchor: وأما نحويو الكوفيين فأنكروا هذا التأويل واستخطئوه ، وزعموا أن ذلك لو كان كما قاله الزاعم

TAB:1:7/r20.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r20.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r20.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the unanimously transmitted genitive reading; he accepts either of its two sound grammatical explanations.
TAB:1:7/r20.anchor: والصواب من القول في تأويله وقراءته عندنا القول الأول

TAB:1:7/r21.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r21.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r21.claim: The wrathful are identified with those described in the Qur'an as cursed and punished for disobedience; God also shows the community the way to avoid their fate.
TAB:1:7/r21.anchor: من لعنه الله وغضب عليه وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير وعبد الطاغوت

TAB:1:7/r22.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r22.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r22.claim: In reports from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, the Prophet identifies the wrathful as the Jews.
TAB:1:7/r22.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «المغضوب عليهم : اليهود »

TAB:1:7/r23.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r23.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r23.claim: At the siege of Wādī al-Qurā, the Prophet answers a man's question by identifying the besieged Jews as the wrathful.
TAB:1:7/r23.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شقيق ، أن رجلاً سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فذكر نحوه

TAB:1:7/r24.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r24.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:7/r24.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, identifies the wrathful as Jews whom God has angered.
TAB:1:7/r24.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : ( غير المغضوب عليهم ) يعني اليهود الذين غضب الله عليهم

TAB:1:7/r25.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r25.speaker: أبو مالك، أبو صالح، ابن عباس، مرة الهمداني، ابن مسعود، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB:1:7/r25.claim: A report collected by al-Suddī from several early authorities identifies the wrathful as the Jews.
TAB:1:7/r25.anchor: عن ابن مسعود ، وعن ناس من أصحاب النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( غير المغضوب عليهم ) هم اليهود

TAB:1:7/r26.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r26.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:1:7/r26.claim: Mujāhid identifies the wrathful as the Jews.
TAB:1:7/r26.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قال : ( غير المغضوب عليهم ) قال : هم اليهود

TAB:1:7/r27.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r27.speaker: الربيع
TAB:1:7/r27.claim: Al-Rabīʿ identifies the wrathful as the Jews.
TAB:1:7/r27.anchor: عن ربيع : ( غير المغضوب عليهم ) قال : اليهود

TAB:1:7/r28.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r28.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:7/r28.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in a report through Ibn Jurayj, identifies the wrathful as the Jews.
TAB:1:7/r28.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ( غير المغضوب عليهم ) قال : اليهود

TAB:1:7/r29.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r29.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
TAB:1:7/r29.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd identifies the wrathful as the Jews.

TAB:1:7/r30.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r30.speaker: زيد
TAB:1:7/r30.claim: Zayd, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd's father, identifies the wrathful as the Jews.
TAB:1:7/r30.anchor: عن أبيه ، قال : ( المغضوب عليهم ) اليهود

TAB:1:7/r31.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r31.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:1:7/r31.claim: One view explains God's anger as His imposing punishment on those He is angry with, in this world or the next.
TAB:1:7/r31.anchor: قال بعضهم : غضب الله على من غضب عليه من خلقه إحلالُ عقوبته بمن غضب عليه ، إما في دنياه ، وإما في آخرته

TAB:1:7/r32.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r32.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:1:7/r32.claim: Another view takes divine anger as God's blame of people and their deeds, and verbal condemnation of them.
TAB:1:7/r32.anchor: وقال بعضهم : غضب الله على من غضب عليه من عباده ذمٌّ منه لهم ولأفعالهم ، وشتمٌ منه لهم بالقول

TAB:1:7/r33.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r33.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:1:7/r33.claim: A third view affirms an intelligible divine attribute called anger, while distinguishing it from human agitation and affirming that God's essence is free of affliction.
TAB:1:7/r33.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الغضب منه معنى مفهوم ، كالذي يعرف من معاني الغضب

TAB:1:7/r34.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r34.speaker: بعض أهل البصرة
TAB:1:7/r34.claim: Some Basrans call lā before “the astray” an added particle that completes the expression but contributes no negation, citing poetry and “what prevented you from not prostrating?”
TAB:1:7/r34.anchor: كان بعض أهل البصرة يزعم أن «لا » مع «الضالين » أدخلت تتميما للكلام والمعنى إلغاؤها

TAB:1:7/r35.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r35.speaker: نحويو الكوفة
TAB:1:7/r35.claim: Kufan grammarians reject an unmotivated added lā at the start of a phrase and reject coordinating it with ghayr if ghayr means “other than” or an exception.
TAB:1:7/r35.anchor: وكان بعض نحويي الكوفة يستنكر ذلك من قوله ، ويزعم أن «غير » التي «مع المغضوب عليهم »

TAB:1:7/r36.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r36.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r36.claim: Al-Ṭabarī agrees with the Kufans: lā is a true negation coordinated with the negative sense of ghayr, so the request is for the path of the favored, not the wrathful or astray.
TAB:1:7/r36.anchor: صحّ وثبت أن لا وجه ل«غير » التي مع «المغضوب عليهم » يجوز توجيهها إليه على صحة إلا بمعنى الجحد والنفي

TAB:1:7/r37.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r37.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r37.claim: The astray are linked to the People of the Book whom God describes as exceeding bounds, following prior errant groups, and straying from the balanced path.
TAB:1:7/r37.anchor: يا أهل الكتاب لا تغلوا في دينكم غير الحق ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل

TAB:1:7/r38.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r38.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r38.claim: In reports from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, the Prophet identifies the astray as the Christians.
TAB:1:7/r38.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ولا الضالين قال : «النصارى »

TAB:1:7/r39.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r39.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r39.claim: In the Wādī al-Qurā report, the Prophet answers that the people asked about are the astray, meaning the Christians.
TAB:1:7/r39.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو محاصر وادي القرى قال : قلت : من هؤلاء ؟ قال : «هؤلاء الضالون : النصارى »

TAB:1:7/r40.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r40.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:1:7/r40.claim: Mujāhid identifies the astray as the Christians.
TAB:1:7/r40.anchor: عن مجاهد : ولا الضالين قال : النصارى

TAB:1:7/r41.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r41.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:7/r41.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, glosses the phrase as the Christians' way, whom God led astray through their false claim about Him.
TAB:1:7/r41.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس : ولا الضالين قال : وغير طريق النصارى الذين أضلهم الله بفريتهم عليه

TAB:1:7/r42.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r42.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:7/r42.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās's explanation, the prayer asks God to inspire true monotheistic religion, spare the worshippers His anger like the Jews, and keep them from Christian error and punishment.
TAB:1:7/r42.anchor: يقول : فألهمنا دينك الحقّ ، وهو لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له ، حتى لا تغضبَ علينا

TAB:1:7/r43.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r43.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:1:7/r43.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in a report through Ibn Jurayj, identifies the astray as the Christians.

TAB:1:7/r44.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r44.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود، وناس من أصحاب النبي
TAB:1:7/r44.claim: The report transmitted by al-Suddī from early authorities identifies the astray as the Christians.
TAB:1:7/r44.anchor: عن مرة الهمداني ، عن ابن مسعود ، وعن ناس من أصحاب النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم : ولا الضالين : هم النصارى

TAB:1:7/r45.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r45.speaker: الربيع
TAB:1:7/r45.claim: Al-Rabīʿ identifies the astray as the Christians.

TAB:1:7/r46.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r46.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
TAB:1:7/r46.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd identifies the astray as the Christians.
TAB:1:7/r46.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد : ولا الضالين النصارى

TAB:1:7/r47.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r47.speaker: زيد
TAB:1:7/r47.claim: Zayd, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd's father, identifies the astray as the Christians.
TAB:1:7/r47.anchor: عن أبيه . قال : ولا الضالين النصارى

TAB:1:7/r48.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r48.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r48.claim: In Arabic, anyone who departs from the intended route and follows an unsound way is astray; Christians receive this label for missing the truth and taking a wrong religious path.
TAB:1:7/r48.anchor: وكل حائد عن قصد السبيل وسالك غير المنهج القويم فضال عند العرب لإضلاله وجه الطريق

TAB:1:7/r49.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r49.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r49.claim: Jews and Christians are both astray and under wrath; God labels each group by a real, recognizable trait, without implying that it lacks the other's blameworthy traits.
TAB:1:7/r49.anchor: إن كلا الفريقين ضُلاّل مغضوب عليهم ، غير أن الله جل ثناؤه وَسَم كل فريق منهم

TAB:1:7/r50.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r50.speaker: بعض أهل الغباء من القدرية
TAB:1:7/r50.claim: Some ignorant Qadarites infer from calling Christians astray, without calling them those who mislead, that God has no causal role in their acts of misguidance.
TAB:1:7/r50.anchor: وقد ظن بعض أهل الغباء من القدرية أن في وصف الله جل ثناؤه النصارى بالضلال

TAB:1:7/r51.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r51.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r51.claim: Arabic can attribute an act to its immediate agent or to its cause; the Qur'an says ships “ran” although another causes their motion, so attributing error to Christians does not exclude divine causation.
TAB:1:7/r51.anchor: وفي قول الله جل ثناؤه : ( حتى إذا كنتم في الفلك وجرين بهم ) بإضافته الجري إلى الفلك

TAB:1:7/r52.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r52.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r52.claim: The Qur'an explicitly says God guides and misguides, including that He misled the one who made desire his god; this refutes the Qadarite inference.
TAB:1:7/r52.anchor: نصّا في آي كثيرة من تنزيله أنه المضلّ الهادي فمن ذلك قوله جل ثناؤه : ( أفرأيت من اتخذ إلهه هواه وأضله الله على علم

TAB:1:7/r53.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r53.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r53.claim: Human beings acquire their acts through their own power and choice, while God creates the acts' actual existence and brings them into being.
TAB:1:7/r53.anchor: فكيف بالفعل الذي يكتسبه العبد كسبا ويوجده الله جل ثناؤه عينا منشأة

TAB:1:7/r54.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r54.speaker: أهل الإلحاد الطاعنون في القرآن
TAB:1:7/r54.claim: Critics ask why al-Fātiḥa has seven verses when, they argue, the meaning of its remaining verses is already contained in “Master of Judgment Day” and “You alone we worship and ask for help.”
TAB:1:7/r54.anchor: فما الوجه إذ كان الأمر على ما وصفت في إطالة الكلام بمثل سورة أم القرآن بسبع آيات

TAB:1:7/r55.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r55.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r55.claim: Earlier scriptures each contain some meanings found together in the Qur'an: the Torah gives admonitions and detail, the Psalms praise and glorify, and the Gospel admonishes and reminds; the Qur'an gathers these and adds more.
TAB:1:7/r55.anchor: كالتوراة التي هي مواعظ وتفصيل ، والزّبور الذي هو تحميد وتمجيد ، والإنجيل الذي هو مواعظ وتذكير

TAB:1:7/r56.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r56.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r56.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the prior books lack a miracle certifying their recipients, whereas the Qur'an's unmatched composition defeats all attempts to produce even a short surah and proves Muhammad's prophethood.
TAB:1:7/r56.anchor: نظمه العجيب ، ورصفه الغريب ، وتأليفه البديع ، الذي عجزت عن نظم مثل أصغر سورة منه الخطباء

TAB:1:7/r57.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r57.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r57.claim: The Qur'an's varied contents—encouragement, warning, commands, prohibitions, stories, argument, and parables—also make its extended expression purposeful.

TAB:1:7/r58.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r58.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r58.claim: Al-Fātiḥa's inimitable arrangement proves prophethood, while its praise and glorification direct people to recognize God's greatness, sovereignty, power, and dominion and to thank Him for His favors.
TAB:1:7/r58.anchor: ليذكروه بآلائه ويحمدوه على نعمائه ، فيستحقوا به منه المزيد ويستوجبوا عليه الثواب الجزيل

TAB:1:7/r59.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r59.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r59.claim: The account of those favored through knowledge of God and His enabling teaches that every religious and worldly blessing comes from Him, directing requests to God rather than idols or rivals.
TAB:1:7/r59.anchor: تعريف عباده أن كل ما بهم من نعمة في دينهم ودنياهم فمنه ، ليصرفوا رغبتهم إليه

TAB:1:7/r60.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r60.speaker: author
TAB:1:7/r60.claim: Recounting punishments for disobedience warns people away from sin and from incurring God's anger, whose consequences lead to destruction.
TAB:1:7/r60.anchor: ترهيب عباده عن ركوب معاصيه ، والتعرض لما لا قبل لهم به من سخطه

TAB:1:7/r61.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r61.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r61.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the Prophet said God answers the worshipper's recitation: He calls al-ḥamdu praise, al-Raḥmān al-Raḥīm commendation, Mālik Yawm al-Dīn glorification, and the rest of the surah the servant's share.
TAB:1:7/r61.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله رب العالمين ، قال الله : حمدني عبدي

TAB:1:7/r62.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r62.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:1:7/r62.claim: A second Abū Hurayra version gives the same recitation exchange but is not attributed to the Prophet.
TAB:1:7/r62.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ، قال : إذا قال العبد : الحمد لله ، فذكر نحوه ، ولم يرفعه

TAB:1:7/r63.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:1:7/r63.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:1:7/r63.claim: Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports the divine saying that the prayer is divided between God and His servant, with the servant receiving what he asks; the first three praises are God's, and what follows is for the servant.
TAB:1:7/r63.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : «قال الله عز وجل : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين وله ما سأل

TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.speaker: بعض النصارى
TABATABAI:2:21-25#11/r2.claim: He also quotes a Christian's parody of al-Fatiha as another failed counter-imitation.

ELMALILI:v1p85/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p85/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p85/r6.claim: He asks God to make the community love those God loves, loathe those God loathes, and be joined to those who have attained.
ELMALILI:v1p85/r6.anchor: Sevdir bize hep sevdiklerini, yerdir bize hep yerdiklerini, yâr et bize erdirdiklerini

ELMALILI:v1p85/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p85/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p85/r7.claim: He praises Muhammad as beloved by God and made beloved to creation, clothed with prophethood, raised from Maqām Ibrāhīm to Maqām Maḥmūd, leader of the pure, and seal of the prophets.
ELMALILI:v1p85/r7.anchor: Sevdin, Habîbini kâinata sevdirdin; sevdin de hil‘at-i risâleti giydirdin. Makām-ı İbrahim’den Makām-ı Mahmûd’a erdirdin

ELMALILI:v1p85/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:v1p85/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:v1p85/r8.claim: Elmalılı asks for blessings and peace for the Prophet and for his family, companions, and followers.
ELMALILI:v1p85/r8.anchor: Salât ü selâm, tahiyyât ü ikrâm, her türlü ihtirâm ona

BURHAN:v1p16/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p16/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p16/r4.claim: Al-Fātiḥa is the Mother of the Book because it contains all three fields: monotheism through 1:4, rulings in 1:5, and reminder from 1:6 onward.
BURHAN:v1p16/r4.anchor: ولهذا المعنى صارت فاتحة الكتاب أم الكتاب لأن فيها الأقسام الثلاثة

BURHAN:v1p359/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r1.claim: The author says the familiar labels for stop quality are not a complete, sound classification and have produced confusion in books on pauses.
BURHAN:v1p359/r1.anchor: فالوجه أن يقال الوقف ضربان اضطرارى واختيارى

BURHAN:v1p359/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r2.claim: A forced pause is caused only by running out of breath and is not restricted to particular places; examples include Ḥamza pausing within words or before a genitive complement.
BURHAN:v1p359/r2.anchor: فالاضطرارى ما يدعو إليه انقطاع النفس فقط وذلك لا يخص موضعا دون موضع

BURHAN:v1p359/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r3.claim: An optional pause is preferable and is classified by how the two parts of the statement depend on each other.
BURHAN:v1p359/r3.anchor: والاختيارى وهو أفضلهما هو الذى لا يكون باعتبار انفصال ما بين جزأى القول

BURHAN:v1p359/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r5.claim: An incomplete pause leaves the preceding part sufficient but the following part dependent; one may stop at “straight,” but cannot begin with “the path of those.”
BURHAN:v1p359/r5.anchor: الثانى الناقص وهو أن يكون ما قبله مستغنيا عما بعده ولا يكون ما بعده مستغنيا عما قبله

BURHAN:v1p359/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p359/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p359/r6.claim: The author raises the possible objection that an omitted verb could be supplied to govern “the path,” leaving the answer beyond this excerpt.
BURHAN:v1p359/r6.anchor: فإن قيل ولم لا يجوز أن يقدر هاهنا الفعل الذى ينتصب به

BURHAN:v3p322/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p322/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p322/r3.claim: The sūrah then shifts from direct address in “You bestowed favor” back to third-person wording, saying “not those who incurred anger” rather than “those with whom You were angry.”
BURHAN:v3p322/r3.anchor: ثم التفت إلى الغيبة بقوله ﴿ غير المغضوب عليهم ﴾ 2 ولم يقل الذين غضبت

BURHAN:v3p325/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p325/r1.speaker: التنوخي والخفاجي وابن الأثير
BURHAN:v3p325/r1.claim: Al-Tanūkhī, al-Khafājī, Ibn al-Athīr, and others classify the passive “those who incurred anger” after direct address as a shift of style.
BURHAN:v3p325/r1.anchor: ذكره التنوخي في الأقصى القريب والخفاجي وابن الأثير وغيرهم

BURHAN:v3p325/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p325/r2.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v3p325/r2.claim: Al-Sakkākī’s account places all six kinds in the final category of iltifāt, the shift by implication.
BURHAN:v3p325/r2.anchor: واعلم أنه على رأى السكاكي تجيء الأقسام الستة في القسم الاخير وهو الانتقال التقديري

BURHAN:v1p352/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p352/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p352/r5.claim: One classification calls a stop sufficient when the next verse has verbal attachment, good and sufficient when attachment is semantic, complete when neither holds, and bad when the sense conflicts; 1:6 continues verbally into 1:7.
BURHAN:v1p352/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن تعلقت الآية بما قبلها تعلقا لفظيا كان الوقف كافيا

BURHAN:v2p195/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p195/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p195/r1.claim: The blessed people are clarified by 4:69 as prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous; this broader verse is the best explanation of the Fatiha phrase.

BURHAN:v2p195/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p195/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p195/r3.claim: Wanting steadfastness on the straight path is itself obedience to God and His Messenger, since guidance to that path entails the obedience that places one with the blessed.
BURHAN:v2p195/r3.anchor: والرغبة إلى الله تعالى فى الثبات عليها هي نفس الطاعة لله ولرسوله

BURHAN:v2p195/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p195/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p195/r4.claim: A phrase may be assigned to a more fitting referent than its apparent one; examples include naming the Fatiha the seven oft-repeated verses though all Qur'an is described as repeated.
BURHAN:v2p195/r4.anchor: وقد يكون اللفظ مقتضيا لأمر ويحمل على غيره لأنه أولى بذلك الاسم منه

BURHAN:v2p455/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p455/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p455/r2.claim: A substitute can make praise more forceful by stating a general description first and then naming its specific instance.
BURHAN:v2p455/r2.anchor: ومن فوائد البدل التبيين على وجه المدح فقولك هل أدلك على أكرم الناس وأفضلهم فلان أبلغ

BURHAN:v2p455/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p455/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p455/r4.claim: Part and inclusion substitutes clarify and specify an antecedent by naming it twice, first generally and then particularly; the forelock example adds its quality as the reason for seizing it.
BURHAN:v2p455/r4.anchor: وفائدة البدل أن ذلك الشيء يصير مذكورا مرتين إحداهما بالعموم والثانية بالخصوص

BURHAN:v2p455/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p455/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p455/r5.claim: A definite noun may be replaced by another definite noun, as in the Fatiha's repeated mention of the straight path.
BURHAN:v2p455/r5.anchor: ويجوز بدل المعرفة من المعرفة نحو ﴿ الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين ﴾

BURHAN:v1p73/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p73/r1.claim: Qur'anic verse endings use either identical letters or letters close in sound; examples include the matched moon and two nearly matched Fatiha endings.
BURHAN:v1p73/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر ﴾ وجميع هذه السورة على الازدواج

BURHAN:v1p73/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p73/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p73/r2.claim: Because sajʿ strictly requires matching letters, the close-but-not-identical endings in these examples do not count as sajʿ even for those who apply that term to Qur'an.
