BURHAN:v1p73/r2.anchor: وهذا لا يسمى سجعا قطعا عند القائلين بإطلاق السجع فى القرآن لأن السجع ما تماثلت حروفه

BURHAN:v1p73/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p73/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi counts the basmala and makes the rest of 1:7 one verse; Abu Hanifa omits the basmala and divides its two phrases. Both count seven verses, but al-Shafiʿi's division better preserves the endings because anʿamta ʿalayhim does not match prior endings.
BURHAN:v1p73/r3.anchor: وبهذا يترجح مذهب الشافعى على مذهب أبى حنيفة فى عد الفاتحة سبع آيات مع البسملة

BURHAN:v1p155/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p155/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p155/r1.claim: The science of ambiguous identities has dedicated books by al-Suhayli and his student Ibn ʿAsakir, and was also studied among the early generations.
BURHAN:v1p155/r1.anchor: وقد صنف فيه أبو القاسم السهيلى كتابه المسمى بالتعريف والإعلام وتلاه تلميذه ابن عساكر

BURHAN:v1p155/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p155/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p155/r4.claim: The people blessed in the Fatiha are identified elsewhere as prophets, truthful people, martyrs, and righteous people.

BURHAN:v1p182/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p182/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p182/r1.claim: Sura endings, like openings, conclude with apt meanings and signal that the discourse has ended, releasing the listener's anticipation of what comes next.
BURHAN:v1p182/r1.anchor: وهى مثل الفواتح فى الحسن لأنها آخر ما يقرع الأسماع فلهذا جاءت متضمنة للمعانى البديعة

BURHAN:v1p182/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p182/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p182/r2.claim: The Fatiha closing spells out the highest request: faith and its blessings, preserved from sins that bring God's anger and from deviation beyond His limits.
BURHAN:v1p182/r2.anchor: ولذلك أطلق الإنعام ولم يقيده ليتناول كل إنعام لأن من أنعم عليه بنعمة الإيمان فقد أنعم عليه بكل نعمة

BURHAN:v3p326/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p326/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v3p326/r2.claim: One explanation says praise uses third person because it ranks below worship, while direct address elevates the worshipper's encounter; similarly, blessing is explicitly attributed to God but anger is phrased obliquely as a matter of etiquette.
BURHAN:v3p326/r2.anchor: وقيل إنما اختير للحمد لفظ الغيبة وللعبادة الخطاب للإشارة إلى أن الحمد دون العبادة في الرتبة

BURHAN:v3p354/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.claim: The four broken plural forms of paucity and the two sound plurals are inherently paucity forms; other plurals may indicate few or many as context determines, as Qur'anic examples show.
BURHAN:v3p354/r4.anchor: واعلم أن جموع التكثير الأربعة وجمعى التصحيح أعنى جمع التأنيث وجمع التذكير كل ذلك للقلة

BURHAN:v3p239#4/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r7.claim: Putting those under wrath before those astray may convey disparagement: Jews preceded Christians historically and were nearer to the Muslims.
BURHAN:v3p239#4/r7.anchor: تقدم اليهود لأنهم كانوا أسبق من النصارى ولأنهم كانوا أقرب إلى المؤمنين بالمجاورة

BURHAN:v4p355/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p355/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p355/r2.claim: لا can also be a coordinating particle, sharing the preceding word’s case while denying the second member what is affirmed of the first.
BURHAN:v4p355/r2.anchor: الخامسة إن تكون عاطفة تشرك ما بعدها في إعراب ما قبلها

BURHAN:v4p355/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p355/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p355/r3.claim: After a conjunction preceded by negation or prohibition, extra لا reinforces the negation; he classifies لا in this verse that way.
BURHAN:v4p355/r3.anchor: الأول بعد حرف العطف المتقدم عليه النفي أو النهي فتجىء مؤكدة له

BURHAN:v4p355/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p355/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BURHAN:v4p355/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda explains the added لا as preventing the mistaken reading that those astray are the same people as those under wrath.
BURHAN:v4p355/r4.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة وقيل إنما دخلت هنا مزيلة لتوهم أن الضالين هم المغضوب عليهم

BURHAN:v4p355/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p355/r5.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v4p355/r5.claim: Another explanation is that لا prevents readers from treating الضالين as coordinated directly with الذين.
BURHAN:v4p355/r5.anchor: وقيل لئلا يتوهم عطف الضالين على الذين

BURHAN:v1p260#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r2.speaker: بعض الأئمة
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r2.claim: Some imams say al-Fatiha affirms lordship, seeks guidance in Islam, and asks protection from Judaism and Christianity.
BURHAN:v1p260#2/r2.anchor: قال بعض الأئمة وسورة الفاتحة تضمنت الإقرار بالربوبية والالتجاء إليه فى دين الإسلام

ITQAN:v3p232/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p232/r1.claim: The verse explicitly attributes favor to God, but avoids saying “those with whom You were angry,” shifting expression so anger is not verbally attributed to God in direct address.
ITQAN:v3p232/r1.anchor: مصرحا بذكر المنعم وإسناد الإنعام إليه لفظا

ITQAN:v4p420/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Fatiha encompasses praise, worship through commands and prohibitions, and promise and warning; every Qur’anic verse falls under one of these topics.
ITQAN:v4p420/r1.anchor: وبيان اشتمالها على علوم القرآن قرره الزمخشري باشتمالها على الثناء على الله تعالى بما هو أهله وعلى التعبد بالأمر والنهي وعلى الوعد والوعيد

ITQAN:v4p420/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r2.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
ITQAN:v4p420/r2.claim: Fakhr al-Din maps the Qur’an’s four aims—God, resurrection, prophethood, and divine decree—onto the Fatiha: praise, Judgment Day, worship and reliance, and guidance through the surah’s end; this supports its name Umm al-Qur’an.
ITQAN:v4p420/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام فخر الدين المقصود من القرآن كله تقرير أمور أربعة الإلهيات والمعاد والنبوات وإثبات القضاء والقدر لله تعالى

ITQAN:v4p420/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.speaker: البيضاوي
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.claim: Al-Baydawi says the Fatiha contains theoretical wisdom, practical rulings in walking the straight path, and knowledge of the ranks of the blessed and abodes of the wretched.
ITQAN:v4p420/r3.anchor: وقال البيضاوي هي مشتملة على الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية التي هي سلوك الطريق المستقيم والاطلاع على مراتب السعداء ومنازل الأشقياء

ITQAN:v4p420/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p420/r4.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v4p420/r4.claim: Al-Tibi divides the Fatiha’s religious knowledge into foundations (God and attributes, prophethood, resurrection), branches (worship), ethical perfection and seeking the path, and accounts of earlier peoples with promise and threat.
ITQAN:v4p420/r4.anchor: وقال الطيبي هي مشتملة على أربعة أنواع من العلوم التي هي مناط الدين

ITQAN:v4p421/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r1.speaker: الغزالي
ITQAN:v4p421/r1.claim: Al-Ghazali lists three essential Qur’anic aims—knowing God, the straight path, and the return in the Hereafter—and three supplementary aims: the obedient, deniers’ speech, and the stations of the path, all signaled by the Fatiha.
ITQAN:v4p421/r1.anchor: وقال الغزالي مقاصد القرآن سنة ثلاثة مهمة وثلاثة متمة الأولى تعريف المدعو إليه كما أشير إليه بصدرها

ITQAN:v4p421/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.speaker: الزركشي وناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.claim: They reconcile the hadith calling the Fatiha two-thirds of the Qur’an by saying it indicates all Qur’anic aims through inclusion and implication, but not direct correspondence; those are two of three modes of indication.
ITQAN:v4p421/r2.anchor: ذكره الزركشي في شرح التنبيه وناصر الدين بن الميلق قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده

ITQAN:v4p421/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.claim: A second explanation counts three kinds of rights—God’s claim on servants, servants’ claim on God, and people’s claims on one another—and says the Fatiha explicitly covers the first two, hence two-thirds.
ITQAN:v4p421/r3.anchor: قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده وحق العباد على الله وحق بعض العباد على بعض وقد اشتملت الفاتحة صريحا على الحقين الأولين فناسب كونها بصريحها ثلثين

ITQAN:v4p421/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.claim: There is no conflict between hadiths calling the Fatiha the greatest surah and al-Baqara the greatest: al-Baqara is greatest among surahs other than the Fatiha because of its detailed laws, parables, and arguments.
ITQAN:v4p421/r5.anchor: قلت ولا تنافي أيضا بين كون الفاتحة أعظم السور وبين الحديث الآخر أن البقرة أعظم السور

ITQAN:v4p421/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.claim: Ibn al-Arabi quotes a teacher saying the Fatiha contains a thousand commands, prohibitions, rulings, and reports; Ibn Umar spent eight years teaching it because of its jurisprudential depth.
ITQAN:v4p421/r6.anchor: قال ابن العربي في أحكامه سمعت بعض أشياخي يقول فيها ألف أمر وألف نهي وألف حكم وألف خبر

ITQAN:v4p490/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p490/r6.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
ITQAN:v4p490/r6.claim: The closing request requires explaining guidance and the straight path and its opposites, the angered and astray and their qualities, and the approved people and their way.
ITQAN:v4p490/r6.anchor: يحتاج إلى بيان الهداية ما هي والصراط المستقيم وأضداده وتبيين المغضوب عليهم والضالين وصفاتهم

ITQAN:v3p284/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.claim: The Fatiha points to all major Qur’anic disciplines: knowledge of God and attributes, prophecy, resurrection, worship, ethical conduct and the straight path, and stories teaching the outcomes of obedience and disobedience.
ITQAN:v3p284/r1.anchor: وقد وجه ذلك بأن العلوم التي احتوى عليها القرآن قامت بها الأديان أربعة علم الأصول ومداره على معرفة الله وصفاته

ITQAN:v3p284/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.claim: By signaling all Qur’anic aims, the Fatiha achieves an exemplary opening and combines beautiful words, pleasing cadence, and rhetorical forms.
ITQAN:v3p284/r2.anchor: فنبه في الفاتحة على جميع مقاصد القرآن وهذا هو الغاية في براعة الاستهلال مع ما اشتملت عليه من الألفاظ الحسنة والمقاطع المستحسنة وأنواع البلاغة

ITQAN:v3p297/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r4.speaker: بعض الأئمة
ITQAN:v3p297/r4.claim: Al-Fatiha affirms lordship, seeks guidance in Islam, and protection from Judaism and Christianity; al-Baqara lays out religion's foundations, while Al Imran answers opponents' doubts, especially Christian reliance on ambiguous verses.
ITQAN:v3p297/r4.anchor: وسورة الفاتحة تضمنت الإقرار بالربوبية والالتجاء إليه في دين الإسلام والصيانة عن دين اليهودية والنصرانية

ITQAN:v3p297/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r5.speaker: بعض الأئمة
ITQAN:v3p297/r5.claim: Al Imran makes pilgrimage obligatory, whereas al-Baqara establishes it and commands completion after beginning; Al Imran addresses Christians more and al-Baqara Jews more, reflecting the Torah's priority to the Gospel.
ITQAN:v3p297/r5.anchor: وأوجب الحج في آل عمران وأما في البقرة فذكر أنه مشروع وأمر بإتمامه بعد الشروع فيه

ITQAN:v3p297/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p297/r6.speaker: بعض الأئمة
ITQAN:v3p297/r6.claim: The Prophet called and fought the Jews after migrating to Medina, while his confrontation with Christians came late; Meccan suras address all people with shared prophetic religion, and Medinan suras address believers and scripturalists.
ITQAN:v3p297/r6.anchor: والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما هاجر إلى المدينة دعا اليهود وجاهدهم وكان جهاده للنصارى في آخر الأمر

ITQAN:v1p227/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p227/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p227/r2.claim: A stop before the phrase is complete is a bad, unintended stop because it gives no benefit or corrupts the sense; “path of those” is an example, and stopping at verse endings is generally permitted.
ITQAN:v1p227/r2.anchor: وإن لم يتم الكلام كان الوقف عليه اضطراريا وهو المسمى بالقبيح لا يجوز تعمد الوقف عليه إلا لضرورة من انقطاع نفس ونحوه

ITQAN:v1p227/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p227/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p227/r5.claim: Starting is always elective and must begin at a self-contained, adequate meaning; it has the same four quality grades as stopping, with examples showing that a bad stop can force an even worse restart.
ITQAN:v1p227/r5.anchor: وأما الابتداء فلا يكون إلا اختياريا لأنه ليس كالوقف تدعو إليه ضرورة فلا يجوز إلا بمستقل بالمعنى موف بالمقصود

ITQAN:v3p51/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p51/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p51/r1.claim: The description “the path of those You favored” is clarified by the verse naming prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous as those God favored.
ITQAN:v3p51/r1.anchor: وقوله ﴿ صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ﴾ بينه قوله ﴿ أولئك الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين ﴾ الآية

ITQAN:v3p51/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p51/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p51/r2.claim: The Sunna explains commands left general in the Qur'an, including how to perform prayer and pilgrimage and the taxable thresholds for kinds of zakat.
ITQAN:v3p51/r2.anchor: وقد بينت السنة أفعال الصلاة والحج ومقادير نصب الزكوات في أنواعها

ITQAN:v3p281/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p281/r1.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين وغيره
ITQAN:v3p281/r1.claim: Qur'anic verse endings fall into only two kinds, identical or near-sounding; their similarity supports counting al-Fatiha as seven verses with the basmala and treating the final phrase as one verse.
ITQAN:v3p281/r1.anchor: قال الإمام فخر الدين وغيره وفواصل القرآن لا تخرج عن هذين القسمين بل تنحصر في المتماثلة والمتقاربة

ITQAN:v3p281/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p281/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p281/r2.claim: The author favors the Shafi'i count: ending verse six at “those You favored” is rejected because that ending resembles none of the sura's other endings, whose sound-pattern similarity must be maintained.
ITQAN:v3p281/r2.anchor: وجعل ﴿ صراط الذين ﴾ إلى آخرها آية فإن من جعل آخر الآية السادسة ﴿ أنعمت عليهم ﴾ مردود بأنه لا يشابه فواصل سائر آيات السورة لا بالمماثلة ولا بالمقاربة

ITQAN:v3p281/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p281/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p281/r3.claim: Rhyme endings can contain enjambment, where the next phrase depends on the ending, and repeated rhyme words; these are flaws in verse poetry but not prose, as Qur'anic examples show.
ITQAN:v3p281/r3.anchor: كثر في الفواصل التضمين والإيطاء لأنهما ليسا بعيبين في النثر وإن كانا عيبين في النظم

ITQAN:v4p382#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r1.claim: An ambiguous expression may be left unexplained when another passage clarifies it: the favored people here are specified elsewhere as prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous.
ITQAN:v4p382#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما الإستغناء ببيانه مع موضع آخر كقوله ﴿ صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ﴾ فإنه مبين في قوله ﴿ مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين ﴾

ITQAN:v3p286/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p286/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p286/r1.claim: Sura endings match the beauty of openings, signal that speech is ending, and leave the listener anticipating what follows; they may conclude with varied rhetorical forms.
ITQAN:v3p286/r1.anchor: هى أيضا مثل الفواتح فى الحسن لأنها آخر ما يقرع الأسماع فلهذا جاءت متضمنة للمعاني البديعة مع إيذان السامع بانتهاء الكلام

ITQAN:v3p286/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p286/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p286/r2.claim: Al-Fatiha's final prayer details the highest request: faith protected from sin and its resulting wrath and error; “those You favored” means believers, and the favor is unrestricted because faith entails every blessing.
ITQAN:v3p286/r2.anchor: والمراد المؤمنون ولذلك أطلق الإنعام ولم يقيده ليتناول كل إنعام

ITQAN:v3p286/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p286/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p286/r3.claim: The favored believers combine the comprehensive blessing of faith with safety from God's anger and from error caused by disobedience and transgressing His limits.
ITQAN:v3p286/r3.anchor: يعني أنهم جمعوا بين النعم المطلقة وهي نعمة الإيمان وبين السلامة من غضب الله تعالى والضلال المسببين عن معاصيه

ITQAN:v2p483/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p483/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p483/r1.claim: غير is an annexed, indefinite noun; it becomes definite only between two opposites, which permits it to modify the definite phrase “those who incurred anger,” though it usually modifies an indefinite.
ITQAN:v2p483/r1.anchor: اسم ملازم للإضافة والإبهام فلا تتعرف ما لم تقع بين ضدين

ITQAN:v2p483/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p483/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p483/r2.claim: غير can function as a circumstantial accusative where “not” fits, or as an exception where “except” fits; as an exception it takes the case of the following noun in the corresponding construction.
ITQAN:v2p483/r2.anchor: وتقع حالا إن صلح موضعها لا واستثناء إن صلح موضعها إلا فتعرب بإعراب الاسم التالي إلا في ذلك الكلام

ITQAN:v2p483/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p483/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p483/r3.claim: In 4:95, غير is read nominative as an adjective to “those who sit,” or as an exception/substitute; accusative as an exception; and, outside the seven readings, genitive as an adjective to “believers.”
ITQAN:v2p483/r3.anchor: وقرئ قوله تعالى ﴿ لا يستوي القاعدون من المؤمنين غير أولي الضرر ﴾ بالرفع على أنها صفة القاعدون

ITQAN:v2p483/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p483/r4.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p483/r4.claim: Raghib lists غير as a pure negation without an added positive sense, as in “a man not standing.”
ITQAN:v2p483/r4.anchor: وفي المفردات للراغب غير تقال على أوجه الأول أن تكون للنفي المجرد من غير إثبات معنى به

ITQAN:v2p483/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p483/r5.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p483/r5.claim: Raghib says غير can mean “except,” allowing it to mark an exception or describe an indefinite noun.
ITQAN:v2p483/r5.anchor: الثاني بمعنى إلا فيستثنى بها وتوصف به النكرة

ITQAN:v2p483/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p483/r6.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p483/r6.claim: Raghib says غير can deny sameness of form while the underlying material is the same, as with water that is hot versus cold.
ITQAN:v2p483/r6.anchor: الثالث لنفي الصورة من غير مادتها نحو الماء إذا كان حارا غيره إذا كان باردا

ITQAN:v2p483/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p483/r7.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p483/r7.claim: Raghib's fourth use refers to a different entity or substance.
ITQAN:v2p483/r7.anchor: الرابع أن يكون ذلك متناولا لذات

ITQAN:v2p502/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p502/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p502/r1.claim: لا can be a noun meaning غير, in which case the inflection appears on the word following it, as in “nor those who go astray.”
ITQAN:v2p502/r1.anchor: ترد لا اسما بمعنى غير فيظهر إعرابها فيما بعدها

ITQAN:v3p232#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r1.claim: For a shift of address to count as الالتفات, the changed pronoun must refer to the same entity and the shift must occur across two sentences.
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r1.anchor: شرط الالتفات أن يكون الضمير في المنتقل إليه عائدا في نفس الأمر إلى المنتقل عنه

ITQAN:v3p232#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r2.speaker: التنوخي وابن الأثير
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r2.claim: They describe a rare shift from active second-person address to passive voice: “those angered” follows “You favored,” meaning those whom You angered; the author of ʿArus al-afrah hesitates over this classification.
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r2.anchor: الثالث ذكر التنوخي في ( الأقصى القريب ) وابن الأثير وغيرهما نوعا غريبا من الالتفات وهو بناء الفعل للمفعول بعد خطاب فاعله أو تكلمه

ITQAN:v3p232#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r6.claim: Moving from a singular, dual, or plural form of address to another is related to الالتفات and has six divisions.
ITQAN:v3p232#2/r6.anchor: نقل الكلام من خطاب الواحد أو الاثنين أو الجمع لخطاب الآخر ذكره التنوخي وابن الأثير وهو ستة أقسام

ITQAN:v4p500/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p500/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p500/r1.claim: The early Successor exegetes mostly received their interpretations from Companions.
ITQAN:v4p500/r1.anchor: فهؤلاء قدماء المفسرين وغالب أقوالهم تلقوها عن الصحابة

ITQAN:v4p500/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p500/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p500/r2.claim: Later collections gathered reports from Companions and Successors; al-Tabari's major commentary surpasses them by weighing views and including grammar and inference.
ITQAN:v4p500/r2.anchor: وبعدهم ابن جرير الطبري وكتابه أجل التفاسير وأعظمها

ITQAN:v4p500/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p500/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p500/r3.claim: Subsequent exegetes shortened chains and copied statements piecemeal, allowing fabricated material in and making sound reports hard to distinguish from weak ones.
ITQAN:v4p500/r3.anchor: ثم ألف في التفسير خلائق فاختصروا الأسانيد ونقلوا الأقوال بترا فدخل من هنا الدخيل

ITQAN:v4p500/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p500/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p500/r4.claim: Despite many later interpretations, the Prophet, Companions, Successors, and their followers identify those who incurred anger as Jews and those astray as Christians; Ibn Abi Hatim knew of no exegetical disagreement.
ITQAN:v4p500/r4.anchor: وتفسيرها باليهود والنصارى هو الوارد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجميع الصحابة والتابعين وأتباعهم حتى قال ابن أبي حاتم لا أعلم في ذلك اختلافا

ITQAN:v4p500/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p500/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p500/r5.claim: Later commentaries often follow one author's specialty: grammarians multiply syntactic possibilities, storytellers collect reliable and unreliable narratives, and jurists expand into legal disputes unrelated to the verse.
ITQAN:v4p500/r5.anchor: ثم صنف بعد ذلك قوم برعوا في علوم فكان كل منهم يقتصر في تفسيره على الفن الذي يغلب عليه

ITQAN:v1p76/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p76/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ITQAN:v1p76/r3.claim: Al-Kashshaf attributes to Ibn Abbas and Mujahid the view that the first sura revealed was “Read”; it reports that most exegetes instead named al-Fatiha.
ITQAN:v1p76/r3.anchor: قال في الكشاف ذهب ابن عباس ومجاهد إلى أن أول سورة نزلت ﴿ اقرأ ﴾ وأكثر المفسرين إلى أن أول سورة نزلت فاتحة الكتاب

ITQAN:v1p76/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p76/r4.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p76/r4.claim: Ibn Hajar rejects the claim that most authorities held al-Fatiha was first, saying the great majority held “Read” and only a tiny minority supported al-Fatiha.
ITQAN:v1p76/r4.anchor: قال ابن حجر والذي ذهب إليه أكثر الأئمة هو الأول وأما الذي نسبه إلى الأكثر فلم يقل به إلا عدد أقل

ITQAN:v1p76/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p76/r5.speaker: أبو ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل
ITQAN:v1p76/r5.claim: A mursal report with trustworthy narrators recounts Muhammad telling Khadija he feared the voice he heard; Waraqa advised him to listen, then taught him the opening of al-Fatiha from the basmala through “those astray.”

ITQAN:v1p76/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p76/r6.speaker: البيهقي
ITQAN:v1p76/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says, if the report is preserved, it may describe al-Fatiha being revealed after “Read” and al-Muddaththir.
ITQAN:v1p76/r6.anchor: وقال البيهقي إن كان محفوظا يحتمل أن يكون خبرا عن نزولها بعدما نزلت عليه

ITQAN:v1p284/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p284/r2.speaker: وائل بن حجر
ITQAN:v1p284/r2.claim: Wail ibn Hujr reports that the Prophet recited “Amen” after “those astray,” prolonging his voice.
ITQAN:v1p284/r2.anchor: وأخرج أبو داود وغيره عن وائل بن حجر سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ ﴿ ولا الضالين ﴾ فقال آمين يمد بها صوته

ITQAN:v1p284/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p284/r3.speaker: الطبراني
ITQAN:v1p284/r3.claim: Al-Tabarani's version says the Prophet said “Amen” three times after the final phrase of al-Fatiha.
ITQAN:v1p284/r3.anchor: وأخرجه الطبراني بلفظ قال آمين ثلاث مرات

ITQAN:v1p284/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p284/r4.speaker: البيهقي
ITQAN:v1p284/r4.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits a variant wording: “Lord, forgive me; amen.”
ITQAN:v1p284/r4.anchor: وأخرجه البيهقي بلفظ قال رب اغفر لي آمين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p328/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p328/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p328/r1.claim: In al-Fātiḥa, ṣirāṭ is the object, al-mustaqīm its adjective, ṣirāṭ alladhīna anʿamta ʿalayhim apposes the preceding phrase, and the remaining clauses modify or coordinate with it.

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p328/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p328/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p328/r2.claim: Syntactic relations are not lexical meanings: word order is not itself a word, and inflection cannot be two signs with one serving as the other's explanation.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p328/r2.anchor: ترتيب اللفظ لا يكون لفظا ، والإعراب وإن كان يكون لفظا

DAMGHANI:v1p460/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r6.claim: Niʿmah can mean prophethood, as in the people favored with prophecy.
DAMGHANI:v1p460/r6.anchor: السادس النعمة النبوة قوله تعالى في فاتحة الكتاب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r1.claim: Lexically, ni'ma is what gives a person enjoyment in life.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r1.anchor: النعمة : ما يحصل للإنسان به التنعم في العيش .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r2.claim: The noun can mean a favor or gracious benefaction, and can also mean wealth; al-na'ama is a gentle wind.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r3.claim: With an open initial n, ni'ma denotes luxurious living; a mutana'im is one living in luxury, and to favor one's children is to make them live luxuriously.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r3.anchor: فأما النعمة - بفتح النون - فهي التنعم . والمتنعم : المترف .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r4.claim: The entry also distinguishes the verb نعم as 'yes' (opposed to لا), with a variant vowel, and as the opposite of بئس.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r4.anchor: وقد تكسر عينها ، ونعم ضد بئس .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r5.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is gracious favor, illustrated by the command to remember God's favor and its parallel in al-Ahzab.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r6.claim: A second sense is religion and Scripture, as in warnings against exchanging God's favor after it came.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r6.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r7.claim: A third sense is Muhammad, whom people recognize as God's favor and then deny.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r8.claim: A fourth sense is reward, as believers rejoice in a favor from God and bounty.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r9.claim: A fifth sense is prophethood, applied to those favored in al-Fatiha and to the command to proclaim the Lord's favor.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r9.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r10.claim: A sixth sense is mercy, as in the phrase 'bounty from God and favor.'
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r10.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r11.claim: A seventh sense is beneficence, as in the statement that no one has a favor owed to be repaid.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r11.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r12.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r12.claim: An eighth sense is ample livelihood, illustrated by God's abundant outward and inward blessings.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r12.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r13.claim: A ninth sense is Islam, in God's favor upon Zayd in the al-Ahzab passage.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r13.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن النعمة في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r14.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r14.claim: A tenth sense is emancipation: God's favor to Zayd was Islam, while the Prophet's favor was freeing Zayd ibn Haritha.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p597/r14.anchor: العتق . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في الأحزاب ]

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba doubts the report that Abdullah omitted Fatiha from his codex and says no Muslim should infer that this learned, Quran-devoted Companion did not know it was Quran.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r2.anchor: فإني أشك فيما روي عن عبد الله من تركه إثباتها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r3.claim: The Prophet praised Abdullah's recitation, telling people who wanted the Quran fresh as revealed to follow Ibn Umm ʿAbd's reading.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r3.anchor: النبي) صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول: «من أحب

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r4.speaker: عمر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r4.claim: Umar described Abdullah as a container filled with knowledge, supporting Ibn Qutayba's case for his learning.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r4.anchor: وعمر يقول فيه: كنيف ملىء علما

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r5.claim: The Prophet's statement لا صلاة إلا بسورة الحمد supports Fatiha's indispensable place in prayer.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r5.anchor: رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يؤم بها، وقال

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r6.claim: Fatiha is the seven oft-repeated and Mother of the Book, meaning its greatest and earliest part; Mecca is similarly called Mother of Villages because it is oldest.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r6.anchor: أم الكتاب، أي أعظمه، وأقدم ما نزل منه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r7.speaker: أهل النظر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r7.claim: The theorists explain that Abdullah did not write Fatiha because compilation guarded against doubt, forgetting, additions, and omissions, while it was short and repeated every prayer and rakʿa.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r7.anchor: أهل النظر، إلى القرآن إنما كتب وجمع

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba concludes that Abdullah knew Fatiha was Quran but saw no need to write it, since no Muslim could neglect learning it or praying with it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p34/r8.anchor: ترك كتابتها وهو يعلم أنها من القرآن

ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r4.claim: The phrase is an adjective for al-ṣirāṭ al-mustaqīm.

ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r5.claim: The hāʾ in ʿalayhim may carry ḍamma or kasra, the two forms used by most readers; a form with an added wāw is also possible.
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r5.anchor: ولك في عليهم ضم الهاء وكسرها (تقول: الذين أنعمت عليهم وعليهم)

ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r6.speaker: سِيبَوَيْهِ
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r6.claim: Sībawayh says the wāw added after masculine hāʾ parallels the added alif in feminine hāʾ forms.
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r6.anchor: وزعم سيبويه أن الواو زيدت على الهاء في المذكر كما زيدت الألف في المؤنث

ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r7.speaker: أصحاب سيبويه والخليل
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r7.claim: Sībawayh's and al-Khalīl's associates explain the added wāw as clarifying the faint hāʾ; it disappears in pause and is not retained as an original letter.
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r7.anchor: والقول في هذه الواو عند أصحاب سيبويه والخليل أنها إنما زيدت لخفاء الهاء وذلك أن الهاء تخرج من أقصى الحلق

ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r8.claim: With a preceding kasra the wāw may change to yāʾ; the Hijazi readings of 28:81 include both hī and hū forms.
ZAJJAJ:v1p49/r8.anchor: فإذا قلت: مررت -، بهو - يا فتى

ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r1.claim: Some Arabs are reported to use a kasra with the second-person kāf in ʿalaykum and bikum, but he rejects this as an anomalous dialect; the correct poetic wording is faḍl aḥlāmikum.

ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r2.claim: Sībawayh quotes the poem with the anomalous form, though its sound transmission is faḍl aḥlāmikum.
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r2.anchor: وهذه لغة شاذة، والرواية الصحيحة: فضل أحلامكم

ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r3.claim: Plural hāʾ forms originally had a wāw, but speakers omit it because mīm suffices and the wāw is heavy; Arabic names do not end in wāw preceded by a vowel.
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r3.anchor: ولكن الميم استغنى بها عن الواو، والواو تثقل على ألسنتهم

ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r4.claim: The reading with the wāw in ʿalayhumū is rare; he says the widespread form without it should be read.
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r4.anchor: ولا ينبغي أن يقرأ إلا بالكثير

ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r5.claim: With genitive ghayr, one analysis makes it a substitute for alladhīna, yielding “the path of those other than the angered.”
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r5.anchor: فيخفض (غير) على وجهين، على البدل من الذين

ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r6.claim: Alternatively, genitive ghayr qualifies alladhīna; although ghayr usually describes an indefinite noun, alladhīna here denotes a category rather than particular people.

ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r7.claim: Accusative ghayr can be an exception, equivalent to “except the angered”; exception ghayr is accusative when what follows illā is accusative.
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r7.anchor: ويجوز نصب (غير) على ضربين: على الحال وعلى الاستثناء

ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r8.claim: Accusative ghayr can instead be a circumstantial, meaning the path of those blessed, not angered.
ZAJJAJ:v1p52/r8.anchor: فأما الحال فكأنك قلت فيها: صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم لا مغضوبا عليهم

ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r1.claim: Al-ḍāllīn is coordinated with al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim; lā is allowed because ghayr already carries negation, as in ghayr ḍārib meaning “not striking.”
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r1.anchor: فإنما عطف بالضالين على المغضوب عليهم، وإنما جاز أن يقع (لا)

ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r2.claim: One cannot say mithla ḍārib in the parallel construction, because Zayd depends on ḍārib and cannot precede it.
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r2.anchor: ولا يجيزون أنت زيدا مثل ضارب، لأن زيدا من صلة ضارب فلا يتقدم عليه

ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r3.claim: After praise and supplication, Arabs use both Amīn and Āmīn; two poems attest the forms.
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r3.anchor: قول القائلين بعد الفراغ من الحمد، ومن الدعاء " آمين " فيه لغتان.

ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r4.claim: An unnamed poet uses Amīn in a prayer that God increase the distance between the speaker and Fataḥl.
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r4.anchor: قال الشاعر: تباعد عني فطحل إذ دعوته. . . أمين فزاد الله ما بيننا بعدا

ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r5.claim: Another unnamed poet uses Āmīnā in a prayer for God's mercy on one who says it.
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r5.anchor: وقال الشاعر أيضا: يا رب لا تسلبني حبها أبدا. . . ويرحم الله عبدا قال آمينا

ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r6.claim: Amīn and Āmīn mean “O God, answer”; they stand in place of a verbal noun for response, like ṣah standing for silence.
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r6.anchor: ومعناه: اللهم استجب، وهما موضوعان في موضع اسم الاستجابة

ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r7.claim: Both are normally paused sounds rather than verb-derived forms; nūn is opened to resolve adjacent quiescent letters, since kasra is heavy after yāʾ, as in ayna and kayfa.
ZAJJAJ:v1p53/r7.anchor: وحقهما من الإعراب الوقف لأنهما بمنزلة الأصوات

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r5.claim: The Fātiḥa explicitly attributes favor to God (‘You bestowed favor’) while describing the blameworthy as those under anger and those astray.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15/r5.anchor: صِرَاطَ الذين أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ المغضوب

NASHR:v1p47/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p47/r10.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v1p47/r10.claim: Khalil transmits from Ibn Kathir accusative ghayra al-maghḍūb, judged sound as a circumstantial phrase or adjective.
NASHR:v1p47/r10.anchor: الخليل بن أحمد عن ابن كثير (غير المغضوب) بالنصب ونصبه حسن على الحال، أو على الصفة

NASHR:v1p47/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p47/r11.speaker: أيوب السختياني
NASHR:v1p47/r11.claim: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani reads al-ḍāllīn with an open hamza in place of the alif, a rare feature in Arabic speech.
NASHR:v1p47/r11.anchor: أيوب السختياني (ولا الضألين) بهمزة مفتوحة في موضع الألف وهو قليل في كلام العرب

NASHR:v1p47/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p47/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p47/r12.claim: Maki deems these noncanonical-imam readings permissible when reliably transmitted, since each has a sound Arabic analysis and agrees with the codex spelling; Ibn al-Jazari says others also share some forms.
NASHR:v1p47/r12.anchor: القراءة به لمن رواه عن الثقات جائزة لصحة وجهه في العربية وموافقته الخط إذا صح نقله

NASHR:v1p227/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p227/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p227/r4.claim: Stopping after these phrases is good because their sense is understood, but starting with attached phrases such as rabb al-ʿālamīn, ṣirāṭ alladhīna, or ghayr al-maghḍūb ʿalayhim is poor, except at verse ends per the Sunnah.
NASHR:v1p227/r4.anchor: الوقف على ذلك وما أشبهه حسن ; لأن المراد من ذلك يفهم، ولكن الابتداء ب (الرحمن الرحيم

NASHR:v2p93/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p93/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p93/r1.claim: Among readers, only al-Azraq lightens an open rāʾ after kasra or a silent yāʾ in a medial or final position; he normally does so without restriction, but tafkhīm returns in stated exceptions, including ṣirāṭ before an istiʿlāʾ letter.
NASHR:v2p93/r1.anchor: وأجمعوا على تفخيمها في هذه الأقسام كلها إلا أن تقع بعد كسرة، أو ياء ساكنة والراء مع ذلك وسط كلمة، أو آخرها فإن الأزرق له فيها مذهب خالف سائر القراء

NASHR:v1p234/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p234/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p234/r2.claim: Sajawandi's mark lā means that one should not begin with the following words; it does not make stopping on the preceding phrase blameworthy, as some imitators assume.
NASHR:v1p234/r2.anchor: بل هو من الحسن يحسن الوقف عليه، ولا يحسن الابتداء بما بعده

NASHR:v1p234/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p234/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p234/r3.claim: Stopping deliberately at ghayr or alladhīna is unanimously forbidden because the first is in construct and the second is connected; Sajawandi's lā forbids beginning there, not stopping before it.
NASHR:v1p234/r3.anchor: على (غير، والذين) اللذين تعمد الوقف عليهما قبيح بالإجماع ; لأن الأول مضاف والثاني موصول

NASHR:v1p272/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p272/r1.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v1p272/r1.claim: Yaqub pronounces the hāʾ of dual and plural pronouns with ḍamma after silent yāʾ; Hamza agrees for ʿalayhim, ilayhim, and ladayhim.
NASHR:v1p272/r1.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب جميع ذلك بضم الهاء، وافقه حمزة في: عليهم وإليهم ولديهم فقط

NASHR:v1p272/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p272/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وقالون
NASHR:v1p272/r4.claim: Before a following vowel, Ibn Kathir and Abu Jaʿfar join plural mīm with a wāw; Qalun varies by route, with many authorities selecting sukūn via Abu Nishit and others selecting ṣila via al-Hulwani.
NASHR:v1p272/r4.anchor: فضم الميم من جميع ذلك، ووصلها بواو في اللفظ وصلا ابن كثير وأبو جعفر، واختلف، عن قالون

NASHR:v1p49/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p49/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة
NASHR:v1p49/r1.claim: Abu Amr, and also Hamza, read ṣirāṭ with a pure zāy; sibilants may substitute for one another, and the reading fits the rasm as does the sīn reading.
NASHR:v1p49/r1.anchor: أبي عمرو، (الزراط) بالزاي الخالصة وجاء أيضا عن حمزة ووجه ذلك أن حروف الصفير يبدل بعضها من بعض

NASHR:v1p49/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p49/r2.speaker: عمر
NASHR:v1p49/r2.claim: Umar reads ghayru al-maghḍūb in the nominative, supplying a predicate such as hum or ulāʾik.
NASHR:v1p49/r2.anchor: وعن عمر - رضي الله عنه -، (غير المغضوب) بالرفع، أي: هم غير المغضوب

NASHR:v1p49/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p49/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن هرمز الأعرج ومسلم بن جندب وعيسى بن عمر الثقفي البصري وعبد الله بن يزيد القصير
NASHR:v1p49/r3.claim: These readers pronounce the hāʾ of ʿalayhim with ḍamma and connect the mīm with a wāw.
NASHR:v1p49/r3.anchor: عبد الرحمن بن هرمز الأعرج ومسلم بن جندب وعيسى بن عمر الثقفي البصري وعبد الله بن يزيد القصير (عليهم) بضم الهاء ووصل الميم بالواو

NASHR:v1p49/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p49/r4.speaker: الحسن وعمرو بن فائد
NASHR:v1p49/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Amr b. Fa'id pronounce the hāʾ with kasra and connect the mīm with a yāʾ.
NASHR:v1p49/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن وعمرو بن فائد (عليهم) بكسر الهاء ووصل الميم بالياء

NASHR:v1p49/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p49/r5.speaker: ابن هرمز
NASHR:v1p49/r5.claim: Ibn Hurmuz also transmits two unconnected forms: ḍamma on both hāʾ and mīm, or kasra on hāʾ with ḍamma on mīm; these and the standard three forms make seven dialect forms.
NASHR:v1p49/r5.anchor: وعن ابن هرمز أيضا بضم الهاء والميم من غير صلة، وعنه أيضا بكسر الهاء وضم الميم من غير صلة فهذه أربعة أوجه وفي المشهور ثلاثة

NASHR:v1p49/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p49/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
NASHR:v1p49/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash describes three further theoretically permissible dialects for ʿalayhim; none of the readers differs about using sukūn when pausing.
NASHR:v1p49/r6.anchor: وذكر أبو الحسن الأخفش فيها ثلاث لغات أخرى لو قرئ بها لجاز، وهي ضم الهاء وكسر الميم مع الصلة

NASHR:v1p332/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p332/r1.speaker: ابن سوار
NASHR:v1p332/r1.claim: Ibn Sawwar reports differing lengths for separated madd: some Hijazi and Basran routes articulate without lengthening, while Hamza, al-Aʿsha, and Qutayba use full length; the rest use a lesser extension. He calls madd before hamza or idghām especially good.
NASHR:v1p332/r1.anchor: أحسن المد من كتاب الله عند استقبال همزة أو إدغام

NASHR:v1p332/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p332/r2.speaker: علي بن فارس
NASHR:v1p332/r2.claim: Ali b. Faris says Hijazi and Basran readers, al-Wali from Hafs, and Qutayba do not extend one letter for another; the remaining readers use full madd, longest with Hamza and al-Aʿsha.
NASHR:v1p332/r2.anchor: إن أهل الحجاز والبصرة والولي، عن حفص وقتيبة

NASHR:v1p332/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p332/r3.speaker: أبو علي المالكي
NASHR:v1p332/r3.claim: Abu Ali al-Maliki ranks Hamza, al-Aʿsha, and Ibn Amir as longest in separated madd, followed by Asim outside al-Aʿsha's route, then al-Kisa'i, though Qutayba is longest among al-Kisa'i's transmitters.
NASHR:v1p332/r3.anchor: فكان أطول الجماعة مدا حمزة والأعشى وابن عامر دونهما، وعاصم في غير رواية الأعشى دونه

NASHR:v1p332/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p332/r5.speaker: ابن مهران
NASHR:v1p332/r5.claim: In al-Mabsut, Ibn Mihran says Abu Jaʿfar, Nafi, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub do not extend across words; listed others do, with Warsh longest, followed by Hamza and Asim via al-Aʿsha. No one disputes extending within one word, though degrees differ.
NASHR:v1p332/r5.anchor: عن المنفصل: أبو جعفر، ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب لا يمدون حرفا لحرف

NASHR:v1p229/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p229/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p229/r1.claim: A pause on an incomplete fragment such as “bi-smi,” “al-ḥamdu,” or “rabbi” leaves the utterance unfinished and without an intelligible meaning.
NASHR:v1p229/r1.anchor: نحو الوقف على: بسم، وعلى: الحمد، وعلى: رب، وملك يوم، وإياك

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r1.claim: The relative pronoun الذين is most eloquently declined with yāʾ in all three cases, though some Arabs use wāw in the nominative; dropping its nūn is permitted, though some restrict that to poetic necessity.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r1.anchor: والأفصح كونه بالياء في أحواله الثلاثة

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r2.claim: Grammarians disagree about how الذين is recognized; unlike الذي, it is restricted to rational beings.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r2.anchor: ويخص العقلاء بخلاف الذي ،   فإنه ينطلق على ذي العلم

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r3.claim: Niʿma denotes ease and softness of living; the south wind and ostrich are also named from softness, and anʿama ʿalayhi means to bestow abundantly.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r3.anchor: لين العيش وخفضه ،   ولذلك قيل للجنوب النعامي

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r4.claim: Anʿama is one of twenty-four functions of the form أفعل: it makes someone possess the base noun, while implying benefaction and taking على instead of its original direct object.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r5.claim: The attached tāʾ is the second-person masculine singular pronoun; أنت consists of two pronouns and is a compound.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r5.anchor: التاء المتصلة بأنعم ضمير المخاطب المذكر المفرد

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r6.claim: Most grammarians treat على as a preposition; Sībawayh and a group of later Basran grammarians treat it as a ظرف noun except in certain constructions. It can express literal or figurative elevation and several other relations.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r6.anchor: حرف جر عند الأكثرين ،   إلا إذا جرت بمن

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r7.claim: The suffix هم is a masculine plural pronoun referring to rational absent people, and it can occupy nominative, accusative, or genitive position.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r7.anchor: هم ضمير جمع غائب مذكر عاقل ،   ويكون في موضع رفع

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r8.claim: The ten reported pronunciations vary the hāʾ and mīm between ḍamma and kasra, mīm sukūn or vowel, and a following yāʾ or wāw: Hamza, the majority, al-Hasan, Ibn Kathīr, Qālūn, al-Aʿraj, and al-Khaffāf are among those named; Ibn Mujāhid adds ʿUmar b. Fāʾid, and ʿAmr b. Fāʾid is also cited.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r9.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r9.claim: Ali identifies the straight path as the Qurʾān; Ibn ʿAbbās is also cited for this interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r9.anchor: الصراط القرآن ،   قاله علي وابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r10.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r10.claim: Al-Mahdawī says a report from the Prophet explains the path as God's Book or faith and its concomitants, Islam and its laws, or the moderate way.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r10.anchor: ذكر المهدوي أنه روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r11.speaker: أبو العالية والحسن
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r11.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Hasan identify the path as the way of the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r12.speaker: فضيل بن عياض
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r12.claim: Fudayl b. ʿIyāḍ interprets the straight path as the way of pilgrimage.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r12.anchor: طريق الحج ،   قاله فضيل بن عياض

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r13.speaker: عثمان
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r13.claim: ʿUthmān interprets the straight path as the Sunan.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r13.anchor: أو السنن ،   قاله عثمان ،   أو طريق الجنة

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r14.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr interprets the straight path as the way to Paradise.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r14.anchor: أو طريق الجنة ،   قاله سعيد بن جبير

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r15.speaker: القشيري
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r15.claim: Al-Qushayrī interprets the straight path as the way of Sunna and the community.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r15.anchor: أو طريق السنة والجماعة ،   قاله القشيري

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r16.speaker: الترمذي
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r16.claim: Al-Tirmidhī interprets the straight path as the way of fear and hope.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r16.anchor: أو طريق الخوف والرجاء ،   قاله الترمذي ،   أو جسر

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r17.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r17.claim: ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd interprets the straight path as the bridge over Hell.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r17.anchor: أو جسر جهنم ،   قاله عمرو بن عبيد

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r18.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r18.claim: One Sufi reading asks for guidance through becoming absent from the path, so that one is not bound to the path; Abū Ḥayyān says such readings do not follow the wording, while acknowledging their experiential insight.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r18.anchor: قول بعضهم : { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } بالغيبوبة عن الصراط لئلا يكون مربوطا بالصراط

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r19.speaker: الجنيد
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r19.claim: Al-Junayd says asking for guidance amid bewilderment is among the clearest pre-eternal attributes; the request seeks the qualities of servanthood to avoid absorption in those attributes.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r19.anchor: قول الجنيد أن سؤال الهداية عند الحيرة من أشهار الصفات

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r20.speaker: الفخر الرازي
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r20.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects identifying the path as the Qurʾān or Islam and its laws because those favored people supposedly lived before the Qurʾān and this Islamic dispensation.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r20.anchor: رد الفخر الرازي على من قال إن الصراط المستقيم هو القرآن

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r21.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says al-Rāzī's objection works only if the favored people are proved to be pre-Islamic; the source will report differing identifications of them, so that premise is unsettled.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r21.anchor: وهذا الرد لا يتأتى له إلا إذا صح أن الذين أنعم الله عليهم

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r22.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r22.claim: The request for guidance follows naturally from the preceding declaration of worship and reliance: worship is sound only through guidance to the clear route that reaches its goal.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r22.anchor: لما أخبر المتكلم أنه هو ومن معه يعبدون الله ويستعينونه

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r23.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r23.speaker: الحسن والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r23.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Dahhāk read صراطاً مستقيماً without the definite article; صراط الذين then apposes a definite expression to an indefinite one, as in 42:52.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r23.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ،   والضحاك : صراطا مستقيما دون تعريف

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r24.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r24.speaker: جعفر الصادق
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r24.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq reads صراط مستقيم with an annexation, meaning the upright religion; with this and the majority reading, صراط الذين is a clarifying apposition of one definite expression to another.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r24.anchor: وقرأ جعفر الصادق : صراط مستقيم بالإضافة ،   أي الدين المستقيم

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r25.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r25.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r25.claim: The apposition identifies the somewhat ambiguous previously mentioned straight path, repeats the request for emphasis, and directs it to the route of those favored.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r25.anchor: لما ذكر قبل { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } كان فيه بعض إبهام

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r26.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r26.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r26.claim: A rare alternative says the second path is different from the first, as if a conjunction had been read between them; the commentators disagree about what this second path denotes.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r26.anchor: ومن غريب القول أن الصراط الثاني ليس الأول ،   بل هو غيره

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r27.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r27.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r27.claim: Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad says the path is knowledge of God and understanding Him.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r27.anchor: العلم بالله والفهم عنه ،   قاله جعفر بن محمد

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r28.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r28.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r28.claim: Other explanations identify the path as observing the obligations and following the Sunan, or as inward agreement with outward practice in the completion of blessing.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r28.anchor: قيل التزام الفرائض واتباع السنن ،   وقيل هو موافقة الباطن للظاهر

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r29.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r29.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r29.claim: The explanation of inward and outward blessing is linked to 31:20, which says God has poured out both manifest and hidden blessings upon you.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r29.anchor: قال تعالى : { وأسبغ عليكم نعمه ظاهرة وباطنة }

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r30.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r30.speaker: ابن مسعود وعمر وابن الزبير وزيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r30.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, ʿUmar, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Zayd b. ʿAlī read صراط من أنعمت عليهم.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r30.anchor: صراط من أنعمت عليهم ،   ابن مسعود ،   وعمر

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r31.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r31.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r31.claim: Among the proposed referents of those favored are prophets, angels, and the unaltered communities of Moses and Jesus; Abū Ḥayyān lists these as alternatives rather than restricting the wording to one group.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r31.anchor: والمنعم عليهم هنا الأنبياء أو الملائكة أو أمة موسى وعيسى الذين لم يغيروا

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r32.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r32.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r32.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for identifying those favored as believers.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r33.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r33.speaker: ابن عطية عن ابن عباس والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r33.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Ibn ʿAbbās and the majority mean the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous, deriving this from 4:69.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r33.anchor: قال ابن عباس : والجمهور أراد صراط النبيين والصديقين

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r34.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r34.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r34.claim: Al-Hasan identifies those favored as the Companions of the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r34.anchor: وقال الحسن : أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r35.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r35.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r35.claim: One group identifies those favored as the believers among the Children of Israel.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r36.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r36.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r36.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also identifies them as Moses' followers before they changed their religion.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r36.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : أصحاب موسى قبل أن يبدلوا

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r37.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r37.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r37.claim: Qatāda limits those favored to the prophets.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r38.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r38.speaker: أبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r38.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies those favored as Muḥammad, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r38.anchor: وقال أبو العالية : محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r39.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r39.speaker: وكيع
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r39.claim: Wakīʿ identifies those favored as Muslims.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r40.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r40.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r40.claim: The wording leaves the blessing unrestricted, so it can encompass every kind of blessing through a general use of the category.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r40.anchor: ولم يقيد الأنعام ليعم جميع الأنعام

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r41.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r41.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r41.claim: Proposed explanations of God's favor include creating people for felicity, rescuing them from destruction, and guiding them to follow the Messenger; the wording itself does not specify a restriction.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r41.anchor: وقيل أنعم عليهم بخلقهم للسعادة ،   وقيل بأن نجاهم من الهلكة

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r42.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r42.speaker: المعتزلة
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r42.claim: The Muʿtazila affirm that God bestows blessing on unbelievers, while other theologians deny it.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r43.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r43.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r43.claim: The prepositional phrase عليهم is in the accusative position because it is governed by an active verb; the same applies to a preposition governed by a non-passive verb or equivalent.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r43.anchor: وموضع عليهم نصب ،   وكذا كل حرف جر تعلق بفعل

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r44.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r44.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r44.claim: The active attribution of favor appeals for acceptance of the request: since God has already favored them, answering their plea for guidance is consistent with His beneficence.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r44.anchor: وبناء أنعمت للفاعل استعطاف لقبول التوسل بالدعاء

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r45.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r45.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r45.claim: The prayer asks that guidance to the path of the favored continue: those who praise God and declare worship and reliance already possess guidance, but ask for its permanence.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r45.anchor: ومضمون هذه الجملة طلب استمرار الهداية إلى طريق من أنعم الله عليهم

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r46.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r46.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r46.claim: Ghayr is always masculine singular; it expresses difference in some respect, originates as an adjective, can mark exception, and remains annexed. It cannot take al and does not ordinarily become definite by annexation.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r46.anchor: مفرد مذكر دائما وإذا أريد به المؤنث جاز تذكير الفعل

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r47.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r47.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r47.claim: Ibn al-Sarrāj says ghayr becomes definite when its complement is one specified entity; Sībawayh allows a non-pure annexation to become definite by intent. The commentators also discuss its fronting in predication.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r47.anchor: ومذهب ابن السراج أنه إذا كان المغاير واحدا تعرف بإضافته إليه

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r48.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r48.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r48.claim: In predication, ghayr or mithl tends to precede its complement; the cited line means the speaker is unlike people who are deceived, and reversed order would distort the point.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r48.anchor: غرضه أنه ليس ممن ينخدع ويغتر

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r49.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r49.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r49.claim: Anger is a change in disposition caused by something disliked; it can also mean turning away, since turning away is one consequence of anger.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r49.anchor: تغير الطبع لمكروه ،   وقد يطلق على الإعراض

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r50.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r50.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r50.claim: Lā can be a particle of negation, prohibition, or augmentation; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the Kufan view that it can be a noun.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r51.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r51.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r51.claim: Ḍalāl can mean ruin, concealment, loss, ignorance of an object's location, waste, neglect, forgetting, departure from the proper route, bewilderment, or hesitation; Qurʾanic usage also includes lack of detailed knowledge and love.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r52.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r52.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r52.claim: The majority read ghayr in the genitive; al-Khalīl reports Ibn Kathīr's accusative reading, also attributed to ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿūd, ʿAlī, and ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Zubayr.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r52.anchor: روى الخليل عن ابن كثير النصب

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r53.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r53.speaker: أبو علي
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r53.claim: Abū ʿAlī parses genitive ghayr as an apposition either to الذين or to the pronoun in عليهم; Abū Ḥayyān calls both analyses weak because apposition by an adjective is weak.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r53.anchor: على البدل من الذين ،   عن أبي علي

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r54.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r54.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r54.claim: Sībawayh parses genitive ghayr as an adjective, treating it as definite through annexation to عليهم; Ibn al-Sarrāj offers a different account of its definiteness.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r55.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r55.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r55.claim: The suggestion that الذين denotes a generic class, allowing ghayr to modify it despite definiteness, undermines the rule that a definite noun is modified only by a definite; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this account.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r55.anchor: ولا أختار هذا المذهب وتقرير فساده في النحو

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r56.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r56.speaker: المهدوي
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r56.claim: Al-Mahdawī and others parse accusative ghayr as a circumstantial accusative from عليهم, or from الذين; Abū Ḥayyān rejects the latter because the genitive complement has no syntactic position for a circumstantial modifier.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r57.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r57.speaker: الأخفش والزجاج
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r57.claim: Al-Akhfash and al-Zajjāj allow accusative ghayr as a disconnected exception because the preceding wording does not include those who are astray; some readers reject this analysis because of lā.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r57.anchor: على الاستثناء ،   قاله الأخفش ،   والزجاج وغيرهما

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r58.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r58.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r58.claim: Some permit accusative ghayr as an exception by treating lā as extra, since they say lā is extra only after prior negation; they cite Qurʾanic and poetic examples, while other grammarians take lā as genuinely negative.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r58.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى الاستثناء جعل لا صلة ،   أي زائدة

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r59.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r59.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r59.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the alleged proof that lā is extra in the verse of the generous man is not decisive: lā itself is the object of أبى, and البخل is its apposition or a causal object.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r59.anchor: ولا دليل في ذلك ،   بل الأظهر أن لا مفعول بأبى

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r60.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r60.speaker: الخليل
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r60.claim: An alternative analysis, attributed to al-Khalīl, treats ghayr as an accusative with an implicit أعني, 'I mean'.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r60.anchor: انتصب غير بإضمار أعني وعزي إلى الخليل

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r61.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r61.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r61.claim: The phrase عليهم is in the nominative position as the passive verb's deputy subject; grammarians dispute whether a prepositional phrase can occupy that role.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r61.anchor: وعليهم في موضع رفع بالمغضوب على أنه مفعول

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r62.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r62.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r62.claim: Lā reinforces the negation already contained in ghayr and is attached to المغضوب عليهم to avoid suggesting that الضالين is coordinated with الذين.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r62.anchor: لتأكيد معنى النفي ،   لأن غير فيه النفي

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r63.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r63.speaker: عمر وأبي
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r63.claim: ʿUmar and Ubayy read غير الضالين, with reports of both accusative and genitive on the rāʾ in the two occurrences; Abū Ḥayyān says the reading marks the angered and astray as distinct, while lā is the likelier emphasis.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r63.anchor: وقرأ عمر وأبي وغير الضالين ،   وروي عنهما في الراء

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r64.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r64.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r64.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī uses the alleged parallel between ghayr and lā to allow a governed object before ghayr; Abū Ḥayyān calls the argument very weak, since similarity of meaning does not transfer syntax without Arabic attestation.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r64.anchor: وأوردها الزمخشري على أنها مسألة مقررة مفروغ منها

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r65.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r65.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r65.claim: Some supply an omitted صراط before ghayr; Abū Ḥayyān finds the estimate weak because it creates awkward apposition or adjective order and other difficult attachment analyses.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r65.anchor: قال التقدير غير صراط المغضوب عليهم

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r66.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r66.speaker: أيوب السختياني
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r66.claim: Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī reads ولا الضألين, turning the alif into hamza to avoid two adjacent sukūns; Abū Ḥayyān says the sound change is not productive, though Abū Zayd and Abū al-Fatḥ attest it as a dialect and cite Arab usage and poetry.

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r67.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r67.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r67.claim: The relative clause of الذين uses a past verb to make God's favor definite and established; the clause with أل uses a participle encompassing all times, and makes the anger passive rather than directly ascribing it to God.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r67.anchor: وجعل الإنعام في صلة الذين ،   والغضب في صلة أل

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r68.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r68.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r68.claim: The passive wording for those angered is tactful in a humble plea: the worshipper attributes favor to the One asked for guidance but avoids confronting Him with the description of vengeance.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r68.anchor: وبناه للمفعول ،   لأن من طلب منه الهداية ونسب الأنعام إليه

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r69.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r69.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r69.claim: The blessing intended is religious; those angered and those astray are general categories covering everyone who incurs anger or goes astray.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r69.anchor: في كل من غضب عليه وضل

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r70.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r70.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r70.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, al-Suddī, and Ibn Zayd identify those angered as Jews and those astray as Christians.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r70.anchor: قاله ابن مسعود ،   وابن عباس ،   ومجاهد ،   والسدي ،   وابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r71.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r71.speaker: عدي بن حاتم عن رسول الله
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r71.claim: The Jews-and-Christians identification is also related from ʿAdī b. Ḥātim from the Prophet; Abū Ḥayyān says it must be adopted if the report is sound.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r71.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم ،   عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r72.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r72.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r72.claim: Another reported identification makes those angered the Jews and those astray the polytheists; Abū Ḥayyān notes other views without specifying them here.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r72.anchor: وقيل اليهود والمشركون ،   وقيل غير ذلك

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r73.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r73.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r73.claim: A Sufi restriction interprets those angered as people who neglect proper courtesy while serving God, and the astray as those who perceive that conduct; Abū Ḥayyān says the wording does not support such restrictions.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r73.anchor: كقول بعضهم غير المغضوب عليهم ،   بترك حسن الأدب

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r74.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r74.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r74.claim: God's anger may mean His intent to requite a sinner, making it an attribute of essence because His knowledge precedes creation and sin; alternatively it is imposing punishment, an attribute of action.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r74.anchor: والغضب من الله تعالى إرادة الانتقام من العاصي

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r75.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r75.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r75.claim: Anger precedes misguidance in the wording although it results from it because it contrasts with favor: favor brings good and requital brings harm; the order also suits the sūra's cadence.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r75.anchor: وقدم الغضب على الضلال ،   وإن كان الغضب من نتيجة الضلال

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r76.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r76.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r76.claim: The conjunctive wāw does not itself establish temporal priority; if Jews and Christians are intended, the order may reflect chronology or the Jews' greater hostility, as they came earlier.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r76.anchor: وكان العطف بالواو الجامعة التي لا دلالة فيها على التقديم والتأخير

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r77.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r77.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r77.claim: The sūra's closing phrases are an instance of parallel cadence (sajʿ mutawāzī), with the final words matching in meter and rhyme; the author also lists specification, apposition, and word order among its rhetorical features.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r77.anchor: وفي هذه السورة من التسجيع المتوازي ،   وهو اتفاق الكلمتين الأخيرتين

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r78.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r78.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r78.claim: Abū Ḥayyān concludes that the sūra is seven verses by consensus apart from disregarded dissent; Meccan and Kufan counters differ over whether the basmala or صراط الذين is an āya, while ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd counts eight and Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī six.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r78.anchor: والإجماع على أنها سبع آيات إلا ما شذ فيه من لا يعتبر خلافه

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r79.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r79.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r79.claim: He says the basmala at each sūra's opening is not an āya, while Ibn al-Mubārak anomalously counted it as an āya in every sūra; Abū Ḥayyān says he does not know the principle behind determining āya length.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r79.anchor: ولم يختلفوا في أن البسملة في أول كل سورة ليست آية

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r80.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r80.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r80.claim: Reports about the sūra's letter count, supposed occasions of revelation, basmala's merit, and many titles are not necessarily causes of revelation or core tafsīr; only sound Prophetic clarification, occasions, and abrogation are indispensable to tafsīr.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r80.anchor: وذكروا سبب نزولها ما لا يعد سبب نزول

ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r81.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r81.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r81.claim: The word Āmīn is not Qurʾān; Abū Ḥayyān omits discussion of its forms, meaning, and prayer ruling, along with introductory istiʿādha, as material outside his intended tafsīr scope.
ABUHAYYAN:1:7/r81.anchor: وليست من القرآن ،   فلذلك أضربنا عن الكلام عليها صفحا

ALUSI:1:7/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r1.claim: The second ṣirāṭ is a fully matching apposition to the first; Ibn Mālik calls it the corresponding or matching apposition to avoid applying ‘whole’ to God in 14:1–2.
ALUSI:1:7/r1.anchor: صِرَاطَ الذين أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ } بدل من الصراط الأول بدل الكل من الكل

ALUSI:1:7/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r2.claim: Apposition reinforces the predication, since it repeats the governing relation, and explains the straight path as the Muslims’ path, emphatically attesting to its rightness.
ALUSI:1:7/r2.anchor: وفائدة الإبدال تأكيد النسبة بناءً على أن البدل في حكم تكرير العامل والإشعار بأن الصراط المستقيم بيانه وتفسيره صراط المسلمين

ALUSI:1:7/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r3.claim: An alternative analysis calls the second phrase an adjective of the first ṣirāṭ.

ALUSI:1:7/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r4.claim: One unusual transmitted interpretation treats the second path as different from the first, as if a conjunction were understood.
ALUSI:1:7/r4.anchor: ومن غريب المنقول أن الصراط الثاني غير الأول وكأنه نوى فيه حرف العطف

ALUSI:1:7/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r5.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ALUSI:1:7/r5.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad identifies the path with knowledge of God and understanding from Him.
ALUSI:1:7/r5.anchor: فعن جعفر بن محمد هو العلم بالله والفهم عنه

ALUSI:1:7/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r6.claim: Another interpretation is conformity between inward and outward life in the full bestowal of blessing.
ALUSI:1:7/r6.anchor: وقيل موافقة الباطن للظاهر في إسباغ النعمة

ALUSI:1:7/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r7.claim: A further interpretation makes the path adherence to obligations and Prophetic practices; al-Ālūsī dismisses it as a departure from the straight path.
ALUSI:1:7/r7.anchor: وقيل التزام الفرائض والسنن ، ولا يخفى أن هذا القول خروج عن الصراط المستقيم

ALUSI:1:7/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read ṣirāṭ man anʿamta ʿalayhim; this is also transmitted from ʿUmar and the Ahl al-Bayt.
ALUSI:1:7/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وزيد بن علي صراط من أنعمت عليهم ، وهو المروي عن عمر وأهل البيت رضي الله تعالى عنهم

ALUSI:1:7/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r9.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI:1:7/r9.claim: Al-Shihāb takes the indefinite relative expression man as evidence that an indefinite name may be applied to God; al-Ālūsī calls this an evident confusion because the genitive is objective, not agentive.
ALUSI:1:7/r9.anchor: قال الشهاب : وفيه دليل على جواز إطلاق الأسماء المبهمة

ALUSI:1:7/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r10.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI:1:7/r10.claim: Al-Rāghib defines bestowal as conveying beneficence to another rational being, so one does not say that someone bestowed a favor on his horse.
ALUSI:1:7/r10.anchor: والإنعام إيصال الإحسان إلى الغير من العقلاء كما قاله الراغب

ALUSI:1:7/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r11.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r11.claim: A reported definition calls a blessing a benefit given by someone superior to a person without compensation.
ALUSI:1:7/r11.anchor: قيل : إن النعمة نفع الإنسان من دونه لغير عوض

ALUSI:1:7/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r12.claim: One view identifies those blessed as believers in general.
ALUSI:1:7/r12.anchor: واختلف في هؤلاء المنعم عليهم فقيل المؤمنون مطلقاً

ALUSI:1:7/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r13.claim: Another view restricts those blessed to the prophets.

ALUSI:1:7/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r14.claim: Another view means the followers of Moses and Jesus before textual alteration and abrogation.
ALUSI:1:7/r14.anchor: وقيل أصحاب موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام قبل التحريف والنسخ

ALUSI:1:7/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r15.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r15.claim: Another view identifies those blessed as the Companions of Muḥammad.
ALUSI:1:7/r15.anchor: وقيل أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:1:7/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r16.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r16.claim: Another view names Muḥammad, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar as those blessed.
ALUSI:1:7/r16.anchor: وقيل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI:1:7/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:1:7/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās’s report in al-Ṭabarī: the blessed include prophets, angels, martyrs, the truthful, and all who obey and worship God; other views restrict the class to some members.
ALUSI:1:7/r17.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن المراد بالذين أنعمت عليهم الأنبياء والملائكة

ALUSI:1:7/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r18.claim: The unrestricted blessing embraces every blessing, in line with the verse saying that people cannot enumerate God’s blessings.
ALUSI:1:7/r18.anchor: ولم يقيد الأنعام ليعم { وَإِن تَعُدُّواْ نِعْمَةَ الله لاَ تُحْصُوهَا }

ALUSI:1:7/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r19.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r19.claim: One view says God blessed them by creating them for felicity.
ALUSI:1:7/r19.anchor: وقيل أنعم عليهم بخلقهم للسعادة . وقيل بأن نجاهم من الهلكة

ALUSI:1:7/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r20.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r20.claim: Another view says God blessed them by rescuing them from destruction; a further view says the blessing was guidance.
ALUSI:1:7/r20.anchor: وقيل بأن نجاهم من الهلكة . وقيل بالهداية

ALUSI:1:7/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r21.claim: Using the active second-person verb is an appeal: since God has already bestowed favor, the worshipper asks Him to grant guidance too; the cited verse of poetry illustrates that God taught people to ask in order to give.
ALUSI:1:7/r21.anchor: وفي بناء أنعمت للفاعل استعطاف فكأن الداعي يقول أطلب منك الهداية

ALUSI:1:7/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r22.claim: The accompanying poem says that God would not have taught people to ask unless He intended to grant their hopes; al-Ālūsī gives no poet’s name.
ALUSI:1:7/r22.anchor: لو لم ترد نيل ما نرجو ونطلبه *** من فيض جودك ما علمتنا الطلبا

ALUSI:1:7/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r23.speaker: اللغويون
ALUSI:1:7/r23.claim: The linguists list ten forms: hāʾ ḍamma/kasra with variable mīm and optional wāw or yāʾ. Attributions name Ḥamza, the majority, al-Ḥasan, ʿUmar b. Khālid/Fāʾid, Ibn Kathīr/Qālūn, al-Aʿraj, Muslim b. Jundub, Ibn Hurmuz, and al-Khaffāf from Abū ʿAmr.
ALUSI:1:7/r23.anchor: وحكى اللغويون في { عَلَيْهِمْ } عشر لغات

ALUSI:1:7/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r24.claim: Ghayr is a matching apposition to alladhīna. Making it an apposition to the pronoun in ʿalayhim is semantically awkward; the relative clause still contains its pronoun because the antecedent is not truly discarded.
ALUSI:1:7/r24.anchor: { غَيْرِ المغضوب عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ الضالين } بدل من { الذين } بدل كل من كل

ALUSI:1:7/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r25.claim: Treating ghayr as an adjective meaning different is weak: ghayr has become a noun and usually does not modify an expressed noun.
ALUSI:1:7/r25.anchor: والبدل بالوصف ضعيف ضعيف لأنها غلبت عليها الاسمية

ALUSI:1:7/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r26.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI:1:7/r26.claim: Sībawayh analyzes ghayr as an explanatory or restrictive adjective of alladhīna; al-Ālūsī explains that the relative is definite generically but can function like an indefinite when only an unspecified subset is intended.
ALUSI:1:7/r26.anchor: وعن سيبويه أنها صفة { الذين } مبينة أو مقيدة

ALUSI:1:7/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r27.speaker: المحققون من علماء العربية
ALUSI:1:7/r27.claim: Some authoritative Arab grammarians allow ghayr to become definite by annexation between two opposite definite terms, as in movement versus stillness; this analysis is adopted by those who rely on it.
ALUSI:1:7/r27.anchor: لأن المحققين من علماء العربية قالوا إنها قد تتعرف بالإضافة وذلك إذا وقعت بين متضادين معرفتين

ALUSI:1:7/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r28.speaker: ابن السري
ALUSI:1:7/r28.claim: Ibn al-Sarrī says ghayr becomes definite when annexed to a definite having only one opposite, since the contrast is then exclusive.
ALUSI:1:7/r28.anchor: وقال ابن السري وغيره : إذا أضيفت { غير } إلى معرف له ضد واحد فقط تعرفت

ALUSI:1:7/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r29.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r29.claim: The objection from 35:37 does not disprove this definiteness: ṣāliḥan may be a fronted circumstantial accusative, or ghayr alladhī may be an apposition to it.
ALUSI:1:7/r29.anchor: لجواز أن يكون { صالحا } حالاً قدمت على صاحبها

ALUSI:1:7/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r30.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ALUSI:1:7/r30.claim: ʿUmar read ghayra in the accusative; a noncanonical report attributes the same reading to Ibn Kathīr. It is best parsed as a circumstantial accusative governed by anʿamta, though other analyses are discussed.
ALUSI:1:7/r30.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه { غَيْرِ } بالنصب ، وروي ذلك شاذاً عن ابن كثير

ALUSI:1:7/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r31.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI:1:7/r31.claim: Al-Akhfash permits the accusative as either a disconnected or connected exception if bestowal is understood generally.
ALUSI:1:7/r31.anchor: وجوز الأخفش أن يكون النصب على الاستثناء المنقطع أو المتصل إن فسر الإنعام بما يعم

ALUSI:1:7/r32.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r32.speaker: الفراء
