ALUSI:1:7/r32.claim: Al-Farrāʾ rejects the exception analysis because ghayr then means siwā and the negative lā cannot be coordinated with it unless lā is treated as extra; al-Ālūsī notes the usage after wāw is unattested.
ALUSI:1:7/r32.anchor: ومنعه الفراء لأنه حينئذٍ بمعنى سوى فلا يجوز أن يعطف عليه ( بلا ) لأنها نفي

ALUSI:1:7/r33.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r33.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI:1:7/r33.claim: A report ascribed to al-Akhfash treats the exception as semantically negative, allowing lā to coordinate by meaning and removing al-Farrāʾ’s objection.
ALUSI:1:7/r33.anchor: وحكى بعضهم عن الأخفش أن الاستثناء في معنى النفي ، فيجوز العطف عليه ( بلا )

ALUSI:1:7/r34.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r34.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI:1:7/r34.claim: Al-Khalīl parses the accusative as governed by an omitted verb, aʿnī, and al-Ālūsī endorses him: exception is problematic and the circumstantial analysis requires an unpersuasive indefinite ghayr.
ALUSI:1:7/r34.anchor: وعند الخليل النصب بفعل محذوف أعني : أعني وبه أقول

ALUSI:1:7/r35.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r35.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:1:7/r35.claim: Some posit an ellipsis, supplying ghayra ṣirāṭ al-maghḍūbi ʿalayhim, and offer several possible syntactic attachments; al-Ālūsī prefers the unelliptical straightforward syntax.
ALUSI:1:7/r35.anchor: وقال بعضهم : في الآية حذف والتقدير غير صراط المغضوب عليهم

ALUSI:1:7/r36.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r36.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r36.claim: The root of anger denotes intensity; the word is also used for a hard rock, a vicious snake, and a scowling she-camel.
ALUSI:1:7/r36.anchor: والغضب أصله الشدة ، ومنه الغضبة الصخرة الصلبة الشديدة

ALUSI:1:7/r37.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r37.speaker: السعد
ALUSI:1:7/r37.claim: In his commentary on al-Miftāḥ, al-Saʿd defines anger as a movement of the soul whose origin is the will to take revenge.
ALUSI:1:7/r37.anchor: فسر تارة بحركة للنفس مبدؤها إرادة الانتقام كما في «شرح المفتاح » للسعد

ALUSI:1:7/r38.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r38.speaker: السعد
ALUSI:1:7/r38.claim: In his commentary on al-Kashshāf, al-Saʿd defines divine anger as the will to take revenge.
ALUSI:1:7/r38.anchor: كما في «شرح المفتاح » للسعد وتارة بإرادة الانتقام كما في «شرح الكشاف » له

ALUSI:1:7/r39.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r39.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r39.claim: A definition in Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid describes anger as a state of the soul followed by the spirit’s outward motion seeking revenge; another account calls it a change when the heart’s blood boils.

ALUSI:1:7/r40.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r40.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r40.claim: A hadith warns people to beware of anger, likening it to a glowing ember in the heart and pointing to swollen neck veins and reddened eyes; no grading or source is given here.
ALUSI:1:7/r40.anchor: اتقوا الغضب فإنه جمرة تتوقد في قلب ابن آدم ألم تروا إلى انتفاخ أوداجه وحمرة عينيه

ALUSI:1:7/r41.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r41.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:1:7/r41.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains God’s anger as His will to punish sinners, bringing punishment upon them as an angry king does to subjects under his authority.
ALUSI:1:7/r41.anchor: وفي «الكشاف » معنى غضب الله تعالى إرادة الانتقام من العصاة وإنزال العقوبة بهم

ALUSI:1:7/r42.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r42.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r42.claim: Following the early generations, al-Ālūsī affirms anger as an eternal divine attribute fitting God’s majesty without specifying how or claiming to know its reality, like mercy.
ALUSI:1:7/r42.anchor: وأنا أقول كما قال سلف الأمة : هو صفة لله تعالى لائقة بجلال ذاته

ALUSI:1:7/r43.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r43.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r43.claim: The hadith God’s mercy preceded His anger means either that mercy’s effects are greater or that mercy appeared earlier.
ALUSI:1:7/r43.anchor: محمول على الزيادة في الآثار أو تقدم ظهورها

ALUSI:1:7/r44.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r44.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r44.claim: Ḍalāl originally means destruction, as in the verses about being lost in the earth and God destroying deeds; in religion it means departing from truth.
ALUSI:1:7/r44.anchor: وأصل الضلال الهلاك ومنه قوله تعالى

ALUSI:1:7/r45.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r45.speaker: أبو أيوب السختياني
ALUSI:1:7/r45.claim: Abū Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī reads al-ḍāʾallīn with hamza, avoiding two adjacent quiescent letters although their meeting is permissible.
ALUSI:1:7/r45.anchor: وقرأ أبو أيوب السختياني { وَلاَ الضألين } بإبدال الألف همزة

ALUSI:1:7/r46.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r46.speaker: أبو زيد
ALUSI:1:7/r46.claim: Abū Zayd records the dialectal forms daʾaba and shaʾaba; this pronunciation is also found in ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd’s reading of 55:39.
ALUSI:1:7/r46.anchor: وحكى أبو زيد دأبة وشأبة وعلى هذه اللغة قراءة عمرو بن عبيد

ALUSI:1:7/r47.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r47.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r47.claim: The cited poem’s word fādaʾhamat exemplifies the same hamzated form; grammarians disagree whether the usage can be extended by analogy.
ALUSI:1:7/r47.anchor: فادهأمت وهل يقاس عليه أم لا ؟ قولان

ALUSI:1:7/r48.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r48.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ALUSI:1:7/r48.claim: A reading with wa-ghayr in place of wa-lā is reported from ʿUmar and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr; the muṣḥaf’s mutawātir reading is wa-lā, which reinforces the negation implicit in ghayr.
ALUSI:1:7/r48.anchor: وروي عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه وعبد الله بن الزبير أنهما كانا يقرآن

ALUSI:1:7/r49.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r49.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:1:7/r49.claim: Aḥmad transmits and Ibn Ḥibbān grades as ḥasan a Prophetic report identifying the objects of anger as Jews and the astray as Christians.
ALUSI:1:7/r49.anchor: وحسنه ابن حبان في «صحيحه » مرفوعاً إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:1:7/r50.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r50.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:1:7/r50.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits the same identification from Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd; Ibn Abī Ḥātim says he knows no disagreement among Qurʾān commentators about it.
ALUSI:1:7/r50.anchor: وأخرجه ابن جرير عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود

ALUSI:1:7/r51.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r51.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r51.claim: Al-Ālūsī also reads the general terms broadly: those erring in outward works, such as sinners, are under anger; those erring in belief are astray. The Prophetic Jewish and Christian identifications remain sound specifications of the general wording.
ALUSI:1:7/r51.anchor: بل الأولى أن يحمل المغضوب عليهم على كل من أخطأ في الأعمال الظاهرة وهم الفساق

ALUSI:1:7/r52.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r52.speaker: من زعم
ALUSI:1:7/r52.claim: Some argue Jews and Christians are too mild a referent because atheists and polytheists are worse; al-Ālūsī rejects this reasoning in light of the sound Prophetic report and criticizes its disregard of hadith.
ALUSI:1:7/r52.anchor: فمن زعم أن الحمل على ذلك ضعيف لأن منكري الصانع والمشركين أخبث ديناً من اليهود والنصارى

ALUSI:1:7/r53.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r53.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI:1:7/r53.claim: Al-Rāzī suggests that those under anger are unbelievers and the astray are hypocrites, analogizing to al-Baqara’s order of believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites; al-Ālūsī rejects the analogy against the Prophetic report.
ALUSI:1:7/r53.anchor: والعجب من الإمام الرازي أنه نقل هذا ولم يتعقبه بشيء سوى أنه زاد في الشطرنج بغلاً

ALUSI:1:7/r54.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r54.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:1:7/r54.claim: Some support the Jewish identification from the verse saying that God cursed and became angry with a group, making some of them apes and swine.
ALUSI:1:7/r54.anchor: واستدل بعضهم على أن المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود بقوله تعالى

ALUSI:1:7/r55.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r55.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:1:7/r55.claim: Some support the Christian identification from the verse warning against following the desires of a people who went astray.
ALUSI:1:7/r55.anchor: وعلى أن الضالين النصارى بقوله تعالى

ALUSI:1:7/r56.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r56.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r56.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the hadith as evidence: anger and straying are also ascribed generally to unbelievers, and both terms apply specifically to Jews and Christians.
ALUSI:1:7/r56.anchor: والأولى الاستدلال بالحديث لأن الغضب والضلال وردا جميعاً في القرآن لجميع الكفار

ALUSI:1:7/r57.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r57.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r57.claim: He offers several reasons for the order: Jews precede Christians historically; bestowal contrasts with retribution rather than misguidance; and Jews are more obstinate, corrupt, hostile to believers, and abased.
ALUSI:1:7/r57.anchor: وإنما قدم سبحانه المغضوب عليهم على الضالين مع أن الضلال في بادئ النظر

ALUSI:1:7/r58.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r58.speaker: السلفي والديلمي وابن عدي
ALUSI:1:7/r58.claim: Al-Salafī, al-Daylamī, and Ibn ʿAdī transmit a report saying that whoever has no charity should curse the Jews; no grading is stated.
ALUSI:1:7/r58.anchor: وورد في الحديث : «من لم يكن عنده صدقة فليلعن اليهود » رواه السلفي والديلمي وابن عدي

ALUSI:1:7/r59.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r59.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r59.claim: Al-Ālūsī says Christians are less culpable and closer to Islam, and a person who is merely astray may still find guidance.
ALUSI:1:7/r59.anchor: والنصارى دون ذلك وأقرب للإسلام منهم ولذا وصفوا بالضلال لأن الضال قد يهتدي

ALUSI:1:7/r60.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r60.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r60.claim: Jews rejected both Jesus and Muḥammad, while Christians rejected only Muḥammad; al-Ālūsī also says Jewish scandals and atrocities exceed those of Christians.
ALUSI:1:7/r60.anchor: أنهم كفروا بنبيين محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وعيسى عليه السلام والنصارى كفروا بنبي واحد

ALUSI:1:7/r61.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r61.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r61.claim: Al-Ālūsī argues that the Christian doctrine of Trinity is no worse than Jewish claims that God is poor, His hand is tied, and Ezra is His son.
ALUSI:1:7/r61.anchor: وقول النصارى/ بالتثليث ليس أفظع من قول اليهود

ALUSI:1:7/r62.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r62.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:1:7/r62.claim: Some explain the delayed mention of the astray by the rhyme of the verse endings; al-Ālūsī accepts this only alongside the other explanations.
ALUSI:1:7/r62.anchor: وقال بعضهم : تأخير الضالين لموافقة رؤوس الآي ولا بأس بضمه إلى تلك الوجوه

ALUSI:1:7/r63.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r63.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r63.claim: The blessing is directly attributed to God as a deferential appeal for guidance to those whose favor is established; anger is put in the passive and left unassigned out of courtesy in a humble request for kindness.
ALUSI:1:7/r63.anchor: وإنما أسند النعمة إليه تعالى تقرباً والمقصود طلب الهداية إلى صراط من ثبت إنعام الله تعالى عليه

ALUSI:1:7/r64.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r64.speaker: ابن الأثير
ALUSI:1:7/r64.claim: Ibn al-Athīr and al-Tanūkhī classify passivizing a verb after addressing its agent as an unusual kind of rhetorical turn; al-Ālūsī accepts it if turn means stylistic variation, and also defends the technical reading through al-Sakkākī’s definition.
ALUSI:1:7/r64.anchor: وقد عد ابن الأثير في «كنز البلاغة » والتنوخي في «الأقصى القريب » بناء الفعل للمفعول بعد خطاب فاعله

ALUSI:1:7/r65.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r65.speaker: جبريل
ALUSI:1:7/r65.claim: Abū Maysara reports that Gabriel taught the Opening to the Prophet and instructed him to say Āmīn after wa-lā al-ḍāllīn; the report is cited from Ibn Abī Shayba and al-Bayhaqī without a grading.
ALUSI:1:7/r65.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة : «أن جبريل أقرأ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتحة الكتاب

ALUSI:1:7/r66.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r66.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:1:7/r66.claim: Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī reports the Prophet’s instruction that the congregation say Āmīn when the imam recites the final words, so that God will love them; Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Mājah, and Ibn Abī Shayba transmit it.
ALUSI:1:7/r66.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI:1:7/r67.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r67.speaker: الحنفية
ALUSI:1:7/r67.claim: The Ḥanafīs conceal Āmīn, following ʿAlī and Ibn Masʿūd; the Shāfiʿīs say it aloud. The report of the majority’s loud recitation is interpreted as instruction or discussion.
ALUSI:1:7/r67.anchor: وإخفاؤها مذهب ساداتنا الحنفية ، وهو مذهب أمير المؤمنين علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI:1:7/r68.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r68.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI:1:7/r68.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the imam should not say Āmīn because he is the supplicant; this is also found in a less famous report from Abū Ḥanīfa, whereas the famous view is that he says it silently.
ALUSI:1:7/r68.anchor: وعن الحسن لا يقولها الإمام لأنه الداعي

ALUSI:1:7/r69.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r69.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل
ALUSI:1:7/r69.claim: Reports from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal and Anas, cited from al-Kashshāf, say the Prophet concealed Āmīn.
ALUSI:1:7/r69.anchor: وروى الإخفاء عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عبد الله بن مغفل وأنس

ALUSI:1:7/r70.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r70.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r70.claim: Āmīn is not part of the Qurʾān by consensus; a slight pause separates it from the sūra. Al-Ālūsī rejects Mujāhid’s contrary attribution as utterly false because it appears in no muṣḥaf.
ALUSI:1:7/r70.anchor: وليست من القرآن إجماعاً ولذا سن الفصل بينها وبين السورة بسكتة لطيفة

ALUSI:1:7/r71.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r71.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI:1:7/r71.claim: Some authorities say that anyone who claims Āmīn is Qurʾān has committed unbelief.
ALUSI:1:7/r71.anchor: حتى ذكر غير واحد أن من قال : إن آمين من القرآن كفر

ALUSI:1:7/r72.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r72.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r72.claim: Āmīn is an Arabic particle functioning as a verb, built on fatḥa to avoid meeting two quiescent letters; its correct meaning is respond, while another view gives it a broader sense including a synonym.
ALUSI:1:7/r72.anchor: وهي اسم فعل مبني على الفتح كأين لالتقاء الساكنين

ALUSI:1:7/r73.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r73.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r73.claim: Another view says Āmīn is used for a broader meaning that includes respond and its synonym.
ALUSI:1:7/r73.anchor: وقيل موضوعة لما هو أعم منه ومن مرادفه

ALUSI:1:7/r74.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r74.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r74.claim: A strange view derives the Arabicized word from the foreign hamīn because fāʿīl is not an Arabic pattern; a response says it may be a unique pattern with analogues, or originally short and lengthened.
ALUSI:1:7/r74.anchor: ومن الغريب ما قيل إنه عجمي معرب همين لما أن فاعيل كقابيل ليس من أوزان العرب ورد بأنه يكون وزناً لا نظير له وله نظائر

ALUSI:1:7/r75.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r75.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:1:7/r75.claim: Another unusual view treats Āmīn as a name of God because it contains a hidden pronoun referring to Him; al-Ālūsī finds this rationale even stranger.
ALUSI:1:7/r75.anchor: ومن العجيب ما قيل إنه اسم الله تعالى والقول في توجيهه أنه لما كان مشتملاً على الضمير المستتر الراجع إليه تعالى

ALUSI:1:7/r76.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r76.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r76.claim: Readers disagree whether the alif in Āmīn is inherently long or short; groups support each origin.
ALUSI:1:7/r76.anchor: وقد تمد ألفه وتقصر وإلى أصالة كل ذهب طائفة

ALUSI:1:7/r77.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r77.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI:1:7/r77.claim: Al-Wāḥidī calls a doubled mīm a dialect form; another view calls it an error. Since Āmīn is a non-Qurʾānic supplication with a sound meaning, some say that pronunciation does not invalidate prayer.
ALUSI:1:7/r77.anchor: وأما تشديد ميمه فذكر الواحدي أنه لغة فيه

ALUSI:1:7/r78.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r78.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI:1:7/r78.claim: Abū Hurayra reports a sound-chain hadith in which the Prophet tells Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that no Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qurʾān passage equals the Opening, calling it the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qurʾān granted to him.
ALUSI:1:7/r78.anchor: ما روي بأسانيد صحيحة عن أبي هريرة رضي الله تعالى عنه : «أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج

ALUSI:1:7/r79.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r79.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r79.claim: Al-Ālūsī calls the sūra the Mother of the Book and a treasure of gnosis; he says some spiritual masters derive cosmic events, Muslim rulers’ names, their histories, and their fates from it, likening it to the Preserved Tablet of what appears in existence.
ALUSI:1:7/r79.anchor: فهي أم الكتاب والحاوية من دقائق الأسرار العجب العجاب حتى إن بعض الربانيين استخرج منها الحوادث الكونية وأسماء الملوك الإسلامية

ALUSI:1:7/r80.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:1:7/r80.speaker: author
ALUSI:1:7/r80.claim: Al-Ālūsī closes by praying for the sūra’s lights to shine upon him and for access to its hidden secrets, declaring God the source of success and guide to verified truth.
ALUSI:1:7/r80.anchor: نسأل الله تعالى أن يمن علينا بإشراق أنوارها والاطلاع على مخزونات أسرارها إنه ولي التوفيق

BAGHAWI:1:7/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r1.claim: The favored are those on whom God bestowed guidance and enabling grace.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r1.anchor: أي مننت عليهم بالهداية والتوفيق قال عكرمة :

BAGHAWI:1:7/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r2.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI:1:7/r2.claim: Ikrima says they are the prophets, whom God kept firm in faith and uprightness.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة : مننت عليهم بالثبات على الإيمان والاستقامة ، وهم الأنبياء

BAGHAWI:1:7/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r3.claim: Another view includes everyone God kept firm in faith among the prophets and believers, as in the verse about those favored alongside the prophets.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r3.anchor: وقيل : هم كل من ثبته الله على الإيمان من النبيين والمؤمنين الذين ذكرهم الله تعالى في قوله

BAGHAWI:1:7/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:1:7/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says they were the followers of Moses and Jesus before they changed their religion.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : هم قوم موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام قبل أن غيروا دينهم ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن
BAGHAWI:1:7/r5.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman identifies them as the Prophet and those with him.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن : هم النبي ومن معه ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
BAGHAWI:1:7/r6.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya identifies them as the Messenger, Abu Bakr, and ʿUmar.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r6.anchor: وقال أبو العالية : هم الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر وعمر رضي الله عنهما ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
BAGHAWI:1:7/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says they are the Messenger and his household.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r7.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد : إنه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأهل بيته ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r8.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
BAGHAWI:1:7/r8.claim: Shahr ibn Hawshab says they are the Prophet's Companions and his household.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r8.anchor: وقال شهر بن حوشب : هم أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأهل بيته .

BAGHAWI:1:7/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r9.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI:1:7/r9.claim: Hamza pronounces the hāʾ in ʿalayhim, ladayhim, and ilayhim with ḍamma.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r9.anchor: قرأ حمزة : ( عليهم ، ولديهم ، وإليهم ) ، بضم هاءاتها ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r10.speaker: يعقوب
BAGHAWI:1:7/r10.claim: Yaʿqub uses ḍamma on each hāʾ preceded by a quiescent yāʾ in dual and plural forms, except in “between their hands and feet.”
BAGHAWI:1:7/r10.anchor: ويضم يعقوب كل هاء قبلها ياء ساكنة تثنية وجمعاً إلا قوله : ( بين أيديهن وأرجلهن )

BAGHAWI:1:7/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r11.claim: Other readers use kasra on the hāʾ, following the preceding quiescent yāʾ, which is the sister of kasra; ḍamma returns to the hāʾ's isolated form.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r11.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بكسرهما ، فمن ضم الهاء ردها إلى الأصل ، لأنها مضمومة عند الانفراد

BAGHAWI:1:7/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r12.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو جعفر
BAGHAWI:1:7/r12.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Jaʿfar lengthen the plural mīm in connected reading unless a quiescent letter follows, in which case they do not lengthen it.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r12.anchor: وضم ابن كثير و أبو جعفر كل ميم جمع مشبعاً في الوصل إذا لم يلقها ساكن ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r13.speaker: نافع
BAGHAWI:1:7/r13.claim: Nafiʿ allows a choice in the plural mīm's lengthening.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r13.anchor: فإن لقيها ساكن فلا يشبع ، ونافع يخير ، ويضم ورش

BAGHAWI:1:7/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r14.speaker: ورش
BAGHAWI:1:7/r14.claim: Warsh uses ḍamma before hamzat al-qaṭʿ.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r14.anchor: ويضم ورش عند ألف القطع ، فإذا تلقته ألف وصل

BAGHAWI:1:7/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r15.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
BAGHAWI:1:7/r15.claim: Before hamzat al-waṣl, Hamza and al-Kisa'i use ḍamma after kasra or silent yāʾ; Abu ʿAmr uses kasra on both letters, as does Yaʿqub when the preceding letter is kasra.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r15.anchor: ضم الهاء والميم حمزة و الكسائي ، وكسرهما أبو عمرو ، وكذلك يعقوب إذا انكسر ما قبله ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r16.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r16.claim: The remaining readers use a ḍamma on mīm and kasra on hāʾ throughout, owing to the yāʾ or preceding kasra and the mīm's original ḍamma.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r16.anchor: والآخرون يقرؤون بضم الميم وكسر الهاء في الكل لأجل الياء ، أو لكسر ما قبلها وضم الميم على الأصل .

BAGHAWI:1:7/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r17.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r17.claim: “Not those angered” means a path other than that of those God wills to punish for disobedience.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r17.anchor: يعني غير صراط الذين غضبت عليهم ، والغضب هو : إرادة الانتقام من العصاة ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r18.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r18.claim: God's anger does not befall sinful believers; it befalls only disbelievers.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r18.anchor: وغضب الله تعالى لا يلحق عصاة المؤمنين إنما يلحق الكافرين .

BAGHAWI:1:7/r19.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r19.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r19.claim: The phrase means those who are not astray from guidance; the root of misguidance conveys destruction and disappearance, like water disappearing in milk.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r19.anchor: أي وغير الضالين عن الهدى . وأصل الضلال الهلاك والغيبوبة ، يقال : ضل الماء في اللبن

BAGHAWI:1:7/r20.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r20.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r20.claim: Here ghayr means “not” and lā means “other than,” allowing coordination; when ghayr means “except,” it cannot be coordinated with lā, as in the rejected phrase “I have Abdullah except Zayd.”
BAGHAWI:1:7/r20.anchor: و( غير ) هاهنا بمعنى لا ، ولا بمعنى غير ، ولذلك جاز العطف عليها ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r21.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r21.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI:1:7/r21.claim: ʿUmar read “the path of those whom You favored,” and Baghawi links this to verses describing the Jews as recipients of anger and a people who strayed.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r21.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه " صراط من أنعمت عليهم " لأن الله تعالى حكم على اليهود بالغضب فقال : ( من لعنه الله وغضب عليه )

BAGHAWI:1:7/r22.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r22.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r22.claim: An unnamed view identifies those angered as the Jews and those astray as the Christians, citing verses on their anger and earlier deviation.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r22.anchor: وقيل المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود ، والضالون هم النصارى فقال : ( ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل )

BAGHAWI:1:7/r23.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r23.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
BAGHAWI:1:7/r23.claim: Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allah says those angered are people of innovation.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r23.anchor: وقال سهل بن عبد الله ( غير المغضوب عليهم ) بالبدعة

BAGHAWI:1:7/r24.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r24.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
BAGHAWI:1:7/r24.claim: Sahl ibn ʿAbd Allah says those astray are people who have left the Sunna.

BAGHAWI:1:7/r25.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r25.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r25.claim: The reader should say Amin after finishing al-Fatiha, separated from it by a brief pause; it may be pronounced short or long.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r25.anchor: والسنة للقارئ أن يقول بعد فراغه من قراءة الفاتحة { آمين } . مفصولا عن الفاتحة بسكتة

BAGHAWI:1:7/r26.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r26.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r26.claim: Amin means “O God, hear and answer.”

BAGHAWI:1:7/r27.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r27.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
BAGHAWI:1:7/r27.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada explain Amin as “so it is” or “so be it.”
BAGHAWI:1:7/r27.anchor: وقال ابن عباس و قتادة : معناه كذلك يكون ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r28.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r28.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI:1:7/r28.claim: Mujahid says Amin is one of God's names.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r28.anchor: وقال مجاهد : هو اسم من أسماء الله تعالى ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r29.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r29.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r29.claim: Another view calls Amin the seal of supplication.

BAGHAWI:1:7/r30.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r30.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:1:7/r30.claim: Another view says Amin is God's seal upon His servants, protecting them from afflictions like a letter's seal protects its contents.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r30.anchor: وقيل هو خاتم الله على عباده يدفع به الآفات عنهم ، كخاتم الكتاب يمنعه من الفساد

BAGHAWI:1:7/r31.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r31.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI:1:7/r31.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when the imam says the final phrase, the congregation should say Amin; imam and angels also say it, and agreement with the angels brings forgiveness of past sins. Baghawi grades it sahih.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r31.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " إذا قال الإمام غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين فقولوا آمين ،

BAGHAWI:1:7/r32.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r32.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI:1:7/r32.claim: The Prophet tells Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that al-Fatiha has no like in Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an and is the seven oft-repeated given to him; graded hasan sahih.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r32.anchor: فقال رسول الله : صلى الله عليه وسلم " والذي نفسي بيده ما أنزل في التوراة ولا في الإنجيل ولا في الزبور

BAGHAWI:1:7/r33.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r33.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:1:7/r33.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that an angel announced two lights never given to a prophet before: al-Fatiha and the closing verses of al-Baqara; every letter recited brings a gift. Graded sahih.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r33.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : " بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعنده جبريل إذ سمع نقضا من فوقه

BAGHAWI:1:7/r34.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r34.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI:1:7/r34.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying a prayer without Umm al-Qur'an is incomplete; Baghawi grades the report sahih.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r34.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم " من صلى صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم القرآن فهي خداج غير تمام "

BAGHAWI:1:7/r35.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r35.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI:1:7/r35.claim: When a Persian worshipper asks about praying behind the imam, Abu Hurayra tells him to recite al-Fatiha silently to himself.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r35.anchor: فقلت يا أبا هريرة إني أحيانا أكون وراء الإمام ؟ فغمز ذراعي وقال : اقرأ بها يا فارسي في نفسك

BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.claim: In a qudsi report, God divides prayer between Himself and His servant and answers each part of al-Fatiha; Baghawi grades it sahih.
BAGHAWI:1:7/r36.anchor: قال الله عز وجل : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ، نصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل ،

BAYDAWI:1:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r1.claim: Ṣirāṭ is an emphatic appositive explaining the first path phrase; the construction identifies the believers’ way as the straight one with force and clarity.

BAYDAWI:1:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r2.claim: One interpretation identifies those blessed with the prophets.

BAYDAWI:1:7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r3.claim: Another interpretation identifies those blessed with the Prophet Muhammad and his companions.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r3.anchor: وقيل : النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه

BAYDAWI:1:7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r4.claim: A third interpretation identifies them as the followers of Moses and Jesus before distortion and abrogation.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r4.anchor: وقيل : أصحاب موسى وعيسى عليهما الصلاة والسلام قبل التحريف والنسخ

BAYDAWI:1:7/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r5.claim: The commentary notes a variant reading of the path phrase without specifying its vocal form in this excerpt.

BAYDAWI:1:7/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r6.claim: Inʿām means conveying a blessing; niʿma originally denotes a pleasing state and is extended to what is enjoyed as blessing.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r6.anchor: والإنعام : إيصال النعمة ، وهي في الأصل الحالة

BAYDAWI:1:7/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r7.claim: Although God's blessings cannot be counted, as 16:18 says, Bayḍāwī divides them into worldly and otherworldly kinds.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r7.anchor: وإن تعدوا نعمة الله لا تحصوها

BAYDAWI:1:7/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r8.claim: Worldly blessings divide into gifts given without acquisition and blessings earned through effort.

BAYDAWI:1:7/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r9.claim: Unacquired spiritual blessings include the spirit, intellect, understanding, thought, speech, and their associated faculties.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r9.anchor: روحاني كنفخ الروح فيه وإشراقه بالعقل

BAYDAWI:1:7/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r10.claim: Unacquired bodily blessings include the body's formation, its faculties, health, and complete limbs.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r10.anchor: وجسماني كتخليق البدن والقوى الحالة فيه

BAYDAWI:1:7/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r11.claim: Acquired blessings include purifying the soul, gaining noble character, adorning the body, and attaining status and wealth.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r11.anchor: والكسبي تزكية النفس عن الرذائل وتحليتها

BAYDAWI:1:7/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r12.claim: The otherworldly blessing is forgiveness, divine approval, and an eternal place in the highest ranks with the angels.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r12.anchor: أن يغفر له ما فرط منه ويرضى عنه

BAYDAWI:1:7/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r13.claim: The verse primarily intends the final, otherworldly blessing and what leads to it, since other blessings are shared by believers and unbelievers.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r13.anchor: والمراد هو القسم الأخير وما يكون وصلة إلى نيله

BAYDAWI:1:7/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r14.claim: Ghayr can be an appositive to those blessed, or an adjective that clarifies or restricts them.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r14.anchor: بدل من { الذين } على معنى أن المنعم

BAYDAWI:1:7/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r15.claim: As a qualifying adjective, the phrase says they combine the absolute blessing of faith with freedom from wrath and error.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r15.anchor: على معنى أنهم جمعوا بين النعمة المطلقة

BAYDAWI:1:7/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r16.claim: The adjective reading works by treating the relative phrase as an indefinite, or by making ghayr definite through its contrastive genitive.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r16.anchor: إجراء الموصول مجرى النكرة إذ لم يقصد به معهود

BAYDAWI:1:7/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r17.speaker: ابن كثير
BAYDAWI:1:7/r17.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads ghayr in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in ʿalayhim, governed by anʿamta.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r17.anchor: وعن ابن كثير نصبه على الحال

BAYDAWI:1:7/r18.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r18.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r18.claim: Other parses take an implied aʿnī, or treat ghayr as an exception if blessings include both groups.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r18.anchor: إن فسر النعم بما يعم القبيلين

BAYDAWI:1:7/r19.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r19.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r19.claim: When anger is attributed to God, it denotes the final outcome or endpoint, not an emotion in God.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r19.anchor: ثوران النفس إرادة الانتقام ، فإذا أسند

BAYDAWI:1:7/r20.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r20.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r20.claim: In the second ʿalayhim phrase, the pronoun is nominative as deputy subject, unlike the first occurrence.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r20.anchor: وعليهم في محل الرفع لأنه نائب مناب الفاعل

BAYDAWI:1:7/r21.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r21.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r21.claim: The lā is an extra particle reinforcing the negation already expressed by ghayr, as in the cited grammatical examples.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r21.anchor: في غير من معنى النفي ، فكأنه قال

BAYDAWI:1:7/r22.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r22.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r22.claim: A variant reading inserts a conjunction before al-ḍāllīn.

BAYDAWI:1:7/r23.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r23.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r23.claim: Ḍalāl is departure from the sound path, whether deliberate or accidental, and ranges across a broad spectrum.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r23.anchor: عن الطريق السوي عمدا أو خطأ ، وله عرض عريض

BAYDAWI:1:7/r24.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r24.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r24.claim: One reported identification makes those under wrath the Jews, citing the description in 5:60.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r24.anchor: قيل : { المغضوب عليهم } اليهود لقوله تعالى فيهم

BAYDAWI:1:7/r25.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r25.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r25.claim: One reported identification makes those astray the Christians, citing 5:77.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r25.anchor: قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيرا

BAYDAWI:1:7/r26.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r26.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r26.claim: Bayḍāwī says a Prophetic report supports identifying the two groups as Jews and Christians; he gives no grading here.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r26.anchor: وقد روي مرفوعا ، ويتجه أن يقال

BAYDAWI:1:7/r27.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r27.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r27.claim: Bayḍāwī also finds apt a general reading: sinners fail in action and incur wrath, while those ignorant of God fail in understanding and go astray.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r27.anchor: ويتجه أن يقال : المغضوب عليهم العصاة

BAYDAWI:1:7/r28.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r28.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r28.claim: The sinner's liability to wrath is supported by 4:93, which says God is angry with the deliberate killer.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r28.anchor: والمخل بالعمل فاسق مغضوب عليه لقوله تعالى

BAYDAWI:1:7/r29.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r29.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r29.claim: The ignorant person's error is supported by 10:32: after truth, only error remains.

BAYDAWI:1:7/r30.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r30.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r30.claim: A hamza reading is noted, attributed to a dialect that avoids two consecutive quiescent sounds.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r30.anchor: على لغة من جد في الهرب من التقاء الساكنين

BAYDAWI:1:7/r31.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r31.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r31.claim: Āmīn is an imperative-like expression meaning “answer” or “grant the prayer”; it is not part of the Qur'an, by consensus.

BAYDAWI:1:7/r32.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r32.speaker: رسول الله
BAYDAWI:1:7/r32.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās asked the Prophet about āmīn; he explained it as “do it” and said it is built on fatḥ to avoid meeting two quiescent sounds.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r32.anchor: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معناه

BAYDAWI:1:7/r33.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r33.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r33.claim: The alif in āmīn may be lengthened or shortened; two poetic lines attest the forms, though their poets are unnamed.

BAYDAWI:1:7/r34.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r34.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r34.claim: It is recommended to end the sūra with āmīn, following the Prophet's report that Gabriel taught it at the end of al-Fātiḥa as a letter's seal.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r34.anchor: علمني جبريل آمين عند فراغي من قراءة الفاتحة

BAYDAWI:1:7/r35.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r35.speaker: علي
BAYDAWI:1:7/r35.claim: ʿAlī calls āmīn the seal of the Lord of the worlds, sealing a servant's supplication.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r35.anchor: قول علي رضي الله عنه : آمين خاتم رب العالمين

BAYDAWI:1:7/r36.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r36.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:1:7/r36.claim: The imam says āmīn aloud in audible prayers, based on the report that the Prophet raised his voice after al-ḍāllīn.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r36.anchor: عليه الصلاة والسلام كان إذا قرأ ولا الضالين قال آمين

BAYDAWI:1:7/r37.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r37.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI:1:7/r37.claim: A report from Abū Ḥanīfa says not to say āmīn; his better-known position is to say it quietly, as narrated from ʿAbd Allāh b. Mughaffal and Anas.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r37.anchor: عن أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه أنه لا يقوله

BAYDAWI:1:7/r38.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r38.speaker: رسول الله
BAYDAWI:1:7/r38.claim: The follower says āmīn with the imam; agreement with the angels' āmīn brings forgiveness of prior sins, according to the Prophetic report.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r38.anchor: لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام :  " إذا قال الإمام

BAYDAWI:1:7/r39.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r39.speaker: رسول الله
BAYDAWI:1:7/r39.claim: The Prophet tells Abū Hurayra that al-Fātiḥa has no equal in the Torah, Gospel, or Qur'an, and is the seven oft-repeated verses and the great Qur'an given to him.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r39.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI:1:7/r40.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r40.speaker: رسول الله
BAYDAWI:1:7/r40.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet's news of two lights granted to him alone: al-Fātiḥa and the closing verses of al-Baqara; reciting either brings a granted response.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r40.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

BAYDAWI:1:7/r41.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:1:7/r41.speaker: رسول الله
BAYDAWI:1:7/r41.claim: Ḥudhayfa b. al-Yamān reports that a child's recitation of al-ḥamdu li-llāh rabbi l-ʿālamīn caused God to lift an otherwise decreed punishment from a people for forty years.
BAYDAWI:1:7/r41.anchor: وعن حذيفة بن اليمان أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI:1:7/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r1.claim: The appositional restatement confirms that the straight way comes only through God's favor and signals that clinging to it means following His messengers.
BIQAI:1:7/r1.anchor: ثم أكد سبحانه وتعالى الإخبار بأن ذلك لن يكون إلا بإنعامه

BIQAI:1:7/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r2.claim: God's blessing reaches every existent, ally or enemy; omitting what was bestowed generalizes the blessing while concentrating the request on its special recipients.
BIQAI:1:7/r2.anchor: لكل موجود عدواً كان أو ولياً

BIQAI:1:7/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r3.claim: Suppressing the object of bestowed makes the wording shorter while expanding its meaning through generalization.
BIQAI:1:7/r3.anchor: وكان حذف المنعم به لإرادة التعميم

BIQAI:1:7/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r4.claim: The Egypt and Damascus example distinguishes coordination, which excludes the second group from the first, from ghayr, which treats the excluded wrongdoers as part of the first group.
BIQAI:1:7/r4.anchor: اتبع طريق أهل مصر مثلاً لا أهل دمشق

BIQAI:1:7/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r5.claim: Since existence itself is a blessing and everyone follows some human path, the request must mean those specially favored with God's mercy, whose opposites are then identified as a warning.
BIQAI:1:7/r5.anchor: فعرف أن المسؤول إنما هو طريق أهل النعمة

BIQAI:1:7/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r6.claim: One rejected group is destined for misery and deliberately fails in action, thereby deserving wrath.

BIQAI:1:7/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r7.claim: The other group was not destined for felicity and falls into ruin through neglect of knowledge.
BIQAI:1:7/r7.anchor: من جهة إخلاله بالعلم فصار إلى العطب

BIQAI:1:7/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r8.claim: Mentioning these groups after hope inspires fear alongside hope and clarifies that the intended blessing is the special grace given to the honored.

BIQAI:1:7/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r9.claim: The people under wrath are those whom God treats as an angry person treats the object of his anger.
BIQAI:1:7/r9.anchor: أي الذين تعاملهم معاملة الغضبان لمن وقع عليه غضبه

BIQAI:1:7/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r10.claim: Ghayr is made definite by annexation to its opposite and serves as an adjective for those who were blessed, like motion being other than rest.

BIQAI:1:7/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r11.claim: Ghayr conveys negation rather than an exception: the wording excludes those characterized by the trait from the outset and avoids suggesting a merely lesser class.

BIQAI:1:7/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r12.claim: The contrast shows the great blessing of the first group: there is no salvation without following them, and deliberate or mistaken departure brings misery, so the earnest should pursue their traces.
BIQAI:1:7/r12.anchor: وأنه لا نجاة إلا باتباعهم وأن من حاد عن سبيلهم عامداً أو مخطئاً شقي

BIQAI:1:7/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r13.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r13.claim: Al-Harali says the wrathful openly show contrariness and deliberate opposition, bringing wrath from above and hatred from below.
BIQAI:1:7/r13.anchor: قال الحرالي : { المغضوب عليهم } الذين ظهر

BIQAI:1:7/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r14.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r14.claim: Al-Harali defines the strayers as people who faced a direction of guidance and veered away without intending to do so.
BIQAI:1:7/r14.anchor: وجهوا وجهة هدى فزاغوا عنها من غير تعمد لذلك

BIQAI:1:7/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r15.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r15.claim: Al-Harali analyzes amīn as a word of resolve rooted in security, expressing confidence that the one invoked will not reject the caller.

BIQAI:1:7/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r16.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r16.claim: Only God can be called upon with this confidence, since every other being is subject to inability or obstruction.
BIQAI:1:7/r16.anchor: وهي{[288]} لا تصلح إلا لله لأن ما دونه لا ينفك عن عجز أو منع

BIQAI:1:7/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r17.claim: Amīn is a vocal form named for the imperative meaning respond.
BIQAI:1:7/r17.anchor: وهو صوت سمي به الفعل الذي هو استجب

BIQAI:1:7/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r18.claim: The ending loops back to the opening invocation of God's name: the first group gains mercy, while the two deviant groups join Satan's party and incur punishment.

BIQAI:1:7/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r19.claim: Because the Fātiḥa's order is obligatory, reversing its parts or inserting material not belonging to it invalidates prayer by disrupting the arrangement.
BIQAI:1:7/r19.anchor: الفاتحة في الصلاة لكونها واجبة في الترتيب

BIQAI:1:7/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r20.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI:1:7/r20.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī says the Qur'an's clearest pillar of inimitability lies in its arrangement and sequence.
BIQAI:1:7/r20.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : فإن القرآن معجز والركن الأبين

BIQAI:1:7/r23.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r23.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r23.claim: Having requested the noblest way, the worshipper asks for its best companions; because blessing may be worldly, he seeks protection from confused or unjust wanderers.
BIQAI:1:7/r23.anchor: ولما طلب أشرف طريق سأل أحسن رفيق فقال

BIQAI:1:7/r24.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r24.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r24.claim: The following disavowal specifies that the requested blessing is not merely worldly, asking refuge from those wandering in confusion or injustice.
BIQAI:1:7/r24.anchor: ولما كانت النعمة قد تخص الدنيوية عينها واستعاذ{[284]} من أولئك

BIQAI:1:7/r25.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r25.speaker: العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي
BIQAI:1:7/r25.claim: Al-Taftāzānī organizes all blessings into first and second creation and preservation, respectively in the transient world and the abiding afterlife.
BIQAI:1:7/r25.anchor: كما قال العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي . إلى جميع النعم فإنها ترجع إلى إيجاد وإبقاء

BIQAI:1:7/r30.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r30.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r30.claim: Al-Taftāzānī says the four later sūras that open with praise point, in sequence, to these four kinds of blessing; Biqāʿī will discuss them at their openings.
BIQAI:1:7/r30.anchor: ثم جاء التصدير بالحمد بعد الفاتحة في أربع سور

BIQAI:1:7/r31.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r31.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r31.claim: Biqāʿī says the root sense of praise turns on reaching the utmost end, entailing expansiveness, encompassing scope, and perhaps humility, satisfaction, and gratitude.
BIQAI:1:7/r31.anchor: مادته بكل ترتيب تدور على بلوغ الغاية ويلزم منه الاتساع والإحاطة والاستدارة

BIQAI:1:7/r33.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r33.speaker: author
BIQAI:1:7/r33.claim: The divine names that follow praise encompass the Qur'an's theoretical doctrines and practical rulings, so the brief Fātiḥa is the Qur'an's mother and title, whose contents the rest unfolds.
BIQAI:1:7/r33.anchor: معاني القرآن من الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية فهي أم القرآن

BIQAI:1:7/r34.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r34.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r34.claim: Al-Harali says God's entire great message is gathered in the seven oft-repeated verses, hidden beneath the Throne until the completion of creation and the final manifestation of praise through Muhammad.
BIQAI:1:7/r34.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي في مفتاح الباب المقفل لفهم القرآن المنزل في آخر الباب التاسع منه : ولننه هذه الأبواب بذكر القرآن ومحتواه على الكتب

BIQAI:1:7/r35.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r35.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r35.claim: Al-Harali maps the stages of creation's unfolding onto successive scrolls, books, and tablets: scrolls concern what changes quickly, books what endures, and tablets what lasts for a time.
BIQAI:1:7/r35.anchor: فالصحف لما يتبدل سريعاً ،   والكتاب لما يثبت ويدوم أمداً

BIQAI:1:7/r36.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r36.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r36.claim: Al-Harali assigns Torah worldly legal penalties, the Gospel principles pointing beyond them to the kingdom, and the Psalms ecstatic praise; the Qur'an includes selections from each mode.

BIQAI:1:7/r37.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r37.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r37.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an gathers these scriptural modes, perfects blessing and religion, and completes the work, citing the completion of religion and the Prophet's mission to perfect noble character.
BIQAI:1:7/r37.anchor: من جميع وجوهه ،   فصار قرآناً جامعاً

BIQAI:1:7/r38.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r38.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r38.claim: The Qur'an develops detailed material in scattered revelations, whereas the seven concise, comprehensive principles of the Mother of the Qur'an are ordered one by one, sufficient without excess or deficiency.
BIQAI:1:7/r38.anchor: أن القرآن مقصود تنزيله التفصيل والجوامع

BIQAI:1:7/r39.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r39.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r39.claim: Al-Harali sees the Fātiḥa as God's disclosure from the beginning of dominion to praise, and the servants' progress from disavowing error to the straight path; the Qur'an gathers their relation.
BIQAI:1:7/r39.anchor: من بدء الملك إلى ختم الحمد

BIQAI:1:7/r40.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r40.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r40.claim: Al-Harali describes the Qur'an's clear, glorious, generous, and wise aspects through audible verses, tested rulings, varied gifts, and the order of creation according to revelation.
BIQAI:1:7/r40.anchor: ومن كريمه وهو ما ظهرت فيه أفانين إنعامه

BIQAI:1:7/r41.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r41.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r41.claim: Al-Harali distinguishes gradual revelation that moves between conditions and rulings as tanzīl from inzāl, which descends from high to low; inzāl has no intermediaries, while tanzīl does.
BIQAI:1:7/r41.anchor: من حال إلى حال وحكم إلى حكم كان تنزيلاً

BIQAI:1:7/r42.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r42.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r42.claim: Al-Harali says Qur'anic explanation is embodied by the active exemplar in his deeds and character, while recitation is arranged according to the needs that arise.
BIQAI:1:7/r42.anchor: وبيانه حيث الإمام العامل به مظهره في أفعاله وأخلاقه كان خلقه القرآن

BIQAI:1:7/r46.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r46.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r46.claim: Al-Harali likens the seven Fātiḥa principles gathered in the Prophet's heart to one instantaneous divine command; the Qur'an is gathered in his heart, recited by his tongue, embodied in action, and revealed gradually.
BIQAI:1:7/r46.anchor: فهو جمع في قلبه ،   وقرآن على لسانه

BIQAI:1:7/r47.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r47.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r47.claim: Al-Harali links the disbelievers' demand for one-time revelation to the Qur'an's descent to the lowest heaven in a blessed night and its subsequent gradual delivery to the Prophet.
BIQAI:1:7/r47.anchor: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن

BIQAI:1:7/r48.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r48.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI:1:7/r48.claim: Al-Harali cites ʿĀʾisha's report that the Prophet's character was the Qur'an, and presents Muhammad as the Qur'an's outward form and its inner meaning embodied.
BIQAI:1:7/r48.anchor: قالت عائشة رضى الله عنها : كان خلقه القرآن

BIQAI:1:7/r49.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r49.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI:1:7/r49.claim: Al-Harali says the first three verses encompass the divine names and attributes, the final three the creatures' approach to God or estrangement from mercy, and the middle verse the bond between them.
BIQAI:1:7/r49.anchor: الآيات الثلاث الأول شاملة لكل معنى تضمنته الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى

BIQAI:1:7/r50.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:1:7/r50.speaker: أبو هريرة
BIQAI:1:7/r50.claim: In the qudsī report from the Prophet, narrated by Abū Hurayra and recorded by Muslim and the four Sunan collections, God says the guidance request belongs to the servant and the servant receives what he asks; no grading is stated.
BIQAI:1:7/r50.anchor: الحديث القدسي الذي رواه مسلم في صحيحه وأصحاب السنن الأربعة عن أبي هريرة

DURR:1:1/r118.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:1/r118.speaker: الله
DURR:1:1/r118.claim: Those favored are prophets and believers blessed with Islam and prophethood.
DURR:1:1/r118.anchor: { صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم } يعني به النبيين والمؤمنين الذين أنعم الله عليهم بالإسلام والنبوة

DURR:1:1/r119.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:1/r119.speaker: الله
DURR:1:1/r119.claim: Those under wrath are identified as Jews, with 5:60 cited.
DURR:1:1/r119.anchor: { غير المغضوب عليهم } يقول : أرشدنا غير دين هؤلاء الذين غضبت عليهم ، وهم اليهود

DURR:1:1/r120.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:1/r120.speaker: الله
DURR:1:1/r120.claim: The astray are identified as Christians, led astray after guidance; the report cites 5:60.
DURR:1:1/r120.anchor: { ولا الضالين } وهم النصارى ، أضلهم الله بعد الهدى ، فبمعصيتهم غضب الله عليهم ( وجعل منهم القردة والخنازير وعبد الطاغوت أولئك شر مكانا ) ( المائدة الآية 60 )

DURR:1:1/r121.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:1/r121.speaker: النبي
DURR:1:1/r121.claim: The Prophet says congregants should say amin when the imam says wa-la al-dallin, and God will love them.
DURR:1:1/r121.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : فإذا قال الإمام { ولا الضالين } فقولوا { آمين } يحبكم الله .

DURR:1:3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:3/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR:1:3/r3.claim: In Qatada's sequential gloss, the Day of Recompense is when creatures are repaid; the worship-prayer is what people should say and directs them to God; the straight path is named, the favored are prophets, the objects of anger are Jews, and the astray are Christians.
DURR:1:3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قول الله { الحمد لله رب العالمين } قال : ما وصف من خلقه . وفي قوله { الرحمن الرحيم } قال : مدح نفسه { ملك يوم الدين }

DURR:1:7/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR:1:7/r1.claim: Umar read “ṣirāṭ man anʿamta ʿalayhim” and repeated “ghayr” before “al-ḍāllīn.”
DURR:1:7/r1.anchor: من طرق عمر بن الخطاب .   أنه كان يقرأ { صراط من أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين } .

DURR:1:7/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR:1:7/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr used the same reading in prayer.
DURR:1:7/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير قرأ { صراط من أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين } في الصلاة .

DURR:1:7/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR:1:7/r3.claim: Al-Hasan read with kasra on hāʾ and mīm and an added yāʾ.
DURR:1:7/r3.anchor: عن الحسن أنه كان يقرأ { عليهمي } بكسر الهاء والميم ،   وإثبات الياء .

DURR:1:7/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r4.speaker: الأعرج
DURR:1:7/r4.claim: Al-Aʿraj read with ḍamma on hāʾ and mīm and an added wāw.
DURR:1:7/r4.anchor: عن الأعرج أنه كان يقرأ { عليهمو } بضم الهاء والميم ،   وإلحاق الواو .

DURR:1:7/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير
DURR:1:7/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr read with kasra on hāʾ, ḍamma on mīm, and an added wāw.
DURR:1:7/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن كثير أنه كان يقرأ { أنعمت عليهمو } بكسر الهاء وضم الميم مع إلحاق الواو .

DURR:1:7/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r6.speaker: ابن اسحق
DURR:1:7/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq read hāʾ and mīm with ḍamma, without adding a wāw.
DURR:1:7/r6.anchor: عن ابن اسحق أنه قرأ { عليهم } بضم الهاء والميم من غير إلحاق واو .

DURR:1:7/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r7.speaker: عكرمة والأسود
DURR:1:7/r7.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Aswad read “ṣirāṭ man anʿamta ʿalayhim” and repeated “ghayr.”
DURR:1:7/r7.anchor: عن إبراهيم قال : كان عكرمة والأسود يقرآنها { صراط من أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين } .

DURR:1:7/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:1:7/r8.claim: Abū Hurayra identifies the phrase as the sixth verse.
DURR:1:7/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال { أنعمت عليهم } الآية السادسة .

DURR:1:7/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:7/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the favored path as that of obedient worshippers among angels, prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous.
DURR:1:7/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم } يقول : طريق من أنعمت عليهم من الملائكة ،

DURR:1:7/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:7/r10.claim: In another report, Ibn ʿAbbās glosses those favored as believers.
DURR:1:7/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله { صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم } قال : المؤمنين .

DURR:1:7/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r11.speaker: أبو زيد
DURR:1:7/r11.claim: Abū Zayd identifies those favored as the Prophet and those with him.
DURR:1:7/r11.anchor: عن أبي زيد في قوله { صراط الذين } قال : النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن معه .

DURR:1:7/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r12.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
DURR:1:7/r12.claim: Al-Rabīʿ b. Anas identifies the favored as prophets, those under wrath as Jews, and the astray as Christians.
DURR:1:7/r12.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس في قوله { صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم } قال : النبيون { غير المغضوب عليهم } قال : اليهود

DURR:1:7/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r13.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:1:7/r13.claim: Mujāhid identifies those under wrath as Jews and the astray as Christians.
DURR:1:7/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد { غير المغضوب عليهم } قال : اليهود { ولا الضالين } قال : النصارى .

DURR:1:7/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR:1:7/r14.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr identifies the objects of wrath and the astray as Jews and Christians.
DURR:1:7/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير { غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين } قال : اليهود والنصارى .

DURR:1:7/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r15.claim: At Wādī al-Qurā, the Prophet identified the objects of wrath as Jews and the astray as Christians; ʿAbd Allāh b. Shaqīq reports the exchange.
DURR:1:7/r15.anchor: وسأله رجل من بني العين فقال : من المغضوب عليهم يا رسول الله ؟ قال : اليهود قال : فمن الضالون ؟ قال : النصارى

DURR:1:7/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r16.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r16.claim: During the siege of Wādī al-Qurā, the Prophet identified one group as Jews under wrath and the other as astray Christians.
DURR:1:7/r16.anchor: قال : هؤلاء { المغضوب عليهم } يعني اليهود قال : يا رسول الله فمن هؤلاء الطائفة الأخرى ؟

DURR:1:7/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r17.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR:1:7/r17.claim: Abū Dharr reports asking the Prophet, who answered that those under wrath are Jews and the astray are Christians.
DURR:1:7/r17.anchor: عبد الله بن شقيق عن أبي ذر قال

DURR:1:7/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r18.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r18.claim: A man from Banū Balʿīn and his cousin asked the Prophet at Wādī al-Qurā about the groups; he identified Jews and Christians.
DURR:1:7/r18.anchor: أنه قال  " أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بوادي القرى فقلت : من هؤلاء عندك ؟

DURR:1:7/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r19.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r19.claim: Ismāʿīl b. Abī Khālid transmits the Prophet’s identification of Jews under wrath and Christians astray.
DURR:1:7/r19.anchor: عن اسماعيل بن أبي خالد  " أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال { المغضوب عليهم } اليهود { والضالون } هم النصارى "

DURR:1:7/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r20.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
DURR:1:7/r20.claim: ʿAdī b. Ḥātim reports the Prophet’s identification of the objects of wrath as Jews and the astray as Christians; al-Tirmidhī graded it ḥasan.
DURR:1:7/r20.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم قال : قال رسول الله

DURR:1:7/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r21.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r21.claim: The Prophet rebuked al-Shurayd for sitting with his left hand behind his back, calling it the posture of those under wrath.
DURR:1:7/r21.anchor: عن الشريد قال :  " مر بي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا جالس هكذا ،   وقد وضعت يدي اليسرى خلف ظهري

DURR:1:7/r22.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r22.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:1:7/r22.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies those under wrath as Jews and the astray as Christians.
DURR:1:7/r22.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال { المغضوب عليهم } اليهود و{ الضالين } النصارى .

DURR:1:7/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r24.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
DURR:1:7/r24.claim: Ibn Abī Ḥātim knows of no exegetical disagreement identifying those under wrath as Jews and the astray as Christians.
DURR:1:7/r24.anchor: قال ابن أبي حاتم : لا أعلم خلافا بين المفسرين في تفسير { المغضوب عليهم } باليهود { والضالين } بالنصارى .

DURR:1:7/r25.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r25.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r25.claim: Abū Maysara reports that Gabriel instructed the Prophet to say Āmīn at al-Fātiḥa’s final phrase, and the Prophet did.
DURR:1:7/r25.anchor: عن أبي ميسرة قال : لما أقرأ جبريل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاتحة الكتاب فبلغ { ولا الضالين } قال :  " قل آمين

DURR:1:7/r26.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r26.speaker: وائل بن حجر
DURR:1:7/r26.claim: Wāʾil b. Ḥujr heard the Prophet say Āmīn after al-Fātiḥa’s ending, prolonging his voice.

DURR:1:7/r27.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r27.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r27.claim: Wāʾil b. Ḥujr also heard the Prophet say “Lord, forgive me” and Āmīn after al-Fātiḥa.
DURR:1:7/r27.anchor: عن وائل بن حجر  " أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين قال { غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين } قال : رب اغفر لي { آمين }

DURR:1:7/r28.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r28.speaker: وائل بن حجر
DURR:1:7/r28.claim: Wāʾil b. Ḥujr reports seeing the Prophet say Āmīn three times after al-Fātiḥa in prayer.

DURR:1:7/r29.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r29.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r29.claim: ʿAlī reports hearing the Prophet say Āmīn after al-Fātiḥa’s final phrase.
DURR:1:7/r29.anchor: عن علي " سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قال { ولا الضالين } قال { آمين }

DURR:1:7/r30.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r30.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
DURR:1:7/r30.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet instructing congregants to say Āmīn at the imam’s ending, promising God’s response.
DURR:1:7/r30.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال : قال رسول الله

DURR:1:7/r31.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r31.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:1:7/r31.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that agreement with the angels’ Āmīn after the imam brings forgiveness of past sins.
DURR:1:7/r31.anchor: عن أبي هريرة  " أن رسول الله

DURR:1:7/r32.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r32.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:1:7/r32.claim: A good-chain report says congregants’ Āmīn meets that of heaven and earth; the one omitting it is like a soldier whose share is missed.
DURR:1:7/r32.anchor: بسند جيد عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله

DURR:1:7/r33.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r33.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r33.claim: Abū Zuhayr al-Numayrī, a Companion, likens Āmīn sealing supplication to a stamp; Abū Dāwūd grades the report ḥasan.
DURR:1:7/r33.anchor: عن أبي زهير النميري وكان من الصحابة أنه كان إذا دعا الرجل بدعاء قال : اختمه { بآمين } فإن آمين مثل الطابع

DURR:1:7/r34.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r34.speaker: عائشة
DURR:1:7/r34.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Jews envied Muslims for nothing as much as saying Āmīn.
DURR:1:7/r34.anchor: عن عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR:1:7/r35.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r35.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:7/r35.claim: A weak report says Jews envied Muslims for Āmīn and urges saying it often.
DURR:1:7/r35.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله

DURR:1:7/r36.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r36.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:1:7/r36.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Jews envy spreading greetings, prayer rows, and Āmīn.
DURR:1:7/r36.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله

DURR:1:7/r37.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r37.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
DURR:1:7/r37.claim: Muʿādh b. Jabal reports that Jews envy returning greetings, prayer rows, and Āmīn behind the imam in obligatory prayer.
DURR:1:7/r37.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل  " أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : إن اليهود قوم حسد

DURR:1:7/r38.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r38.speaker: أنس
DURR:1:7/r38.claim: Anas reports that Muslims received greetings, prayer in rows, and Āmīn as gifts; Moses supplicated while Aaron affirmed.
DURR:1:7/r38.anchor: عن أنس قال : قال رسول الله

DURR:1:7/r39.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r39.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:1:7/r39.claim: A weak report calls Āmīn the seal of the Lord of the worlds upon believers’ tongues.
DURR:1:7/r39.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم  " آمين خاتم رب العالمين على لسان عباده المؤمنين "

DURR:1:7/r40.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r40.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:7/r40.claim: Through al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn ʿAbbās says Āmīn means “Lord, do it.”
DURR:1:7/r40.anchor: عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال  " قلت يا رسول الله ما معنى آمين ؟ قال : رب افعل "

DURR:1:7/r41.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r41.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:1:7/r41.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits the same gloss from Ibn ʿAbbās.
DURR:1:7/r41.anchor: من طريق الكلبي عن ابن صالح عن ابن عباس .   مثله .

DURR:1:7/r42.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r42.speaker: هلال بن يساف ومجاهد
DURR:1:7/r42.claim: Hilāl b. Yasāf and Mujāhid say Āmīn is one of God’s names.
DURR:1:7/r42.anchor: عن هلال بن يساف ومجاهد قالا { آمين } اسم من أسماء الله .

DURR:1:7/r43.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r43.speaker: حكيم بن جبير
DURR:1:7/r43.claim: Ḥakīm b. Jubayr likewise says Āmīn is one of God’s names.

DURR:1:7/r44.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r44.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
DURR:1:7/r44.claim: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī recommended saying “O God, forgive me” and Āmīn at al-Fātiḥa’s end.
DURR:1:7/r44.anchor: عن إبراهيم النخعي قال : كان يستحب إذا قال الإمام { غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين } أن يقال : اللهم اغفر لي { آمين } .

DURR:1:7/r45.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r45.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:1:7/r45.claim: Mujāhid advised asking God for Paradise and refuge from the Fire at al-Fātiḥa’s end.
DURR:1:7/r45.anchor: عن مجاهد قال : إذا قال الإمام { غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين } فقل : اللهم إني أسألك الجنة وأعوذ بك من النار .

DURR:1:7/r46.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r46.speaker: الربيع بن خيثم
DURR:1:7/r46.claim: Al-Rabīʿ b. Khuthaym said one may use any supplication at this point.
DURR:1:7/r46.anchor: عن الربيع بن خيثم قال : إذا قال الإمام { غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين } فاستعن من الدعاء ما شئت .

DURR:1:7/r47.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r47.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR:1:7/r47.claim: Ismāʿīl b. Muslim reports Ubayy’s reading with “ghayr” before both groups, then Āmīn and the basmala.
DURR:1:7/r47.anchor: عن إسماعيل بن مسلم قال : في حرف أبي بن كعب { غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين آمين بسم الله }

DURR:1:7/r48.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r48.speaker: الحسن
DURR:1:7/r48.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses Āmīn as “O God, answer.”
DURR:1:7/r48.anchor: قال إسماعيل : وكان الحسن إذا سئل عن { آمين } ما تفسيرها ؟ قال : هو اللهم استجب .

DURR:1:7/r49.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:1:7/r49.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:1:7/r49.claim: Anas reports that saying Āmīn after the basmala and al-Fātiḥa prompts the angels in heaven to seek forgiveness for the reciter.
DURR:1:7/r49.anchor: عن أنس قال  " قال رسول الله

ABUDAWUD:821/r2.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.claim: In a hadith qudsi transmitted by Abu Hurayra, God divides al-Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise and glorification receive divine responses, worship is mutual, and the guidance petition belongs to the servant.
ABUDAWUD:821/r2.anchor: قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى قَسَمْتُ الصَّلاَةَ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ عَبْدِي

ABUDAWUD:779/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:779/r1.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
ABUDAWUD:779/r1.claim: Samura reports two pauses in the Prophet’s prayer, at the opening takbir and after al-Fatiha’s closing words; Imran disputed his memory, but Ubayy ibn Kaʿb affirmed that Samura had preserved it.
ABUDAWUD:779/r1.anchor: فَحَدَّثَ سَمُرَةُ بْنُ جُنْدُبٍ، أَنَّهُ حَفِظَ عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم سَكْتَتَيْنِ

ABUDAWUD:780/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:780/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABUDAWUD:780/r1.claim: Qatada explains that one pause was when prayer began and another after recitation, adding a clarification associating the latter with saying al-Fatiha’s final words.
ABUDAWUD:780/r1.anchor: قُلْنَا لِقَتَادَةَ مَا هَاتَانِ السَّكْتَتَانِ قَالَ إِذَا دَخَلَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَإِذَا فَرَغَ مِنَ الْقِرَاءَةِ

ABUDAWUD:934/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:934/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUDAWUD:934/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that when the Prophet recited al-Fatiha’s closing words, he said Amin loudly enough for the first row to hear.
ABUDAWUD:934/r1.anchor: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا تَلاَ

ABUDAWUD:935/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:935/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي هريرة
ABUDAWUD:935/r1.claim: The Prophet instructs followers to say Amin after the imam recites these words; when their utterance coincides with the angels’, their previous sins are forgiven.
ABUDAWUD:935/r1.anchor: أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ

ABUDAWUD:972/r1.author: ABUDAWUD
ABUDAWUD:972/r1.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUDAWUD:972/r1.claim: Abu Musa relays the Prophet’s prayer instructions: align rows, follow the imam’s takbir, bowing, and prostration; say Amin after 1:7 and praise God after the imam’s praise; the taught tahiyyat has an Ahmad transmission with two omissions.

BUKHARI:782/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:782/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
BUKHARI:782/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet instructing worshippers to say amin after the imam recites this close of al-Fatiha; agreement with the angels brings forgiveness for past sins.
BUKHARI:782/r1.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ إِذَا قَالَ الإِمَامُ ‏{‏غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ

BUKHARI:4475/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4475/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
BUKHARI:4475/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet instructing worshippers to say amin after the imam recites this close of al-Fatiha; agreement with the angels brings forgiveness for past sins.
BUKHARI:4475/r1.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ إِذَا قَالَ الإِمَامُ ‏{‏غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ

DURR-FULL:v1p12/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r2.speaker: أم سلمة
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet recited the Fātiḥa including the basmala and called it seven verses.
DURR-FULL:v1p12/r2.anchor: عن أم سلمة قالت قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم {بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين

DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.speaker: الله عز وجل
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.claim: In Abū Hurayra's report, God says the prayer is divided between Him and His servant: the opening praise is His, the middle is shared, and the servant receives what he asks in the remainder.
DURR-FULL:v1p18/r2.anchor: فإني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: قال الله عز وجل قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين

DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.speaker: ربكم
DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.claim: The continuation of Ubayy b. Kaʿb's report assigns the first three Fātiḥa verses to God, the middle verse to both, and the final three to the servant; worship is the servant's and aid comes from God.
DURR-FULL:v1p19/r1.anchor: ثلاث لي وثلاث لك وواحدة بيني وبينك

DURR-FULL:v1p10/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r1.speaker: ورقة
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r1.claim: A first-revelation account has Khadīja praise Muhammad's trustworthiness, kinship, and honesty; Waraqa tells him to stand when the call comes, then affirms him as a prophet on Moses's pattern, foretold by Jesus, after he recites the Fātiḥa and shahāda.
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r1.anchor: فقال له ورقة: أبشر ثم أبشر فإني أشهد أنك الذي بشر به ابن مريم وأنك على مثل ناموس موسى وأنك نبي مرسل

DURR-FULL:v1p10/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r2.speaker: رجل من بني سلمة
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r2.claim: A man of Banū Salima reports that after the clan and ʿAmr b. al-Jamūḥ's sons accepted Islam, ʿAmr's wife asked him to hear his son's recitation; he praised the Fātiḥa as beautiful and asked if all the man's words were like it.
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r2.anchor: عن رجل من بني سلمة قال: لما أسلم بني سلمة وأسلم ولد عمرو بن الجموح قالت امرأة عمرو له

DURR-FULL:v1p10/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r3.claim: Mujāhid transmits from Abū Hurayra that Iblīs groaned when the Fātiḥa descended.
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r3.anchor:
عن أبي هريرة
أن إبليس رن حين أنزلن فاتحة الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v1p10/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r4.claim: Mujāhid says the Fātiḥa was revealed in Medina; multiple transmitted routes repeat this view.
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: نزلت فاتحة الكتاب بالمدينة

DURR-FULL:v1p10/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r5.claim: Qatāda instead says the Fātiḥa was revealed in Mecca, differing from Mujāhid's Medinan view.
DURR-FULL:v1p10/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قال: نزلت فاتحة الكتاب بمكة

IBNASHUR:1:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:2/r5.claim: The guided path includes a desire to take the people favored by God as a good example.
IBNASHUR:1:2/r5.anchor: الرابع الرغبة في التحلي بالأسوة الحسنة بما تضمنه { صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم }

IBNASHUR:1:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:2/r6.claim: The supplication seeks safety from explicit misguidance, represented by those under wrath.
IBNASHUR:1:2/r6.anchor: الخامس التهمم بالسلامة من الضلال الصريح بما تضمنه { غير المغضوب عليهم }

IBNASHUR:1:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:2/r7.claim: It also seeks protection from thought becoming confused by falsehood disguised as truth, which is the further form of misguidance.
IBNASHUR:1:2/r7.anchor: السادس التهمم بسلامة تفكيرهم من الاختلاط بشبهات الباطل المموَّه بصورة الحق وهو المسمى بالضلال

IBNASHUR:1:6/r47.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:6/r47.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:6/r47.claim: The comprehensive reading makes the transition to the following request, for the path excluding those under anger or astray, apt to the context.

IBNASHUR:1:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r1.claim: He parses “the path of those You favored” as either an appositive or explanatory apposition for “the straight path.”
IBNASHUR:1:7/r1.anchor: بدل أو عطف بيان من { الصراط المستقيم } ، وإنما جاء نظم الآية بأسلوب الإبدال أو البيان

IBNASHUR:1:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r2.claim: The prayer first asks for a clear, easy way to salvation; identifying it as the way of the favored adds a further honor.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r2.anchor: المقصود من الطلب ابتداء هو كون المهدى إليه وسيلة للنجاة واضحة سمحة سهلة

IBNASHUR:1:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r3.claim: The appositive restates the path generally and then specifies it, strengthening its meaning through a repetition comparable to emphasis.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r3.anchor: ما في أسلوب الإبدال من الإجمال المعقب بالتفصيل ليتمكن معنى الصراط للمطلوب فضل تمكن

IBNASHUR:1:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r4.claim: He finds no meaningful superiority between parsing the phrase as a matching appositive and as explanatory apposition; grammarians offer no decisive semantic distinction.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r4.anchor: واعتبار البدلية مساو لاعتباره عطف بيان لا مزية لأحدهما على الآخر خلافا لمن حاول التفاضل بينهما

IBNASHUR:1:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR:1:7/r5.claim: The author reads al-Zamakhsharī’s account as finding emphasis in the apposition’s doubling and repetition of wording and syntactic government.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r5.anchor: قال في « الكشاف » : « فإن قلت ما فائدة البدل ؟ قلت فائدته التوكيد لما فيه من التثنية والتكرير »

IBNASHUR:1:7/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r6.claim: Repeating a name before attaching its intended complement makes the named subject feel cherished; he illustrates this with Qurʾānic repetitions and al-Aḥwaṣ’s repeated verb.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r6.anchor: وإن إعادة الاسم في البدل أو البيان لِيُبنى عليه ما يُراد تعلقه بالاسم الأول أسلوبٌ بهيج من الكلام البليغ

IBNASHUR:1:7/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r7.speaker: ابن جني
IBNASHUR:1:7/r7.claim: Ibn Jinnī explains that repeating a verb is acceptable when a complement attached to the second occurrence adds new meaning; he cites al-Aḥwaṣ’s line.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r7.anchor: قال ابن جني في « شرح مشكل الحماسة » عند قول الأحوص :

IBNASHUR:1:7/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r8.claim: He cannot explain Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī’s objection to parsing “they led them astray” as an apposition; perhaps Abū ʿAlī instead took it as a new sentence.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r8.anchor: قلت ولم يتضح توجيه امتناع أبي علي فلعله امتنع من اعتبار { أغويناهم } بدلا من { أغوينا } وجعله استئنافا

IBNASHUR:1:7/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r9.claim: The relative description of the favored and the attribution of favor to God honor them in contrast with the two rejected groups.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r9.anchor: وفي استحضار المنعم عليهم بطريق الموصول ، وإسناد فعل الإنعام عليهم إلى ضمير الجلالة ، تنويه بشأنهم

IBNASHUR:1:7/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r10.speaker: الشيخ الجد
IBNASHUR:1:7/r10.claim: The author’s grandfather applied the generosity appeal here to the Prophetic supplication, “as You blessed Abraham.”
IBNASHUR:1:7/r10.anchor: كما قرره الشيخ الجد قدس الله سره في قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم « كما صليتَ على إبراهيم »

IBNASHUR:1:7/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r11.claim: Asking to join the favored in rank also implies emulating the means by which they rose; it prepares disavowal of the other groups with hope and seeking refuge.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r11.anchor: مع ما في ذلك من التعريض بطلب أن يكونوا لاحقين في مرتبة الهدى بأولئك المنعم عليهم

IBNASHUR:1:7/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r12.claim: Niʿma derives from naʿīm, comfort, ease of living, what suits a person, and luxury; its verb has the patterns of samiʿa, naṣara, and ḍaraba.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r12.anchor: والنعمة بالكسر وبالفتح مشتقة من النعيم وهو راحة العيش وملائم الإنسان والترفه

IBNASHUR:1:7/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r13.claim: The noun can denote a good condition; its kasra form marks a state, and its scope expanded from sensory pleasures to beneficial non-sensory goods.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r13.anchor: والنعمة الحالة الحسنة لأن بناء الفعلة بالكسر للهيئات ومتعلق النعمة اللذات الحسية

IBNASHUR:1:7/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r14.claim: The requested favors are complete goods unspoiled by harm or a bad end, encompassing pure worldly benefits and, especially, benefits of the afterlife.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r14.anchor: فالمراد من النعمة في قوله : { الذين أنعمت عليهم } النعمةُ التي لم يَشُبْها ما يكدرها ولا تكون عاقبتها سُوأَى

IBNASHUR:1:7/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r15.claim: These favors include worldly gifts and achievements, bodily and spiritual goods, and afterlife rewards; their central substance is guidance, including wise use of gifted goods.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r15.anchor: فيشمل النعم الدنيوية الموهوبيَّ منها والكسبيَّ ، والرُّوحانيَّ والجثمانيَّ ، ويشمل النعم الأخروية

IBNASHUR:1:7/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r16.claim: The favored are recipients of complete favor, so their path fittingly explains the straight path: guidance itself is a blessing, and they were guided to it.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r16.anchor: فالمراد من المنعم عليهم الذين أفيضت عليهم النعم الكاملة ولا تخفى تمام المناسبة بين المنعم عليهم وبين المهديين

IBNASHUR:1:7/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r17.claim: One reading takes the favored as the best people of earlier communities, especially prophets and messengers; Islam answers the prayer by gathering and surpassing the sound guidance of prior laws.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r17.anchor: والذين أنعم الله عليهم هم خيار الأمم السابقة من الرسل والأنبياء الذين حصلت لهم النعمة الكاملة

IBNASHUR:1:7/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r18.claim: He also considers the favored to be prophets and messengers, whose state was fuller than that of their peoples; Jacob enjoined his sons to die as Muslims.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r18.anchor: أو المراد من المنعم عليهم الأنبياء والرسل فإنهم كانوا على حالة أكمل مما كان عليه أممهم

IBNASHUR:1:7/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r19.claim: Earlier communities were not all able to bear the fullest ideal; prophets nevertheless kept that ideal, as with abstaining from even non-intoxicating wine, later forbidden to this whole community.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r19.anchor: فقد كان القدر غير المسكر منه مباحا وإنما يحرم السكر أو لا يحرم أصلا غير أن الأنبياء لم يكونوا يتعاطون القليل

IBNASHUR:1:7/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r20.claim: Whether the favored means prophets, their best followers, or earlier Muslims, the request is for a complete path suited to guidance available in each age.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r20.anchor: فسواء فسرنا المنعم عليهم بالأنبياء أو بأفضل أتباعهم أو المسلمين السابقين فالمقصد الهداية إلى صراط كامل

IBNASHUR:1:7/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r21.claim: Under each account of the favored, the request for guidance has the same possible force explained for the preceding verse: attainment, increase, or continuance.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r21.anchor: والقول في المطلوب من { اهدنا } على هذه التقادير كلها كالقول فيما تقدم من كون { اهدنا } لطلب الحصول أو الزيادة أو الدوام

IBNASHUR:1:7/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r22.claim: The prayer discounts benefits that are not ultimately pure: unbelievers enjoy real worldly gifts, but these bring anxiety about their end and punishment in the afterlife; the scholarly dispute over calling them favored is fruitless.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r22.anchor: والكافر منعم عليه بما لا يمترى في ذلك ولكنها نعم تحفها آلام الفكرة في سوء العاقبة ويعقبها عذاب الآخرة

IBNASHUR:1:7/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r23.speaker: القراء العشرة
IBNASHUR:1:7/r23.claim: All ten readers pronounce ghayr in the genitive; syntactically it may modify the favored or stand in apposition, with the author preferring the adjectival reading.
