IBNASHUR:1:7/r23.anchor: كلمة غير مجرورة باتفاق القراء العشرة ، وهي صفة للذين أنعمت عليهم ، أو بدل منه والوصف والبدلية سواء في المقصود

IBNASHUR:1:7/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r24.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r24.claim: He prefers treating ghayr as an adjective: its descriptive sense outweighs apposition, which conventionally names the same entity as its antecedent.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r24.anchor: وإنما قدم في « الكشاف » بيان وجه البدلية لاختصار الكلام عليها ليفضي إلى الكلام على الوصفية

IBNASHUR:1:7/r25.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r25.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r25.claim: Although ghayr is usually indefinite, it can describe this relative phrase because “those You favored” denotes no one specified group and is generic in sense.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r25.anchor: فكان في المعنى كالنكرة وإن كان لفظه لفظ المعرفة فلذلك عرف بمثله لفظا ومعنى ، وهو { غير المغضوب }

IBNASHUR:1:7/r26.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r26.speaker: ابن هشام عن ابن السراج والسيرافي
IBNASHUR:1:7/r26.claim: Ibn Hishām attributes to Ibn al-Sarrāj and al-Sīrāfī the account that ghayr becomes definite by negating a unique opposite; Ibn al-Ḥājib selects it for 4:95, and the author sees its result as close to the other account.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r26.anchor: هكذا نقل ابن هشام عن ابن السراج والسيرافي وهو الذي اختاره ابن الحاجب في أماليه على قوله تعالى : { غير أولي الضرر }

IBNASHUR:1:7/r27.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r27.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR:1:7/r27.claim: Sībawayh treats ghayr like an active participle meaning “different,” and similarly classifies mithl, siwā, and ḥasb; it becomes definite when permanence is intended.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r27.anchor: ونقل عن سيبوبه أن غيراً إنما لم تتعرف لأنها بمعنى المغاير فهي كاسم الفاعل

IBNASHUR:1:7/r28.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r28.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r28.claim: The qualification seeks refuge from communities once guided who later corrupted understanding, disobeyed, privileged worldly desires, or failed to preserve their guidance.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r28.anchor: ومن غرض وصف { الذين أنعمت عليهم } بأنهم { غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين } التعوذ مما عرض لأمم

IBNASHUR:1:7/r29.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r29.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r29.claim: The groups are broader than Jews and Christians: the first exemplifies deliberate religious rebellion, the second losing the way through misunderstanding; this reading makes the prayer meaningful after Islam superseded their religions.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r29.anchor: وليس يلزم اختصاص أول الوصفين باليهود والثاني بالنصارى فإن في الأمم أمثالهم

IBNASHUR:1:7/r30.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r30.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r30.claim: He says their earlier error was not yet deliberate and had not incurred divine anger; Jews exemplify the first group and Christians the second, but neither label is exclusive.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r30.anchor: والظاهر أنهم لم يحق عليهم غضب الله قبل الإسلام لأنهم ضلوا عن غير تعمد فلم يسبق غضب الله عليهم قديما

IBNASHUR:1:7/r31.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r31.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r31.claim: Adding the second negation advances from refuge against the graver fate to the lesser: escaping anger-inducing error does not cover lesser misguidance; the order also suits the verse endings.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r31.anchor: ارتقاء في التعوذ من شر سوء العاقبة لأن التعوذ من الضلال الذي جلب لأصحابه غضب الله لا يغني عن التعوذ

IBNASHUR:1:7/r32.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r32.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r32.claim: Human anger is a psychic response to what displeases, producing aversion and harsh treatment; revenge may follow but is not essential, contrary to those who make it definitional.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r32.anchor: والذي يظهر لي أن إرادة الانتقام ليست من لوازم ماهية الغضب بحيث لا تنفك عنه ولكنها قد تكون من آثاره

IBNASHUR:1:7/r33.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r33.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r33.claim: Because literal anger entails change, which cannot apply to God, the attribution means its consequence—punishment, humiliation, or worldly exclusion—or a representational metaphor.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r33.anchor: فقد وجب على المؤمن صرف إسناد الغضب إلى الله عن معناه الحقيقي

IBNASHUR:1:7/r34.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r34.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r34.claim: Early generations often left ambiguous attributes uninterpreted to focus on practice; later scholars used sound Arabic-based interpretation to answer false claims and clarify doctrine.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r34.anchor: وكان السلف في القرن الأول ومنتصف القرن الثاني يمسكون عن تأويل هذه المتشابهات

IBNASHUR:1:7/r35.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r35.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r35.claim: Divine anger is God’s treatment of those who oppose guidance, ranging up to the lasting punishment of polytheists and hypocrites; dislike is lesser, and both differ from creative will.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r35.anchor: فغضبُ الله تعالى على العموم يرجع إلى معاملته الحائدين عن هديه العاصين لأوامره ويترتب عليه الانتقام وهو مراتب

IBNASHUR:1:7/r36.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r36.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR:1:7/r36.claim: A hadith says God dislikes gossip, excessive questioning, and idle talk; the author uses it to distinguish dislike from anger.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r36.anchor: فقد ورد في الحديث : « ويكره لكم قيل وقال وكثرة السؤال » ، ويقابلهما الرضى والمحبة

IBNASHUR:1:7/r37.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r37.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r37.claim: Ethicists treat anger as the root of courage within the primary virtues; balanced force yields courage, while excess produces rashness and rancor and deficiency produces cowardice.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r37.anchor: واعلم أن الغضب عند حكماء الأخلاق مبدأ من مجموع الأخلاق الثلاثة الأصلية التي يعبر عن جميعها بالعدالة وهي : الحكمة والعفة والشجاعة

IBNASHUR:1:7/r38.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r38.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR:1:7/r38.claim: When a man asked for advice, the Prophet repeatedly answered, “Do not become angry”; the author applies this to anger for oneself, which leads to injustice.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r38.anchor: ولذلك كان من جوامع كلم النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم " أن رجلا قال له أوصني قال : لا تغضب فكرر مرارا فقال : لا تغضب " رواه الترمذي

IBNASHUR:1:7/r39.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r39.speaker: بعض ملوك الفرس
IBNASHUR:1:7/r39.claim: An unnamed Persian king said his reign endured because he punished according to the offense rather than according to anger.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r39.anchor: وسئل بعض ملوك الفرس بم دام ملككم ؟ فقال : لأنا نعاقب على قدر الذنب لا على قدر الغضب .

IBNASHUR:1:7/r40.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r40.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR:1:7/r40.claim: The Prophet did not become angry for himself, but became angry for God when a divine sanctity was violated; the author approves anger used to protect public and religious interests.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r40.anchor: وقد ورد أن النبيء كان لا يغضب لنفسه فإذا انتهكت حرمة من حرمات الله غضب لله .

IBNASHUR:1:7/r41.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r41.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r41.claim: Lā coordinates the straying with the objects of ghayr; contrary to the reported view of Makki ibn Abī Ṭālib, it is not needed to prevent attachment to the favored.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r41.anchor: قال مكي ابن أبي طالب إن دخول ( لا ) لدفع توهم عطف ( الضالين ) على

IBNASHUR:1:7/r42.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r42.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r42.claim: He takes the extra lā as verbal reinforcement of negation after ghayr, following Arabic coordination under negation, as in 5:19.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r42.anchor: فالحق أن ( لا ) مزيدة لتأكيد النفي المستفاد من لفظ ( غير ) على طريقة العرب في المعطوف على ما في حيز النفي

IBNASHUR:1:7/r43.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r43.speaker: السيد
IBNASHUR:1:7/r43.claim: Al-Sayyid says lā prevents the mistaken inference that only the combined group is excluded, allowing one group to remain affirmed; the author distinguishes this from the semantic extra lā in 7:12.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r43.anchor: وقال السيد في « حواشي الكشاف » لئلا يتوهم أن المنفي هو المجموع فيجوز ثبوت أحدهما ، ولما كانت غير في معنى النفي

IBNASHUR:1:7/r44.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r44.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r44.claim: Ḍalāl is missing the intended road through error, knowingly or unknowingly, like a lost camel; its use for religious or intellectual error is metaphorical.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r44.anchor: والضلال سلوك غير الطريق المراد عن خطإ سواء علم بذلك فهو يتطلب الطريق أم لم يعلم

IBNASHUR:1:7/r45.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r45.speaker: قالوا
IBNASHUR:1:7/r45.claim: In religious usage, misguidance opposes full faith and ranges from neglecting recommended practice to unbelief; the author defines it as absence of guidance and notes sealing as its extreme form.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r45.anchor: قالوا وله عرض عريض أدناه ترك السنن وأقصاه الكفر

IBNASHUR:1:7/r46.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r46.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r46.claim: The angry group knowingly rejects religion or relies on wildly strained interpretations driven by desire; the straying group includes those who distort true religions through misunderstanding. Both are accountable for failing to seek truth.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r46.anchor: فالمغضوب عليهم جنس للفرق التي تعمدت ذلك واستخفت بالديانة عن عمد أو عن تأويل بعيد جدا

IBNASHUR:1:7/r47.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r47.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r47.claim: An ellipsis-like matching (iḥtibāk) implies both groups share both qualities, while assigning each its leading description shows that the strayers’ error is less severe.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r47.anchor: فحصل شبه الاحتباك وهو أن كلا الفريقين نال حظا من الوصفين إلا أن تعليق كل وصف على الفريق

IBNASHUR:1:7/r48.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r48.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR:1:7/r48.claim: A report in al-Tirmidhī, which the author grades ḥasan, names Jews as an example of the angered and Christians as an example of the straying, not as exclusive referents.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r48.anchor: فاليهود مَثَلٌ للفريق الأول والنصارى من جملة الفريق الثاني كما ورد به الحديث عن النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم في « جامع الترمذي » وحسَّنه

IBNASHUR:1:7/r49.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r49.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r49.claim: Arab listeners knew Jews in Khaybar, al-Naḍīr, Medina, and Yemen, and Arab Christians such as Taghlib, Kalb, and parts of Quḍāʿa; both had altered their faith.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r49.anchor: فقد كان العرب يعرفون اليهود في خيبر والنضير وبعض سكان المدينة وفي عرب اليمن

IBNASHUR:1:7/r50.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r50.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:1:7/r50.claim: Islam’s straight path is clear in proof and sound in method, as the Qurʾān says; the law also distinguishes valid disagreement within Islam from disagreement that leaves it.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r50.anchor: وفي وصف الصراط المسؤول في قوله : { اهدنا الصراط المستقيم } بالمستقيم إيماء إلى أن الإسلام واضح الحجة قويم المحجة

IBNASHUR:1:7/r51.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r51.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR:1:7/r51.claim: The Prophet says a qualified jurist who reaches the right answer earns two rewards, and one who errs earns one, acknowledging differing degrees of sound judgment.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r51.anchor: من اجتهد وأصاب فله أجران ومن اجتهد وأخطأ فله أجر واحد

IBNASHUR:1:7/r52.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r52.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR:1:7/r52.claim: Most readers kasrate the hāʾ in plural and dual pronouns after a silent yāʾ to avoid heaviness; this matches the dialects of Qays, Tamīm, and Saʿd ibn Bakr.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r52.anchor: فالجمهور قرأوها بكسر الهاء تخلصا من الثقل لأن الهاء حاجز غير حصين

IBNASHUR:1:7/r53.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r53.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب
IBNASHUR:1:7/r53.claim: Ḥamza dammas the hāʾ in ʿalayhim, ilayhim, and ladayhim only, while Yaʿqūb dammas it in every pronoun of this class; the former follows a Quraysh and Ḥijāzī dialect.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r53.anchor: وقرأ حمزة عليهم وإليهم ولديهم فقط بضم الهاء وما عداها بكسر الهاء

IBNASHUR:1:7/r54.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r54.speaker: يعقوب
IBNASHUR:1:7/r54.claim: Yaʿqūb reads every pronoun of this type with a preceding silent yāʾ and a dammated hāʾ.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r54.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب كل ضمير من هذا القبيل مما قبل الهاء فيه ياء ساكنة بضم الهاء

IBNASHUR:1:7/r55.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r55.speaker: الجمهور وابن كثير وأبو جعفر وقالون
IBNASHUR:1:7/r55.claim: At pause-free connection before a vowel, most readers leave the plural mīm silent; Ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, and Qālūn in one transmission lengthen its damma, a dialect also illustrated by Labīd.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r55.anchor: فالجمهور قرأوا : { عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم } بسكون الميم وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وقالون في رواية عنه بضمة مشبعة : { غير المغضوب عليهم }

IBNASHUR:1:7/r56.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:1:7/r56.speaker: ورش
IBNASHUR:1:7/r56.claim: Warsh lengthens a damma on the plural mīm when a hamza follows, but not before ghayr here; all readers leave the mīm silent at pause.
IBNASHUR:1:7/r56.anchor: وقرأ ورش بضم الميم وإشباعها إذا وقع بعد الميم همز دون نحو : { غير المغضوب عليهم } وأجمع الكل على إسكان الميم في الوقف .

IBNHIBBAN:1797/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1797/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNHIBBAN:1797/r1.claim: Nuaim reports that Abu Hurayra began with the basmala, recited the Fatiha, said amin at its end with the congregation, and performed the prayer actions before saying his prayer most resembled the Prophet's.
IBNHIBBAN:1797/r1.anchor: صليت وراء أبي هريرة فقال: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ثم قرأ بأم الكتاب حتى إذا بلغ {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين} قال: آمين

IBNHIBBAN:1804/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1804/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:1804/r1.claim: The Prophet instructs worshippers to say amin when the imam reaches the verse's ending; the imam and angels say it too, and agreement with the angels brings forgiveness of past sins.
IBNHIBBAN:1804/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " إذا قال الإمام {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين} ، فقولوا:

IBNHIBBAN:1804/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1804/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNHIBBAN:1804/r2.claim: Abu Hatim explains that matching the angels means saying amin sincerely for God, free of vanity, showing off, or desire for reputation, as the angels do.
IBNHIBBAN:1804/r2.anchor: قال أبو حاتم رضى الله تعالى عنه: معنى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "فمن وافق تأمينه تأمين الملائكة"

IBNHIBBAN:1805/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:1805/r1.speaker: وائل بن حجر
IBNHIBBAN:1805/r1.claim: Wail ibn Hujr reports that while praying with the Prophet, he heard him say amin after reciting ‘nor those astray.’
IBNHIBBAN:1805/r1.anchor: عن وائل بن حجر أنه صلى مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: فوضع اليد اليمنى على اليد اليسرى فلما قال: {ولا الضالين} ، قال: "آمين"

IBNMAJAH:844/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:844/r1.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
IBNMAJAH:844/r1.claim: Samura reports two Prophetic pauses, at prayer's start and after recitation of this ending; Imran objected but Ubayy confirmed Samura, and Qatada says the pause lets the reciter regain breath.
IBNMAJAH:844/r1.anchor: عَنْ سَمُرَةَ بْنِ جُنْدُبٍ، قَالَ سَكْتَتَانِ حَفِظْتُهُمَا عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ

IBNMAJAH:846/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:846/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNMAJAH:846/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's prayer instructions: followers listen during the imam's recitation and say amin when he finishes with these words.
IBNMAJAH:846/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ ‏"‏ إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ الإِمَامُ لِيُؤْتَمَّ بِهِ

IBNMAJAH:853/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:853/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNMAJAH:853/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra says people had stopped saying amin; the Prophet said it aloud after the Fatiha's closing words, loud enough for the first row to hear and the mosque to reverberate.
IBNMAJAH:853/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ تَرَكَ النَّاسُ التَّأْمِينَ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r13.claim: Reports from companions who witnessed revelation identify those who incurred wrath as Jews and those astray as Christians.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r13.anchor: المراد من ) المغضوب عليهم ( اليهود ومن ) الضالين ( النصارى

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r1.claim: The phrase “the path of those” is a substitute for the previously mentioned straight path.

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن الزبير
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r2.claim: ʿUmar and Ibn al-Zubayr read “the path of those whom You favored” as “the path of whom You favored.”
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r2.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب ، وابن الزبير : «صراط من أنعمت عليهم »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r3.claim: The relative plural derives from لذٍ; its yāʾ drops with nunation and returns when the definite article is prefixed.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r3.anchor: وأصله «لذٍ » ، حذفتْ منه الياء للتنوين كما تحذف من عمٍ ، وقاضٍ ، فلما دخلته الألف واللام ثبتت الياء

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r4.claim: الذي is an indefinite, deficient relative noun requiring a clause and a resumptive pronoun; its singular is indeclinable, while its dual forms decline.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r4.anchor: و «الذي » اسم مبهم ناقص محتاج إلى صلة وعائد

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r5.claim: Some Arabs inflect the plural relative, using اللذون in the nominative.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r5.anchor: من يعرب جمعه ، فيقول في الرفع اللذون ،

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r6.claim: The form الذي is conventionally written with one lām in singular and plural because it is so frequent.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r6.anchor: وكتب الذي بلام واحدة في الإفراد والجمع تخفيفاً لكثرة الاستعمال

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وجمهور من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r7.claim: They identify the favored people as prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous, citing the description of those whom God guides to a straight path.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r7.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وجمهور من المفسرين : إنه أراد صراط النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also glosses the favored people simply as the believers.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضاً : «المنعم عليهم هو المؤمنون »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r9.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the favored people as the Companions of Muḥammad.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن : «المنعم عليهم أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r10.speaker: فرقة من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r10.claim: A group of commentators takes them to be the believers among the Children of Israel, appealing to the command to remember God’s favor on Israel.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r10.anchor: وحكى مكي وغيره عن فرقة من المفسرين أن المنعم عليهم مؤمنو بني إسرائيل

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also identifies them as Moses’ people before they changed their way; the author says this is the same as the preceding Israelite interpretation.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : «المنعم عليهم أصحابُ موسى قبل أن يبدلوا » .

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r12.speaker: قتادة بن دعامة
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r12.claim: Qatāda restricts the favored people to the prophets.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r12.anchor: وقال قتادة بن دعامة : «المنعم عليهم الأنبياء خاصة »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r13.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r13.claim: As Makki transmits it, Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the favored people as Muḥammad, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r13.anchor: وحكى مكي عن أبي العالية أنه قال : «المنعم عليهم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأبو بكر عمر »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r14.claim: The author says Abū al-ʿĀliya’s identification makes the straight path the way of Muḥammad, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar; this is stronger because calling the persons themselves a path is figurative.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r14.anchor: وهذا أقوى في المعنى ، لأن تسمية أشخاصهم طريقاً تجوز

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r15.speaker: حمزة
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r15.claim: Ḥamza reads the pronoun with ḍamma on hāʾ and a quiescent mīm; the other readers use kasra on hāʾ and differ over mīm.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r15.anchor: فقرأ حمزة «عليهُمْ » بضم الهاء وإسكان الميم

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r16.speaker: الباقون
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r16.claim: The remaining readers pronounce hāʾ with kasra, while differing over the mīm.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r16.anchor: قرأ الباقون في جميعها بكسر الهاء واختلفوا في الميم

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r17.speaker: نافع
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r17.claim: Reports give Nāfiʿ a choice between mīm with ḍamma and sukūn; since he did not object to ḍamma, the author infers his own reading used sukūn.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r17.anchor: فروي عن نافع التخيير بين ضمها وسكونها ، وروي عنه أنه كان لا يعيب ضم الميم ، فدل ذلك على أن قراءته كانت بالإسكان

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r18.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r18.claim: Ibn Kathīr links the mīm with a wāw when it is pronounced with ḍamma, whether the preceding hāʾ has ḍamma or kasra.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r18.anchor: وكان عبد الله بن كثير يصل الميم بواو انضمت الهاء قبلها أو انكسرت فيقرأ

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r19.speaker: ورش
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r19.claim: Warsh uses kasra on hāʾ and pauses on mīm, but supplies a pronounced wāw when an original alif follows the mīm.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r19.anchor: وقرأ ورش الهاء مكسورة والميم موقوفة ، إلا أن تلقى الميم ألفاً أصلية فيلحق في اللفظ واواً

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r20.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر والكسائي
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r20.claim: Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, and al-Kisāʾī use kasra on hāʾ and sukūn on mīm in the basic form.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r20.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو ، وعاصم ، وابن عامر ، والكسائي ، يكسرون ، ويسكنون الميم

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r21.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r21.speaker: عاصم وابن كثير ونافع
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r21.claim: Before a following consonant, ʿĀṣim, Ibn Kathīr, and Nāfiʿ retain kasra on hāʾ but put ḍamma on mīm.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r21.anchor: فكان عاصم ، وابن كثير ، ونافع يمضون على كسر الهاء وضم الميم

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r22.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r22.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r22.claim: Before a following consonant, Abū ʿAmr uses kasra on both hāʾ and mīm.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r22.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو يكسر الهاء والميم فيقول : { عليهم الذلة } و { إليهم اثنين }

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r23.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r23.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r23.claim: Before a following consonant, al-Kisāʾī uses ḍamma on both hāʾ and mīm.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r23.anchor: وكان الكسائي يضم الهاء والميم معاً ، فيقرأ { عليهم الذلة } و { من دونهم امرأتين }

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r24.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r24.speaker: أبو بكر أحمد بن موسى
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r24.claim: He says hāʾ varies between kasra and ḍamma only when preceded by kasra or a quiescent yāʾ; otherwise hāʾ is ḍamma.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r24.anchor: قال أبو بكر أحمد بن موسى : وكل هذا الاختلاف في كسر الهاء وضمها إنما هو في الهاء التي قبلها كسرة أو ياء ساكنة ، فإذا جاوزت هذين لم يكن في الهاء إلا الضم

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r25.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r25.speaker: أبو بكر أحمد بن موسى
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r25.claim: When no hāʾ preceded by kasra or quiescent yāʾ comes before mīm, he allows only mīm with ḍamma or sukūn, as in منكم and أنتم.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r25.anchor: فإذا لم يكن قبل الميم هاء قبلها كسرة أو ياء ساكنة لم يجز في الميم إلا الضم والتسكين في مثل قوله تعالى : منكم وأنتم

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r26.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r26.speaker: صاحب الدلائل
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r26.claim: He catalogs forms with a wāw after mīm, without the wāw, with mīm ḍamma, and with kasra and yāʾ, reflecting several combinations of vowels.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r26.anchor: وحكى صاحب الدلائل قال : «قرأ بعضهم عليهمو بواو وضمتين ، وبعضهم بضمتين

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r27.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r27.speaker: ابن جني
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r27.claim: Ibn Jinnī transmits from Aḥmad ibn Mūsā forms with an extended wāw, unextended ḍamma, and mīm sukūn; Ḥasan and ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid also read with an extended yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r27.anchor: قال ابن جني( {[105]} ) : «حكى أحمد بن موسى عليهمو

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r28.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r28.speaker: الحسن وعمرو بن فائد والأعرج
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r28.claim: Additional transmitted forms include kasra on mīm without yāʾ-lengthening and al-Aʿraj’s kasra on hāʾ with ḍamma on mīm without lengthening.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r28.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعمرو بن فائد «عليهمي » . وقرىء

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r29.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r29.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r29.claim: The combinations amount to ten forms: five with hāʾ ḍamma and five with hāʾ kasra, though only six are transmitted from canonical readers.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r29.anchor: وهذه القراءات كلها بضم الهاء إلا الأخيرة وبإزاء كل واحدة منها قراءة بكسر الهاء فيجيء في الجميع عشر قراءات

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r30.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r30.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r30.claim: The majority of named readers read ghayr with kasra; Ibn Kathīr reads it with fatḥa, though kasra is also reported from him.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r30.anchor: فقرأ نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بخفض الراء ، وقرأ بن كثير

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r31.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r31.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r31.claim: On the genitive reading, ghayr can be an appositive to الذين or an adjective to an indefinite, since الذين here is not specifically singled out.

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r32.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r32.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r32.claim: On the accusative reading, ghayr can be circumstantial, exceptive, or an implied direct object of “I mean.”

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r33.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r33.speaker: الخليل
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r33.claim: A similar account is transmitted from al-Khalīl for the accusative parsing of ghayr.

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r34.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r34.speaker: أبو بكر بن السراج
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r34.claim: Ibn al-Sarrāj argues that ghayr plus its definite complement is definite here: an understood, unique opposite makes “other than the recipients of favor” identifiable.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r34.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن السراج( {[111]} ) : «والذي عندي أن { غير }

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r35.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r35.speaker: أبو بكر بن السراج
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r35.claim: Ordinarily ghayr and mithl remain indefinite despite annexation because “other than you” and likenesses have innumerable possible referents; a single known opposite makes ghayr definite.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r35.anchor: وإنما تنكرت ( غير ) ومثل مع إضافتهما إلى المعارف من أجل معناهما

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r36.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r36.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r36.claim: He explains that Ibn al-Sarrāj preserves الذين as definite and permits a definite adjective, while others treat ghayr as indefinite and approximate الذين to a general noun.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r36.anchor: أبقى أبو بكر { الذين } على حد التعريف ، وجوز نعتها ب { غير } لما بينه من تعرف غير

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r37.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r37.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r37.claim: The author calls the genitive reading the clear choice, noting it is the reading of the majority and is also reported from Ibn Kathīr.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r37.anchor: والاختيار الذي لا خفاء به الكسر . وقد روي عن ابن كثير

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r38.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r38.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد وعدي بن حاتم عن النبي
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r38.claim: They identify those under wrath as Jews and the astray as Christians; the same interpretation is reported from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim from the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r38.anchor: و { المغضوب عليهم } اليهود ، والضالون النصارى . وهكذا قال ابن مسعود

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r39.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r39.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r39.claim: The author says scripture repeatedly describes God’s wrath against Jews, citing their incurring wrath and the punishment of Sabbath-breakers.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r39.anchor: ذكر غضب الله على اليهود متكرر فيه

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r40.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r40.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r40.claim: Here divine wrath means God’s manifesting ordeals, punishments, humiliation, and similar signs that He has emphatically distanced them from His mercy.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r40.anchor: وغضب الله تعالى عبارة عن إظهاره

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r41.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r41.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r41.claim: The committed Christians had followed a true religious law before Muḥammad’s law arrived; once it came, they went astray.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r41.anchor: والنصارى كان محققوهم على شرعة قبل ورود شرع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فلما ورد ضلوا

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r42.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r42.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r42.claim: Other Christians were already astray because their accounts of Jesus diverged from the beginning.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r42.anchor: وأما غير محققيهم فضلالهم متقرر منذ تفرقت أقوالهم في عيسى عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r43.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r43.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r43.claim: He links the Christians’ error to the verse describing a people who strayed earlier, misled many, and left the right way.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r43.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى فيهم : { ولا تتبعوا أهواء قوم قد ضلوا من قبل وأضلوا كثيراً

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r44.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r44.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r44.claim: Makkī says lā prevents readers from mistaking the astray for a coordinate of الذين.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r44.anchor: قال مكي رحمه الله حكاية( {[118]} ) : دخلت { لا } في قوله { ولا الضالين }

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r45.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r45.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r45.claim: Another reported explanation treats lā as emphatic, with the force of ghayr.

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r46.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r46.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r46.claim: Al-Ṭabarī calls lā extra, citing a rajaz line where ألا تسخرا is understood as أن تسخر.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r46.anchor: وحكى الطبري أن { لا } زائدة ، وقال : هي هنا على نحو ما هي عليه في قول الراجز

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r47.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r47.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r47.claim: The author rejects al-Ṭabarī’s reading of al-Aḥwaṣ’s line as proof that lā is extra: it means they reproach him for wanting not to love amusement, so lā is operative.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r47.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه : وبيت الأحوص إنما معناه إرادة أن لا أحبه ف ( لا ) فيه متمكنة

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r48.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r48.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r48.claim: Al-Ṭabarī also cites ما منعك أن لا تسجد and a poem after an earlier negation, where lā may be omitted because the opening negation governs the later clause.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r48.anchor: وإنما جاز أن تكون لا بمعنى الحذف ، ولأنها تقدمها الجحد

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r49.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r49.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وأبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r49.claim: ʿUmar and Ubayy read a second ghayr before “the astray”; both accusative and genitive forms are reported for each ghayr.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r49.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب وأبي بن كعب :«غير المغضوب عليهم وغير الضالين »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r50.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r50.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r50.claim: In answer to al-Ṭabarī’s question about assigning one label to each group, the author says Jewish transgression, obstinacy, rejection despite signs, and killing prophets characteristically warrant wrath; Christians’ basic unbelief is astray shared by all unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r50.anchor: والقول في ذلك أن أفاعيل اليهود من اعتدائهم ، وتعنتهم ، وكفرهم

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r51.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r51.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r51.claim: Calling Christians astray does not support the Qadari argument that they created their own misguidance: as with a wall collapsing or a tree moving, God created their misguidance while they acquired the act of straying.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r51.anchor: لأن هذا إنما هو كقولهم تهدم الجدار وتحركت الشجرة

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r52.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r52.speaker: أيوب السختياني
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r52.claim: Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī reads الضألين with a short hamza to avoid two adjacent sukūns, treating it as a dialect form.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r52.anchor: وقرأ أيوب السختياني( {[126]} ) : «الضألين » بهمزة غير ممدودة كأنه فر من التقاء الساكنين ، وهي لغة

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r53.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r53.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r53.claim: Consensus counts al-Fātiḥa as seven verses, ending them respectively at العالمين, الرحيم, الدين, نستعين, المستقيم, أنعمت عليهم, and ولا الضالين; he says the weak dispute over the basmala was discussed earlier.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r53.anchor: وأجمع الناسُ على أنَّ عدد آي سورة الحمد سبعُ آيات

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r54.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r54.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r54.claim: The Prophet tells worshippers to say Āmīn when the imam says “nor those who are astray”; the angels in heaven say it, and agreement with them brings forgiveness of past sins.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r54.anchor: روى أبو هريرة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : إذا قال الإمام

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r55.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r55.speaker: جبريل
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r55.claim: A report says Gabriel taught the Prophet al-Fātiḥa at its revelation; after the Prophet recited it, Gabriel told him to say Āmīn.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r55.anchor: وروي أن جبريل عليه السلام لما علم النبي عليه السلام فاتحة الكتاب وقت نزولها فقرأها قال له : «قل آمين »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r56.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r56.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r56.claim: ʿAlī calls Āmīn the seal of the Lord of the worlds, with which the believing servant seals his supplication.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r56.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه : «آمين خاتم رب العالمين ، يختم بها دعاء عبده المؤمن »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r57.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r57.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r57.claim: A report says the Prophet heard a man supplicate and said his request was assured if he concluded; when asked how, he answered: with Āmīn.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r57.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سمع رجلاً يدعو فقال : «أوجب إن ختم . فقال له رجل بأي شيء يختم يا رسول الله ؟ قال : «بآمين »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r58.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r58.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن وأحمد بن يحيى ثعلب
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r58.claim: Most scholars understand Āmīn as “O God, answer” or “Answer, Lord,” and al-Ḥasan and Thaʿlab are named for this explanation.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r58.anchor: ومعنى » آمين «عند أكثر أهل العلم : اللهم استجب

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r59.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r59.speaker: جعفر بن محمد ومجاهد وهلال بن يساف
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r59.claim: Another view makes Āmīn one of God’s names; it is reported from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Mujāhid, and Hilāl ibn Yasāf.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r59.anchor: وقال قوم : » هو اسم من أسماء الله تعالى « ، روي ذلك عن جعفر بن محمد

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r60.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r60.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r60.claim: A further report calls Āmīn the name of a seal used to stamp the books of the people of Paradise, which they receive by faith.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r60.anchor: وقد روي أن » آمين «اسم خاتم يطبع به كتب أهل الجنة

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r61.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r61.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r61.claim: The author infers from these reports that supplicants should say Āmīn at the end of every supplication and after al-Fātiḥa outside prayer, without loud recitation.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r61.anchor: فمقتضى هذه الآثار أن كل داع ينبغي له في آخر دعائه أن يقول : «آمين » وكذلك كل قارىء للحمد في غير صلاة ، لكن ليس بجهر الترتيل

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r62.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r62.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r62.claim: One legal view has every worshipper—imam, praying alone, or follower—say Āmīn if they recite or hear al-Fātiḥa.

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r63.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r63.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r63.claim: In the Mudawwana, Mālik says the imam does not say Āmīn, while followers say it quietly and a person praying alone says it.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r63.anchor: وقال مالك في المدونة : «لا يقول الإمام » آمين «ولكن يقولها من خلفه ويخفون ، ويقولها الفذ »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r64.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r64.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r64.claim: Other reports from Mālik say that the imam says Āmīn either quietly or aloud, or does not say it during audible prayer.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r64.anchor: وقد روي عن مالك رضي الله عنه : أن الإمام يقولها أسرّ أم جهَرَ . وروي عنه : «الإمام لا يؤمن في الجهر »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r65.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r65.speaker: ابن حبيب
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r65.claim: Ibn Ḥabīb holds that the imam should say Āmīn.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r65.anchor: وقال ابن حبيب : «يؤمن » . وقال ابن بكير

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r66.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r66.speaker: ابن بكير
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r66.claim: Ibn Bukayr says the imam may choose whether to say it.

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r67.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r67.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r67.claim: The disagreement concerns the imam; no disagreement applies to the person praying alone or the follower except for Ibn Nāfiʿ’s position.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r67.anchor: فهذا الخلاف إنما هو في الإمام ، ولم يختلف في الفذ ولا في المأموم إلا ابن نافع

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r68.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r68.speaker: ابن نافع
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r68.claim: Ibn Nāfiʿ says a follower says Āmīn only if he hears the imam reach “nor those who are astray”; if too far away to hear, he omits it.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r68.anchor: قال في كتاب ابن حارث : «لا يقولها المأموم إلا إن سمع الإمام يقول { ولا الضالين }

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r69.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r69.speaker: ابن عبدوس
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r69.claim: Ibn ʿAbdūs tells a distant follower to estimate the length of the recitation and then say Āmīn.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r69.anchor: وقال ابن عبدوس : «يتحرى قدر القراءة ويقول آمين »

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r70.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r70.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r70.claim: Āmīn is built on fatḥa because two sukūns meet; fatḥa is lighter with yāʾ than the other vowel options.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r70.anchor: وهي لفظة مبنية على الفتح لالتقاء الساكنين ، وكأن الفتح مع الياء أخف من سائر الحركات

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r71.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r71.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r71.claim: Some Arabs lengthen Āmīn; a poetic line repeats the long form and imagines needing two thousand Āmīns.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r71.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول «آمين » فيمده ، ومنه قول الشاعر( {[10]} )

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r72.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r72.speaker: جبير بن الأضبط
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r72.claim: Some Arabs shorten it to أمين, as in a line attributed to Jubayr ibn al-Aḍbaṭ.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r72.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول «أمين » بالقصر ، ومنه قول الشاعر : [ جبير بن الأضبط ]

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r73.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r73.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r73.claim: One unnamed explanation takes agreeing with the angels to mean agreement in the response to prayer.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r73.anchor: فقيل في الإجابة ، وقيل في خلوص النية

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r74.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r74.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r74.claim: A second unnamed explanation takes it to mean sincerity of intention.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r74.anchor: وقيل في خلوص النية ، وقيل : في الوقت

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r75.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r75.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r75.claim: A third unnamed explanation takes it to mean agreement in timing.

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r76.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r76.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r76.claim: The author prefers agreement in timing together with sincere intention and wholehearted turning to God; the response follows from this state.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r76.anchor: والذي يترجح أن المعنى فمن وافق في الوقت مع خلوص النية ، والإقبال على الرغبة إلى الله تعالى بقلب سليم

IBNATIYYA:1:7/r77.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r77.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r77.claim: He concludes that a person in this state is upon the straight path.
IBNATIYYA:1:7/r77.anchor: لأن من هذه حاله فهو على الصراط المستقيم

MALIK:187/r3.author: MALIK
MALIK:187/r3.speaker: الله تبارك وتعالى
MALIK:187/r3.claim: The qudsi report assigns the final plea for guidance to the servant and says the servant receives what he asks.

MALIK:194/r1.author: MALIK
MALIK:194/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MALIK:194/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet tells the congregation to say amen after the imam's final phrase; agreement with the angels brings forgiveness of past sins.
MALIK:194/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

MUSLIM:878/r3.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:878/r3.speaker: الله تعالى
MUSLIM:878/r3.claim: When the servant asks for the guided path and names those favored rather than those under anger or astray, Allah says this request is for the servant and grants what was asked.
MUSLIM:878/r3.anchor: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم * صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين

MUSLIM:904/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:904/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSLIM:904/r1.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet’s prayer instructions: keep the rows straight, follow the imam’s takbīr, bowing, and prostration after him, and recite the sitting testimony.
MUSLIM:904/r1.anchor: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خطبنا فبين لنا سنتنا وعلمنا صلاتنا فقال

MUSLIM:904/r2.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:904/r2.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
MUSLIM:904/r2.claim: Abu Musa says the Prophet taught worshippers to answer the recitation’s ending with Amin, so that God answers them; the teaching arose after a man spoke during prayer.
MUSLIM:904/r2.anchor: عن حطان بن عبد الله الرقاشي قال صليت مع أبي موسى الأشعري صلاة

MUSLIM:920/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:920/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSLIM:920/r1.claim: The Prophet promises forgiveness of previous sins when the reciter and those behind him say Amin in unison with the heavenly utterance.
MUSLIM:920/r1.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7187/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7187/r1.speaker: النبي عن أبي هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7187/r1.claim: When the imam finishes al-Fatiha, worshippers should say Amin; if their response coincides with the angels' and imam's, their past sins are forgiven.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7187/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إذا قال الإمام: {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:7660/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7660/r1.speaker: النبي عن أبي هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7660/r1.claim: The Prophet instructs the congregation to say Amin after the imam's recitation; agreement with the angels' Amin brings forgiveness for past sins.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:7660/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إذا قال الإمام: {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9682/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9682/r1.speaker: النبي عن أبي هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9682/r1.claim: The Prophet teaches followers not to anticipate the imam, to say Amin at the end of al-Fatiha, and to answer ‘Our Lord, praise belongs to You’ after the imam says God hears praise; agreement with the angels brings forgiveness for those in the mosque.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9682/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعلمنا أن لا نبادر الإمام بالركوع

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9804/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9804/r1.speaker: النبي عن أبي هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9804/r1.claim: When the reciter finishes al-Fatiha, those behind him say Amin; agreement with the heavenly congregation's Amin brings forgiveness for past sins.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9804/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا قال القارئ: {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:9922/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9922/r1.speaker: النبي عن أبي هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9922/r1.claim: The Prophet orders worshippers to say Amin after the imam; whoever's response matches the angels' is forgiven past sins.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:9922/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " إذا قال الإمام: {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:10449/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10449/r1.speaker: نعيم المجمر عن أبي هريرة
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10449/r1.claim: Na'im al-Mujmir reports that Abu Hurayra recited al-Fatiha in prayer, said Amin at its close, then said the takbir for bowing; Abu Hurayra said his prayer most resembled the Prophet's.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:10449/r1.anchor: أن نعيما المجمر، حدثه أنه، صلى وراء أبي هريرة " فقرأ أم القرآن فلما قال: {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:18854/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18854/r1.speaker: وائل بن حجر عن النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18854/r1.claim: Wa'il reports that the Prophet said Amin quietly after al-Fatiha, placed his right hand over his left in prayer, and gave salutation to both sides.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18854/r1.anchor: عن وائل، أو سمعه حجر، من وائل قال: صلى بنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فلما قرأ: {غير المغضوب عليهم ولا الضالين}

MUSNAD-AHMAD:18873/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18873/r1.speaker: وائل بن حجر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18873/r1.claim: Wa'il saw the Prophet place his right hand over his left and raise his hands to his ears at the prayer's opening; the Prophet said Amin aloud after al-Fatiha.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18873/r1.anchor: عن وائل قال: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يضع يده اليمنى على اليسرى في الصلاة

MUSNAD-AHMAD:19595/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19595/r1.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19595/r1.claim: The Prophet says to follow the imam: say Amin at al-Fatiha's end so God answers, follow his bowing and prostration, and say ‘Our Lord, praise belongs to You’ after he says God hears praise; his movements are offset so followers do not precede him.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19595/r1.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: علمنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاتنا وسنتنا فقال: " إنما الإمام ليؤتم به، فإذا كبر فكبروا

MUSNAD-AHMAD:19627/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19627/r1.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري عن النبي
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19627/r1.claim: The Prophet teaches that the congregation says Amin after al-Fatiha and follows the imam's prayer movements; he moves first, with the imam's delay balanced by the followers' own delay.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:19627/r1.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: علمنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلاتنا وسنتنا فقال: " إنما الإمام ليؤتم به، فإذا كبر فكبروا

NASAI:909/r3.author: NASAI
NASAI:909/r3.speaker: رسول الله
NASAI:909/r3.claim: The same report assigns the servant’s request for the favored path, away from those under wrath and those astray, to the servant; God grants what the servant asks.
NASAI:909/r3.anchor: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAI:830/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:830/r1.speaker: أبو موسى
NASAI:830/r1.claim: Ḥiṭṭān reports that a congregant declared prayer established through piety and almsgiving; Abū Mūsā recalled the Prophet’s rule to follow the imam, say amin after 1:7 for God’s answer, and mirror the imam’s movements.
NASAI:830/r1.anchor: صلى بنا أبو موسى فلما كان في القعدة دخل رجل من القوم فقال أقرت الصلاة بالبر والزكاة

NASAI:905/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:905/r1.speaker: نعيم المجمر
NASAI:905/r1.claim: Nuʿaym reports that Abu Hurayra recited the basmala and al-Fātiḥa in prayer, said amin after 1:7, and was echoed by the congregation; he affirmed his prayer resembled the Prophet’s.
NASAI:905/r1.anchor: عَنْ نُعَيْمٍ الْمُجْمِرِ، قَالَ صَلَّيْتُ وَرَاءَ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ فَقَرَأَ

NASAI:927/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:927/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASAI:927/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s instruction to say amin when the imam reaches 1:7; whoever’s amin coincides with the angels’ is forgiven for previous sins.
NASAI:927/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAI:929/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:929/r1.speaker: رسول الله
NASAI:929/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s command to say amin after the imam recites 1:7, promising forgiveness of past sins when the worshipper’s response matches the angels’.
NASAI:929/r1.anchor: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ

NASAI:932/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:932/r1.speaker: وائل بن حجر
NASAI:932/r1.claim: Wāʾil b. Ḥujr’s father reports that the Prophet raised his hands below his ears at the opening takbir and said amin after reciting 1:7.
NASAI:932/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَبْدِ الْجَبَّارِ بْنِ وَائِلٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، قَالَ صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAI:932/r2.author: NASAI
NASAI:932/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAI:932/r2.claim: The Prophet said twelve angels hurried to carry a worshipper’s abundant, good, blessed praise, and nothing stopped it before it reached the Throne.
NASAI:932/r2.anchor: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAI:1064/r1.author: NASAI
NASAI:1064/r1.speaker: أبو موسى
NASAI:1064/r1.claim: Abū Mūsā reports that the Prophet taught worshippers to say amin after the imam recites 1:7, so God answers them.
NASAI:1064/r1.anchor: سَمِعَ أَبَا مُوسَى، قَالَ إِنَّ نَبِيَّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم خَطَبَنَا وَبَيَّنَ لَنَا سُنَّتَنَا

NASAI:1064/r2.author: NASAI
NASAI:1064/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAI:1064/r2.claim: The Prophet directs worshippers to follow the imam’s takbirs, bowing, and prostration, which the imam performs before them; they answer his praise with a prayer for God’s praise.
NASAI:1064/r2.anchor: قَالَ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAI:1064/r3.author: NASAI
NASAI:1064/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAI:1064/r3.claim: When seated, worshippers should begin with al-taḥiyyāt, salutations, and the testimony; the Prophet calls these seven words the greeting of prayer.
NASAI:1064/r3.anchor: قَالَ نَبِيُّ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF:1:7/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r1.claim: Sirat alladhina is appositive to the straight path and repeats the request for guidance.

KASHSHAF:1:7/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r2.claim: The apposition reinforces and explains the straight path as the Muslims' path, certifying its uprightness emphatically.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r2.anchor: فائدته التوكيد لما فيه من التثنية والتكرير

KASHSHAF:1:7/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r4.claim: The blessing is general to include every blessing; whoever receives Islam receives every blessing.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r4.anchor: من أنعم عليه بنعمة الإسلام لم تبق نعمة إلا أصابته

KASHSHAF:1:7/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF:1:7/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as Moses's companions before they changed.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : هم أصحاب موسى قبل أن يغيروا

KASHSHAF:1:7/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r6.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF:1:7/r6.claim: Another view identifies them as the prophets.

KASHSHAF:1:7/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF:1:7/r7.claim: Ibn Masud reads sirat man anʿamta ʿalayhim.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «صراط من أنعمت عليهم »

KASHSHAF:1:7/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r8.claim: Ghayr can be appositive to those blessed, meaning they are spared God's anger and error.

KASHSHAF:1:7/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r9.claim: Alternatively, ghayr is an adjective: the blessed combine faith with safety from anger and error.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r9.anchor: أو صفة على معنى أنهم جمعوا بين النعمة المطلقة

KASHSHAF:1:7/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r10.claim: Ghayr can modify the definite relative phrase because it is undelimited and the angry and astray are opposites of the blessed.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r10.anchor: قلت : { الذين أنعمت عليهم } لا توقيت فيه

KASHSHAF:1:7/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r11.speaker: النبي وعمر بن الخطاب وابن كثير
KASHSHAF:1:7/r11.claim: The accusative ghayra is a circumstantial reading attributed to the Prophet, Umar, and Ibn Kathir.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r11.anchor: وهي قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعمر بن الخطاب

KASHSHAF:1:7/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r12.claim: Those who incurred anger are identified as Jews, with 5:60 cited.

KASHSHAF:1:7/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r13.claim: Those astray are identified as Christians, with 5:77 cited.

KASHSHAF:1:7/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r14.claim: God's anger is His will to avenge sinners and punish them, acting as a king does when angry with a subordinate.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r14.anchor: هو إرادة الانتقام من العصاة ، وإنزال العقوبة بهم

KASHSHAF:1:7/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r15.claim: The first ʿalayhim is accusative as object of anʿamta; the second is nominative as agent in the passive phrase.

KASHSHAF:1:7/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r16.claim: La appears because ghayr already carries negation: neither the angered nor the astray.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r16.anchor: لما في غير من معنى النفي

KASHSHAF:1:7/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r17.speaker: عمر وعلي
KASHSHAF:1:7/r17.claim: Umar and Ali read wa-ghayr al-dallin.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r17.anchor: وعن عمر وعلي رضي الله عنهما أنهما قرآ : وغير الضالين

KASHSHAF:1:7/r18.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r18.speaker: أيوب السختياني
KASHSHAF:1:7/r18.claim: Ayyub reads with hamza; Amr ibn Ubayd also uses a hamza form.

KASHSHAF:1:7/r19.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r19.speaker: أبو زيد
KASHSHAF:1:7/r19.claim: The hamza dialect avoids meeting two quiescent consonants, as in Abu Zayd's shaʾba and daʾba.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r19.anchor: وهذه لغة من جد في الهرب من التقاء الساكنين

KASHSHAF:1:7/r20.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r20.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r20.claim: Amin is a sound-form used as the name of the verb respond, like words meaning wait, hurry, and come.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r20.anchor: صوت سمي به الفعل الذي هو استجب

KASHSHAF:1:7/r21.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r21.speaker: ابن عباس والنبي
KASHSHAF:1:7/r21.claim: Ibn Abbas asked the Prophet what Amin means, and the Prophet answered, do it.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r21.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معنى آمين

KASHSHAF:1:7/r22.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r22.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r22.claim: Amin has long and short alif, both attested by poetry.

KASHSHAF:1:7/r23.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r23.speaker: النبي وجبريل
KASHSHAF:1:7/r23.claim: Gabriel taught the Prophet Amin at the end of al-Fatiha and called it a seal on a book.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r23.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : "  لقنني جبريل عليه السلام آمين

KASHSHAF:1:7/r24.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r24.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:1:7/r24.claim: Amin is not Quran because it was not entered in the codices.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r24.anchor: وليس من القرآن بدليل أنه لم يثبت في المصاحف

KASHSHAF:1:7/r25.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r25.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF:1:7/r25.claim: Al-Hasan says the imam should not say Amin because the imam is the supplicant.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r25.anchor: وعن الحسن : لا يقولها الإمام لأنه الداعي

KASHSHAF:1:7/r26.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r26.speaker: أبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF:1:7/r26.claim: Abu Hanifa is reported to say the imam should not say Amin.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r26.anchor: وعن أبي حنيفة رحمه الله مثله

KASHSHAF:1:7/r27.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r27.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
KASHSHAF:1:7/r27.claim: The well-known position of Abu Hanifa and his followers is to say Amin silently.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r27.anchor: والمشهور عنه وعن أصحابه أنه يخفيها

KASHSHAF:1:7/r28.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r28.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل وأنس والنبي
KASHSHAF:1:7/r28.claim: Silent recitation is reported from the Prophet by Abdullah ibn Mughaffal and Anas.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r28.anchor: وروى الإخفاء عبد الله بن مغفل وأنس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF:1:7/r29.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r29.speaker: الشافعي
KASHSHAF:1:7/r29.claim: Al-Shafii holds Amin is said aloud.

KASHSHAF:1:7/r30.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r30.speaker: وائل بن حجر والنبي
KASHSHAF:1:7/r30.claim: Waʾil ibn Hujr reports that the Prophet said Amin aloud after wa-la al-dallin.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r30.anchor: وعن وائل بن حجرأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا قرأ : ولا الضالين

KASHSHAF:1:7/r31.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r31.speaker: النبي وأبي بن كعب
KASHSHAF:1:7/r31.claim: The Prophet says al-Fatiha has no equal in the Torah, Gospel, or Quran and is the seven oft-repeated verses and great Quran given to him.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r31.anchor: وعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأبيّ بن كعب

KASHSHAF:1:7/r32.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:1:7/r32.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان والنبي
KASHSHAF:1:7/r32.claim: Hudhayfa reports that when a child recites al-Fatiha amid certain punishment, God hears and lifts it for forty years.
KASHSHAF:1:7/r32.anchor: وعن حذيفة بن اليمان أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

TIRMIDHI:2953/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:2953/r2.speaker: الله تعالى
TIRMIDHI:2953/r2.claim: In the divine report the Opening is divided into halves: praise belongs to God, the central pledge of worship and seeking help is shared, and its closing requests belong to the worshipper, who receives what he asks.
TIRMIDHI:2953/r2.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين فنصفها لي ونصفها لعبدي ولعبدي ما سأل

TIRMIDHI:248/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:248/r1.speaker: وائل بن حجر
TIRMIDHI:248/r1.claim: Wāʾil b. Ḥujr reports that the Prophet recited the verse’s ending, said amin, and extended his voice on it.
TIRMIDHI:248/r1.anchor: عن وائل بن حجر، قال سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TIRMIDHI:248/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:248/r2.speaker: author
TIRMIDHI:248/r2.claim: Tirmidhi says many Companions, Successors, and later scholars, including al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Isḥāq, hold that a man raises his voice when saying amin rather than hiding it.
TIRMIDHI:248/r2.anchor: ومن بعدهم يرون أن الرجل يرفع صوته بالتأمين ولا يخفيها

TIRMIDHI:248/r3.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:248/r3.speaker: محمد
TIRMIDHI:248/r3.claim: Muḥammad prefers Sufyan’s account: Shuʿba misidentifies Ḥujr, adds ʿAlqama to the chain, and reports a lowered voice where the stronger wording says the Prophet extended it.
TIRMIDHI:248/r3.anchor: سمعت محمدا يقول حديث سفيان أصح من حديث شعبة في هذا وأخطأ شعبة في مواضع من هذا الحديث

TIRMIDHI:248/r4.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:248/r4.speaker: أبو زرعة
TIRMIDHI:248/r4.claim: Abu Zurʿa also judges Sufyan’s version more accurate; al-ʿAlāʾ b. Ṣāliḥ transmits a version like Sufyan’s.
TIRMIDHI:248/r4.anchor: وسألت أبا زرعة عن هذا الحديث فقال حديث سفيان في هذا أصح من حديث شعبة

TIRMIDHI:248/r5.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:248/r5.speaker: أبو عيسى
TIRMIDHI:248/r5.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report from Wāʾil b. Ḥujr hasan.
TIRMIDHI:248/r5.anchor: قال أبو عيسى حديث وائل بن حجر حديث حسن

MAWARDI:1:7/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r1.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:7/r1.claim: One view identifies those favored as the angels.

MAWARDI:1:7/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r2.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:7/r2.claim: Another view identifies those favored as the prophets.

MAWARDI:1:7/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r3.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:7/r3.claim: Another view identifies them as believers in earlier scriptures.

MAWARDI:1:7/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r4.speaker: وكيع
MAWARDI:1:7/r4.anchor: والرابع : أنهم المسلمون وهو قول وكيع

MAWARDI:1:7/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
MAWARDI:1:7/r5.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd identifies them as the Prophet and his Companions.
MAWARDI:1:7/r5.anchor: هم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   ومَنْ معه مِنْ أصحابه ،   وهذا قول عبد الرحمن بن زيد

MAWARDI:1:7/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن الزبير
MAWARDI:1:7/r6.claim: Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr read min an‘amta alayhim instead of alladhina an‘amta alayhim.
MAWARDI:1:7/r6.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب وعبد الله بن الزبير : ( صِرَاطَ مَنْ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ

MAWARDI:1:7/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r7.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
MAWARDI:1:7/r7.claim: Adi ibn Hatim reports that the Prophet identified those under wrath as Jews and those astray as Christians; al-Mawardi says all exegetes agree.
MAWARDI:1:7/r7.anchor: روى عن عديِّ بن حاتم قال : سألتُ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   عن المغضوب عليهم ،   فقال :  "  هُمُ اليَهُود  "  وعن الضالين فقال :  "  هُمُ النَّصارى

MAWARDI:1:7/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI:1:7/r8.claim: Al-Mawardi says all exegetes agree that those under wrath are Jews and those astray are Christians.

MAWARDI:1:7/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r9.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:7/r9.claim: One interpretation takes God’s wrath in its familiar sense as anger among people.

MAWARDI:1:7/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r10.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:7/r10.claim: Another interpretation takes wrath as the will to exact vengeance, since the linguistic root implies harshness, which cannot be ascribed to God.
MAWARDI:1:7/r10.anchor: أنه إرادة الانتقام ،   لأن أصل الغضب في اللغة هو الغلظة ،   وهذه الصفة لا تجوز على الله تعالى

MAWARDI:1:7/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r11.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:7/r11.claim: A third interpretation is that God’s wrath means His condemnation of them.
MAWARDI:1:7/r11.anchor: أن غضبه عليهم هو ذمه لهم

MAWARDI:1:7/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r12.speaker: unattributed
MAWARDI:1:7/r12.claim: A fourth interprets wrath as a kind of punishment named anger, just as God’s blessings are named mercy.
MAWARDI:1:7/r12.anchor: أنه نوع من العقوبة سُمِّيَ غضباً ،   كما سُمِّيَتْ نِعَمُهُ رَحْمَةً

MAWARDI:1:7/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI:1:7/r13.claim: Misguidance is the opposite of guidance.

MAWARDI:1:7/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI:1:7/r14.claim: God singles out Jews as the objects of wrath because they are the most hostile.
MAWARDI:1:7/r14.anchor: وخصّ الله تعالى اليهود بالغضب ،   لأنهم أشد عداوة

MAWARDI:1:7/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:1:7/r15.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
MAWARDI:1:7/r15.claim: Umar ibn al-Khattab reads ghayr before al-dallin as well, repeating ghayr in the phrase.
MAWARDI:1:7/r15.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب ( غَيْرِ الْمغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَغَيْرِ الضَّآلِّين ) .

NASAFI:1:1/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:1/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
NASAFI:1:1/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra reports God’s dialogue dividing the Fatiha between Himself and the servant: praise, glorification, and exaltation belong to God; the worshipper’s request for guidance and the response to it belong to the servant, while worship and aid are shared.
NASAFI:1:1/r12.anchor: قال الله تعالى قسمت الصلاة أي الفاتحة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ولعبدي ما سأل

NASAFI:1:7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:7/r1.claim: ‘The path of those You favored’ is an apposition for ‘the path,’ repeating its governing element for emphasis and clarifying that the straight path is the Muslims’ path.
NASAFI:1:7/r1.anchor: { صِرَاطَ الذين أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ } بدل من الصراط وهو في حكم تكرير العامل

NASAFI:1:7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:7/r2.claim: The favored people are believers and prophets, or Moses’s people before they altered their religion.
NASAFI:1:7/r2.anchor: وهم المؤمنون و الأنبياء عليهم السلام أو قوم موسى صلى الله عليه وسلم قبل أن يغيروا

NASAFI:1:7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:7/r3.claim: ‘Other than those under anger, nor those astray’ can be an apposition to ‘those favored’ or an adjective describing them; they unite the full blessing of faith with safety from anger and error.
NASAFI:1:7/r3.anchor: { غَيْرِ المغضوب عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ الضالين } بدل من الذين أنعمت عليهم ، يعني أن المنعم عليهم

NASAFI:1:7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:7/r4.claim: Although ghayr normally does not become definite through annexation, it can modify the definite alladhina here: between opposites it takes definiteness, and both terms are generic yet partly specified, balancing their ambiguity and particularity.
NASAFI:1:7/r4.anchor: وإنما ساغ وقوعه صفة للذين وهو معرفة و «غير » لا يتعرف بالإضافة لأنه إذا وقع بين متضادين

NASAFI:1:7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:7/r5.claim: The first ‘upon them’ is in the accusative position as an object, while the second is in the nominative position as a subject.
NASAFI:1:7/r5.anchor: و«عليهم » الأولى محلها النصب على المفعولية ، ومحل الثانية الرفع على الفاعلية

NASAFI:1:7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:7/r6.claim: God’s anger means His will to take vengeance on liars and punish them, treating them as a king does those under his authority when angry.
NASAFI:1:7/r6.anchor: وغضب الله إرادة الانتقام من المكذبين وإنزال العقوبة بهم

NASAFI:1:7/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r7.speaker: قيل
NASAFI:1:7/r7.claim: One view identifies those under anger as Jews, citing God’s curse and anger in 5:60, and those astray as Christians, citing their earlier error in 5:77.
NASAFI:1:7/r7.anchor: وقيل : المغضوب عليهم هم اليهود لقوله تعالى : { مَن لَّعَنَهُ الله وَغَضِبَ عَلَيْهِ } [ المائدة : 60 ]

NASAFI:1:7/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r8.speaker: البصريون
NASAFI:1:7/r8.claim: Basran grammarians treat la as an extra particle for emphasis.
NASAFI:1:7/r8.anchor: و«لا » زائدة عند البصريين للتوكيد ، وعند الكوفيين هي بمعنى غير

NASAFI:1:7/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r9.speaker: الكوفيون
NASAFI:1:7/r9.claim: Kufan grammarians understand la here to mean ghayr, ‘other than.’

NASAFI:1:7/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:7/r10.claim: Amin is a spoken formula meaning ‘answer/respond,’ treated as a noun for the imperative just as ruwayd means ‘wait.’ It has long and short forms; the short vowel length is original, while the long form lengthens the hamza.
NASAFI:1:7/r10.anchor: آمين صوت سمي به الفعل الذي هو استجب كما أن رويد اسم لأمهل

NASAFI:1:7/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r11.speaker: ابن عباس عن رسول الله
NASAFI:1:7/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas asked the Messenger about amin’s meaning, and he answered, ‘Do it.’
NASAFI:1:7/r11.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن معنى آمين فقال : «افعل »

NASAFI:1:7/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI:1:7/r12.claim: A cited poem witnesses the long form amina; another line uses amin and asks God to increase the distance between the lovers.
NASAFI:1:7/r12.anchor: قال : يا رب لا تسلبّني حبها أبدا*** ويرحم الله عبداً قال آمينا

NASAFI:1:7/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:1:7/r13.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
NASAFI:1:7/r13.claim: The Prophet said Gabriel taught him amin after he finished reciting the Fatiha and compared it to a seal on a letter; amin is not Qur’an because it does not appear in the codices.
NASAFI:1:7/r13.anchor: لقنني جبريل آمين عند فراغي من قراءة فاتحة الكتاب

QURTUBI:1:7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r1.claim: “The path of those” is an appositive replacing the first mention of the path, as in “Zayd, your father, came to me.”
QURTUBI:1:7/r1.anchor: صراط بدل من الأول بدل الشيء من الشيء

QURTUBI:1:7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r2.claim: The request means “Keep guiding us”: a person may be guided to a road and then cut off from it.
QURTUBI:1:7/r2.anchor: أدم هدايتنا ، فإن الإنسان قد يهدى إلى الطريق ثم يقطع به

QURTUBI:1:7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r3.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
QURTUBI:1:7/r3.claim: Ja'far ibn Muhammad offers another path: knowledge of God and understanding from Him.
QURTUBI:1:7/r3.anchor: وقيل : هو صراط آخر ، ومعناه العلم بالله جل وعز والفهم عنه ، قاله جعفر بن محمد

QURTUBI:1:7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r4.claim: Qur'anic usage has alladhina in three cases; Hudhayl has nominative alladhun, and other Arabs use alladhu or alladhi.
QURTUBI:1:7/r4.anchor: ولغة القرآن " الذين " في الرفع والنصب والجر وهذيل تقول : اللذون في الرفع

QURTUBI:1:7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r5.claim: Ten alayhim forms include six transmitted reader forms (varying hāʾ/mīm vowels, added yāʾ or wāw) and four further forms transmitted from Arabs: عليهُمِ, عليهُم, عليهِمُ, عليهِمِ.
QURTUBI:1:7/r5.anchor: وهذه الأوجه الستة مأثورة عن الأئمة من القراء

QURTUBI:1:7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI:1:7/r6.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says all ten pronunciations of alayhim are correct.

QURTUBI:1:7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن الزبير
QURTUBI:1:7/r7.claim: Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr read “the path of whom You favored,” using man instead of alladhina.
QURTUBI:1:7/r7.anchor: قرأ عمر بن الخطاب وابن الزبير رضي الله عنهما " صراط من أنعمت عليهم "

QURTUBI:1:7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r8.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
QURTUBI:1:7/r8.claim: Most commentators identify those favored as prophets, truthful, martyrs, and righteous, following 4:69; al-Qurtubi says other views return to this.
QURTUBI:1:7/r8.anchor: فقال الجمهور من المفسرين : إنه أراد صراط النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين

QURTUBI:1:7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r9.claim: The verse refutes Qadariyya, Mu'tazila, and Imamiya claims that human will suffices and humans create their acts: repeated requests for guidance and protection from deviation show dependence on God, as does 3:8.
QURTUBI:1:7/r9.anchor: في هذه الآية رد على القدرية والمعتزلة والإمامية ؛ لأنهم يعتقدون أن إرادة الإنسان كافية

QURTUBI:1:7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r10.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
QURTUBI:1:7/r10.claim: Most commentators identify those under wrath as Jews and the astray as Christians; 2:61, 3:112, and 48:6 concern Jewish wrath, and 5:77 Christian error.
QURTUBI:1:7/r10.anchor: فالجمهور أن المغضوب عليهم اليهود والضالين النصارى ، وجاء ذلك مفسرا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI:1:7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI:1:7/r11.claim: The Prophet's interpretation is transmitted in Adi ibn Hatim's report; al-Qurtubi calls it best and most authoritative. No grading is stated.
QURTUBI:1:7/r11.anchor: في حديث عدي بن حاتم وقصة إسلامه ، أخرجه أبو داود الطيالسي في مسنده

QURTUBI:1:7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:1:7/r12.claim: An alternative says those under wrath are polytheists and the astray are hypocrites.
QURTUBI:1:7/r12.anchor: وقيل : " المغضوب عليهم " المشركون . و " الضالين " المنافقون

QURTUBI:1:7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r13.speaker: السلمي والماوردي
QURTUBI:1:7/r13.claim: Al-Sulami and al-Mawardi report that those under wrath neglect the sura in prayer and the astray miss its blessing.
QURTUBI:1:7/r13.anchor: حكاه السلمي في حقائقه والماوردي في تفسيره وليس بشيء

QURTUBI:1:7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r14.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI:1:7/r14.claim: Al-Mawardi rejects that view: where reports conflict and disagreement spreads, one cannot assign this judgment to the verse.
QURTUBI:1:7/r14.anchor: قال الماوردي : وهذا وجه مردود ؛ لأن ما تعارضت فيه الأخبار وتقابلت فيه الآثار وانتشر فيه الخلاف

QURTUBI:1:7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:1:7/r15.claim: Another view assigns wrath to followers of innovations and error to those straying from prophetic practices; al-Qurtubi calls it good but prefers the Prophet's explanation.
QURTUBI:1:7/r15.anchor: وقيل : " المغضوب عليهم " باتباع البدع و " الضالين " عن سنن الهدى . قلت : وهذا حسن

QURTUBI:1:7/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r16.claim: Alayhim is grammatically nominative in sense because the underlying construction is “wrath came upon them.”
QURTUBI:1:7/r16.anchor: في موضع رفع ؛ لأن المعنى غضب عليهم

QURTUBI:1:7/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r17.claim: Arabic anger connotes severity: a harsh person is ghadub, a fierce serpent al-ghadub, and a folded camel-hide shield ghadba for its toughness.
QURTUBI:1:7/r17.anchor: والغضب في اللغة الشدة . ورجل غضوب أي شديد الخلق . والغضوب : الحية الخبيثة لشدتها

QURTUBI:1:7/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r18.claim: Divine anger can mean God's will to punish, an essential attribute, or the punishment itself, an attribute of action; a hadith says charity extinguishes the Lord's anger.
QURTUBI:1:7/r18.anchor: ومعنى الغضب في صفة الله تعالى إرادة العقوبة ، فهو صفة ذات

QURTUBI:1:7/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r19.claim: Dalal is departure from the intended course and truth; milk disappearing into water illustrates it, as does 32:10 for being lost in earth through death and becoming dust.
QURTUBI:1:7/r19.anchor: الضلال في كلام العرب هو الذهاب عن سنن القصد وطريق الحق ، ومنه : ضل اللبن في الماء أي غاب

QURTUBI:1:7/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r20.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r20.claim: Duldula means a smooth stone rolled along by water in a valley; ghadba can mean a differently colored mountain rock, illustrated by poetry.
QURTUBI:1:7/r20.anchor: والضُّلَضِلَة : حجر أملس يردده الماء في الوادي

QURTUBI:1:7/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r21.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وأبي بن كعب
QURTUBI:1:7/r21.claim: Umar and Ubayy read ghayr with accusative or genitive r; genitive parses as apposition or adjective, with two explanations for its definiteness, attributed respectively to al-Farisi and al-Zamakhshari.
QURTUBI:1:7/r21.anchor: قرأ عمر بن الخطاب وأبي بن كعب

QURTUBI:1:7/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r22.claim: Accusative ghayr can be circumstantial or an exception; al-Khalil also permits an implied “I mean.”
QURTUBI:1:7/r22.anchor: والنصب في الراء على وجهين : على الحال من الذين

QURTUBI:1:7/r23.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r23.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI:1:7/r23.claim: Al-Tabari regards la in “nor the astray” as extra, as in 7:12.
QURTUBI:1:7/r23.anchor: فقيل هي زائدة ، قاله الطبري . ومنه قوله تعالى

QURTUBI:1:7/r24.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r24.speaker: مكي والمهداوي
QURTUBI:1:7/r24.claim: Makki and al-Mahdawi say la is emphatic, preventing the assumption that the astray are joined to those favored.
QURTUBI:1:7/r24.anchor: وقيل : هي تأكيد دخلت لئلا يتوهم أن الضالين معطوف على الذين

QURTUBI:1:7/r25.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r25.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI:1:7/r25.claim: The Kufans take la to mean ghayr, citing Umar's and Ubayy's reading.

QURTUBI:1:7/r26.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r26.speaker: author
QURTUBI:1:7/r26.claim: The underlying form is al-dallilin: the first lam loses its vowel and assimilates into the next.
QURTUBI:1:7/r26.anchor: الأصل في " الضالين " : الضاللين حذفت حركة اللام الأولى ثم أدغمت اللام في اللام

QURTUBI:1:7/r27.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r27.speaker: أيوب السختياني
QURTUBI:1:7/r27.claim: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani reads with an unlengthened hamza to avoid two adjacent vowelless sounds; al-Qurtubi calls it a dialect.
QURTUBI:1:7/r27.anchor: وقرأ أيوب السختياني : " ولا الضالين " بهمزة غير ممدودة

QURTUBI:1:7/r28.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r28.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI:1:7/r28.claim: Abu Zayd heard Amr ibn Ubayd use the dialectal hamza in 55:39; Arabs also say da'bah and sha'bah.
QURTUBI:1:7/r28.anchor: حكى أبو زيد قال : سمعت عمرو بن عبيد - يقرأ : " فيومئذ لا يسأل عن ذنبه إنس ولا جأن "

QURTUBI:1:7/r29.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:1:7/r29.speaker: أبو الفتح
QURTUBI:1:7/r29.claim: Abu al-Fath cites Kathir's form ahma'arrat as evidence for the same dialect.
QURTUBI:1:7/r29.anchor: وعلى هذه اللغة قول كُثَير : إذا ماالعَوَالي بالعَبِيطِ احْمَأَرَّتِ

RAZI:1:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:1/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:1:1/r1.claim: Razi sketches the sūra’s sequence: seek refuge from sins, begin good works in God’s name, praise and recognize his lordship and mercy, heed judgment, worship and seek help, ask guidance, and avoid ignorance and error.
RAZI:1:1/r1.anchor: بسم الله الرحمان الرحيم } نشرع في أداء كل الخيرات والمأمورات

RAZI:1:7/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r1.claim: Razi presents the path of those favored by God as a station of extraordinary rank, whose beginnings become visible through the preceding exposition.
RAZI:1:7/r1.anchor: فما أجل هذه المقامات وأعظم مراتب هذه الدرجات

RAZI:1:7/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r2.claim: The sūra contains inexhaustible discussions and secrets; the claim that it contains ten thousand questions suits the audience's understanding of its vast implications.
RAZI:1:7/r2.anchor: هذه السورة مشتملة على مباحث لا نهاية لها ، وأسرار لا غاية لها

RAZI:1:7/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r3.claim: Razi illustrates how analyzing Aʿūdhu billāh requires definitions and subdivisions of nouns, verbs, particles, and the possible derivations of the name Allah.
RAZI:1:7/r3.anchor: لا يمكن تحصيل به العلم كما ينبغي إلا بعد معرفة الاسم والفعل والحرف أولا

RAZI:1:7/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r4.claim: The inquiry can descend from words into speech and phonetics, respiratory and vocal anatomy, sensory qualities, philosophical categories, substances, accidents, existence, and knowledge.
RAZI:1:7/r4.anchor: المباحث المتعلقة بالصوت وكيفية حدوثه وكيفية العضلات المحدثة للأصوات والحروف

RAZI:1:7/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r5.claim: At the furthest epistemological stage, he asks how the unknown can be judged contrary to the known if its nature is unknown, since that judgment would make it known.
RAZI:1:7/r5.anchor: فلما حكمنا على غير المعلوم بكونه مقابلا للمعلوم ، وجب أن يكون غير المعلوم معلوما

RAZI:1:7/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r6.claim: A second method counts every proof, objection, reply, and separately stated linguistic alternative as its own question, multiplying the issues extracted from a short passage.
RAZI:1:7/r6.anchor: كل واحد من تلك الوجوه والدلائل مسألة بنفسها

RAZI:1:7/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r7.claim: Razi distinguishes ordinary derivation from greater derivation, which studies permutations of a word's consonants; he gives 2, 6, 24, and 120 permutations for words of two through five letters.
RAZI:1:7/r7.anchor: أما الاشتقاق الأصغر فمثل اشتقاق صيغة الماضي والمستقبل من المصدر

RAZI:1:7/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r8.claim: Greater derivation is difficult beyond triliteral roots because quadriliteral and quinqueliteral permutations proliferate and are mostly unused; even triliteral roots often have unused permutations.
RAZI:1:7/r8.anchor: كأنه لا يمكن رعايته إلا في الكلمات الثلاثية لأن تقاليبها لا تزيد على الستة

RAZI:1:7/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r9.claim: Razi says five permutations of ك ل م are attested and share force or intensity: speech affects hearing and mind, a wound, rough ground, striking, kneading, and power.
RAZI:1:7/r9.anchor: تركيب الكاف واللام والميم بحسب تقاليبها الممكنة الستة تفيد القوة والشدة

RAZI:1:7/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r10.claim: Kalima can denote one word or extended connected speech; the latter is metaphorical, by part-for-whole naming or because connected speech resembles a single unit.
RAZI:1:7/r10.anchor: إطلاق لفظ الكلمة على المركب مجاز ، وذلك لوجهين

RAZI:1:7/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r11.claim: The Qurʾānic uses of kalima include Jesus, created by God's command or in a short time, and God's acts, called His words; both uses are explained by the preceding metaphorical grounds.
RAZI:1:7/r11.anchor: يقال لعيسى كلمة الله ، إما لأنه حدث بقوله «كن » أو لأنه

RAZI:1:7/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:1:7/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:1:7/r12.claim: Razi reads the six permutations of ق و ل as expressing movement or lightness, explaining qawl as easy on the tongue and adducing examples such as the swift bird and animal.
RAZI:1:7/r12.anchor: هذا التركيب بحسب تقاليبه الستة يدل على الحركة والخفة
